title: refactor(parser): delegate redshift, googlesql, trino, doris, starrocks, cassandra analysis to omni
body:
## Summary

Switches the remaining six parser adapters (`redshift`, `googlesql` [shared by `bigquery` and `spanner`], `trino`, `doris`, `starrocks`, `cassandra`) to delegate query-span extraction and statement analysis helpers to `github.com/bytebase/omni/<engine>/analysis`, removing the local Bytebase duplicates (-5k+ net lines across 67 files):

- **redshift**: Deleted `query_span_extractor.go`, `system_objects.go`, `system_resource.go`; delegated `GetQuerySpan` (`analysis.ResolveQuerySpan`), `validateQuery` (`analysis.ValidateQuery`), `explainStatement` (`analysis.ExplainStatement`), `statementWithResultLimit` (`analysis.StatementWithResultLimit`), `Diagnose` (`analysis.Diagnose`), `extractChangedResources` (`analysis.ExtractChangedResources`), `GetStatementType` (`analysis.StatementTypeOf`), and `GetStatementRanges` (`analysis.StatementRanges` + UTF-16 mapper).
- **googlesql**: Collapsed `query_span_extractor.go` onto `omni/googlesql/analysis.ResolveQuerySpan` and `statement_type.go` onto `analysis.StatementTypeOf`, removing unused `IsSetStatement` from `query_type.go`.
- **trino**: Deleted `query_span_extractor.go` and `query_type.go` (plus unused `viewDefinitions` in `completion.go`); delegated `GetQuerySpan` (`analysis.ResolveQuerySpan`, with `WithFunctionStmt` inner-query fallback until https://github.com/bytebase/omni/issues/1497), `Diagnose` (`analysis.Diagnose`), and `validateQuery` (`analysis.ValidateQuery`, still refusing un-explained/`EXPLAIN ANALYZE` `WithFunctionStmt` until https://github.com/bytebase/omni/issues/1497 while allowing plain `EXPLAIN`).
- **doris & starrocks**: Deleted local `query_span_extractor.go` and `query_type.go` in both forked engines; delegated `GetQuerySpan`, `explainStatement`, `statementWithResultLimit`, `Diagnose`, `validateQuery`, `SplitSQL`, `GetStatementRanges` (+ UTF-16 mapper), and `extractChangedResources` to `omni/{doris,starrocks}/analysis`. In StarRocks, `_statistics_` remains a system database (workaround in `starrocks/query_span.go`), `EXPLAIN`/`DESC` with `INTO OUTFILE` stays refused (`starrocks/query.go`, checked when `"outfile"` appears), and plan-only `TRACE ... SELECT` (`OptimizerTraceStmt`) is now accepted as read-only by `omni/starrocks/analysis.ValidateQuery`. Updated Doris `_statistics_` fixture, `SET GLOBAL` validation rows, and fallback `LIMIT` test expectations to match `omni`. Tracking issue for remaining `omni` follow-ups: https://github.com/bytebase/omni/issues/1497.
- **cassandra**: Deleted `query_span_extractor.go` and delegated `GetQuerySpan` to `omni/cassandra/analysis.ResolveQuerySpan`.

## Verification

- `GOGC=off GOMEMLIMIT=10GiB golangci-lint run -j 8 --allow-parallel-runners` — 0 issues.
- `go test -count=1 ./backend/plugin/parser/redshift/... ./backend/plugin/parser/googlesql/... ./backend/plugin/parser/bigquery/... ./backend/plugin/parser/spanner/... ./backend/plugin/parser/trino/... ./backend/plugin/parser/doris/... ./backend/plugin/parser/starrocks/... ./backend/pl

title: fix(mcp): close a session that sits idle for an hour (BYT-10375)
body:
## Summary

Clients that leave `/mcp` without sending DELETE left their sessions open until the process exited. go-sdk keeps a stateful session until it gets a DELETE, a failed initialize, or its `SessionTimeout` fires, and Bytebase set no timeout. Each session held one goroutine parked in `streamableServerConn.Read` and about 9 KiB. In #21721 a production server had 27,904 such goroutines 48 hours after a restart, from a few people using the Claude MCP connector.

- The handler sets `SessionTimeout` to `mcpSessionIdleTimeout`, one hour. A session closes once it has gone that long with no POST in flight.
- A POST in flight pauses the clock, so a long call is not cut off. A confirmation form is shown inside its tool call (`TestDecideIssueApprovesOnConfirmation`), so it is held open the same way; that case was not timed. A GET, new or held open, does not reset the clock.
- A client that comes back after expiry gets 404 and must initialize again, as the MCP spec requires.
- `newServerWithStore` delegates to the new `newServerWithIdleTimeout`, so tests shorten the timeout through the production construction.

The Cloud SQL dialer leak that #21721 first reported is a separate bug, fixed in #21726 (3.24.1 and 3.25.0).

## This reverses #21299

#21299 left `SessionTimeout` unset: "reaping a live idle session breaks it: the SDK client does not re-initialize, it surfaces the error." That is still true of go-sdk's client. The cost of no timeout is now measured, and it is larger: the leak grows without bound. On the #21721 server it likely raised the memory baseline; both OOM kills there coincided with SQL Editor results over 100,000 rows.

## What a client sees

Measured with Claude Code 2.1.328 in `-p` mode, against main plus a 2-minute timeout, through a logging proxy:

- The session closed two minutes after the last call. No ping kept it alive.
- The next tool call got 404. Claude Code initialized again, retried on the new session, and the call returned its normal result.
- Recovery opened three sessions within about a second, and none was deleted when the process exited. The timeout will close them, as it closed the session in the next bullet.
- A process that exits without DELETE leaves its session open. The timeout closed it two minutes after its last request.

The claude.ai connector is not checked yet (test plan, last item).

## Breaking Changes

- An MCP session now closes once it has gone an hour with no POST in flight. A client that returns after that gets 404 and must initialize again, as the MCP spec requires.
- Claude Code 2.1.328 does this in `-p` mode (above); its interactive UI and the claude.ai connector are not checked yet. An app built on go-sdk's client gets `ErrSessionMissing` and has to reconnect. Before this change, its idle session stayed open until the server restarted.

## Not in this change

- **A form the client shows and then abandons**, a confirmation or a database choice. The tool call waits for the answer with no deadline,

No rule logic changed.

`statementLineForOffset` stays in `snowflake/base_rule.go`: `rule_where_require_select.go:51` calls it.

## 2. The stale SDL guide (`5f27c8ae87`)

The 2,079-line `docs/adding-new-object-to-sdl-mode.md` described the pre-cutover architecture; its samples called `schema.MetadataDiff`, `base.NewGraph`, `generateCreateTable`, and `schema.SDLChunks`, none of which exists after the cutovers. It is replaced by a short guide to the current contract:

- omni owns the metadata protobuf (`DatabaseSchemaMetadata`, `SchemaMetadata`) and the engine catalog (load, definition, diff, migration).
- `backend/plugin/schema/<engine>` registers catalog entry points; `backend/plugin/schema/schema.go` dispatches them through `GetDatabaseDefinition`, `GetDatabaseMetadata`, `SDLMigration`, `DiffSDLMigration`, and `DiffMigration`.
- The MySQL-family metadata wrapper is `omnicatalog.Engine` / `omnicatalog.DiffMetadata`; the unloadable-object lookup is `omnicatalog.snapshotObject`, and PostgreSQL's equivalent is `snapshotObjects`.
- Each path maps to an existing test: `get_database_definition_test.go` with `testdata/get_database_definition.yaml`, `get_database_metadata_test.go` with `testdata/get_database_metadata.yaml`, `metadata_migration_test.go`, `sdl_migration_test.go` (`TestSDLMigration_CreateTable`, `TestMySQLSDLDropAdvices`), and the driver's `TestDumpRendersTheSyncedMetadata`.

Every cited path resolves in this tree; every cited Go symbol was checked with `git grep -n -w`.

title: fix(db): read CockroachDB task run sessions from its catalog
body:
## Summary

`GetTaskRunSession` fell through to the `db.SQLDB` fallback for CockroachDB and ran PostgreSQL's session query. That query fails on CockroachDB:

```
unknown signature: pg_blocking_pids(int) (SQLSTATE 42883)
```

Removing only `pg_blocking_pids` is not enough: CockroachDB's `pg_stat_activity` compatibility view answers **no rows**, so the endpoint returned an empty session. This was visible through the product API on `cockroachdb/cockroach:v25.2.3` with a running task:

```
cluster_queries: SELECT pg_sleep(20)   application_name=bytebase-taskrun-<uid>
pg_stat_activity: 0 rows
```

CockroachDB now reads the active query from `crdb_internal.cluster_queries` left-joined with `crdb_internal.cluster_sessions` on `session_id`, mapping `session_id`, `query`, `phase`, `database`, `user_name`, `application_name`, `client_address`, `session_start` (`BackendStart`, left unset if unavailable), and `start` (`QueryStart`) onto `TaskRunSession.Postgres.Session`. Blocking relationships stay empty because CockroachDB has no `pg_blocking_pids` equivalent.

## Tests

- `TestGetSessionCockroachFallback` (new, `backend/api/v1/rollout_service_test.go`) runs the fallback through sqlmock, asserts the query reads `crdb_internal.cluster_queries` and `crdb_internal.cluster_sessions` (and rejects `pg_stat_activity` and `pg_blocking_pids`), uses string session IDs, and verifies `BackendStart` / `QueryStart` mapping including when `session_start` is unavailable.
- `go test -count=1 ./backend/api/v1/`
- `golangci-lint run --fix` then `golangci-lint run`, both clean.
- Product-path check against `cockroachdb/cockroach:v25.2.3`: a task run executing `SELECT pg_sleep(20)` returns `application_name=bytebase-taskrun-102`, `query=SELECT pg_sleep(20)` from `GetTaskRunSession`, and multi-statement sessions preserve `session_start` across queries. PostgreSQL's reader path was re-run and still returns its session.

Not merged; opened for review.

title: chore(deps): pin omni to main 8ca542c01
body:
The omni pin has been `v0.0.0-20261118130520-426aecf60b7e`, a merge of `bytebase/omni#1430`'s head (`f48105a`) onto the then-current `main` (`3ffa03a`). It is not an ancestor of `main`: `main` is `8ca542c01`, and `426aecf` shares no future with it, so the next digest bump would have walked past that branch merge and dropped `#1430` silently.

This pins `main` instead.

**The pin**

```
github.com/bytebase/omni v0.0.0-20261119114350-8ca542c0188d
```

`8ca542c0188dbc4ca18db65d5ad7f4d469ec37a9` is `origin/main` at the time of writing (`fix(starrocks): work the rest of compat.tsv, 203 rows to none (#1467)`), and `git merge-base --is-ancestor 8ca542c01 origin/main` holds. It is 51 commits ahead of the branch point the old pin was built on (`3ffa03a`).

**`#1430`, now on `main`, and what it changes for Doris**

`#1430` landed on `main` as `6d4568b`. The old pin carried the same content only because it pinned that PR's head — which is the whole reason for this bump.

A Doris kernel built without the PL/SQL grammar (SelectDB 4.0.12+/4.1.8+/5.0.5+, apache/doris#58700), or an account without the catalogue's privilege, answers the function and procedure catalogues with an error instead of an empty set. The dump used to fail whole, which Bytebase reads as "this database states no schema at all". Now:

- the dump keeps the objects it can state and leaves the routines out, but only for the three refusals the server states about the probe itself: a statement the kernel's grammar has no rule for, the `1044`/`1142`/`1227` privilege refusals, and "Table [routines] does not exist in database [information_schema]";
- every other `1105` — an internal error, an overload, a query timeout, "No backend available as scan node" — still fails the dump, so a database whose backends are down no longer syncs with every function silently missing;
- a view calling a function the dump cannot state is now an error naming the view and the function, instead of a script that cannot be restored.

`starrocks/driver` is unchanged: its dump sends no routine probe. Bytebase's Doris adapter is a pass-through to `omni/doris/driver`, so this is the user-visible fix the pin carries.

**What the rest of the 51 commits are**

Compat work on parsers and catalogs: StarRocks's `compat.tsv` tail and its `TRACE`/`CACHE`/task/load/`DESC` plans (`#1467`, `#1433`, `#1461`), Doris `COPY INTO` and procedure statements (`#1437`), GoogleSQL pipe syntax, `TABLE`, `SHOW`, `IMPORT MODULE`, `UNDROP`, graph subqueries and `CREATE PROPERTY GRAPH OPTIONS` (`#1444`, `#1452`, `#1462`, `#1470`), OceanBase table factors, expressions and materialized-view DDL (`#1443`, `#1440`, `#1474`, `#1465`, `#1423`), plus code-accurate refusals for MySQL/MariaDB/TiDB/Oracle/MSSQL/Redshift/Snowflake/Trino. `pg` moves test data only, and `bigquery`, `clickhouse`, `spanner`, `cockroachdb`, `databricks`, `dynamodb`, `elasticsearch`, `hive`, `mongo`, `redis` and the shared `driver`/`metadata` packages are untouched.

title: fix(review): stop calling P2 findings advisory only
body:
## Summary

The P2 priority badge's tooltip said "Advisory only." (zh-CN "仅供参考。"). But every open thread holds the automatic rollout whatever its priority, under SQL Review V2 and beside V1 alike. So an unresolved P2 stops the rollout while its badge says it has no effect.

The tooltip now says what resolving the thread means, as P1's already does, and leaves blocking to the rollout footer ("N unresolved threads. Rollout was not created automatically."):

| Locale | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| en-US | Advisory only. | A suggestion. Resolve it once read, whether or not you apply it. |
| zh-CN | 仅供参考。 | 建议项。阅读后即可解决，不要求采纳。 |
| ja-JP | 参考情報です。 | 提案です。確認したら、採用しない場合も解決してください。 |
| es-ES | Solo informativo. | Una sugerencia. Se resuelve tras leerla, se aplique o no. |
| vi-VN | Chỉ mang tính tham khảo. | Một gợi ý. Hãy giải quyết sau khi đọc, dù có áp dụng hay không. |

The same text is the hover hint on the P2 count in the Review status bar. P0 still has no tooltip and P1's is unchanged.

Two comments are corrected as well:
- `useAIReviewBesideV1`: the AI review's findings do hold the rollout, as open threads.
- `LevelPriorityBadge`: V1 levels only *display* as P0/P1. A V1 error still holds the rollout and a warning does not.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm fix`: no changes
- [x] `pnpm test`: 803/804 files passed. The one failure, `src/modules/agent/store/agent.test.ts`, is in a module this PR does not touch, and it passed when rerun alone together with `ReviewResult.test.tsx`
- [x] Each locale resolves `plan.review.thread.priority.p2` to the new text
- [ ] Not checked in a browser: a P2 thread comes only from an AI review run, and the E2E harness has no AI model configured

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: chore(agent): distinguish API failures from unknown outcomes
body:
- Separate RPC outcomes from side effects, including not-sent, acknowledged, failed, unknown, and partial results.
- Prevent silent replay of protected requests while retaining normal confirmation and continuation workflows.
- Preserve receipts across reloads and tabs, show outcomes inline, and warn before intentionally repeating uncertain requests.
- Harden result deduplication, history cleanup, and legacy receipt migration.

+import { useTranslation } from "react-i18next";
+import type { AgentApiExecutionEvidence } from "../logic/apiExecution";
+
+export function AgentApiOutcome({
+  execution,
+}: {
+  execution?: AgentApiExecutionEvidence;
+}) {
+  const { t } = useTranslation();
+  if (execution?.result === "not-sent") return t("agent.api-recovery.not-sent");
+  switch (execution?.effects) {
+    case "acknowledged":
+      return t("agent.api-recovery.acknowledged");
+    case "partial":
+      return t("agent.api-recovery.partial");
+    case "none":
+      return execution.reason === "import-none-created"
+        ? t("agent.api-recovery.none-created")
+        : t("agent.api-recovery.rejected");
+    case "possible":
+      if (execution.result === "failed")
+        return t("agent.api-recovery.failed-possible");
+      if (execution.result === "succeeded")
+        return t("agent.api-recovery.possible");
+  }
+  return t("agent.api-recovery.unknown");

title: feat(review): run the AI SQL review beside SQL Review V1
body:
## Summary

Runs the AI SQL review beside SQL Review V1, for workspaces that keep V1's review policies and plan checks and want the AI review on top of them. The AI review never reads or writes V1 configuration: its findings are issue comments, and V1's policies and levels stay as they are. Under SQL Review V2 (dev builds) the existing behavior is kept, except where noted.

## Changes

### AI review beside SQL Review V1

- On servers without SQL Review V2, the AI review runs as an add-on to V1. Its prompt states no standard rule; the V2 prompt is unchanged.
- It runs from the draft onward, as under V2: it starts when the issue is created and again whenever the plan's SQL changes, and RunReview accepts a draft. Submitting for review does not review the same SQL again.
- Findings are comment threads on the SQL and in Activity, authored by "AI review", the name the review uses everywhere beside V1.

![Inline AI review comment](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/rebelice/44bab6764a672cadcae1a07233c6963b/raw/06-issue-inline-comment.png)

### Open comment threads hold the rollout beside V1

- Beside V1, every open comment thread holds the automatic rollout, whoever opened it (AI review or a person), and resolving a thread asks the rollout creator to check again. Under V2 the review and its threads already held the rollout; that is unchanged.
- Deploy states the condition: "Bytebase will automatically create the rollout when all checks pass, every thread is resolved, and the issue is approved."

![Deploy condition](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/rebelice/44bab6764a672cadcae1a07233c6963b/raw/09-deploy-condition.png)

### Plan and issue page

- The Review section's Automated review bar shows the AI review together with V1's checks (SQL review, online migration, plan check run). Every row has the same format: conclusion, counts, Details (the latest run in Activity, or the Checks drawer) and Rerun. While the AI review applies, the Changes section drops its Checks row and shows the affected-rows estimate under the SQL.
- Beside V1 the Review section opens on a draft too: the approval note ("Approval starts when you submit for review."), the Automated review bar, and Activity with the comment box. Before, a V1 draft showed only "Submit for review to proceed".

![Automated review bar](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/rebelice/44bab6764a672cadcae1a07233c6963b/raw/07-issue-automated-review.png)

![Draft review](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/rebelice/44bab6764a672cadcae1a07233c6963b/raw/10-draft-review.png)

### V1 levels shown as the review's priorities

Display only; stored policies and results keep their levels. An error shows as P0 (the SQL must change) and a warning as P1 (a person must accept it), in the AI review's colors:

- Policy pages: the level switch, the level filter and the "Priority" column (was "Error Level").
- Every plan check result: the Automated review counts, the Checks drawer (filters, summary, each result), the Changes section'

title: fix(frontend): render every dropdown in the overlay layer (BYT-10562)
body:
Fixes BYT-10562.

## Before

On the project Issues page, opening a filter such as `current-approver:` drew the status tabs (Waiting for Approval / Open / Closed / All) on top of the menu's heading and help text.

![Before: the status tabs paint over the Current approver menu](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d67aa0a6-3171-4c0c-b3ac-ddc92dd7c0d5)

The search menu was rendered inline: `absolute` with `LAYER_SURFACE_CLASS`, which is `z-10`. The status tabs also carry `z-10`, and nothing between the two creates a stacking context, so the tie went to DOM order and the tabs, which come later, won.

The tabs were one case of a general problem. Five hand-built dropdowns used the same inline pattern, and `Combobox` did too unless the caller passed `portal`. Any of them could be covered by a later sibling with its own `z-index` (sticky table headers, the plan detail header at `z-20`) or clipped by an `overflow` ancestor. `check-layering` didn't catch them, because it can't resolve what an imported constant like `LAYER_SURFACE_CLASS` contains.

## After

The menu renders in the overlay layer, above the page, and covers the tabs.

![After: the Current approver menu renders above the status tabs](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/20f16cbe-7494-4ece-902a-50e2d5fc0c2f)

Every dropdown, popover and floating panel now mounts into `getLayerRoot("overlay")`:

| Surface | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `AdvancedSearch` (19 pages: issues, plans, releases, databases, audit log, SQL Editor panes…) | inline `absolute z-10` | shared `Popover`, anchored to the search bar at its width. Focus stays in the input, which keeps owning arrow keys, Enter and Escape |
| `AccountMultiSelect` (Members, grant-access dialog, masking exemptions, saved-query grants) | inline | `Popover` with the field as trigger; the search box takes focus on open |
| Issue label picker | inline | `Popover` |
| Issue review popover (desktop) | inline | `Popover`, right-aligned under the Review button |
| Sync Schema changelog picker | inline | `Popover` |
| `Combobox` and its wrappers | inline unless the caller passed `portal` | always portaled; the `portal` prop is removed from `Combobox`, 6 wrappers and 20 call sites |
| `SelectionActionBar` | inline `fixed z-10` | the viewport bar mounts into the overlay layer; the container bar keeps a local `z-10` |

The four components that used `useClickOutside` (or `useEscapeKey`) now use Popover's own dismissal. `AdvancedSearch` keeps its outside-press handler, which now treats a press inside the menu as inside the search.

Comboboxes that rendered inline could grow wider than their field (`w-max`). Now every Combobox is exactly the field's width, as the ones that already passed `portal` were, so long option text wraps.

## Guardrail

`check-layering` has a new rule: a feature file that uses `LAYER_SURFACE_CLASS` or `LAYER_BACKDROP_CLASS` must mount into `getLayerRoot`. Otherwise the class is just a bare `z-10` on an inline element. Run aga

title: refactor(review): remove run_type from stored review results (BYT-10523)
body:
## Problem

A stored review result names the reviewer that found it: `run_type` is `RULE` or `AI`. Since #22104 and #22120, one thread holds what both reviewers say about an operation, so the label no longer describes a thread. The rerun is the only code that reads it, to tell a rule's thread from a thread of the AI review. `rule_type` already tells that: a result of a standard rule carries it, and a result that the AI review posts on its own does not.

## Change

This is step 3 after #22104 and #22120, and the last one ([BYT-10523](https://linear.app/bytebase/issue/BYT-10523)).

- **Proto.** `run_type` is removed from `IssueCommentPayload.ReviewMetadata`. It is also removed from `ReviewRunCompletion`, where no code reads or writes it. The `ReviewRun.Type` enum goes with them. Both fields are reserved by number and by name, because the stored JSON is keyed by name.
- **Rerun.** `earlierResults` takes a result with `rule_type` set as a rule's thread, and any other result as the AI review's.
- **Store.** `CompleteReviewRun` rejects a result with no review metadata. It used to reject a result that named no reviewer.
- **No migration.** Rows written before this change keep the `runType` key. The store decodes a comment with `DiscardUnknown`, so the key is ignored, and `rule_type` tells those rows apart as it does new ones.

Only the store proto changes. The v1 API and the frontend have had no `run_type` since the review became one run per issue.

Example, the same rule finding stored before and after:

```jsonc
// before
{"runType": "RULE", "ruleType": "DISALLOW_DROP_OBJECT", "codes": ["DO101"], "priority": "P1"}
// after
{"ruleType": "DISALLOW_DROP_OBJECT", "codes": ["DO101"], "priority": "P1"}
```

## Tests

- `TestListIssueCommentReadsRowsThatHoldRunType` reads a rule's result, an AI review's result, and a completion event that still hold the key.
- `TestReviewRunKeepsBothReviewersThreadsAcrossRuns` drives both real executors through the store twice. The second time it writes the key back into the stored rows after the first run. Both times a rerun keeps both threads, and a run with the AI review off supersedes the AI review's thread.
- The full store suite, the review run tests in `backend/api/v1`, and the claim and collision tests in `backend/tests` pass. Lint is clean in the changed files, and the server builds.
- Codex review: one local round, clean.
- On a dev server whose metadata held 181 results and 30 completion events with the key: reruns of two issues kept their threads and priorities, and a new issue's results are stored without the key.

### Live runs

Real omni rules and real models, through `ReviewExecutor` and `CompleteReviewRun`, on `main` at `ea6d1108bf` and on this branch. Seven cases, five runs each, on `claude-sonnet-5-5`, `gemini-3.8-flash`, and `deepseek-v4-pro`.

title: feat(instance): support connection string autofill for additional engines
body:
## Summary

Extend **Import from URL** connection-string autofill on the create-instance form (following #22102) from 4 engines (`MySQL`, `PostgreSQL`, `SQL Server`, `Oracle`) to all 20 credential/endpoint-based engines in Bytebase. `PostgreSQL + Neon` keeps its existing ADR-0006 field, and the 4 cloud-IAM-only engines (`Spanner`, `BigQuery`, `DynamoDB`, `CosmosDB`) remain excluded.

### Newly supported engines (16)

- **MySQL family**: `MariaDB` (`mariadb://`, `mysql://`; port `3306`), `TiDB` (`mysql://`, `tidb://`; `4000`), `OceanBase` (`mysql://`, `oceanbase://`; `2883`, preserving `#` in `user@tenant#cluster`), `StarRocks` (`starrocks://`, `mysql://`; `9030`), and `Doris` (`doris://`, `mysql://`; `9030`), all ignoring `/dbname` and mapping TLS options.
- **PostgreSQL family**: `CockroachDB` (`postgresql://`, `postgres://`, `cockroachdb://`, `cockroach sql --url`, `psql`, libpq `key=value`; `26257`, database + TLS) and `Redshift` (`redshift://`, `jdbc:redshift://`, `postgresql://`, `postgres://`, `psql`, libpq `key=value`; `5439`, database without TLS controls).
- **MongoDB**: `mongodb://`, `mongodb+srv://`, and `mongosh` commands; populates SRV mode, multi-host `additionalAddresses`, `replicaSet`, `directConnection`, `authenticationDatabase` (from `--authenticationDatabase`, `?authSource`, or falling back to decoded URI path `/<defaultauthdb>` on standard `mongodb://` URIs while leaving `mongodb+srv://` unset unless explicit so DNS TXT `authSource` is not overridden), and explicit `?tls`/`?ssl` as well as SRV certificate-verification overrides (`tlsInsecure`, `tlsAllowInvalidCertificates`, `tlsAllowInvalidHostnames`, `sslInsecure`) even when `?tls`/`?ssl` is omitted (leaving normal SRV URIs unset so native SRV TLS defaults remain intact, and rejecting `mongodb+srv://` URIs with explicit `?tls=false`/`?ssl=false` since SRV preserves native TLS when `useSsl` is false).
- **Redis**: `redis://`, `rediss://`, `redis-sentinel://`, `rediss-sentinel://`, and `redis-cli [--tls] -u`; switches between Standalone, Cluster, and Sentinel modes, populates `additionalAddresses`, Sentinel `masterName`/`masterUsername`/`masterPassword`, handles explicit empty username (`redis://:pass@host`), and maps TLS.
- **Analytics / Search / Wide-Column / Warehouses**:
  - `ClickHouse`: `clickhouse://`, `clickhouses://` (`9440`), `clickhouse+native://` (`9000`), and native TLS parameters.
  - `Snowflake`: `snowflake://`, `jdbc:snowflake://`, and `https://<account>.snowflakecomputing.com` (normalizing the account locator, supporting both `user` and `user:pass` / `?user=&password=`, clearing stale key-pair fields on URL import, and keeping `authenticationPrivateKey` optional in `DataSourceForm` / `validation.ts` for password auth compatibility).
  - `Elasticsearch`: `https://` (`443`), `http://` (`80`), `elasticsearch://`, and `opensearch://` (`9200`) with empty-path validation and TLS.
  - `Cassandra`: `cassandra://` with multi-host `additionalAddresses` (`9042`) and TLS.

title: chore: improve access grant actions and confirmations
body: ## Summary - Replace crowded text actions with compact icons and an overflow menu. - Use anchored Activate/Revoke confirmation popovers with loading states, inline errors, retry, and keyboard focus restoration. - Hide state-changing actions for expired grants, including revoked grants, and recheck expiration before submission. - Preserve loaded rows during refresh and update confirmation copy across five locales. - Document guidelines for contextual confirmation popovers. Before: After: ## Verification - 37 focused tests passed. - Desktop and mobile browser checks passed. - TypeScript and production build passed. - Full workspace gate encountered unrelated Agent formatting/i18n failures.
author: ecmadao

--- docs/agents/frontend-ux.md (+23/-3)
@@ -178,7 +178,8 @@ Use semantic utilities backed by CSS custom properties:
 | --- | --- |
 | Resource creation or editing with multiple fields while retaining list context | `Sheet` |
 | Multi-section settings or editing with a durable route | Full page form |
-| Confirmation, destructive acknowledgment, single-field prompt, or read-only result | `Dialog` or `AlertDialog` |
+| Reversible state transition affecting one existing row, with concise consequences | Anchored confirmation `Popover`, subject to the requirements below |
+| Other confirmation, destructive acknowledgment, single-field prompt, or read-only result | `Dialog` or `AlertDialog` |
 | Long or route-worthy multi-step workflow | Full page wizard |
 | Short multi-step workflow that benefits from parent context | Wide sheet wizard |
 
@@ -446,14 +447,33 @@ needs a new reusable size.
 ### Dialogs And Destructive Actions
 
 - Use `Dialog` for short blocking work, not multi-section resource forms.
-- Use `AlertDialog` for destructive confirmation that requires explicit
-  acknowledgment.
+- Use `AlertDialog` for irreversible or high-impact destructive confirmation
+  and destructive bulk acknowledgment.
 - Dialog content has 24px padding by default. Do not add an inner padding shell.
 - The primary action is last in reading order. A destructive action uses the
   destructive variant and names the operation precisely.
 - Dialog and alert-dialog content MUST have an accessible title and a concise
   description when consequences are not obvious.
 
+### Contextual Confirmation Popovers
+
+- A reversible state transition affecting one existing resource, such as
+  activating or revoking one access grant, MAY use a non-modal shared `Popover`.
+  This exception does not cover resource deletion, bulk operations, or actions
+  requiring high-risk acknowledgment; use a dialog for those.
+- The popover MUST name the action and its consequence, offer Cancel and an
+  explicitly named confirmation action, and use the destructive variant when
+  appropriate. It MUST have an accessible title and description.
+- Anchor to a persistent row control. When opened from a dropdown, close the
+  menu, transfer focus to the popover without returning it to the menu trigger,
+  and return focus to the persistent control when the popover closes. Use the
+  shared semantic overlay family so table clipping does not hide the popover.
+- Do not dim or block the page. Escape and clicking outside MUST cancel before
+  submission; dismissing a pending confirmation MUST NOT imply cancellation of
+  an operation already submitted.
+- Prevent duplicate submissions, show the pending state, and keep failures in
+  the popover with a retry path rather than silently closing it.
+
 ### Wizards
 
 - Use the shared step indicator and stable footer actions.

title: feat(review): show the AI review's facts under a standard rule finding (BYT-10523)
body:
## Problem

A standard rule flags a statement by its form, and the AI review never sees that finding. A sentence of the review's prompt tells the model to leave the rule's check alone. So when the model finds no problem on a flagged statement, the thread shows the rule's sentence and nothing more. For `ALTER TABLE public.accounts DROP COLUMN plan` that is "Drops column `plan` of `public.accounts`." The author still has to find out how much data the drop loses and whether anything reads the column, which the review has already looked up. This is the "prompt-based suppression instead of shared findings" gap of [BYT-10523](https://linear.app/bytebase/issue/BYT-10523).

## Change

Each review call is given the rule findings on its database and adds facts to them. This is step 2 after #22104.

- **Review.** The user message lists the standard findings posted on the database, each with an id. A section of the system message says what to do with them: do not report one again, and add the facts its text lacks that help the author decide, such as how much data the statement touches and what else uses the object. The answer has one more key, `facts`. A review with no standard finding sends the prompt it sends today.
- **Thread.** The facts are plain text after the rule's sentence. The thread keeps the rule, its codes, its priority, its databases, and its fingerprint. Facts never change the priority.
- **Problem first.** A finding that holds a problem of the AI review shows the problem and no facts, since the problem already says what the statement touches.
- **Cannot run.** A statement that the rule says cannot run, such as one on a missing table, gets no facts.
- **Databases.** The facts of several databases go to one summary call per finding, at most 20 a run. It writes one shared paragraph, and up to three groups where the databases disagree. Facts from only part of a finding's databases name those databases. A failed summary shows one database's facts and counts the rest.
- **Rerun.** A comment of facts stays as first written, so an unchanged statement keeps its text and costs no summary call. A problem found later replaces it. The exception is a problem that the facts already state. The merge call decides that, and only for facts that name no database and a problem that does not raise the priority.
- **Switch-off.** A review that ends because the AI review was switched off posts the rule results with nothing of the AI review on them.

There is no proto, API, or storage change.

One behavior changes on purpose. On `main` the model reports a missing table again, and its text joins the rule's thread. Here the model is told that the finding is posted, so that thread shows the rule's sentence alone.

Example: `DROP VIEW public.v_account_revenue;` and then `ALTER TABLE public.accounts DROP COLUMN plan;` on ten databases. Before, the drop's P1 `DO101` thread reads "Drops column `plan` of `public.accounts`." After, the same thread reads:

> Drops column `plan

body:
## Summary

Cuts `backend/plugin/schema/tidb` over to `github.com/bytebase/omni/tidb/catalog`, following the Oracle (#22109), SQL Server (#22114) and MySQL-family (#22116) cutovers.

`schema/tidb` registered Bytebase's own 1,166-line copy of the MySQL differ/generator as TiDB's `GenerateMigration`, so every TiDB metadata diff fell back to `GetDatabaseSchemaDiff` + `GenerateMigration`. omni's `tidb/catalog` exports `LoadMetadataInto`, `Diff` and `GenerateMigration`, so the diff moves there and the generator, its test and its corpus are deleted.

| | before | after |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `schema/tidb` (non-test) | 2,036 | 914 |

Diffstat: `+495 / −2,873` (net −2,378; 1,604 of the deletions are the deleted generator corpus).

**Stacked on #22116**, which adds the shared `backend/plugin/schema/internal/omnicatalog` half the three MySQL-family diffs use: load both snapshots under one synthetic database, refuse a changed object a catalog could not install, strip the generator's qualifier for that database. This PR's shim is the same ~20-line adapter for TiDB's catalog. Merge #22116 first.

## The fork rule, applied

TiDB is a MySQL fork in omni, so every fact the MySQL family's shim depends on was re-verified on `tidb/catalog` rather than inherited:

- **Tables, indexes, foreign keys, partitions, views and generated columns all load and diff.** The deleted corpus's 29 cases load without a single per-object problem, including foreign-key creates and drops and TiDB's clustered-index and `AUTO_RANDOM` attributes.
- **`AUTO_RANDOM` keeps its shard count.** TiDB reports `AUTO_RANDOM(5)` for a column created without one; the catalog renders that, the old generator wrote the bare keyword. `TestDiffMetadataTiDBColumnAttributes` pins both directions of a change.
- **Routines, triggers and events are unreachable, not merely unsupported.** `tidb/catalog` installs and diffs tables, views and sequences only (its `LoadMetadataReport` keys are `table:`, `view:`, `sequence:`), so the deleted generator's function/procedure/trigger/event branches had no diff to render. Nothing can reach them either: Bytebase's TiDB extractor rejects `CREATE FUNCTION` and `CREATE TRIGGER` and `CREATE EVENT` at parse time and fails on `CREATE PROCEDURE` at execution, and TiDB itself supports none of them. Deleting those branches therefore loses nothing that a TiDB snapshot can contain.
- **TiDB has no SDL form**, so nothing changes on the SDL paths: `schema/tidb` registers no `DiffSDLMigration` and no `SDLDropAdvices`, and this PR registers none. `GetDatabaseDefinition` already ignored `ctx.SDLFormat`.

## Dump text is untouched

The `get_database_definition.yaml` and `get_database_metadata.yaml` goldens are unchanged, byte for byte: TiDB's definition path has been a shim over `tidb/catalog` since #22025, and its metadata extractor (`get_database_metadata.go`, 272 lines, including the local catalog→proto conversion omni's TiDB catalog does not export) stays exactly as it was. body:
## Summary

Cuts the MySQL family's last Bytebase differ — `schema/mysql/generate_migration.go`, 1,422 lines — over to omni, following the Oracle (#22109) and SQL Server (#22114) pilots.

The package's state at this pin decides the shape. MySQL's own `GetDatabaseDefinition`, `GetDatabaseMetadata`, metadata diff, SDL diff, drop advices and multi-file definition already ran on `omni/mysql/catalog` (#22025, #22037); the legacy generator survived only as the metadata diff registered for **MariaDB** and **OceanBase**. Both engines now have their own catalog in omni — `mariadb/catalog` and `oceanbase/catalog`, forked from MySQL's, each with `LoadMetadataInto`, `Diff` and `GenerateMigration` — so the generator has no caller left.

| `schema/mysql` (non-test) | 3,301 | 1,564 |
| `schema/mariadb` | 39 | 84 |
| `schema/oceanbase` | 1,051 | 1,096 |
| `schema/internal/omnicatalog` | — | 318 |
| family total | 4,391 | 3,062 |

Diffstat: `+1,208 / −4,504` (net −3,296; 2,288 of the deletions are the deleted generator corpus).

## Why one PR for three engines, not three

`schema/mysql/generate_migration.go` was one file serving three registrations, and MariaDB owns no schema package of its own (39 lines, a walk-through only). Splitting the deletion from the two re-registrations would leave either a dead generator or a diff path with no generator. OceanBase's package had nothing legacy left to delete on its own — its definition and metadata are already omni shims — so a separate `refactor(oceanbase)` PR would have contained only the re-registration.

**MariaDB is handled inside the MySQL PR**, as its package doc now says: `schema/mariadb` gains its metadata diff, and the stale claim that `mariadb/catalog` lacks `LoadMetadata`/`Diff`/`GenerateMigration` (true when the walk-through was written, false now) is corrected there.

## The fork rule, applied

MariaDB and OceanBase are MySQL forks in omni, and each fact is re-verified on the engine's own catalog rather than inherited:

- **MariaDB must not use the MySQL catalog.** omni's MySQL loader installs a `WITH SYSTEM VERSIONING` table as plain `NOT NULL` columns with no versioning at all; a MySQL diff would drop history silently. MariaDB's fork keeps `PERIOD FOR SYSTEM_TIME` and `WITH SYSTEM VERSIONING`, and `TestDiffMetadataKeepsSystemVersioning` pins it.

- **INVISIBLE renders differently per engine:** `int(11) DEFAULT NULL INVISIBLE` (MariaDB) vs `int DEFAULT NULL /*!80023 INVISIBLE */` (OceanBase).

## The two inventory facts, re-checked at `omni@426aecf`

1. **The catalog exports no single-table definition — still true.** `mssql/catalog` exports `DatabaseDefinition`, `GetViewDefinition`, `GetFunctionDefinition`, `GetProcedureDefinition`, `Diff` and `GenerateMigration`, and no `GetTableDefinition`. `GetTableDefinition` therefore keeps Bytebase's renderer (with its spatial-index helpers), which is why `get_database_definition.go` shrinks to `table_definition.go` instead of disappearing.
2. **"Spatial-index option loss" — does not reproduce on the path this shim uses.** The definition fixtures carrying spatial indexes (`spatial_indexes_geography`, `spatial_indexes_geometry`, `spatial_indexes_advanced_configurations`, `spatial_indexes_mixed_with_constraints`) come out byte-identical: `BOUNDING_BOX`, `GRIDS`, `CELLS_PER_OBJECT`, `PAD_INDEX`, `FILLFACTOR` and the `OFF` lock options all survive. The only spatial change is on the migration path, where the catalog omits `ALLOW_ROW_LOCKS = ON` and `ALLOW_PAGE_LOCKS = ON` because `ON` is the server default; every non-default option is kept. That is a text normalization, not a lost option, and it is one of the named parity cases below.

`stripUnrenderedFacts` preserves the old renderer's omissions so the dump stays byte-identical: no sequences, synonyms, triggers, extended-property comments, default-constraint names, and every `SkipDump` flag stays ignored. `restoreLegacyModuleText` keeps the stored module text, so a definition ending in `;` still gains a second one and an `ALTER` header stays `ALTER`. All 21 `get_database_definition.yaml` goldens pass unchanged.

The one difference the strip does not remove is **module ordering**: the catalog creates a function after any function its body names and before a table default or view body that references it, where the old renderer wrote functions and procedures last. ## What

Pilot for the parser-layer reduction described in `docs/design/engine-code-to-omni.md` (Phase 2). CockroachDB's statement-type classifier and changed-resource extractor now delegate to `omni/cockroachdb/analysis`; the Bytebase package keeps only the `parser/base` registration, the `storepb` conversion, and the metadata lookup adapter.

- `resource_change.go` (477 lines) and `statement_type.go` (179 lines) are deleted.
- `analysis.go` (117 lines) adapts Bytebase `base.AST` values into omni `statements.Statements`, calls `analysis.StatementTypes` / `analysis.ExtractChangedResources`, and converts the result back into `storepb.StatementType` / `base.ChangeSummary`.
- `changeMetadata` implements omni's `ChangeMetadata` over `model.DatabaseMetadata`, preserving the existing relation/index name matching.

Net: **656 deleted, 117 added, 539 lines removed** from `backend/plugin/parser/cockroachdb` (805 → 266 non-test lines).

## Why not completion in this pilot

Completion was measured first, as requested. Bytebase has **10,497 non-test completion lines** at this pin:

| engine | Bytebase | omni at pin |
|---|---:|---:|
| pg (also registered for Snowflake/CockroachDB) | 1,677 | 475 |
| mysql (also ClickHouse/StarRocks/Doris) | 1,267 | 973 |
| mariadb | 1,264 | 974 |
| oceanbase | 1,264 | 974 |
| tsql | 2,065 | 639 (`mssql`) |
| plsql | 1,395 | none |
| tidb | 499 | 1,074 |
| partiql | 512 | 141 |
| redshift | 203 | 698 |
| trino | 192 | 1,286 |
| mongodb | 159 | 625 |

The tidb/redshift/trino/mongodb/partiql files are already shims. The remaining Bytebase reimplementations are pg + mysql family + tsql + plsql (~8,932 lines).

A direct cutover is **not** differentially identical on the recorded fixtures:

- pg: 214 / 235 fixture inputs differ.
- mysql: 151 / 200 fixture inputs differ.

The differences are behavioral, not just missing fields: omni returns a broader relation set in some column contexts, a narrower set in INSERT column lists, and different CTE stand-in behavior. omni candidates also carry no `Definition`/`Comment`/`Priority`, which the editor renders. Completion therefore needs an omni API/parity change first; shimming it now would change user-facing suggestions. This PR pilots the judgment surface where omni is already the exact implementation instead.

## Parity evidence

The existing CockroachDB expectations were run before deleting the Bytebase implementation and pass unchanged after the cutover:

- `TestGetStatementTypes` (all statement forms, CTEs, statement sources, EXPLAIN ANALYZE)
- `TestExtractChangedResources*` (DML counts, INSERT row counts, search-path replay, SET LOCAL/ROLLBACK/DISCARD, cross-database indexes, DDL, index lookup, EXPLAIN ANALYZE)

The omni extractor also adds savepoint search-path handling that the old Bytebase copy lacked; no existing expectation changes.

## Gates

- `gofmt` on changed Go files.
- `GOGC=off GOMEMLIMIT=10GiB golangci-lint run --fix -j 8 --allow-parallel-runners`, then without `--fix`:

The catalog sync queries, the value conversions and the statement classification are deleted.

- Adapter: `redshift.go` 270, `execute.go` 68, `query.go` 63 — **401 non-test lines** against 1,574 before. Deleted: `sync.go` (769), `query.go` (179), `role.go` (90), `stats.go` (71), `dump.go` (14).
- Deleted tests: `sync_test.go` (34) and `stats_test.go` (77) tested `getPgVersionAndRedshiftVersion` and `getAffectedRowsFromPlan`, which are now omni's; omni's `redshift/driver/sync_test.go` and `stats_test.go` hold the same cases (the documented version string, and the two published EXPLAIN plans). `redshift_test.go` gains the config-mapping cases, and `cutover_parity_test.go` is the differential harness.
- **No caller change and no `go.mod` change.** No package names `*redshift.Driver`; plancheck reaches `CountAffectedRows` through `db.RowEstimator` (the adapter keeps it, delegating to the driver); the pin `e65c4bfc2588` already carries `redshift/driver`.

## db.Driver, method by method

| Method | Implementation |
| --- | --- |
| `Open` | `redshiftConfig` (data source → `driver.Config`) then `redshiftdriver.Open`; an SSH data source becomes `Config.Dial`; no server contact, as before |
| `Close` | held session, then driver, then SSH client, `multierr`-combined |
| `Ping` | driver `Ping` |
| `Execute` | `base.ParseTransactionConfig` → `ExecuteOptions.Transaction` (`Transactional`/`AutoCommit`), `CreateDatabase` passed through, task-run log via `executeLogger` |
| `QueryConn` | one driver session held from the first call until `Close`, serialized by a mutex (`OwnsQuerySession`, so `sql_service` opens no `*sql.Conn`); `Schema`/`Limit`/`Explain`/`MaxResultBytes`/`MaskingEnabled` → `QueryOptions`; results via `util.OmniResultToQueryResult` |
| `SyncInstance` | driver instance → `db.InstanceMetadata`; each `driver.Role.Attribute` is the same pointer the old driver built |
| `SyncDBSchema` | driver database metadata; `driver.ErrNotFound` → `common.NotFound("database %q not found")`, the old message |

title: refactor(oracle): drive schema conversion through omni
body:
## Summary

Pilot cutover of `backend/plugin/schema/oracle` to `github.com/bytebase/omni/oracle/catalog`.

- Deletes Oracle's hand-written renderer (`get_database_definition.go`, 852 lines) and migration differ/generator (`generate_migration.go`, 2,328 lines).
- Adds `oracle.go` (148 lines) that registers the same `schema.*` surface over omni's catalog: `DatabaseDefinition`, the single-object definitions, and `RegisterDiffMetadataMigration` using `LoadMetadata` → `Diff` → `GenerateMigration`.
- Keeps the existing metadata extractor (`get_database_metadata.go` + `metadata_helpers.go`, 1,046 lines). Lifting it is a separate parity decision: omni's `LoadSQL` normalizes check expressions, adds view `dependency_columns`, prefixes materialized-view definitions with their build/refresh clause, changes `NVARCHAR2`/`NCHAR` lengths, and leaves the inferred type off an untyped virtual column.
- Preserves two old renderer defects with `stripUnrenderedFacts`: it omitted identity clauses and index `INVISIBLE` state. Dump output is unchanged until those fixes can ship with their own release note.

Measured result for the package:

| | before | after |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| non-test lines | 4,226 | 1,194 |
| diffstat | | `+312 / −3,631` (net −3,319) |

This is 32% of the inventory's ~13k legacy schema lines, and the largest Bytebase `schema/<engine>` package that was still wholly independent of an omni catalog.

## Why Oracle rather than PostgreSQL

PostgreSQL is larger (6,685 non-test lines), but it already routes metadata and SDL diffs through `omni/pg/catalog`; Oracle was still entirely independent at this pin. Omni's `oracle/catalog` is a direct port of this package (`DatabaseDefinition`, `Diff`, `GenerateMigration`, and the object renderers), so every registry entry point maps to an existing omni function. MSSQL is similarly independent, but its catalog does not export a single-table definition, and its corpus showed spatial-index option loss, so it is not the clean first step.

## Parity evidence

The old implementation is deleted, so the differential is against recorded expectations:

- `TestGenerateMigration` (35 cases) now calls `schema.DiffMigration` and keeps the unchanged goldens for 29 cases.
- `TestCutoverParity` adds the six cases whose only difference was a trailing blank line from the legacy generator; each is asserted as `legacyExpected == catalogExpected + "\n"`. All other migration text is byte-identical.
- `TestGetDatabaseDefinition` still uses the pre-cutover goldens; `stripUnrenderedFacts` keeps the old renderer's known identity and index-visibility omissions so those stay byte-identical. The defects are recorded beside the shim, and `backend/plugin/aireview`'s invisible-index test still passes for the same reason.
- Metadata extraction is unchanged, so `TestGetDatabaseMetadata` and its 12 fixtures stay as they were.

No caller changes: all outside callers still use the same `schema.*` functions (`backend/api/v1/database_service.go`, `ba
author: d-bytebase

--- backend/plugin/schema/oracle/cutover_parity_test.go (+108/-0)
@@ -0,0 +1,108 @@
+package oracle
+
+import (
+	"os"
+	"testing"
+
+	metadatapb "github.com/bytebase/omni/metadata"
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
+	"google.golang.org/protobuf/proto"
+	"gopkg.in/yaml.v3"
+
+	storepb "github.com/bytebase/bytebase/backend/generated-go/store"
+	"github.com/bytebase/bytebase/backend/plugin/schema"
+	"github.com/bytebase/bytebase/backend/store/model"
+)
+
+// cutoverParityCase holds a fixture's two expected migration texts: the
+// catalog's, and the same script with its trailing blank line.
+type cutoverParityCase struct {
+	Description     string `yaml:"description"`
+	LegacyExpected  string `yaml:"legacyExpected"`
+	CatalogExpected string `yaml:"catalogExpected"`
+}
+
+// TestCutoverParity pins the fixture cases where the catalog migration ends
+// after the last statement while the second expected text keeps one trailing
+// blank line. Every other case in generate_migration.yaml is byte-identical and
+// is covered by TestGenerateMigration.
+func TestCutoverParity(t *testing.T) {
+	content, err := os.ReadFile("testdata/cutover_parity.yaml")
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	var cases []cutoverParityCase
+	require.NoError(t, yaml.Unmarshal(content, &cases))
+
+	fixtureContent, err := os.ReadFile("testdata/generate_migration.yaml")
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	var fixture []generateMigrationCase
+	require.NoError(t, yaml.Unmarshal(fixtureContent, &fixture))
+	byDescription := make(map[string]generateMigrationCase, len(fixture))
+	for _, tc := range fixture {
+		byDescription[tc.Description] = tc
+	}
+
+	for _, tc := range cases {
+		t.Run(tc.Description, func(t *testing.T) {
+			source, ok := byDescription[tc.Description]
+			require.True(t, ok, "parity case is missing from generate_migration.yaml")
+			migration, err := schema.DiffMigration(storepb.Engine_ORACLE,
+				parseMetadata(t, source.OldMetadata), parseMetadata(t, source.NewMetadata))
+			require.NoError(t, err)
+			require.Equal(t, tc.CatalogExpected, migration)
+			// The fixture's second text keeps the trailing blank line; the
+			// catalog's does not.
+			require.Equal(t, tc.LegacyExpected, migration+"\n")
+		})
+	}
+}
+
+// TestMetadataMigrationKeepsLegacyOmissions pins the migration path to the same
+// compatibility strip as the definition path. An identity column or an invisible
+// index in the target must not reach the catalog diff.
+func TestMetadataMigrationKeepsLegacyOmissions(t *testing.T) {
+	oldMetadata := &metadatapb.DatabaseSchemaMetadata{Schemas: []*metadatapb.SchemaMetadata{{
+		Name: "APP",
+		Tables: []*metadatapb.TableMetadata{{
+			Name:    "T",
+			Columns: []*metadatapb.ColumnMetadata{{Name: "ID", Type: "NUMBER", Nullable: false}},
+		}},
+	}}}
+	newMetadata := proto.CloneOf(oldMetadata)
+	table := newMetadata.Schemas[0].Tables[0]
+	table.Columns = append(table.Columns, &metadatapb.ColumnMetadata{
+		Name:               "SEQ",
+		Type:               "NUMBER",
+		Nullable:           false,
+		IsIdentity:         true,
+		IdentityGeneration: metadatapb.ColumnMetadata_ALWAYS,
+		IdentitySeed:       1,
+		IdentityIncrement:  1,
+	})
+	table.Indexes = []*metadatapb.IndexMetadata{{
+		Name:        "IDX_T_ID",
+		Expressions: []string{"ID"},
+		Visible:     false,
+	}}
+
+	source := model.NewDatabaseMetadata(oldMetadata, nil, nil, storepb.Engine_ORACLE, false)
+	target := model.NewDatabaseMetadata(newMetadata, nil, nil, storepb.Engine_ORACLE, false)
+	migration, err := schema.DiffMigration(storepb.Engine_ORACLE, source, target)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	require.NotEmpty(t, migration)
+	require.NotContains(t, migration, "IDENTITY")
+	require.NotContains(t, migration, "GENERATED")
+	require.NotContains(t, migration, "INVISIBLE")
+}
+
+// TestMaterializedViewDefinitionDropsIndexVisibility pins the per-object path to
+// the same compatibility strip as the database definition: an index's INVISIBLE
+// state is deferred.
+func TestMaterializedViewDefinitionDropsIndexVisibility(t *testing.T) {
+	definition, err := GetMaterializedViewDefinition("", &metadatapb.MaterializedViewMetadata{
+		Name:       "MV",
+		Definition: "SELECT 1 FROM DUAL",
+		Indexes:    []*metadatapb.IndexMetadata{{Name: "IDX_MV", Expressions: []string{"1"}, Visible: false}},
+	})
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	require.NotContains(t, definition, "INVISIBLE")
+}

title: fix(deps): update github.com/bytebase/omni to 426aecf
body:
This updates `github.com/bytebase/omni` from `e65c4bf` to `426aecf`, a merge of current omni `main` (`3ffa03a`) and bytebase/omni#1430 (`f48105aa`).

#1430 is still open pending human approval. Pinning the merge keeps the BYT-10211 Doris dump fix the old pin carried, which a bump to `main` alone would revert. Once #1430 lands, this should be re-pointed at omni `main`.

The update also adopts two changes from omni `main`:

- **#1432 removes `ast.MergeStmt`.** StarRocks has no MERGE statement, so the StarRocks parser drops the three analysis arms that named it. `SET DEFAULT STORAGE VAULT` no longer parses either; its test case moves to the reject set.
- **#1417 unpacks the server message a batch's row reader fails on.** The mssql cutover parity test no longer records "divide by zero in a batch" as a known difference, and normalizes the recorded container name in unpacked errors.

The bump also carries the other user-visible omni changes since the old pin: BigQuery DDL affected rows and `NULL` collations; Snowflake documented command forms and `TOP` as a column name; Redshift TEMPLATE/GRANT/ASSUMEROLE forms; GoogleSQL hint and property-graph forms; TiDB planner estimates and partition order; Doris/StarRocks `USE CATALOG`/cluster; mssql DROP names and `ALTER TABLE ... ADD INDEX`; StarRocks storage volume/warehouse/charset statements; Trino `JSON_TABLE`; StarRocks refusing Doris residue; Doris `VALUES`, DESCRIBE/SHOW tails, `CREATE USER` options and `EXPORT` remote storage; and the Doris routine-catalogue tolerance.

`go test -count=1 -p 1 ./backend/...` passes. No golden was re-recorded.

Not merging.

title: fix(review): post one thread when the AI review and a standard rule flag one operation (BYT-10533)
body:
## Problem

The review posts two threads for one operation. A standard rule flags it, and the AI review flags it again in a thread of its own. Only a sentence of the AI review's prompt keeps the two reviewers apart, and no step compares their findings. For `WALK_THROUGH` the prompt hands the check to the model on purpose, so a missing table always gets two threads ([BYT-10533](https://linear.app/bytebase/issue/BYT-10533)).

## Change

One operation has one thread. This is the first of three steps.

- **Merge.** The rule findings join the merge call beside the AI review's findings. A rule finding is a fixed member: the model puts problems with it and nothing else.
- **Thread.** A problem on the operation of a rule finding is written into that finding's thread as plain text, and posts no thread of its own. The thread keeps the rule, its codes, its databases, and its fingerprint.
- **Priority.** The thread shows the highest priority among the rule and its problems. A problem that only restates the rule's condition never raises it. A sentence of the AI review policy does.
- **Rerun.** The merge says whether the comment already states the run's problems. Then the comment stays, else it is written again. A problem that was fixed leaves the thread, and the priority is the rule's again. A comment stays only when it was written for every database of the rule finding and the run's problems are on every one of them too, since the merge sees no database name.
- **Guards.** A problem joins a rule finding only when that finding is on every database the problem is on. A failed merge call drops nothing: every finding posts on its own, as today.

The review prompt is unchanged. The merge prompt gains a section only in a call that holds a rule finding, so a merge of AI findings alone sends the prompt it sends today. There is no proto, API, or storage change.

Example: `ALTER TABLE public.accounts DROP COLUMN plan`, where a view reads the column. Before, the line has a P1 `DO101` thread and a P0 AI thread. After, it has one P0 `DO101` thread:

> Drops column `plan` of `public.accounts`.
>
> The view `public.v_account_revenue` selects `a.plan` and groups by it, so without `CASCADE` the drop fails with `cannot drop column plan of table accounts because other objects depend on it`.
>
> Suggested fix: Recreate the view without `plan` in the same migration, before the drop.

Not in this PR: the review call does not receive the rule findings yet (step 2, BYT-10523), and a stored finding keeps `run_type` (step 3).

## Tests

- Unit tests in `backend/plugin/aireview` and `backend/runner/reviewrun`. One drives both real executors through the store: one thread posts, an unchanged rerun keeps the comment, a higher priority reopens a resolved thread, and a run with the AI review off leaves the rule's text.
- The review run tests in `backend/api/v1` and `backend/tests` pass. Lint is clean in the changed packages, and the server builds.
- Codex review, four local rounds: the fir

+}
+
+func checkAuditLogSearchPlanCaching(t *testing.T, dateStyle string, parameters map[string]string) {
+	t.Helper()
+	ctx := context.Background()
+	db, s, dsn := testcontainer.NewMetadataDB(t)
+	if len(parameters) > 0 {
+		require.NoError(t, s.Close())
+		metadataURL, err := url.Parse(dsn)
+		require.NoError(t, err)
+		query := metadataURL.Query()
+		for key, value := range parameters {
+			query.Set(key, value)
+		}
+		metadataURL.RawQuery = query.Encode()
+		configuredStore, err := store.New(ctx, metadataURL.String(), false)
+		require.NoError(t, err)
+		t.Cleanup(func() { require.NoError(t, configuredStore.Close()) })
+		s = configuredStore
+	}
+
+	// Prepared statements belong to a connection; inspect the one used by every search.
+	s.GetDB().SetMaxOpenConns(1)
+	s.GetDB().SetMaxIdleConns(1)
+
+	_, err := s.GetDB().ExecContext(ctx, `SELECT set_config('DateStyle', $1, false)`, dateStyle)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+
+	_, err = db.ExecContext(ctx, `INSERT INTO workspace (resource_id) VALUES ('ws-test'), ('ws-other')`)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+
+	createdAt := time.Date(2026, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 123456000, time.UTC)
+	upperBound := createdAt.Add(2 * time.Second)
+	const approveMethod = "/bytebase.v1.IssueService/ApproveIssue"
+	const updateMethod = "/bytebase.v1.PlanService/UpdatePlan"
+	const project = "projects/target"
+
+	_, err = db.ExecContext(ctx, `
+		INSERT INTO audit_log (resource_id, workspace, created_at, payload)
+		SELECT 'noise-' || n, 'ws-test', $1,
+			jsonb_build_object('parent', 'projects/other', 'method', $2::text)
+		FROM generate_series(1, 1000) AS n
+	`, createdAt, updateMethod)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+
+	for _, row := range []struct {
+		id        string
+		workspace string
+		parent    string
+		method    string
+		at        time.Time
+	}{
+		{"before-lower", "ws-test", project, approveMethod, createdAt.Add(-time.Microsecond)},
+		{"at-lower", "ws-test", project, approveMethod, createdAt},
+		{"tie-a", "ws-test", project, updateMethod, createdAt.Add(time.Second)},
+		{"tie-b", "ws-test", project, approveMethod, createdAt.Add(time.Second)},
+		{"at-upper", "ws-test", project, updateMethod, upperBound},
+		{"after-upper", "ws-test", project, approveMethod, upperBound.Add(time.Microsecond)},
+		{"other-workspace", "ws-other", project, approveMethod, createdAt},
+		{"other-method", "ws-test", project, "/bytebase.v1.SQLService/Query", createdAt},
+	} {
+		payload, err := protojson.Marshal(&storepb.AuditLog{
+			Parent: row.parent,
+			Method: row.method,
+			User:   "users/test@example.com",
+		})
+		require.NoError(t, err)
+		_, err = db.ExecContext(ctx, `
+			INSERT INTO audit_log (resource_id, workspace, created_at, payload)
+			VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4)
+		`, row.id, row.workspace, row.at, payload)
+		require.NoError(t, err)
+	}
+
+	filterQ, err := store.GetSearchAuditLogsFilter(`
+		(method == "/bytebase.v1.IssueService/ApproveIssue" || method == "/bytebase.v1.PlanService/UpdatePlan")
+		&& create_time >= "2026-01-02T03:04:05.123456789Z"
+	`)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	cutoff := createdAt.Add(789 * time.Nanosecond)
+	filterQ = store.ApplyRetentionFilter(filterQ, &cutoff)
+	filterQ = store.ApplyCreateTimeUpperBound(filterQ, upperBound.Add(789*time.Nanosecond))
+	orders, err := store.GetAuditLogOrders("create_time asc")
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	limit := 2
+	parent := project
+	wantTimes := map[string]time.Time{
+		"at-lower": createdAt,
+		"tie-b":    createdAt.Add(time.Second),
+		"tie-a":    createdAt.Add(time.Second),
+		"at-upper": upperBound,
+	}
+
+	for range 8 {
+		var ids []string
+		for offset := 0; offset < 4; offset += limit {
+			logs, err := s.SearchAuditLogs(ctx, &store.AuditLogFind{
+				Workspace:   "ws-test",
+				Project:     &parent,
+				FilterQ:     filterQ,
+				Limit:       &limit,
+				Offset:      &offset,
+				OrderByKeys: orders,
+			})
+			require.NoError(t, err)
+			require.Len(t, logs, limit)
+			for _, log := range logs {
+				ids = append(ids, log.ResourceID)
+				require.Equal(t, "ws-test", log.Workspace)
+				require.Equal(t, project, log.Payload.Parent)
+				require.Equal(t, "users/test@example.com", log.Payload.User)
+				require.Contains(t, []string{approveMethod, updateMethod}, log.Payload.Method)
+				require.WithinDuration(t, wantTimes[log.ResourceID], log.CreatedAt, 0)
+			}
+		}
+		require.Equal(t, []string{"at-lower", "tie-b", "tie-a", "at-upper"}, ids)
+	}

+	err = s.GetDB().QueryRowContext(ctx, `
+		SELECT count(*) FROM pg_prepared_statements WHERE statement LIKE $1
+	`, "%FROM audit_log%").Scan(&preparedSearches)
+	require.NoError(t, err)

title: feat(instance): autofill create-instance form from connection strings
body:
## Summary

Add an **Import from URL** action to the `Connection` section header on the create-instance form for MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQL Server, and Oracle so users can paste connection URLs or strings from cloud consoles and database tools to autofill discrete connection fields. Neon manual entry keeps its existing ADR-0006 field and pooled-endpoint check.

Supported formats:
- PostgreSQL accepts `postgresql://` and `postgres://` URIs (with an optional `psql` prefix) and libpq `key=value` strings.
- MySQL accepts `mysql://` URIs and ignores `/dbname` since MySQL connections operate at the instance level.
- SQL Server accepts ADO.NET semicolon `Key=Value;` strings (including `tcp:host,port`, `host\instance`, and quoted or brace-escaped values) and `sqlserver://` URIs.
- Oracle accepts Easy Connect / Easy Connect Plus strings (with an optional `sqlplus` prefix) and `oracle://` URIs, switching between Service Name and SID accordingly.

UX and behavior details:
- **Import from URL** sits flush with the `240px` form input column as a soft surface chip (`appearance="soft"`) while **Need help? Ask Agent** remains right-aligned, opening an origin-aware anchored popover so `Authentication` stays the first field row in `Connection`.
- Pasting a valid string immediately populates the connection fields, closes the popover (discarding the plaintext secret from the DOM), and confirms via a toast notification.
- Typing a string manually submits via `Enter` or **Import**; invalid pastes or submissions keep the popover open with inline validation recovery copy, including calling out when the string belongs to another supported engine.
- Maps explicit TLS settings (`sslmode`/`ssl`, `ssl-mode`/`sslaccept`/`tls`/`ssl`, `Encrypt` and `TrustServerCertificate`, `tcps://`/`SSL`) into Bytebase's TLS controls and drops unrecognized client or ORM parameters.
- Skips template password placeholders such as `{your_password}` and `[YOUR-PASSWORD]` and moves focus directly to the Password input when no password was supplied.

## Screenshots

### Import from URL popover
![Import from URL popover](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/RainbowDashy/14bbe3a2b8746cd48085172a66d7aac5/raw/1-popover.jpg)

### Cross-engine validation recovery
![Cross-engine validation recovery](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/RainbowDashy/14bbe3a2b8746cd48085172a66d7aac5/raw/2-validation.jpg)

### Autofilled connection fields
![Autofilled connection fields](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/RainbowDashy/14bbe3a2b8746cd48085172a66d7aac5/raw/3-autofilled.jpg)

- `pnpm --dir frontend fix`
- `pnpm --dir frontend test`

title: fix(pg): skip syncing Neon's reserved postgres system database
body:
## Summary

Neon reserves `postgres` alongside `template0` and `template1` as a service-managed system database (`cloud_admin`-owned) and omits it from both the Neon Console and the Management API (`/databases`) during branch discovery. However, because `postgres` still exists in `pg_database` on Neon computes and generic PostgreSQL instances legitimately use `postgres` for application schemas, syncing a `NEON` instance previously registered `postgres` in Bytebase.

- Propagate `Vendor` on `db.ConnectionContext` from `DBFactory.GetDataSourceDriver`.
- Skip `"postgres"` in `pg.Driver.SyncInstance` when `vendor == NEON`, keeping `pg.Driver.Open` bootstrap fallback connections and `getDatabases` catalog queries unchanged. This covers scheduled and manual `SyncInstance`, `ListInstanceDatabase`, and soft-deletion when an existing PostgreSQL instance's vendor type is updated to `NEON`.
- Record the contract in ADR-0006 and add integration coverage in `backend/plugin/db/pg` and `backend/runner/schemasync`.

## Verification

- `go test -count=1 ./backend/plugin/db/ ./backend/plugin/db/pg/ ./backend/runner/schemasync/`
- `go test -count=1 ./backend/api/v1/ -run '^(TestNeon|TestImportInstances)'`
- `GOGC=off GOMEMLIMIT=10GiB golangci-lint run -j 8 --allow-parallel-runners`
- `go build -ldflags "-w -s" -p=16 -o ./bytebase-build/bytebase ./backend/bin/server/main.go`

title: refactor(mysql): drive mysql through omni
body:
## What this does

Replaces the inside of `backend/plugin/db/mysql` with an adapter over `github.com/bytebase/omni/mysql/driver`, and over `omni/mariadb/driver` for the `MARIADB` value this package has always registered. `db.Driver` is unchanged.

Deleted: the engine's sync queries (`sync.go`, 1,759 lines), dump renderer, value conversion, statement classification, role sync, plan estimate and their tests (`mysql_test.go`, `stats_test.go`, `sync_test.go`, 2,163 lines). The driver conversation now belongs to omni; Bytebase keeps the connection path and the product-side seams.

## Size and budget

The measured budget was 706 adapter lines / 17 files / +363 −104.

This adapter is **952 non-test lines** (`mysql.go` 690, `helpers.go` 68, `sqlprobe.go` 161, `synonyms.go` 33) and **390 test lines**. It is 246 lines over budget, all deliberate:

- +~100 for `GetDB`: the adapter owns a second `*sql.DB` built from the same resolved config so gh-ost keeps its direct connection; the contract's pool is private to omni.
- +~20 for the one held `QueryConn` session.
- +~80 for `db.Prober` over a contract session (`START TRANSACTION`, pre-executions, statement, `ROLLBACK`).
- +~40 for the package doc that records the deltas below.

The retained `sqlprobe.go` is the proof's 155-line legacy `*sql.DB` estimate bridge; `advisor/mysql` and `advisor/mariadb` tests still call it. Production estimates go through `db.RowEstimator` / omni's `CountAffectedRows`.

## Decisions

- **GetDB is kept, not replaced by a `db.SQLDB` seam.** `db.Driver` is unchanged on this base, gh-ost runs five binlog probes through `GetDB`, and MySQL/MariaDB are the engines where gh-ost is actually offered. The adapter therefore owns a direct-connection pool built from the same resolved config (including tunnel and TLS) and closes it with the driver. Every existing caller compiles and behaves as before; no product-side `GetDB` migration is in this PR.
- **`QueryConn` holds one session from the first call until `Close`.** The editor sends one statement at a time on a driver it keeps, so `SET @x` then `SELECT @x` and a temporary table across calls work as they did on the caller's pooled `*sql.Conn`. Pinned by `TestAdapterHoldsOneSessionAcrossQueryConnCalls`.
- **An editor request keeps one server connection.** The adapter implements `db.SessionQuerier`, so `sql_service.go` does not open a `*sql.Conn` from `GetDB` that `QueryConn` would ignore. Its three request paths leave `conn` nil and the held session serves the stream. `GetDB` remains for gh-ost and task-run session monitoring.
- **A failed `Open` releases what it acquired.** `Open` now defers `Close` until it succeeds, so invalid TLS material after an SSH tunnel, a failed contract open, or a failed direct-pool build does not leak the tunnel or dialer.
- **Advisor path.** `db.Prober` and `db.RowEstimator` are implemented on the adapter and asserted with `var _`. `CountAffectedRows` delegates to omni, which issues `SET SESSION explain_json_format

title: refactor(oracle): drive oracle through omni
body:
Replace Bytebase's Oracle driver internals with an adapter over `github.com/bytebase/omni/oracle/driver` (already in the pinned omni `1fd58c9d1`, so no pin bump). `db.Driver` is unchanged.

## The adapter

`backend/plugin/db/oracle` keeps the product-side glue: the data source → contract conversion (TLS material, SSH tunnel, SID/service name, extra connection parameters), the `QueryContext`/`ExecuteOptions` mapping, the `-- txn-mode` directive, the v1pb conversion through `util.OmniResultToQueryResult`, the task-run logger, and the advisor probes. Sync, the metadata-rendered dump, queries, change scripts, plan estimates and the database-link probe are the driver's.

3,298 lines deleted, 533 added. Adapter non-test: 500 lines (335 without comments/blanks) across 4 files; the proof measured 390. The overshoot is the package's known-difference list and the SQL\*Plus blanking below, neither of which the proof measured.

## The private-link guard

The trap: the guard's interface took the caller's `*sql.Conn`, and with `GetDB()` returning nil it would have refused **every** linked read with `the driver exposes no session connection`.

It now checks no connection at all. `OwnsPrivateDatabaseLink(ctx)` asks the driver, which runs `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM SYS.USER_DB_LINKS` on a session of its own. The only refusal left is a driver that cannot report at all (`the driver cannot report the executing account's private database links`), and the admin-data-source exemption is unchanged.

Pinned by:
- `TestLinkedReadReachesTheStatementAfterTheCutover` (`backend/api/v1`): a `GetDB() == nil` driver that reports no private link lets a linked read through to the statement, unmarked and unrefused; owning one still refuses with `PermissionDenied`, an error still returns `Internal`, admin and no-linked-column reads still pass.
- `TestOwnsPrivateDatabaseLinkAsksTheDriver`: the capability on the nil-`GetDB` shape.

## Probe and the dry run

`Probe` honours `ProbeContext.Autocommit`: the Oracle dry run passes it because `EXPLAIN PLAN FOR` is a PL/SQL block opener, so the statement runs alone on its own session. A non-autocommit probe is refused rather than run, because the contract's `Session` has no transaction to roll pre-executions back with. `TestProbeRunsTheDryRunAutocommit` covers both, plus ORA-00942 on a bad statement.

## Session continuity

`QueryConn` holds one omni session on the driver from the first call until `Close`, under a mutex, as the caller's `*sql.Conn` was: the API keeps the driver for an editor stream and calls `QueryConn` once per statement. `TestQueryConnKeepsTheSessionForTheDriver` runs `ALTER SESSION SET NLS_DATE_FORMAT` in one call and reads the formatted value back in the next.

## SQL\*Plus commands

`SET DEFINE OFF` and friends are not SQL, and Oracle refuses them over a session (ORA-00922). The old path skipped them because Bytebase's splitter did; the driver sends every segment its splitter yields. The adapter blanks them out of the script

## Summary

Cut `backend/plugin/db/doris` over to `github.com/bytebase/omni/doris/driver`. The package is now an adapter over the omni driver: it maps `db.ConnectionConfig` onto `driver.Config`, keeps Bytebase's SSH tunnel and TLS material on this side of the seam, and converts the contract's results back into `v1pb.QueryResult` / `metadatapb.DatabaseSchemaMetadata`. The catalog sync queries, the server-DDL dump renderer, the value conversion and the statement classification are deleted.

- `doris.go` 398 → 179, `execute.go` new 83, `query.go` 76 → 125: **387 non-test lines, 287 of them code**, against the cutover proof's measured adapter of 363. For scale, the StarRocks adapter (#22084) is 389 lines, 287 code, so this is that same adapter rather than a re-derived one; the proof's 363 was an estimate written before the sync mapping and the result conversion existed.
- `sync.go` (387 lines) and `dump.go` (387) deleted; the package's non-test code goes 1,248 → 387.
- `sync_test.go` (39), `dump_test.go` (67) and `dump_routine_probe_test.go` (143) deleted with the symbols they tested; `doris_test.go` is rewritten as adapter tests (config mapping, transaction mapping, task-run log, cell and result conversion) and `doris_live_test.go` is a live suite behind `DORIS_TEST_HOST`.
- **0 callers, 0 product files, no `go.mod` change.** No package names the concrete `*doris.Driver`, no `db.Prober` / `RowEstimator` / `ColumnExtraLookup` path exists for Doris before or after, and the existing pin (`1fd58c9d1`) already contains `doris/driver`.
- Clean, as before: `go.mod`'s pin needs no bump.

## Statement paths before and after

| Path | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| connection | `sql.Open("mysql", dsn)` with `multiStatements`, `maxAllowedPacket=0`, `interpolateParams`, a registered SSH dialer and a registered TLS key | `driver.Config` → `gomysql.NewConnector`, the same three parameters, `Config.Dial`, `Config.TLS`, the same 2h/50/15 pool settings |
| ping | `db.PingContext` | the same (omni `Ping`) |
| instance sync | `SELECT VERSION()`, `SHOW VARIABLES LIKE 'lower_case_table_names'`, `information_schema.SCHEMATA` minus `information_schema`/`_statistics_` | `SELECT @@version_comment, VERSION()`, the same variables query, the same catalog query minus `information_schema`/`_statistics_`/`mysql`/`__internal_schema`, `ORDER BY SCHEMA_NAME` |
| schema sync | columns / views / `mv_infos()` / tables / SCHEMATA, MySQL-family default handling | the same five queries and the same mapping in omni |
| statement classification | `base.ValidateSQLForEditor` → Doris splitter + validator | `doris/analysis.ValidateQuery` (the same AST gate) |
| limit / explain rewrite | `base.StatementWithResultLimit` / `base.ExplainStatement` | `analysis.RewriteResultLimit` / `analysis.ExplainStatement`; the requested explain format is still ignored |
| query | the caller's `*sql.Conn`, `/*app=bytebase*/` on the query path only, `util.RowsToQueryResult` + Doris value conversion | one

Cut OceanBase's driver over to `github.com/bytebase/omni/oceanbase/driver`. `db.Driver` is unchanged; the adapter is the only code that changed, and no product file does.

## Shape

Deleted 1,848 non-test lines and 490 test lines of the engine's own implementation — `sync.go` (1,490: the sync SQL, defaults decoding, view/trigger/event/routine readers), `role.go` (136), `query.go` (78), `stats.go` (41), `synonyms.go` (33), `dump.go` (25) — plus the fake-row test scaffolding those tests injected a `*sql.DB` for.

| | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| non-test lines in `backend/plugin/db/oceanbase` | 2,519 | 688 |
| files | 7 | 2 (`oceanbase.go`, `probe.go`) |

688 against the proof's 512: +60 is wave 0's `db.Prober` seam (the proof's three-method `liveProber` plus its `*sql.DB` bridge became a generic compensating-transaction probe in the adapter), +15 is the session the driver now keeps, and the rest is the package doc that records every delta below.

Everything product stays in the adapter: the AWS RDS and Google Cloud SQL IAM tokens, the RDS CA bundle, SSH tunnels, TLS material, the MySQL family's extra-parameter rule (`allowAllFiles` refused), the `-- txn-mode` / `-- txn-isolation` directive, the task-run logger, the `QueryContext` mapping and the v1pb conversion.

## Methods

`GetDB() *sql.DB` returns nil. The API already guards a nil handle, so no caller changes; the editor's `*sql.Conn` is not the contract's session.

| method | now |
| --- | --- |
| `Open` | builds `driver.Config` (host/port/database/user/password, `ApplicationName: "bytebase"` for the `/*app=bytebase*/` comment, `TLS`, `Dial`, `Params`) and calls `oceanbasedriver.Open`; does not reach the server |
| `Close` | closes the held session, the pool, and the SSH tunnel |
| `Ping` | driver's pool |
| `GetDB` | nil |
| `Execute` | parses the transaction directive, maps mode/isolation, delegates with `executeLogger` |
| `QueryConn` | holds one session for the driver's lifetime under a mutex, delegates, converts through `util.OmniResultToQueryResult`, keeps the typed plan out of an explain request |
| `SyncInstance` | driver's instance → `db.InstanceMetadata` with `MysqlLowerCaseTableNames` and roles |
| `SyncDBSchema` | driver's `SyncDatabase` |
| `Dump` | driver's `Dump` (omni's OceanBase catalog — the same function Bytebase's schema registry already called) |
| `Probe` | `db.Prober`: pre-executions and the statement in one transaction on one session, rolled back |
