title: feat(gitops): turn the GitOps page into a three-step setup (BYT-10423)
body:
### Why

A project owner wants database changes to travel the same way as code changes: a developer adds a SQL file to a pull request, Bytebase reviews it there, and merging the pull request deploys it to the databases, one environment after another.

To get there, a pipeline in the repository must act in Bytebase on the right databases. Before setup, the pipeline and Bytebase know nothing about each other, and the knowledge that connects them is split between the owner and Bytebase:

- The pipeline does not know which databases to change, or in which order.
- Bytebase does not know the pipeline. The pipeline needs an account in Bytebase, a rule for which repository may use it, and a role in the project.
- The repository has no workflow that calls Bytebase. The workflow carries about ten values that must match Bytebase.
- A mistake shows only when a pipeline runs. That can be days later, in the git provider, in front of a developer who did not do the setup. Some mistakes give a passing job that deploys nothing.

### What changes

The GitOps page becomes the setup itself. Nothing is saved; the files in the repository are the setup. The change improves how the owner goes through setup, and fixes cases where setup produced files that did not work.

**Improvements**

- **Setup is a step-by-step flow.** Three steps with one question or one task each: Databases, Workload identity, Workflow files. A row on top names every step, and Back and Continue stay at the bottom of the window. A step opens only when the steps before it are complete. Other products guide a setup with choices the same way.
- **Each step shows the result of its decision.** Step 1 shows the deploy order: the picked databases by environment, in the order the rollout deploys them. Step 2 shows what setup reads from the identity: its git provider, the repositories that can sign in, and its role in the project.
- **The owner answers two questions, and every other value is read.** The git provider comes from the identity, so there are no GitHub and GitLab tabs to choose from. The environments come from the databases. The files arrive complete.
- **Creating an identity does not leave setup.** Opened from step 2, the dialog offers GitHub Actions and GitLab CI only, closes after Create, and the new identity is picked.
- **The files are shorter and easier to copy.** They have no sign-in script: `bytebase-action` signs in as `BYTEBASE_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY` (#21974), which removes 18 lines from every GitHub job and 10 from every GitLab job. Each file shows its path and a copy button. A file longer than 12 lines shows its first 12 lines with "Show all N lines"; Copy always takes the whole file.
- **The migration folder can be changed.** It is `migrations/` by default, and an edit updates the files.
- **The page says what it covers and what comes next.** A line on every step says setup writes files for GitHub Actions and GitLab CI. Step 3 ends with what happens once the files are on the default branc

title: fix(review): tint only the priority in the review's finding counts (BYT-10499)
body:
## What

The SQL review row on the plan page counts open findings by priority. Each count was one tinted pill, "P1 2", so the count read as part of the label, and the mark did not match the P1 badge on each finding (BYT-10499).

```
before   [P0 1] [P1 2] · now
after    [P0] 1  [P1] 2 · now
```

- A count is the badge a finding carries, `P1`, then the number in the row's secondary text color, the same color as the time beside it.
- Priorities sit 12px apart, so each number reads as belonging to the badge before it.
- The pair stays one button with the same hover text and click. On hover only the number darkens and underlines, because a link's underline would run through the badge.

This is the change of #21976 by @rebelice, with the same lines. #21983 moved the counts into one review row, so #21976 no longer merges. This PR replaces it.

## Test

- `AutomatedReviewSection.test.tsx`: the badge holds the priority alone and the count is its own element. The assertion fails with the old markup.

- Checked on a dev build, since the row sits behind SQL Review V2 and the E2E harness serves a release bundle without it. A plan with one P0 and two P1 rule findings shows `[P0] 1  [P1] 2 · now`. Only the badges have a background, and the numbers take the color of the time. Hovering the P1 count darkens and underlines the number and leaves the badge as it is.

title: fix(plan): draw a finding's production badge as the environment's own badge
body: The production badge in a comment card's title bar (BYT-10500) drew its own copy of the environment badge. It kept the tint of the environment's color but set the text to the bar's gray and left out the production shield. Next to the same environment's badge on the page, it looked like a different color from the one the workspace picked. The card now draws `EnvironmentBadge` itself, the component the product uses for an environment everywhere else. The bar only caps the badge's width. ## Screenshots A real plan page. A rule review finding (P1) is on a database in the production environment "Prod", which the workspace colored green. The Targets row above it is the badge the product draws for the same environment. | Before | After | | --- | --- | | | | Measured on the page: before, the card's badge had text `rgb(82, 82, 91)` (the bar's gray) and no icon, while the Targets badge had `rgb(22, 163, 74)` and the shield. After, both compute to `rgb(22, 163, 74)` on `rgba(22, 163, 74, 0.1)` with the shield, and their markup is the same apart from the width class. ## Root cause and design delta **Cause:** the marker was a hand-made copy of a product object's component, and the copy changed one property. The store was not at fault: it carried the configured color, and the tint used it. **What the design missed:** `docs/design/plan-comment-card.md` called the badge "the environment's own badge" and in the same decision kept its text in the bar's gray, rejecting the environment's text color. It had no rule saying a marker that stands for an existing product object must look like that object. **Delta (in this PR):** - New **invariant 9**: a marker that stands for an object the product already draws is that object's own component (`ReviewResult`'s priority badge, `EnvironmentBadge`). The bar may limit its width; it never changes its color, text or icon. - **Invariant 6**: the production badge joins the P0/P1 badge and "Outdated" as the bar's colored items, in the workspace's color. - **D4**: the badge is `EnvironmentBadge`: name and shield in the environment's color on a 10% tint, or the default color. The "gray text on the tint" option is now listed as rejected, with the reason. - **Markers table**, slice 6's tests and the invariant-delivery table now match. **Trade-off:** D4 originally chose gray text because colored text is loud in the bar. A workspace that colors production red now gets red text near the P0 badge. The name, the shield and the badge's position after the priority still tell them apart. ## Tests `CommentThreadCard.test.tsx`: for environments colored red, green and with no color (so the default color), the bar's badge has the same markup as `EnvironmentBadge` rendered alone for that envi

title: fix(mcp): decide_issue shows its comment under the choice
body:
## Summary

`decide_issue`'s confirmation form put the decision's comment at the end of its approval line. That line runs past the terminal's edge, so Claude Code cut it, and the comment the user confirms ended in "…". A form read in Claude Code 2.1.322, on a 140-column terminal, showed this in both of its renderers. The comment now goes under the choice, as the form's description, the way the masking exemption grant shows its reason since #21912.

- A decision with a comment sends `Comment: "<comment>"` as the choice's description, quoted with `%q` so a line break stays on one line. A decision without a comment sends no description.
- Every other line of the message is unchanged.
- What an answer binds is unchanged. The signed answer is taken over the issue, its plan or grant, and the comment, and an answer replayed with another comment is still refused.

## What the renderers show

- **Default:** the description wraps and shows whole, so the comment does too.
- **Fullscreen:** the description's first row shows, cut with "…" at the terminal's edge. The comment now has that whole row, where the approval line left it about 50 columns. A comment longer than a row is still cut there, as the exemption reason is.

## Not in this change

An access request's last line runs 142 columns before any comment: its terms, the approval step and the requester. So on a 140-column terminal its tail is cut whatever happens to the comment. `decide_issue` keeps its layout, as #21912 kept it.

## Test plan

- [x] `TestDecideIssueApprovesOnConfirmation` and `TestDecideIssueRejectsOnConfirmation`: the message ends at the requester, and the form's schema carries the comment as the choice's description.
- [x] `TestDecideIssueDescribesAnAccessRequest`: the last line carries no comment.
- [x] `TestDecideIssuePutsTheCommentUnderTheChoice`: a decision with no comment sends no description, and a comment with a line break is one quoted line under the choice.
- [x] Mutation checks, run with `go test -overlay`: the comment back on the approval line, no description, a description with no comment, and the comment without `%q` each fail a test.
- [x] CI's `go test -p=8 -timeout 30m -ldflags "-w -s" -v ./backend/tests ./backend/api/v1 ./...` with `TZ=UTC`: 133 packages ok. golangci-lint v2.15.0, the release CI pins: 0 issues. `go build` of the server.

title: refactor(review): keep one review run row for each issue
body:
Third of three PRs for BYT-10505, stacked on #21985. The design is in `docs/design/plan-one-review.md`.

Since #21985 an issue has one review run. It is stored under a fixed type, beside the rows each reviewer used to have. This PR removes those rows and the type.

## What changes

- Migration `3.25.3` deletes the `review_run` rows of the types `RULE` and `AI`, drops the `type` column, and makes the key `(project, issue_id)`.
- The store reads and writes a review run by project and issue.
- `docs/pre-pr-checklist.md` lists the new key.

An issue left with no row gets its job from the next trigger: the rollout creator starts a missing review, and so does Run on the plan page. Nothing has read the removed rows since #21985, so the plan page shows the same before and after the migration.

## Breaking Changes

- The key of an existing table changes: `review_run` goes from `(project, issue_id, type)` to `(project, issue_id)`.
- The `type` column is dropped. A server from before this PR cannot run a review against the migrated schema, so with replicas of mixed versions the old ones fail their review runs until they are upgraded.
- The rows of the types `RULE` and `AI` are deleted. Their findings stay as comments.

## Verification

- Go: `golangci-lint` v2.15.0 (the 45 findings already on main, none in the changed files), `backend/migrator` with a test that applies the migration to rows of all three types, the full `backend/store` suite, `backend/api/v1`, `backend/runner/reviewrun`, `backend/runner/taskrun`, and the review run lifecycle, claim and collision tests in `backend/tests`, server build.
- Server: a throwaway metadata database held a `REVIEW` row and a `RULE` row for one issue. The server migrated it to 3.25.3 and left the one row with the key `(project, issue_id)`. The plan page showed the same two findings and Rerun ran the review again.
- Live: on this branch the job ran on `claude-sonnet-5-5` (20 s) and `gpt-5.6-terra` (34 s) against the plan used in #21985, with the same five findings, each merged across the 10 sampled databases, and the three AI threads kept.

Refs BYT-10505.

title: feat(review): run the review as one job
body:
Second of three PRs for BYT-10505, stacked on #21983 and followed by #21986. The design is in `docs/design/plan-one-review.md`.

#21983 shows one review but still runs each reviewer as its own job. This PR runs the review as one job, so the review is one action with one outcome: it posts every finding, or on an error it posts none.

## What changes

**One job.** A trigger leaves one job for the issue in `review_run`. One executor runs the standard rules, then the AI review, and skips a reviewer that is off. An error in either one ends the job, so a failure of the rules costs no model call.

- The job ends in one transaction. On success it posts the findings of both reviewers and resolves its earlier findings that it no longer reports. On failure it stores its error and changes no finding.
- The job is stored with the type `REVIEW`. Jobs of the two earlier types are no longer read. The next PR removes them and drops the type from the key.
- A stored finding keeps the reviewer that found it. The API does not show it. The AI review uses it to find its own earlier findings.
- A failed run now reports a code: `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED`, `UNAVAILABLE`, `DEADLINE_EXCEEDED`, `FAILED_PRECONDITION`, or `UNKNOWN`.

**Sample.** Both reviewers cover the CI sample of the project, or every database when the project sets no sample size. Before, the standard rules covered every database.

**Rollout.** The rollout is created only when the review has succeeded on the current SQL and every thread is resolved. A failed review holds the rollout until Retry.

**Plan checks.** `RunPlanChecks` no longer restarts the review, because a review can cost model calls. "Re-run all" on the plan page starts the checks and the review, and asks first when the AI review is on.

**Plan page.** The coverage hint on the review row describes one sample for the whole review. Activity shows one entry for each review.

## Worth knowing

- The rule findings now wait for the AI review, and an AI error leaves no finding of that run. The findings of the last successful review stay as they were.
- A rule finding's identity includes its databases. Where the sample shrinks them, the first run after this change posts that finding again and resolves the earlier thread as superseded.
- An open issue reads "Not run yet" until its first job of the new type. The rollout creator starts that job when it next looks at the plan, and Run on the page starts it too.

## Live test on four models

The job ran against a real plan before this PR was opened, to check that the AI review still merges a finding across databases, still leaves out what a standard rule reports, and still keeps its threads across runs. The plan has four statements and targets 50 databases, with a CI sample of 10.

Thirteen runs in all, nine before the rebase onto #21983 and four after:

- `claude-sonnet-5-5`: 21 s, 22 s, 22 s, 21 s
- `gpt-5.6-terra`: 31 s, 35 s, 31 s
- `deepseek-v4-pro`: 248 s, 302 s, 194 s

body:
Fourth of six implementation PRs for the plan comment card redesign (BYT-10500). It builds slice 2 of `docs/design/plan-comment-card.md` (#21968).

**Depends on:** nothing unmerged. Slices 1 (#21972) and 4 (#21973) and the group's Show/Hide (#21980) are on main. It shares no file with any open PR of this series.

## What changes

The Activity card takes the same title bar as the Changes section, and every card gets the new frame (D2, D3, D4, D5 in Activity, the rest of D6, D10):

- **Title**: the change's label, as its tab shows it, or "Deleted change", or "Comment on the plan" for a thread that is not on lines. The fold control is named by the title and the lines: "hr_test, lines 4–5". When two changes share a label, the name carries the change's number, as the title does.
- **Right end of the bar**: the line range, then "View in Statement" in the link color.
- **State labels**: "Resolved", "Outdated" and "Statement unavailable" sit after the title as text with an icon, never a filled badge. "Outdated" takes the warning color; the others stay `text-control`. While the anchor state is pending, none of them and no link shows.
- **Body**: the SQL excerpt sits in the body under the bar, drawn as today (Excerpt 1 restyles it).
- **Folding**: a card starts unfolded when open and folded when resolved, folds when it becomes resolved and unfolds when reopened. The card keeps this state. A click on the title, markers or state labels folds it too; a click on the lines, the link or the empty part of the bar does not.
- **Every card has a bar**: `ThreadSummary`, the resolved summary row, is deleted, with the `collapsible` and `renderContext` paths and `ThreadComment`'s unused `actions` and `label` props.
- **Frame**: `rounded-lg` and `border-control-border` with no shadow, in both places (the Changes section loses its `shadow-sm`). The lines under the bar and above the footer stay `border-block-border`. `docs/agents/frontend-ux.md` gains the exception for the comment card's corner and border, and `check-ui-guideline.mjs` allows `rounded-lg` only in the files that draw a comment card.
- **Footer**: shown only when the reader can reply or resolve.
- **Narrow widths**: the bar stays one 32px row on a desktop, a long title truncating with its full text on hover. When the parts cannot fit, as on a phone, the lines and the link drop together to a second row at the right end.

Design rows and invariants delivered: the three Activity rows of Title; every row of State labels, lines and link; Excerpt and Footer; the Activity row of Folding; in Activity, the white bar and footer of invariant 2, invariant 4 apart from the production badge, and invariant 6 for the other state labels; invariants 5, 7 and 8 in full; invariant 3 for every thread card (PR 6/6 adds the composer). Invariant 2 holds in full after PR 6/6 (the composer and the excerpt), and invariants 4 and 6 after PR 5/6 (the production badge).

title: feat(review): show one review on the plan page
body:
BYT-10505. The design is in `docs/design/plan-one-review.md`, added here.

This PR now holds all three parts of the stack. #21985 (one job) and #21986 (one row for each issue) were merged into this branch, so it lands them together.

The plan page splits the review into two reviewers, Standard rules and AI review, each with its own row, status and findings. Telling them apart brings the author nothing: any open finding holds the rollout, whoever posted it, and the author handles both kinds the same way. This PR makes the review one review, on the page, in the API, and in the backend.

## What changes

**API.** An issue has one review run.

- `GetReviewRun` and `RunReview` keep their names. The resource name is now `projects/{project}/issues/{issue}/reviewRun`, with no reviewer in it.
- `ReviewRun` loses `type` and the `Type` enum. `status` becomes `state` (`RUNNING`, `SUCCEEDED`, `FAILED`), as AIP-216 asks. `error` becomes `google.rpc.Status`, with a code: `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED`, `UNAVAILABLE`, `DEADLINE_EXCEEDED`, `FAILED_PRECONDITION`, or `UNKNOWN`.
- `run_type` is removed from a review result and from the run completion event. A standard rule result is the one that carries `rule_type`.
- `RunReview` starts the review. A reviewer that is off is skipped, not refused.

**One job.** A trigger leaves one job for the issue in `review_run`. One executor runs the standard rules, then the AI review, and skips a reviewer that is off. An error in either one ends the job, so a failure of the rules costs no model call.

- The job ends in one transaction. On success it posts the findings of both reviewers and resolves its earlier findings that it no longer reports. On failure it stores its error and changes no finding.
- A stored finding keeps the reviewer that found it. The API does not show it. The AI review uses it to find its own earlier findings.

**Sample.** Both reviewers cover the CI sample of the project, or every database when the project sets no sample size. Before, the standard rules covered every database.

**Rollout.** The rollout is created only when the review has succeeded on the current SQL and every thread is resolved. A failed review holds the rollout until Retry. Before, the rollout waited only for the standard rules.

**Plan checks.** `RunPlanChecks` no longer restarts the review, because a review can cost model calls. "Re-run all" on the plan page starts the review and then the checks, and asks first when the AI review is on.

**Plan page.** One row, "SQL review", replaces the Standard rules row and the AI review row.

- Every finding names SQL review as its author. A rule finding keeps its rule name and code.
- One Rerun button. It asks first when the AI review is on, because a run makes model calls.
- Deploy lists one line for the review, and the finding walker steps through every finding.
- Activity shows one entry for each review, heading the group of the findings it posted.
- The coverage hint on the row describes one sample for th

title: feat(mcp): administer_workspace creates a CI identity with its GitOps role after a confirmation
body:
## Summary

MCP sessions could not create a CI identity: `CreateWorkloadIdentity` was refused as a credential mint, and the agent had no way to give an identity a role. This PR gives `administer_workspace` a fourth entry. It creates a workload identity that GitHub Actions or GitLab CI jobs in one repository sign in as, then grants it the GitOps Service Agent role in its project, after the user confirms one form. This is journey 4 (GitOps) of admin changes over MCP (BYT-9292).

- **Two handler fixes, for every caller.** On main, `CreateWorkloadIdentity` stored an identity in an archived project, and the grant that follows then fails. It also stored an identity whose ID holds `/`: the identity's name, `workloadIdentities/{email}`, is split on `/`, so the server could sign it in but never read, update or delete it. The create now refuses both before storing anything (NotFound, InvalidArgument). The ACL already refused a missing project, and another workspace's, before the handler runs; it lets an archived project through.
- **Classes.** `CreateWorkloadIdentity` moves from FORBIDDEN to WRITE, and `ProjectService/SetIamPolicy` from EXCLUDED to WRITE. The gate serves the create only with a confirmation for the new identity's name, not its parent, and the grant only with one for the project. `administer_workspace` attaches each to its own call, so `call_api` is refused for both. `UpdateWorkloadIdentity` stays FORBIDDEN; `GetWorkloadIdentity`, `ListWorkloadIdentities`, `DeleteWorkloadIdentity`, `UndeleteWorkloadIdentity` and `WorkspaceService/SetIamPolicy` stay EXCLUDED.
- **One form, as the console's dialog.** The console's creation dialog (#21942) grants GitOps Service Agent right after the create. An earlier plan had two entries, the create and a generic role grant; this PR follows the console instead. The role is fixed (the create request has no role field). Other roles, and grants to other members, stay in the console.
- **What the entry takes.** `parent` (a project), `workloadIdentityId`, a `title`, and `providerType` GITHUB or GITLAB with a `subjectPattern`. The tool sets the provider's issuer and the audience `bytebase`, the console's presets and what the generated GitOps workflows request. It refuses another issuer, another audience, a JWKS URL, and every other field by name.
- **One repository per identity, every job in it.** The tool takes `repo:OWNER[@OWNER_ID]/REPO[@REPO_ID]:*` and `project_path:GROUP/PROJECT:*`, read by two new functions in `wif` beside the matcher. The handler's `matchSubject` decided this (oracle below): a name prefix such as `repo:acme/deploy*` admits `acme/deployer` too; a branch pattern admits no job that references an environment, and the generated GitOps workflows deploy in environments and check on pull requests; several patterns the handler stores match no token. Branch, environment, pull request and owner-wide patterns go to the console.
- **Journey 4's form**, as its test pins it:

title: fix(review): count only new findings on a review's Activity line (BYT-10495)
body:
## What

On the plan page, each completed review writes one line in Activity. A later run read "1 new, 1 still found, 1 no longer found" (BYT-10495). The counts named no noun and compared the run with an earlier one the reader does not see, so "1 no longer found" read like a missing resource.

Every run now says only how many findings it posted:

```
Standard rules reviewed the SQL · 1 new finding
AI review reviewed the SQL · 2 new findings
Standard rules reviewed the SQL · no new findings
```

- A finding the run reports again keeps its earlier thread, which the page already shows, so the line leaves it out. The same goes for a finding the run no longer reports.
- The line no longer carries an open count. It showed only above zero, so "1 new finding" beside "2 new findings, 1 open" read as two kinds of line. Each finding's card shows whether it is open, and the Automated review row counts what still needs attention.
- `kept_count` and `superseded_count` stay in the API. This line no longer reads them.
- The examples in `docs/design/plan-review-findings-group.md` follow the new wording.

## Test

- `ReviewActivityTimeline.test.tsx` has one case per wording.
- `pnpm --dir frontend test` passes.
- Checked on a dev build with both reviewers, since the line sits behind SQL Review V2 and the E2E harness serves a release bundle without it. A new plan edited twice gave "1 new finding" and "2 new findings", then "no new findings" from both, then "1 new finding" from both.

title: chore(deps): drop the bytebase/tidb parser fork replace
body:
## What

Remove the last remnant of the TiDB pingcap migration: the unversioned `github.com/pingcap/tidb/pkg/parser => github.com/bytebase/tidb/pkg/parser` replace, plus the Renovate `ignoreDeps` entry that existed only because bumps were no-ops under the replace. `go mod tidy` swaps the go.sum entries and adds `coreos/go-semver` as a new indirect.

## Why it is safe

- Since #21949 no Bytebase package imports the module. It stays in the build only through gh-ost → go-mysql, which compile `pkg/parser/{charset,format,mysql,terror}`.
- Both consumers — bytebase/gh-ost2 v1.1.11 and go-mysql v1.15.0 — declare upstream `v0.0.0-20260504140133-511dba1dbe17` in their own go.mods; the replace was silently downgrading them to a Nov-2025 fork snapshot. MVS keeps selecting the same version, now actually fetched from upstream.
- Fork↔upstream diff of the compiled packages: `charset`, `format`, `terror` are byte-identical; `mysql` differs only by upstream additions (TiDB nextgen version helpers — the source of the go-semver indirect — and a FORMAT() locale rewrite), none on go-mysql's call path.

## Verification

- `go mod tidy` is idempotent; full server build.
- `go test ./backend/component/ghost/` (the gh-ost consumer path) passes.
- E2E boot smoke on the `embed_frontend` build (`workspace-banner` spec): 3 passed — the binary with upstream parser packages boots, provisions sample instances, and serves login/settings flows.

title: fix(review): read automated review times to the minute
body:
## Problem

The Automated review rows showed "38 seconds ago" and "30 seconds ago" side by side, ticking every second. The reviewers finish seconds apart, so the two ages changed at different moments (BYT-10503).

## Change

- The rows read "now" through the first minute, then count in minutes. GitHub's `relative-time` also shows seconds by default and offers `precision="minute"` for places like this. This follows that option for these rows and leaves every other timestamp as it is.
- `HumanizeTs` gains `precision`, `"second"` by default. It applies to the `queue` label, the only mode whose label is an age.
- In `datetime.ts` the relative unit table is keyed by precision. The label and the boundary that schedules it read the same table, so a minute-precision label wakes once at its first minute instead of every second.
- `timestamp-display.md` lists the automated review rows and the reason.

Showing one review instead of two rows (BYT-10505) would also remove the out-of-step pair, but a single row would still tick each second.

## Testing

- `datetime.test.ts`: the minute-precision reading reads "now" within a minute on either side, changes at one minute, and agrees with the second-precision reading from a minute on. It also joins the boundary sweep, which checks the scheduled change instant against the reading at each sampled age.
- `HumanizeTs.test.tsx`: a minute-precision label renders and re-renders on its own reading, and the other modes ignore the prop.
- `AutomatedReviewSection.test.tsx`: both reviewer rows ask for minute precision.
- `pnpm --dir frontend test` passes.
- Checked in a Vite dev build against a dev server with SQL Review V2 on. A fresh rule review reads "now", and "1 minute ago" a minute later. The E2E suite covers SQL review V1, which has no such row, so there is no browser scenario.

Refs BYT-10503, BYT-10369

title: refactor(pg,redshift,cockroachdb): read timestamp precision from native pgx field descriptions
body:
## What

Removes the `github.com/jackc/pgx/v5 => github.com/bytebase/pgx/v5` fork (the `replace` in `go.mod`). The fork carried a single patch: it made the `stdlib` database/sql driver's `ColumnTypeDecimalSize` report fractional-seconds precision for `timestamp`/`timestamptz`, which upstream pgx only reports for `numeric`.

## Why we don't need the fork

That precision is the column's `atttypmod` — already on the wire in the pgx **field description**. The fork existed only because `database/sql`'s `ColumnType` interface has no way to carry the type modifier, so it overloaded `DecimalSize`. Reading the field description directly removes the need for any patched driver.

It can't come from anywhere cheaper: a query result column need not map to a catalog column (`SELECT now()`, casts, expressions, joins), and PostgreSQL drops trailing fractional zeros in text output, so the value itself has already lost the precision. The field description is the authoritative source.

## How

- **`util.PgColumnTypeModifiers`** describes the statement without executing it (anonymous `Prepare`, no server-side prepared statement) and returns each result column's type modifier.
- **`util.RowsToQueryResultIndexed`** threads the zero-based column index to the converter so a driver can supply per-column metadata; the existing `RowsToQueryResult` / `RowsToLimitedQueryResult` are unchanged passthroughs, so the other engines are untouched.
- **pg, redshift, cockroachdb** read the modifiers once per statement (after any `SET`, before running the statement) and map them to the fractional-seconds precision (`-1`/unknown → 6), replacing the `DecimalSize` call. Per the forked-engine rule, all three pgx-based engines are handled together.

## Behavior

Unchanged: both the old fork and the new path read the same `atttypmod`, so `Accuracy` is identical. If a describe ever fails, the column falls back to the default precision of 6 (same as an unspecified precision), and the statement itself still runs and reports its own errors.

## Verification

- Rewired `TestConvertValueTimestampFromDriver` (real PostgreSQL container) to the native path; it asserts `PgColumnTypeModifiers` returns `[-1, 3, -1, -1, -1]` and that `timestamptz(3)` → `Accuracy=3`, unspecified columns → `6`. This is end-to-end proof on real engine output that the native path replaces the fork.
- `gofmt`, `golangci-lint` v2.15.0 (0 issues), and the full server build pass.
- Frontend rendering of `Accuracy` is unchanged by this PR, so no new browser E2E was added.

## Follow-up (not in this PR)

The upstream PR [jackc/pgx#2704](https://github.com/jackc/pgx/pull/2704) is no longer needed by Bytebase, and the `bytebase/pgx` fork can be retired once this lands.

title: feat(action): sign in with a workload identity inside bytebase-action (BYT-10421)
body:
### Why

The GitOps page generates workflows that sign in with a workload identity. Each job carries a shell script that fetches the CI's OIDC token, exchanges it at `/v1/auth:exchangeToken` and passes the result to `bytebase-action` as `--access-token`.

- The script is 18 lines in four GitHub jobs and 10 lines in four GitLab jobs.
- The GitHub step writes the token to `$GITHUB_OUTPUT` unmasked, and the next step interpolates it into its command line.
- The token lasts one hour and a static `--access-token` cannot be renewed, so a rollout that waits longer fails.

### What changes

`bytebase-action` signs in with the workload identity itself. A job names the identity and needs no sign-in step:

```yaml
    permissions:
      id-token: write
    env:
      BYTEBASE_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY: ci@workload.bytebase.com
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: bytebase-action check --url=https://bytebase.example.com --project=projects/example --targets=instances/example/databases/example --file-pattern="migrations/*.sql"
```

The action uses the first of these that is set:

1. An access token, from `--access-token` or `BYTEBASE_ACCESS_TOKEN`.
2. `--workload-identity`, the new flag.
3. A service account, from its flags or environment variables.
4. `BYTEBASE_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY`, the environment variable.

The variable ranks last because every generated workflow already sets it for its script. It takes effect only where the action failed before with `service-account is required`.

The CI job's ID token comes from:

- `BYTEBASE_ID_TOKEN`, when set. This covers GitLab `id_tokens` and any other OIDC issuer.
- GitHub's token endpoint otherwise, with the audience `bytebase` or `--workload-identity-audience`.

Custom headers are sent to Bytebase only, not to GitHub's endpoint.

### Behavior changes

- **Sign-in is the first call.** A refused sign-in ends the run before the version check. It used to appear first as the warning `Unable to get server version`, then fail on the next request.
- **A sign-in failure prints one line**, `sign in as <identity>: <reason>`, with no stack trace. It replaces `failed to login`. On GitHub the same line is also an `::error::` annotation.
- **No usage text on a runtime failure.** Once the flags parse, a failure no longer prints the flag list.
- **With no credential set**, the error names all three methods. It was `service-account is required and cannot be empty`.
- **A service account and a workload identity both set** logs a warning that names the two.
- **An ID token sent over `http`** to a host other than loopback logs a warning.

Existing workflows are unaffected: they pass `--access-token`, which still wins, and `ExchangeToken` does not change. There is no server, proto or schema change.

### Rollout

This is the action half. The generator keeps emitting the script until a follow-up PR, which must merge after this one has reached Cloud: the Cloud workflow restarts the server before it pushes the `:cloud` action im
author: boojack
diff:
--- action/README.md (+61/-0)
@@ -37,18 +37,31 @@ These flags apply to the main `bytebase-action` command and its subcommands (`ch
 
 -   **`--url`**: The Bytebase instance URL. Required.
 
+-   **`--workload-identity`**: The workload identity email. The action signs in as it with the CI job's ID token, so the job stores no secret. This is the recommended sign-in.
+    -   Default: `""` (empty string). If not provided via flag, reads from the `BYTEBASE_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY` environment variable.
+    -   See [Sign-in](#sign-in) for where the ID token comes from.
+
+-   **`--workload-identity-audience`**: The audience of the ID token requested from GitHub.
+    -   Default: `bytebase`. If not provided via flag, reads from the `BYTEBASE_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_AUDIENCE` environment variable.
+    -   It must be one of the audiences the workload identity allows.
+
 -   **`--service-account`**: The service account email.
     -   Default: `""` (empty string). If not provided via flag, reads from the `BYTEBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT` environment variable.
 
 -   **`--service-account-secret`**: The service account password.

+
+The action signs in once, before any other request. It uses the first of these that is set:

+1.  An access token, from `--access-token` or `BYTEBASE_ACCESS_TOKEN`.
+2.  `--workload-identity`, the flag.
+3.  A service account, from `--service-account` and `--service-account-secret` or their environment variables.
+4.  `BYTEBASE_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY`, the environment variable.

+A workload identity needs the CI job's ID token:
+
+-   **GitHub Actions**: give the job `permissions: id-token: write`. The action requests the token itself.

+      sql-review:

+        env:

+
+    ```yaml

+      id_tokens:

+`BYTEBASE_ID_TOKEN` is also read on GitHub, and wins over the token GitHub would issue.

title: [2/9] feat(plan): give a comment's avatar its own column and indent replies
body: Fourth of eight implementation PRs for the plan comment card redesign (BYT-10500). It builds slice 4 of the design doc in #21968, `docs/design/plan-comment-card.md`. **Depends on:** nothing. It is independent of #21972 (slice 1); whichever merges second needs only a rebase. ## What changes D7, "Comment text sits in its own column", in both places a thread shows (the Changes section and Activity draw the same card): - **First comment**: the avatar gets a 20px column of its own. The author row, the "Applies to" row of a finding, its priority and title, and the text sit beside it, so they share one left edge that the avatar does not. - **Replies**: indented by the avatar column, so a reply's avatar starts where the first comment's text starts, and joined to the first comment by a line under its avatar. The `bg-control-bg/50` band behind replies is gone. "N replies hidden · Show all" stays, inside the indented column. Design rows delivered: First comment and Replies (Body and footer). Nothing else changes; the reply footer and its composer are untouched. ## Screenshots Real page, built from this branch and from `main`: a thread with one reply in the Changes section. | Before | After | | --- | --- | | | | ## Tests - `ThreadComment.test.tsx`: for a comment and for a review result, the avatar is a column of its own beside the content, never inside it; the reviewer's avatar is in that column. - `CommentThreadCard.test.tsx`: a reply is indented and the first comment is not; the replies carry no grey band; the joining line shows only when there are replies; each comment's avatar column comes before its content. - E2E `plan-detail-review.spec.ts`: on a thread with replies, the first comment's text starts after its avatar column, a reply's avatar lines up with the first comment's text, and the joining line runs under the first avatar. Gates: `pnpm fix`, `pnpm test` (741 files, 10,556 tests). E2E `plan-detail-review.spec.ts` (CUJ L, CUJ M, the service-account and C4–C5 groups): 15 passed, 2 failed. Both failures also fail on `main`: "A step held only by a service account" and the C5 test marked as expected to fail, which now passes. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: [1/9] feat(plan): give comment cards in the Changes section a title bar that folds
body:
First of nine implementation PRs for the plan comment card redesign (BYT-10500). It builds slice 1 of the design doc in #21968, `docs/design/plan-comment-card.md`.

**Depends on:** nothing.

## What changes

In the Changes section, every comment thread under a SQL line is now one white card that starts with a title bar.

- **The bar names the lines** (D3): "Comment on line 1" or "Comment on lines 4–5". The range label that showed only when two threads' ranges differed is gone.
- **A folded thread is its bar alone** (D4): the dense collapsed row (author, priority badge, summary, reply count, time) is deleted. A folded card says where the thread is, what state it is in and how urgent it is, nothing about what it says.
- **The bar says how urgent a finding is** (D4): after the title, a P0 or P1 finding shows the badge `ReviewResult` already draws, folded and unfolded. A P2 finding and a person's thread show none. The row this PR deletes was what showed a folded finding's priority, so its replacement lands here.
- **Any thread folds from the bar** (D5): an icon-only fold control at the left, with `aria-expanded`, named by the title, replaces the close button in the author row. A click anywhere else on the bar folds too, as a pointer shortcut: the fold control stays the one focusable control, a click on a control inside the bar keeps its own meaning, and a drag that selects text does not fold. The statement layer still owns the fold state: unfolding selects the thread in the stepper, folding clears that selection, and the reader's own Resolve folds the card.
- **"Resolved" moves into the bar** (from D6), right after the title, as text with an icon in `text-control`. Nothing in the bar uses `text-control-light`. `ThreadStateBadge` is shared, so the Activity card's "Resolved" also changes color; the Activity card is otherwise untouched until slice 2.
- **The bar and the footer are white** (invariant 2, in the Changes section), where the bar was gray and the footer tinted. The Activity card's footer changes with slice 2.
- **The footer shows only when the reader can act**: a reader who can neither reply nor resolve sees none.

Design rows and invariants delivered: Title (Changes section, lines); the three priority rows of Markers; State labels ("Resolved"); Footer; Folding (Changes section) and its click row; in the Changes section, the white bar and footer of invariant 2, invariants 4 (apart from the production badge), 5 and 7; invariant 6 for the badge and "Resolved". None of these holds in full yet: by the doc's invariant table, slice 2 finishes 5 and 7 in Activity, slice 6 finishes 4 and 6 with the production badge, and invariant 2 holds in full after slices 5 and Excerpt 1.

## For review

- **Unsaved edits.** A reply draft survives folding a card (the layer keeps it). An unsaved edit of a comment does not: the comment unmounts when its card folds. The design leaves this unchanged and says this PR settles it in review. With the whole bar now folding

title: feat(workload-identity): record the external workload on audit rows (BYT-10494)
body:
### Why

A workload identity lets a CI job sign in with its OIDC token. Bytebase checks the token's subject against the identity's pattern and then discards it, so the audit log names the identity and never the job behind it.

With a pattern such as `repo:my-org/*`, every repository in the organization signs in under one actor, and the log cannot tell them apart.

### What changes

Each audit row a federated workload produces now carries the issuer and subject of the token it signed in with, on the exchange and on every call made with the issued token.

```proto
message AuditLog {
  FederatedIdentity federated_identity = 13;
}

message FederatedIdentity {
  string issuer = 1;  // the token's "iss" claim
  string subject = 2; // the token's "sub" claim
}
```

| Surface | What it shows |
|---|---|
| API | `AuditLog.federated_identity` (output only) |
| Search | `federated_subject == "repo:my-org/app:ref:refs/heads/main"` |
| Stdout | `federated_issuer` and `federated_subject` |
| Console | The subject as a second line under the actor, with subject and issuer in a tooltip |

How it gets there:

- `ExchangeToken` issues a token with an RFC 8693 `act` claim holding the external `iss` and `sub`.
- The auth interceptor copies the claim to the audit row for unary and streaming calls.
- The values are recorded for audit and never read for authorization.

No migration. The audit payload is JSONB, and rows written before this change lack the key.

### Behavior changes

- **The successful exchange row now names its actor**, `workloadIdentities/{email}`. It was empty. A refused exchange still names none.
- **An exchange is refused when the subject exceeds 1024 bytes.** The subject rides in every request header and every row.

### Screenshots

Two workload identity rows above ordinary rows. The subject sits under the actor, and its tooltip shows the subject and issuer:

![Audit log with a federated identity tooltip](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8f6d7555-2f08-44ad-b341-c4a518834ee2)

### Alternatives considered

- **Flat `principal_subject` only.** A subject is unique only within its issuer, and the issuer could not be recovered once the identity's config is edited.
- **Two flat fields.** Same data, but one identifier becomes two independent fields.
- **One composite string.** Needs escaping, and the `==`-only filter could not search by subject.
- **Google-style `authentication_info`.** The actor and `mcp_delegation` would stay outside it.
- **A token ID on later rows.** Attribution would need a join the audit search does not have.
- **Reuse `service_data`.** It holds one value that `UpdateSetting` and `SetIamPolicy` already fill.

The full list, goals and references: `docs/design/audit-federated-identity.md`.

### Not in this change

- **Export.** `ExportAuditLogs` writes eight fixed columns, so the field does not reach exports.
- **MCP.** A workload identity token used at `/mcp` loses the identity when the internal credential is minted.

author: zchpeter
diff:
--- docs/design/plan-review-findings-group.md (+160/-0)
@@ -0,0 +1,160 @@
+# Plan review findings group
+
+Status: proposal · 2026-11-11
+
+When Standard rules or AI review finishes a run on a plan, the Activity timeline records it as one
+line, such as "Standard rules reviewed the SQL · 2 findings, 1 open", with a Show or Hide control.
+The findings that run posted are comment threads. Today each one is its own timeline entry, with
+its own icon, at the same level as the review line that owns it, so nothing on the page says which
+findings belong to which review. The rule this doc lands on: **a review and the findings it posted
+share one bordered group in Activity, and a comment from a person stays its own entry.**
+
+This is the third of three docs, each in its own PR. [Plan comment card](plan-comment-card.md)
+covers the card each finding is drawn as. The second, Plan comment SQL excerpt, covers the SQL
+shown inside it.
+
+## Problem
+
+This applies where SQL Review V2 is on (`sqlReviewV2Enabled()`), which is where a completed run is
+one line. Under `frontend/src/routes/project/plan-detail/components/review/`:
+
+- **A finding is a sibling of its review.** `buildTimelineEntries` (`timelineEvents.ts`) emits one
+  `review-run` entry for the run and then one entry per finding. `ReviewActivityTimeline.tsx`
+  renders the run with `ReviewRunActivityRow` and each finding with `ThreadActivityRow`, which
+  gives it a timeline icon of its own and a card offset by `ml-3`.
+- **Show and Hide have no visible scope.** Show reveals a run's findings as further entries below
+  the line. With two reviews in a row, the reader cannot see where one review's findings end.
+- **Show and Hide read as static text.** The control is a link `Button` whose color is overridden
+  with `text-control-light`, so it looks like the timestamp beside it. BYT-10508 reports this.
+
+## Principle
+
+> In a timeline, an entry that owns other entries holds them. Ownership is shown by containment,
+> one level deep, and never by indentation alone.
+
+## Decisions
+
+**D1 · A review and its findings share one group.** The review line becomes the first line of a
+bordered group, and the finding cards sit inside it. The findings lose their own timeline icon; the
+review keeps its icon on the timeline. Show and Hide keep their place on the review line and now
+act on a visible group. Rejected: indenting the findings under their review line with nothing
+joining them. It leaves two card edges on the page, the indented findings and a person's comment
+further left, and reads as a misalignment. Rejected: a vertical line down the indented findings,
+which is what GitHub draws for the threads of a review. It adds a second vertical line beside
+the timeline's own and keeps two card edges. Rejected: giving every thread a line of its own,
+such as "commented on the SQL", so that no card is indented. It costs a line for each comment
+from a person and shows ownership less plainly than a group does. It is the fallback if D4 is
+not accepted.
+
+**D2 · The group is a border and nothing else.** `border-block-border`, with the corners of the
+cards it holds and with no shadow, no fill and no title bar. A comment card is `rounded-lg` in
+[Plan comment card](plan-comment-card.md), so the group is too: a sharper frame around rounder
+cards reads as two unrelated boxes. That doc changes the guideline and its scanner to allow the
+corner in the files that draw a comment card, and the slice that builds the group adds the
+group's file to them. The cards inside keep their title bar and their darker border,
+`border-control-border`. The two levels look different, so it stays clear that the finding is
+the unit and the group only says where it belongs. The review line sits inside the border with
+`px-3 py-2`, so a folded group has 8px above and below its text and does not read as crowded.
+The cards sit below the line with 12px on each side and 8px between them.
+
+**D3 · A person's comment stays a top-level entry.** Its card starts on the group's left edge, so
+the page has one outer edge. Findings sit 12px inside it, and the border explains why.
+
+**D4 · The UX guideline gains one exception.** `docs/agents/frontend-ux.md` says "Do not put cards
+inside cards." The rule stays. The slice that builds D1 amends it to:
+
+> Do not put cards inside cards, with one exception. A **group frame** MAY hold the cards that
+> belong to one parent entry in a list or timeline when all of the following hold:
+>
+> - The frame's first line names the parent and carries the control that shows or hides the group.
+> - The frame is a border only: `border-block-border`, with the corners of the cards it holds and
+>   with no shadow, no fill and no title bar. The cards inside keep their own.
+> - Nesting stops there. A card inside a group frame MUST NOT contain another framed box.
+> - Only a parent that has cards gets a frame. Hiding them folds the frame to its first line. A
+>   parent with no cards is a plain line.
+
+The first condition ties the frame to ownership, so it cannot be used for decoration. The second
+keeps the two levels distinct. The third caps the depth at two. The fourth prevents a frame around
+nothing, and keeps an entry the same shape when it is hidden and shown.
+Rejected: dropping the rule. It exists to stop decorative nesting, and that reason still holds.
+
+**D5 · Show and Hide fold the whole group.** The group is a card whose first line is the review
+line, and Show and Hide are its fold control:
+
+- A run is open by default while one of its findings is still current, meaning no later run has
+  superseded it. Show and Hide override the default. This does not change.
+- An open group shows the card of every finding the run posted.
+- A hidden group is folded to its first line, inside its frame. It shows no finding card,
+  whatever replies the findings have.
+- A review with no findings has nothing to fold. It is a plain line with no frame and no Show.
+- A hidden group opens when one of its findings is asked for from elsewhere on the page, so the
+  page can scroll to the card it was asked to show. The timeline already does this for its
+  folded middle, which unfolds when a card inside it is asked for.
+
+Today a hidden run still shows the findings `needsActivityCard` in `threadModel.ts` keeps: one
+people replied to, or one the Changes section cannot show. So when every finding of a review has
+a reply, Hide changes nothing but its own word, and reads as broken. A hidden finding is not
+lost: the review line still counts it, as in "2 findings, 1 open", and Show brings it back.
+The old rule also kept a card on the page for a finding the Changes section cannot show, which
+is where `focusInActivity` in `useFocusThread.ts` sends the reader. Opening the group on such a
+request keeps that jump working.
+Rejected: keeping that rule. A control that sometimes hides is worse than one that always does.
+Rejected: a hidden review as a plain line. The entry would change from a box to a sentence and
+back each time it is toggled.
+
+**D6 · The group wraps whatever a review line is.** BYT-10505 proposes showing Standard rules and
+AI review as one review. This design does not depend on the outcome: the group belongs to a review
+line, however many reviewers the page distinguishes.
+
+**D7 · Show and Hide look like actions.** The control drops the `text-control-light` override and
+takes the shared link `Button`'s own color, the same as "View in Statement" on a finding's card.
+Hover and keyboard focus come from the shared button. Rejected: a chevron in place of the word. It
+would sit directly above the cards' own fold chevrons, and it is less clear which one folds what.
+Rejected: an outlined button, which is heavier than the one line it sits on.
+
+## States
+
+| Review | Activity shows |
+| --- | --- |
+| No findings | The review line alone |
+| Open, with findings | A group: the review line, then one card per finding |
+| Hidden, with findings | The group folded: its frame around the review line, with Show |
+| A later review | The line says what changed: "1 new, 1 still found, 1 no longer found" |
+| A finding a later run reports again | Its thread stays with the run that first posted it, as today |
+| A comment from a person | Its own entry, outside any group |
+
+## Scope
+
+Frontend and one guideline file. Two PRs. Each leaves main shippable and names what it depends on.
+
+1. **Show and Hide in the link color (D7).** Depends on nothing. It does not need the group or the
+   new card.
+   - `ReviewActivityTimeline.tsx`: the Show and Hide control in `ReviewRunActivityRow` drops the
+     `text-control-light` override.
+   - Tests: `ReviewActivityTimeline.test.tsx` (the control carries no color override).
+2. **Group (D1 to D5).** Depends on the slice of [Plan comment card](plan-comment-card.md) that
+   gives the Activity card its title bar and its corners. The slice is named by what it builds
+   because its number can change while that doc is in review.
+   - `timelineEvents.ts`: a run's finding entries become children of its `review-run` entry, and
+     a hidden run has none. `needsActivityCard` in `threadModel.ts` then has no caller and goes.
+   - `ReviewActivityTimeline.tsx`: `ReviewRunActivityRow` renders the group. `ThreadActivityRow`
+     keeps rendering a person's thread. A focus request for a finding opens its group before the
+     timeline scrolls to it.
+   - `foldTimeline.ts`: a group stays together when a long history folds, as an open run's line
+     and cards do today.
+   - `docs/agents/frontend-ux.md`: the exception in D4.
+   - `frontend/scripts/check-ui-guideline.mjs` and its test: the group's file joins the files the
+     scanner allows `rounded-lg`.
+   - Tests: `timelineEvents.test.ts` (the default from D5; an open run has every finding and a
+     hidden run has none, with and without replies), `ReviewActivityTimeline.test.tsx` (a finding
+     renders inside its review's group and without a timeline icon; a hidden review with findings
+     renders its frame around the review line and no card; a review with no findings renders no
+     frame; a focus request for a finding in a hidden review opens the group and scrolls to the
+     card), `foldTimeline.test.ts`. E2E:
+     `frontend/tests/e2e/plan-detail/plan-detail-review.spec.ts`.
+
+## Not in this PR
+
+- Grouping review events by SQL change, which is the other half of BYT-10508.
+- Merging the two reviewers into one review. That is BYT-10505.
+- The wording of review lines, which is BYT-10495.

diff:
--- docs/design/plan-comment-sql-excerpt.md (+123/-0)
@@ -0,0 +1,123 @@
+# Plan comment SQL excerpt
+
+Status: proposal · 2026-11-11
+
+In the Activity timeline, a comment thread on lines of SQL shows those lines above the comment, so
+a reader can tell what the comment is about without opening the statement. Today every commented
+line in that excerpt is tinted, whatever the comment says, and the comment starts on the same left
+edge as the line numbers, so it reads as more lines of the statement. The rule this doc lands on:
+**the excerpt sits on gray inside the white card, marks the commented lines with a bar beside the
+line numbers, tints no line, and sits inset from the comment below it.**
+
+This is the second of three docs, each in its own PR. [Plan comment card](plan-comment-card.md)
+covers the card the excerpt sits in. The third, Plan review findings group, covers how findings
+sit under the review that posted them.
+
+## Problem
+
+`SqlExcerpt` in
+`frontend/src/routes/project/plan-detail/components/threads/StatementAnchorContext.tsx` renders the
+recorded lines of the sheet revision a thread was made on.
+
+- **Every commented line is tinted.** A line inside the anchored range gets `bg-accent/12`. The
+  Changes section tints by severity and Activity is always accent, so the same finding has two
+  colors in two places. [Plan comment card](plan-comment-card.md) removes the tints in the Changes
+  section; this doc removes the last one.
+- **The tint is the only range marker.** The excerpt starts two lines above the range
+  (`CONTEXT_LINES_BEFORE`), so without the tint nothing separates context from the commented lines.
+- **The comment runs on from the SQL.** Each excerpt row is padded `px-3`, and the comment below is
+  padded `px-2 sm:px-3`, so the line numbers and the author's avatar start on the same edge.
+  Both are on the same white.
+- **An outdated excerpt is faded.** When the thread's lines have changed or cannot be placed, the
+  excerpt renders at `opacity-60`. That takes the syntax colors under the 4.5:1 contrast minimum:
+  a quoted identifier falls to about 3.4:1 against the background.
+
+## Principle
+
+> The SQL in a comment card is a quotation. Set it on the statement's gray, mark what the comment
+> is about with a rule in the margin, the way a quotation is marked, and keep the quotation
+> visibly apart from the comment.
+
+## Decisions
+
+**D1 · Two lines of context stay, in normal colors.** The excerpt keeps `CONTEXT_LINES_BEFORE = 2`
+and the context lines keep their syntax colors. Rejected: showing only the commented lines. A range
+that starts mid-statement, such as an `ADD COLUMN` line, is hard to read without the `ALTER TABLE`
+above it. Rejected: gray context lines with no other marker. The reader has to compare text colors
+to find the range, and a context of one short line barely differs.
+
+**D2 · A bar beside the line numbers marks the range.** Rows inside the range carry a 3px bar in
+`control`, 8px left of the line numbers. No line is tinted: every row has the excerpt's one
+ground, from D5. The title bar of the card names the same lines in words. VS Code marks commented
+lines the same way, with a bar in the margin. Rejected: darker, bolder line numbers for the range and no bar. It is the quietest option
+and the easiest to miss.
+
+**D3 · The SQL is inset from the comment.** The excerpt's left padding becomes the start of the
+comment's text column once [Plan comment card](plan-comment-card.md) D7 gives the avatar its own
+column: the comment's own left padding, a 20px avatar and an 8px gap. The comment is padded
+`px-2 sm:px-3`, so the inset is 36px below the `sm` breakpoint and 40px from it up
+(`pl-9 sm:pl-10`), where today it is 12px at every width. The line numbers then line up with the
+comment's text and the avatar column stays clear. Only the SQL moves. The comment below it, its
+replies and the reply footer stay where [Plan comment card](plan-comment-card.md) puts them.
+GitHub's conversation view does the same thing: the comment starts at the box's left edge and the
+code sits behind a number gutter about 64px wide. Rejected: a bordered comment
+box that starts at the code column. Inside a review's group it would be a third frame, which
+the Plan review findings group doc rules out. Rejected: indenting the
+comment instead of the SQL. The comment loses width and still sits in the code's column.
+
+**D4 · An outdated or unavailable excerpt is gray, not faded.** `opacity-60` goes. The lines render
+in `text-control` without syntax colors, which is 7:1 on the excerpt's ground. The lighter
+`text-control-light` is 4.4:1 there, under the minimum. The missing syntax colors are what say
+the lines are no longer current. The bar from D2 still marks the range.
+
+**D5 · The excerpt sits on gray.** Its ground is `bg-control-bg`, and the card around it is
+white. This is the rule of [Plan comment card](plan-comment-card.md) that SQL is on gray and the
+card is white, applied inside the card. The statement in the Changes section takes the lighter
+`bg-control-bg/50`. The excerpt is a small band inside a white card on a white page, and the
+lighter gray barely shows there. The ground and the inset from D3 work together: the ground
+says which rows are SQL, and the inset lines the numbers up with the comment's text. Rejected:
+a white excerpt set apart by the inset alone. The SQL and the comment are still one sheet.
+Rejected: `bg-control-bg/50`, for the reason above.
+
+## States
+
+The excerpt follows the anchor state `StatementAnchorContext` already computes. When it renders
+does not change: it renders once the recorded sheet has loaded, with whatever lines of the range
+the sheet's preview holds. This doc changes only how it is drawn.
+
+| Anchor state | Excerpt |
+| --- | --- |
+| `CURRENT` | Context and range in syntax colors, bar on the range |
+| `OUTDATED` | The recorded lines in gray, bar on the range |
+| `UNAVAILABLE`, the recorded sheet loaded | The recorded lines in gray, bar on the range |
+| `UNAVAILABLE`, a large sheet's preview ends inside the range | The lines the preview holds, in gray, as today |
+| `UNAVAILABLE`, the recorded sheet did not load | No excerpt |
+| `PENDING` | No excerpt until the sheet loads; it loads when the card nears the viewport, as today |
+| Range starts on line 1 or 2 | Fewer than two context lines, as today |
+
+## Scope
+
+Frontend only. One PR. It depends on the comment column slice of
+[Plan comment card](plan-comment-card.md), the one that builds D7 there. That slice sets the
+comment's text column, which D3 here lines up with. The slice is named by what it builds because
+its number can change while that doc is in review.
+
+1. **Excerpt (D1 to D5).**
+   - Files: `StatementAnchorContext.tsx` (`SqlExcerpt`): drop `bg-accent/12` and `opacity-60`, add
+     the `bg-control-bg` ground, the bar and the `pl-9 sm:pl-10` inset, and render a dimmed
+     excerpt as plain text in `text-control` instead of the colorized HTML. The condition that
+     mounts `SqlExcerpt` does not change.
+   - Tests: `StatementAnchorContext.test.tsx`: the excerpt carries the ground and no row has a
+     background of its own; rows inside the range carry the marker and rows outside do not; a
+     dimmed excerpt uses `text-control`, no opacity and no colorized HTML; rows carry the inset
+     class pair.
+
+## Not in this PR
+
+- Starting the context at the first line of the statement the range belongs to, instead of a fixed
+  two lines above it.
+- Showing how the statement differs now from the revision an outdated comment was made on.
+- Limiting the height of a very long range.
+- The color of the excerpt's line numbers.
+- Hiding the excerpt when a large sheet's preview ends inside the commented range. Today it shows
+  the lines the preview holds, and this doc leaves when the excerpt renders as it is.

title: docs(design): plan comment card
body:
Design doc only. No code changes. This is the first of three design PRs for the plan comment card:

1. **This PR**: the comment card.
2. #21969: the SQL excerpt in an Activity card. Stacked on this PR.
3. #21970: findings grouped under their review. Stacked on this PR.

A comment on a plan's SQL is auxiliary information about the statement. The statement is what gets reviewed, approved and run, and a comment helps someone judge it. Today the page marks a comment with its strongest signals: tinted lines, dense folded rows, and a box as wide as the statement. It also draws the thread differently in the Changes section and in Activity.

## What the doc decides

**[Plan comment card](https://github.com/bytebase/bytebase/blob/worktree-byt-10500-comment-card-design/docs/design/plan-comment-card.md).** A comment thread is one white card in both places, set on a gray statement, with no color on the SQL, a title bar that names its lines and says how urgent the thread is, and the same folded form everywhere.

- D1: no color on commented lines. The four line tints go. The highlight while selecting lines for a new comment stays and turns neutral gray.
- D2: the frame has a width limit (`max-w-3xl`), 8px corners (`rounded-lg`), a darker border (`border-control-border`) and no shadow. Both differ from the UX guideline, which asks for `rounded-sm` on framed surfaces and keeps `border-control-border` for controls. The slice that sets the frame writes one exception for the comment card into the guideline, and for the corner into its scanner (`check-ui-guideline.mjs`) and the scanner's tests.
- D3: a title bar names the lines, "Comment on lines 1–7". In Activity it names the change and the lines.
- D4: a folded thread is its title bar. The bar carries the badge of a P0 or P1 finding, and the badge of a production environment the finding applies to: that environment's own name, in gray text on a light tint of its color, with no border. The two existing folded rows are deleted.
- D5: any thread can be folded, not only a resolved one, and a click on its title bar folds it. In Activity the lines and the link at the right end of the bar do not fold. Who owns the fold state does not change.
- D6: "Resolved" and "Statement unavailable" are gray text labels in the bar. "Outdated" is the same label in the warning color.
- D7: comment text sits in its own column, and replies are indented and joined by a line.
- D8: the new-comment composer is the same card.
- D9: the "Applies to" row is unchanged.
- D10: a thread that is not on lines has a bar too, titled "Comment on the plan".
- D11: the statement is on gray and the card is white, from its bar to its footer.

The doc's section "The card" is the reference for building it. It names the card's four parts, gives each part's content as a rule over facts the code already has, and states eight invariants that hold for every card. The build plan says which rows and invariants each PR delivers.

title: feat(review): list, search and copy every reviewer of an approval step
body: Design doc and implementation: the approval step reviewer list. **Every holder of a step's role is reachable from that step's reviewer list: the list opens on click, holds every holder, searches them by name or email, and lets you copy any reviewer's email.** A customer asked for this: their approval role is bound to a group with many members, and the list under the step stopped at 50 with "and N more", with no way to see the rest or search them. The full list was already loaded in the browser (`useApprovalCandidates`), so the 50-row cap was only a rendering limit. ## What the doc decides - **D1 · A popover that opens on click.** The trigger stops opening on hover, because a hover popover closes when the pointer leaves and can't hold a search box. It gets a focus ring and a pointer cursor. A dialog was rejected because its scrim hides the plan; a sheet because the UX contract gives sheets to creating or editing. - **D2 · The full list, with no cap and no "load more".** Every candidate is already in the browser, so "load more" would only hold rows back. --- docs/design/approval-reviewer-list.md (+139/-0)
@@ -0,0 +1,139 @@
+# Approval step reviewer list
+
+Status: proposal · 2026-11-10
+
+Each current or pending step in a plan's approval flow shows an avatar stack and "N reviewers".
+Hovering it lists the people who hold the step's role, but only the first 50, followed by "and N
+more". A role bound to a large group can have more than a thousand holders, so the person a plan's
+creator is looking for is often among the hidden ones, and the list has no search.
+**Every holder of a step's role is reachable from that step's reviewer list: the list opens on
+click, holds every holder, searches them by name or email, and lets you copy any reviewer's email.**
+
+## Problem
+
+A customer (2026-11-05) asked for two things: show all available reviewers, including those past
+the first 50, and let users search the full list by name. The current list
+(`NodeReviewers` in `frontend/src/routes/project/plan-detail/components/review/ReviewApprovalFlow.tsx`)
+cannot do either:
+
+- It renders `candidates.slice(0, 50)` and summarizes the rest as "and N more". Nothing reveals them.
+- It opens on hover (`openOnHover`), and a hover popover closes when the pointer leaves, so it
+  cannot hold a search box. Its `div` trigger already takes focus and opens on click, Enter or
+  Space, but it shows no focus ring and a default cursor, so neither path is visible. The UX
+  contract requires a visible keyboard focus state on interactive elements
+  (`docs/agents/frontend-ux.md`, Borders, Corners, Focus, And Layers).
+- The "+N" overflow avatar is a fixed `size-5` circle, so a count such as "+1200" spills out of it.
+
+The data is not the limit. `useApprovalCandidates` (`frontend/src/routes/project/useApprovalCandidates.ts`)
+already loads every active holder of the role into the browser, expanding groups, and sorts them:
+the current user first, then people before service accounts and workload identities, then by title.
+The 50-row cap is only a rendering limit.
+
+The list renders in three places, all through `ReviewApprovalFlow`:
+
+| Place | Renders |
+| --- | --- |
+| Review section of the plan page | `PlanReviewSection.tsx` → `ReviewApprovalFlow` |
+| Bypass confirmation sheet | `bypassDeploy.tsx` → `ReviewApprovalFlow` |
+| Header Plan status popover | `PlanStatusAction.tsx` → `ReviewApprovalFlow compact` → `CompactVerticalFlow` → `FlowNode` |
+
+## Principle
+
+> Make the safe path the easy path. If finding an approver is hard, people go around the approval
+> flow and chase someone in chat instead. The reviewer list answers "who can approve this?" for
+> every holder of the role, not the first 50.
+
+## Decisions
+
+**D1 · A popover that opens on click.** The trigger (avatar stack plus "N reviewers") stops
+opening on hover. It opens the shared `Popover` on click, Enter or Space, as it already can, and
+shows a focus ring and a pointer cursor. Focus moves into the popover, Escape closes it and returns
+focus to the trigger, and a click outside closes it. Rejected: keeping hover, which closes when the
+pointer leaves and so cannot hold a search box. Rejected: a `Dialog`, whose scrim hides the plan
+while the user only looks someone up. Rejected: a `Sheet`, which the contract's surface table
+gives to creating or editing a resource.
+
+**D2 · The full list, with no cap and no "load more".** The popover lists every candidate in one
+scrolling list and drops "and N more". Only the rows in view are mounted (virtualized, with
+`@tanstack/react-virtual`, already a frontend dependency), so a role with thousands of holders
+costs no more to open than one with fifty. Rejected: "load more" in pages of 50. The contract's
+load-more pattern is for results paged from the server (frontend-ux.md, With Pagination Or Load
+More), and every candidate is already in the browser, so a load-more button would only hold back
+rows the page already has.
+
+**D3 · Search by name or email, in the browser.** Above the list, a `SearchInput` filters
+candidates by a case-insensitive substring match on the title or the email. It searches every
+candidate, including service accounts and workload identities, and keeps the list's order. The
+contract allows filtering in the browser when the full bounded set is loaded and the user is not
+misled about server-wide search (frontend-ux.md, Without Pagination); the list is the step's
+complete set. The search box appears only when the step has more than 10 candidates. When nothing
+matches, the list says so and offers a button that clears the search.
+
+**D4 · A copy button on every row.** Each row ends with the shared `CopyButton`, which copies the
+row's email and confirms with the shared "Copied" toast, or "Copy failed". The button is always
+visible, so it works on touch screens and needs no hover to discover. Its accessible name names
+the row ("Copy email for Ana Patel"), since a list of identical "Copy" buttons is ambiguous to a
+screen reader; `CopyButton` gains an optional label for this. Every row gets one, including
+service accounts and workload identities, so the rule has no exceptions. Rejected: showing the
+button only on hover or focus, which hides it on touch screens. Rejected: copying when the email
+text is clicked, which nobody would discover and which fights text selection.
+
+**D5 · One reviewer list in all three places.** The Review section, the bypass sheet and the
+header Plan status popover render the same trigger and popover. In the header, the reviewer list
+is a popover inside a popover: opening it or clicking inside it must not close the Plan status
+popover, and Escape closes the reviewer list first. Rejected: making the count in the header plain
+text, which would remove a list the header shows today.
+
+**D6 · The overflow count grows to fit.** The "+N" count keeps its 20px height and widens when
+the count needs more room, so "+1200" stays inside it. Once it can widen it is a text label, which
+the UX contract gives `rounded-xs` corners; `rounded-full` stays with the avatars.
+
+What does not change: the avatar stack shows the first three candidates; the order is the one
+`useApprovalCandidates` produces; the last plan editor stays in the list with its "Can't approve"
+line, and the warning under the step stays; a step with no holders still reads "No reviewers" and
+has nothing to open.
+
+## States
+
+| Step's candidates | Trigger | Popover |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Project policy still loading | Nothing rendered | None |
+| No holders | "No reviewers", not a button | None |
+| 1 to 10 | Avatar stack and "N reviewers" | Every candidate, each with a copy button; no search box |
+| More than 10 | Avatar stack and "N reviewers" | Search box, then every candidate, each with a copy button |
+| Search with matches | Unchanged | Matching candidates in the same order |
+| Search with no match | Unchanged | "No reviewers match" with a button that clears the search |
+| Copy clicked | Unchanged | Shared "Copied" toast, or "Copy failed" when the browser refuses |
+
+## Scope
+
+One PR. It holds this doc and the frontend change, and needs no backend change.
+
+1. **Reviewer list (D1–D6).**
+   - Files: `ReviewApprovalFlow.tsx` (`NodeReviewers`: the trigger and the "+N" count); a new
+     `ReviewerList.tsx` beside it for the popover body (search, list, rows);
+     `frontend/src/components/ui/copy-button.tsx` (optional accessible label); the five locale files
+     for the search placeholder, the empty-search message and the copy label, with the unused
+     `and-n-more` keys removed.
+   - Unit tests. `ReviewApprovalFlow.test.tsx`: the popover does not open on hover, opens on
+     click, stays open when the pointer leaves, and lists every reviewer; the "+N" count shows
+     every candidate past the third and widens to fit. `ReviewerList.test.tsx`: a holder past the
+     50th is found by name or email; search keeps the order; no search box at 10 or fewer; the
+     empty-search state clears; each row's copy button names its person and copies its email.
+     `copy-button.test.tsx`: the label becomes the accessible name.
+   - E2E: `frontend/tests/e2e/plan-detail/plan-detail-review.spec.ts` opens the reviewer list by
+     clicking instead of hovering ("the step lists the service account as its reviewer"), and a new
+     case opens the list from the header Plan status popover and closes it with Escape while the
+     header popover stays open.
+
+## Not in this PR
+
+- Notifying a reviewer from the list. Bytebase already sends "Approval required" to the project's
+  webhooks when a step starts, mentioning the people who can approve it, and direct-messages them
+  where the webhook has direct messages on (`NotifyApprovalRequested` in
+  `backend/component/review/evaluator.go`). A per-reviewer reminder needs a backend endpoint
+  first: one that resends through that channel to one person, limits how often, reports delivery
+  and writes the audit log.
+- Choosing a specific reviewer for a plan. Approval is by role; any holder can approve.
+- Grouping the list by the group that grants the role.
+- The folded "N pending" chip's popover, which shows avatars and a count, not a list.

title: refactor(plsql): merge query-span extractors and clean up the last omni-marked helpers
body:
Two related finishing steps of the omni naming cleanup.

**1. plsql query-span extractor merge.** The Oracle (PL/SQL) query span had a base `querySpanExtractor` plus an `omniQuerySpanExtractor` that embedded it — vestigial dual-era scaffolding now that omni is the sole path. Fold the wrapper's `source`/`topLevelTableSourcesFrom` fields into the base, re-point every method receiver at `querySpanExtractor`, drop the wrapper type and `newOmniQuerySpanExtractor` (callers use `newQuerySpanExtractor`), and simplify `clone()`.

**2. Rename the last omni-marked local helpers across engines.** These are the identifiers whose plain unmarked name collides with an existing local symbol, so the earlier mechanical passes left them:

- local parse vars: `omniErr` → `err`, `omniStmts` → `stmts`/`parsed`, `omniStmt` → `parsedStmt`, `omniSummary` → `rawSummary`
- elasticsearch: `omniSpan` → `rawSpan`, `omniCurrent` → `srcNode`, `omniRanges` → `rawRanges`; googlesql/trino `omniSpan` → `rawSpan`
- helpers: `isExplainAnalyzeOmni` → `isExplainAnalyzeStmt` (pg), `omniTableName` → `rangeVarTableName` (advisor/pg), `omniColumnName` → `alterCmdColumnName` (mysql-family advisors), `omniJoinType` → `toJoinType` (mysql-family parsers)

Pure renames / behavior-preserving struct merge; the query-span, advisor and schema test suites pass unchanged. The omni-package import aliases are untouched. With this and the sibling extractor-merge PRs (#21964, #21965), no engine carries a vestigial omni marker.
