title: chore(deps): drop the retired pingcap/tidb go.mod and renovate entries
body:
## What

Bytebase's TiDB parsing migrated off `github.com/pingcap/tidb` to `github.com/bytebase/omni` (#21949), dropping the main `pingcap/tidb` module from the build graph. This removes the now-dead references:

- **`go.mod`**: removed the `github.com/pingcap/tidb => github.com/bytebase/tidb` replace directive. `go list -m github.com/pingcap/tidb` now reports "not a known dependency", confirming the module is gone.
- **`renovate.json`**: removed the `"github.com/pingcap/tidb"` entry from `ignoreDeps`.

## Deliberately kept

`github.com/pingcap/tidb/pkg/parser` (its require line, its `replace` to the bytebase fork, and its `ignoreDeps` entry) is **still a live indirect dependency** — its `charset`/`format`/`mysql`/`terror` subpackages are pulled in transitively via `go-mysql-org/go-mysql` through the gh-ost component. `go mod why` on the *root* `pkg/parser` package reports it as unneeded, but the subpackages are in the build graph, so the module stays, pinned to the bytebase fork. `pingcap/errors` and `pingcap/log` likewise remain (via go-mysql / `pkg/parser/charset`).

## Verification

- `go build ./...` — green
- `go mod verify` — all modules verified
- `go.sum` unchanged (transitive hashes for the still-needed fork retained)

title: refactor(tidb): delete the pingcap parser bridge, drop pingcap/tidb dep
body:
## Summary

Completes the TiDB → omni migration. Every TiDB AST consumer is now on omni, so the native **pingcap parser bridge is dead code** — this removes it and, with no importer left, drops `github.com/pingcap/tidb` from the module's direct dependencies.

### What's deleted
- **`parser/tidb`**: `ast.go` (`AST`, `GetTiDBAST`, `PingCapASTProvider`); the pingcap functions in `tidb.go` (`ParseTiDB`, `ParseTiDBForSyntaxCheck`, `applyTiDBLineTracking`, `newTiDBParser`, `convertParserError`, `SetLineForMySQLCreateTableStmt`, the dead `TypeString`); and `OmniAST.AsPingCapAST` with its cached pingcap parse. `tidb.go` is now just the parser registration.
- **`parser/tidb/diagnose.go`**: migrated from `ParseTiDB` to the omni path (`parseTiDBStatements`), which already yields a `base.SyntaxError`.
- **`advisor/tidb/utils.go`**: dropped the dead `case *tidbparser.AST` fallback arm in `getTiDBOmniNodes` (omni is the sole parser; nothing reaches it).
- **`tokenizer`**: `SetLineForMySQLCreateTableStmt` and its now-orphaned helpers (`matchMySQLTableConstraint`, `scanTo`) — the only pingcap users there.
- Obsolete bridge tests.

### go.mod
With no remaining importer, `go mod tidy` removes `github.com/pingcap/tidb` from the direct requires. `pkg/parser` stays as an `// indirect` module-graph entry (no package is imported — `go mod why` confirms), and the fork `replace` directives are kept. The MySQL-family drivers' only `pingcap/tidb` references are comment URLs and a Docker image string, not Go imports.

Net: **11 files, +11 / −1394**.

- `go test ./backend/plugin/parser/tidb/ ./backend/plugin/parser/tokenizer/ ./backend/plugin/advisor/tidb/ ./backend/plugin/schema/tidb/ ./backend/plugin/db/tidb/`

title: refactor(tidb): migrate schema walk-through to the omni catalog
body:
## Summary

Rewrites the schema/tidb walk-through as a `catalog.Exec` simulation over the omni TiDB catalog, mirroring the MySQL walk-through:

1. Load the existing schema into the catalog.
2. Run the DDL.
3. Map the first catalog error to an `*storepb.Advice` (via `mapTiDBErrorToCode` / `tidbCatalogErrorAdviceContent`).
4. Convert the updated catalog back to metadata, reusing `tidbCatalogToProto`.

This drops the **last `pingcap/tidb` import** from `backend/plugin/schema/tidb` (production and the `generate_migration` test's parse check, now via `ParseTiDBOmni`), and shrinks `walk_through.go` from a ~1400-line hand-written state machine to the shared catalog flow.

Bumps the omni pin to pick up the TiDB catalog DDL validations (bytebase/omni#806).

## Fixtures

Reconciled to the catalog's TiDB-faithful behavior. Cases that leaned on the old pingcap walk-through accepting DDL real TiDB v8.5 rejects now assert the rejection:

- an unsupported collation (`utf8mb4_polish_ci` — outside TiDB's new-collation set; switched valid cases to `utf8mb4_unicode_ci` to keep their coverage),
- a standalone `CREATE FULLTEXT INDEX`,
- dropping a column covered by a composite index.

Error advice contents were also normalized to the MySQL walk-through's phrasing.

## Note

`pingcap/tidb` stays in `go.mod`: the MySQL-family drivers (`db/mysql`, `db/tidb`, `db/oceanbase`, `db/doris`, `db/starrocks` sync) and the testcontainer helper still use `pingcap/tidb/pkg/parser/mysql` constants, and the parser/tidb pingcap bridge still has a defensive consumer. Those are separate follow-ups.

## Test plan

- `go test ./backend/plugin/schema/tidb/` (walk-through + generate-migration + metadata)
- `go test ./backend/plugin/parser/tidb/ ./backend/plugin/advisor/tidb/ ./backend/plugin/schema/mysql/ ./backend/plugin/parser/mysql/` (omni pin bump)
- full server build; `golangci-lint` clean on the package

title: refactor(tidb): parse schema metadata with the omni catalog
body:
## What

Migrates `backend/plugin/schema/tidb/get_database_metadata.go` (`RegisterGetDatabaseMetadata`) off the hand-written pingcap-AST extractor onto the omni TiDB catalog — the same catalog-Exec model `schema/mysql` uses. Simulate the DDL in a scratch database (`catalog.New` + `Exec`) and read the catalog back into `DatabaseSchemaMetadata` via `tidbCatalogToProto`. This removes pingcap from `get_database_metadata.go` (follows the merged #21945, which bumped the omni pin to `d769ab6a` and made `advisor/tidb` pingcap-free).

The omni catalog records what the native TiDB sync records but the old extractor dropped — verified against `db/tidb/sync.go`'s `setColumnMetadataDefault`:
- per-column **character set and collation** (sync reads these from `information_schema`),
- **string and boolean column defaults** (`DEFAULT 'pending'`, `DEFAULT false`→`'0'`),

so the parsed metadata is now better aligned with live sync (fewer schema-diff false positives), not less.

### View definitions
omni qualifies a view body's same-database references with the current database, exactly as live TiDB's `information_schema.VIEWS` does (verified against TiDB v8.5.5 — same-db refs are qualified with the real db name). Because `GetDatabaseMetadata` simulates in a throwaway database, `tidbViewDefinition` strips that scratch-database qualifier so the stored definition stays database-agnostic, matching the MySQL schema package's unqualified view bodies (zero `tmp` refs in the re-recorded fixtures).

## Verification

- `go build ./backend/...` — OK
- `go test ./backend/plugin/schema/tidb/` — all pass (`TestGetDatabaseMetadata` + `TestGenerateMigration` golden fixtures re-recorded for the richer, sync-aligned output; `TestWalkThrough` unchanged).
- Golden-diff review: column `type` values unchanged (only charset/collation added alongside), all default changes additive, no `tmp` leak.

## Scope note

`walk_through.go` is the last pingcap importer in `schema/tidb`. It's a larger catalog-Exec rewrite (prechecks + an omni-catalog-error → advice-code mapping) whose test asserts exact advice codes/content and resulting metadata with no record mode, so it needs careful manual fixture work for a safety feature — tracked as a focused follow-up. The error sentinels port cleanly (omni/tidb/catalog exposes the same `catalog.Error` set mysql maps), so it's de-risked, just substantial.

title: refactor(tidb): bump omni pin; migrate prior-backup DDL detection off pingcap
body:
## What

Bumps the omni pin and migrates the `advisor/tidb` prior-backup DDL detection off pingcap, making `advisor/tidb` pingcap-free.

- **omni pin → `d769ab6a`** — brings `ast.IsDDL`, the CURRENT_TIMESTAMP default spelling fix, and the TiDB catalog-parity work. Full `go build ./backend/...` + `go mod tidy` clean; `schema/mysql` (the other omni-catalog consumer) and `parser/tidb` stay green.
- **`advisor_builtin_prior_backup_check`** — the mixed-DDL-and-DML gate now classifies statements with omni's `ast.IsDDL`, over the omni statements it already fetches for DML-mixing detection, instead of pingcap's `DDLNode` interface. `ast.IsDDL` matches pingcap's `DDLNode` set exactly, including the forms omni reshapes: `DROP VIEW` (its own `DropViewStmt` vs pingcap's `DropTableStmt{IsView}`) and `ADMIN REPAIR`/`ADMIN CLEANUP` (`AdminStmt` kinds vs pingcap's `RepairTableStmt`/`CleanupTableLockStmt`).
- Deletes `getTiDBNodes` (its only consumer) and the pingcap imports from `advisor/tidb`, plus the stale dual-path comments and the obsolete bridge-miss test.

## Verification

- `go build ./backend/...` — OK
- `go test ./backend/plugin/advisor/tidb/` — all pass, including the `CREATE SEQUENCE + UPDATE` mixed-DDL case (omni now parses the sequence/flashback grammar that previously forced the pingcap path).
- `grep -rl github.com/pingcap/tidb backend/plugin/advisor/tidb` → none.

## Scope note

The plan was to also migrate `schema/tidb` in this PR, but the `get_database_metadata` rewrite hit an omni-side blocker: `omni/tidb/catalog`'s `View.Definition` re-deparses view bodies and qualifies table refs with the scratch database name (`SELECT ... FROM \`tmp\`.\`p\``), unlike `omni/mysql/catalog` which keeps the raw unqualified text. That would leak `tmp` into view metadata and generated DDL. The column/index/FK/default/charset work is done and sync-aligned; the schema migration resumes once the omni view-definition behavior is settled. (`schema/tidb` stays on pingcap in this PR.)

title: fix(review): collapse an inline thread resolved in the SQL editor (BYT-10496)
body:
Fixes [BYT-10496](https://linear.app/bytebase/issue/BYT-10496).

## Problem

Resolving an inline thread in the plan's SQL editor marked it Resolved but left the full card open. The Activity timeline already collapses resolved threads. The editor did not, because `StatementThreadsLayer` owns expansion through `expandedRoots`, and resolving never removed the thread from that set.

## Fix

`ThreadStack` passes `onThreadStateChanged` to the card. The card fires it only after its own successful resolve or reopen, never on a refresh. A resolve collapses the thread to its summary row, the same path as the card's close button.

- Resolve, from the button or from a reply with "Resolve thread" checked: the thread collapses to its row with the Resolved badge.
- Clicking the row expands it. Reopen keeps it expanded.
- A failed resolve keeps the card open.
- A resolve by someone else (a refresh) leaves the card open, so the editor does not shift under the reader.

## Evidence

Plan detail SQL editor: Resolve → collapses to the row → click the row → expanded → Reopen.

![Resolve collapses the thread](./byt-10496-resolve-collapses-thread.gif)

## Tests

- `ThreadStack.test.tsx`: resolving from the card collapses the thread; reopening does not. The test fails without the fix.
- `pnpm --dir frontend fix` and `pnpm --dir frontend test` pass.

![byt-10496-resolve-collapses-thread](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e28a9acf-7cf3-4cba-b84a-19a7559bcb84)

title: feat(workload-identity): redesign the creation flow as a four-step dialog (BYT-10429)
body:
### Why

A workload identity lets a CI job sign in to Bytebase with the job's OIDC token instead of a stored secret. Today it is created in one sheet with up to eleven fields:

- The account's name and email come first, before the user has said what will sign in.
- The provider is a dropdown, and the issuer and subject pattern are hidden under "Advanced". The subject pattern decides which jobs can sign in, yet nothing explains it.
- Editing Owner, Repository or Branch rebuilds the pattern from scratch. That silently widens a hand-written pattern such as `repo:acme-corp/deploy:environment:prod` to `repo:acme-corp/deploy:*`.
- There is no way to set GitHub's owner ID. Without it, a rule trusts the owner name alone, and anyone who registers a freed name can sign in. The server already accepts `repo:OWNER@ID/...` since #21931.
- The role is optional, so an identity can be saved that signs in and can do nothing.
- After Create the sheet closes with a toast. The email the workflow needs is not shown, and there is no way to check that the identity works.

### What changes

The sheet is replaced by a four-step dialog that asks one question per step. The layout follows the Claude Platform's "Connect workload" wizard: a left rail, one question per step, and choice cards.

| Step | Question | What the user does |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Token source | Where do your CI jobs get their token? | Picks GitHub Actions, GitLab CI or Other OIDC. Issuer URL and Audiences are prefilled and read-only, with Edit. |
| 2. Repositories | Which repositories can sign in? | Types Owner, Repository (optional) and, for GitHub, Owner ID (optional). The subject pattern is built from them and shown read-only, with Edit. |
| 3. Account | Who is it in Bytebase? | Email is prefilled as `<repo>-ci`. Display name is optional. Role defaults to GitOps Service Agent, read-only with Edit. |
| 4. Done | | Copies the email, and optionally copies a test workflow that checks the identity can sign in. |

Before and after:

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Order | Name and email first, then the provider | Token source, then repositories, then the account |
| Provider | Dropdown | Three choice cards |
| Subject pattern | Hidden under Advanced; rebuilt on every field edit | Always visible, read-only until Edit; a field edit replaces only its own part and never widens the pattern |
| GitHub owner ID | Not available | Optional field, with a box that explains the name-reuse risk |
| Role | Optional; an identity could be saved with no permission | Required in the UI, defaults to GitOps Service Agent |
| After Create | Toast, sheet closes | Done step with the email, Copy, and a test workflow |
| Edit | Same sheet; closes with a toast after save | The same four steps with a one-line "Editing ..." banner; Update on step 3 saves and shows step 4 with the test file |
| Height | Changes with content | Fixed (680px, or the window height minus 64px); only the step body scrolls |

title: refactor(tidb): migrate the SQL-editor query validator off pingcap to omni
body:
## What

Migrates `validateQuery` (the SQL-editor read-only gate, `RegisterQueryValidator`) in `backend/plugin/parser/tidb/query.go` off the native pingcap parser onto omni — removing query.go's last pingcap import.

- Parses with `base.ParseStatements` and classifies on `omni/tidb/ast` nodes. omni folds set operations into `SelectStmt`, so one case covers `SELECT` and `UNION`/`INTERSECT`/`EXCEPT`.
- `hasSelectInto` walks the omni tree with `ast.Inspect` checking `SelectStmt.Into`, so an `INTO OUTFILE` export on any set-operation arm, subquery, or CTE is still refused (the export gate). `explainReads` keeps the plain-`EXPLAIN` vs `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` read distinction.
- Removed the native pingcap `selectIntoVisitor`/`Accept` walk.

## Verification

- `go build ./backend/...` — OK; `go vet` clean.
- `go test ./backend/plugin/parser/tidb/` — passes, including the full `TestValidateSQLForEditor`, `TestValidateQueryExplainAnalyze`, and `TestValidateQueryExportGate` (all 16 export-gate shapes: exports on first/second/third arms, braced arms, nested set-ops, through CTEs and subqueries, under plain EXPLAIN and EXPLAIN ANALYZE).

### Behavior note
omni accepts `WITH ... INSERT ... VALUES`, which TiDB v8.5.5 rejects at parse (a CTE may precede `INSERT ... SELECT`, not `INSERT ... VALUES`). The validator still **refuses** it — classified as a non-read INSERT rather than surfacing a parse error — so the editor blocks it either way. The test is updated to assert the refusal. Tightening omni to reject that form is a separate omni change.

Part of the TiDB pingcap→omni migration. After this, the only remaining `parser/tidb` pingcap importers are the `AsPingCapAST` bridge (`ast.go`, `tidb.go`), kept for `advisor/tidb`'s intentionally-deferred DDL-detection path and `schema/tidb` (blocked on omni catalog parity). `github.com/pingcap/tidb` stays in `go.mod` until those land.

title: refactor(tidb): migrate changed-resource extraction off pingcap to omni
body:
## What

Migrates `backend/plugin/parser/tidb/resource_change.go` (changed-resource extraction, `RegisterExtractChangedResourcesFunc`) fully onto `github.com/bytebase/omni/tidb/ast`. It previously parsed each statement with the native pingcap AST via the `AsPingCapAST` bridge, using omni only as a fallback for statements pingcap rejected.

- `extractChangedResources` now reads the omni AST directly (`GetOmniNode`) and feeds a single `getResourceChanges` that handles the DDL cases (CREATE/DROP/ALTER/TRUNCATE/RENAME table, CREATE/DROP index, LOAD DATA, IMPORT INTO, and the view/sequence database-only targets) alongside DML table recording, descending omni's `[]TableExpr` FROM through joins.
- omni reshapes a few nodes handled here: DROP VIEW is its own `DropViewStmt` (not pingcap's `DropTableStmt.IsView`); `TruncateStmt`/`RenameTableStmt` carry lists; a multi-table `DELETE`'s sources are `Tables` + `Using`.
- The DML counting/sampling path (`countOmniDML`, `addBatchSampleDML`) was already on omni and is unchanged; the dead pingcap walkers (`getResourceChanges`, `extractResultSetNode`/`extractJoin`/`extractTableSource`/`extractTableName`/`extractTableRefs`, the pingcap `addTiDBObjectDatabase`) are removed.

## Verification

- `go build ./backend/...` — OK
- `go test ./backend/plugin/parser/tidb/ -run TestExtractChangedResources` — all pass unchanged (DDL, truncate, load/import, view/sequence database-only targets, and the DML count/sample matrix).
- `go vet` clean.

Part of the TiDB pingcap→omni migration (plan: `docs/plans/2026-11-10-tidb-pingcap-omni-migration.md`). Independent of the stats/statement-type/limit PR (#21937) and the query-span PR (#21939). `github.com/pingcap/tidb` stays in `go.mod`; remaining importers are `statement_type.go`/`limit.go` (#21937), the query-span extractor (#21939), `validateQuery`, the `tidb.go`/`ast.go`/tokenizer bridge, `advisor/tidb`'s deferred DDL path, and `schema/tidb`.

title: refactor(tidb): migrate query-span extraction off pingcap to omni
body:
## What

Migrates the TiDB **query-span extractor** off `github.com/pingcap/tidb/pkg/parser` onto `github.com/bytebase/omni/tidb/ast`, mirroring the mysql/pg/mssql omni query-span extractors. This is the largest piece of the TiDB pingcap→omni migration (plan: `docs/plans/2026-11-10-tidb-pingcap-omni-migration.md`, added in #21937).

- **`query_span_extractor.go`** — dispatches on omni nodes. omni's Postgres-shaped AST folds set operations into `SelectStmt` (`SetOp`/`Left`/`Right`), models FROM as a `[]TableExpr` of `TableRef`/`JoinClause`/`SubqueryExpr`, and drops the `TableSource` wrapper (aliases live on `TableRef`/`SubqueryExpr`). Access-table collection moves from a pingcap `Accept` visitor to an omni `Walk` visitor with the same CTE-scope and locking-table handling. Recursive CTEs use omni's `UnwrapParenSource` anchor walk.
- **`query_type.go`** — classifies omni statement nodes; omni has no `DMLNode`/`DDLNode` marker interface, so the DDL/DML families are enumerated.
- **`util.go`** — `omniExprLoc` reads each node's source range (omni's `Loc` field is not method-promoted) so an unaliased select item keeps its original source text as its name (matching pingcap `Text()`).
- **`query.go`** — drops the now-unused pingcap table-list walkers. `validateQuery` still parses with pingcap — migrating the read-only validator is a follow-up.

## Verification

- `go build ./backend/...` — OK
- `go test ./backend/plugin/parser/tidb/` — pass, with the **query-span fixtures unchanged** (`TestGetQuerySpan`, 25 cases) plus `TestExplainAnalyzeAccessTables` (19 subcases) and the recursive-CTE tests.
- `golangci-lint run` — clean.

### Behavior note
`EXPLAIN` by SQL digest (`EXPLAIN ANALYZE 'digest'`) now surfaces as an omni parse error rather than the pingcap digest-form rejection — the statement is rejected either way. `EXPLAIN FOR CONNECTION` still parses to a stmt-less `ExplainStmt` and keeps its clear "not supported" message. The test is updated to cover both.

`github.com/pingcap/tidb` stays in `go.mod`; remaining TiDB importers (the `validateQuery` validator, `resource_change.go`, `advisor/tidb`'s deferred DDL path, `schema/tidb`) are tracked in the plan doc.

title: refactor(tidb): first self-contained migrations off pingcap to omni
body:
## What

The first self-contained TiDB importers moving off `github.com/pingcap/tidb` onto `github.com/bytebase/omni`, plus the migration plan. Each is a registered entry point or isolated helper with no dependency on the `AsPingCapAST` bridge or on omni catalog parity.

1. **`backend/plugin/db/tidb/stats.go`** — `countDMLTargets`/`countTableSources` (affected-rows estimation) parse with `ParseTiDBOmni` and walk `omni/tidb/ast`. omni's DML shape is clean: `DeleteStmt.Tables` holds the delete targets in every form, `UpdateStmt.SetList` carries assignments with `ColumnRef.Table` qualifiers, and the FROM join is a `[]TableExpr` of `TableRef`/`JoinClause`/`SubqueryExpr`.
2. **`backend/plugin/parser/tidb/statement_type.go`** — `GetStatementTypes` classifies via `GetOmniNode` and switches on omni node types. omni's separate `DropViewStmt` replaces pingcap's `DropTableStmt.IsView` flag.
3. **`backend/plugin/parser/tidb/limit.go`** — the result-limit rewrite parses with omni, sets the LIMIT on the omni `SelectStmt` (omni folds set-ops into `SelectStmt`, collapsing the old two-case switch), and re-serializes with `omni/tidb/deparse.RestoreSelectWith(stmt, RestoreStringWithoutCharset)` — byte-identical to the previous `format.Restore` output, so the golden test is unchanged.
4. **`docs/plans/2026-11-10-tidb-pingcap-omni-migration.md`** — full importer inventory, omni-side gap analysis (**none block the migration**), reshape notes, and the recommended order.

## Verification

- `go build ./backend/plugin/...` — OK
- `go test ./backend/plugin/db/tidb/ ./backend/plugin/parser/tidb/` — pass, including the pure `TestCountDMLTargets` (9 cases), `TestGetAffectedRows*`, `TestGetStatementType`, and `TestGetStatementWithResultLimit` (golden output unchanged).
- `golangci-lint run` on both packages — clean.

`github.com/pingcap/tidb` stays in `go.mod`; it is removed only once every importer is migrated. Remaining (see the plan doc): the `parser/tidb` query-span cluster, `advisor/tidb`'s intentionally-deferred DDL-detection path, and `schema/tidb` (blocked on omni's TiDB catalog reaching parity).

title: refactor(tidb): retire omni/pingcap parser dispatcher
body:
## What

omni is now the sole TiDB parser. The registered TiDB `ParseStatementsFunc` (`parseTiDBStatements` in `omni.go`) parses every statement with omni; a statement omni rejects surfaces as a `base.SyntaxError` instead of falling back to the native pingcap parser.

This retires the omni-first/pingcap-fallback dispatcher. [Phase 1 assessment](https://github.com/bytebase/bytebase) measured omni's TiDB parser against TiDB v8.5.5 across 4 real-SQL corpora (31,601 rows) and found **0 acceptance gaps**, so the per-statement pingcap safety net is no longer earning its keep.

## Changes

- Deleted `dispatcher.go` / `dispatcher_test.go` — the omni-reject → pingcap fallback path.
- Deleted `metrics.go` / `metrics_test.go` — the fallback telemetry (`tidb_dispatcher_omni_fallback_total` counter + its reason classifier), which existed only to drive the now-reached retirement decision.
- Moved the surviving pieces to their natural homes: the omni-only statement parser and `convertOmniParseError` into `omni.go`; `parsePingCapSingleStatement` into `tidb.go` next to its only remaining caller, `ParseTiDBForSyntaxCheck`.

## What is deliberately **unchanged**

- `OmniAST.AsPingCapAST()` and `ParseTiDBForSyntaxCheck` stay. These are a **separate** compatibility shim: they hand un-migrated advisors a pingcap AST for statements omni **accepts**. They are not the dispatcher fallback (which fired on omni **rejection**).
- `go.mod` / `go.sum` are untouched. `github.com/pingcap/tidb` is still imported by `advisor/tidb`, `schema/tidb`, the `db/{tidb,mysql,oceanbase,doris,starrocks}` drivers, and `parser/tokenizer`, so it does not become unused. Only the dispatcher's *use* of it is gone.

## Accepted regression

The pingcap fallback still caught a little TiDB grammar newer than the pinned v8.5.5 that omni rejects but pingcap-master accepts — notably **`TRAFFIC CAPTURE`** and **`COLUMNAR INDEX`** (both `CREATE ... COLUMNAR INDEX` and `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMNAR INDEX`). A clean dispatcher delete stops accepting those; they now surface as parse errors. This tradeoff is accepted for now; closing the omni gaps for that newer grammar is possible follow-up.

Verified against the live omni pin (`804a5b3`): `TRAFFIC CAPTURE` and the two `COLUMNAR INDEX` forms are omni-reject / pingcap-accept, while `FLASHBACK DATABASE`, `CREATE SEQUENCE`, `BATCH ... DELETE` and `IMPORT INTO` are now accepted by omni (they used to rely on the fallback). The new `omni_test.go` cases pin both the happy path and the omni-reject-surfaces-error behavior.

## Verification

- `gofmt -w` on changed files
- `go build ./...`
- `go vet ./backend/plugin/parser/tidb/ ./backend/plugin/advisor/tidb/ ./backend/plugin/schema/tidb/ ./backend/plugin/db/tidb/`
- `go test ./backend/plugin/parser/tidb/ ./backend/plugin/advisor/tidb/ ./backend/plugin/schema/tidb/` — all pass
- `golangci-lint` v2.15.0 (CI pin) — 0 issues

title: fix(ha): clarify server replica license error and clean up heartbeat on shutdown  Fixes #21918
body:
## Problem

When multiple Bytebase server pods connect to the metadata database without an HA license, the error `multiple replicas detected (%d) but HA is not enabled in license` is triggered. Users frequently misinterpret this as Bytebase policing their target database replicas (such as ClickHouse replica nodes) rather than Bytebase server instances. Furthermore, during rolling updates or restarts, terminating pods linger in `replica_heartbeat` for up to 30 seconds before expiring, causing transient license errors on single-replica setups.

## Fix

1. Clarified the error message in `backend/enterprise/license.go` to explicitly state `Bytebase server replicas` sharing the metadata database and instruct the user to scale down to 1 replica or upgrade to HA.
2. Added `DeleteReplicaHeartbeat` to `backend/store/replica_heartbeat.go` and invoke it in `backend/runner/heartbeat/runner.go` on graceful shutdown (`ctx.Done()`).

## Not breaking

Additive and clarifying changes only. No database migrations, API contract changes, or backward-incompatible modifications.

## Tests

- Added `TestCheckReplicaLimit` in `backend/enterprise/license_test.go` covering Community single-replica allowance, multi-replica error check, HA license allowance, and scale-down recovery.
- Verified `go vet ./backend/enterprise/ ./backend/runner/heartbeat/` passes cleanly.
- Verified build succeeds with `$env:GOOS = 'linux'; go build ./backend/bin/server/main.go`.

title: fix(wif): accept ID-based GitHub OIDC subjects
body:
## Problem

GitHub now issues ID-based subjects (`repo:owner@123/name@456:...`) for repositories created, renamed or transferred after 2026-07-15. The name-based patterns the workload identity form writes, such as `repo:owner/name:*`, no longer prefix-match these subjects. The token exchange fails with "subject mismatch".

## Fix

The existing prefix match is unchanged. For `repo:` patterns there is now a second way to pass. The owner, owner ID, repository and repository ID named in the pattern are compared with the token's `repository_owner`, `repository_owner_id`, `repository` and `repository_id` claims. The rest of the pattern is compared with the end of `sub`. A pattern the write path refuses still matches nothing, and the second check never admits another owner or repository.

## Not breaking

The second check only adds matches, so every token accepted today is still accepted. There is no API, storage, migration or frontend change, and the error text is unchanged.

## Tests

- `TestMatchSubject`: 24 cases covering both subject formats, owner and repository IDs, other owners and repositories, refused patterns, and non-GitHub patterns.
- `TestValidateTokenAcceptsIDBasedGitHubSubject`: signed tokens through `ValidateToken`.
- `go test` and `go vet` pass for `./backend/plugin/idp/wif/`.
- `golangci-lint` v2.15.0 (the CI version) reports no issues in the package.

Fixes BYT-10349

title: fix(review): leave the standard rules' conditions out of the AI review
body:
The AI review reported problems the standard rules already post, such as an UPDATE with no WHERE clause, so one problem got two threads. The two runs start together and never see each other's results. Instead of matching results after both finish, the prompt now tells the model which standard rules apply to each database, and what to do with each.

What the model does with a standard rule:

- A rule the standard review evaluates on the database's engine is left to it. The model still reports a statement that avoids the rule's form but keeps its risk, such as `WHERE 1=1`.
- A rule that is off is left alone, along with any statement that avoids its form.
- A rule that is on but not evaluated on the engine is the model's. That covers engines without a standard review, rules an engine's omni package does not implement (Snowflake's WALK_THROUGH), and WALK_THROUGH everywhere: the walk stops at a statement it cannot follow, such as a DO block, and does not say where. A missing object both reviews catch therefore gets two threads.
- A rule covers its condition and the risk it names, nothing more. A dropped column that a view reads is still reported, as a broken view.
- A policy sentence that names a condition, such as "Every UPDATE needs a WHERE clause", brings it back whatever the rule's state, so both reviews may post it. A general aim, such as "Protect production data", does not.
- The AI policy editor says the AI review does not repeat the standard rules and skips the ones that are off.

The changes:

- `standard_rules_prompt.md` explains the three states, each with its reason. `standard_rules.go` lists each rule with one sentence and its state for the review. ONLINE_MIGRATION and PRIOR_BACKUP are left out: they judge the change's options, which the model does not see.
- `base_prompt.md` no longer names the conditions the rules own, and its line about a rule engine checking style, which no v2 rule does, is gone.
- The executor reads the effective rule policy once per run and marks a rule as the standard review's only where the engine's omni package implements it. The per-engine rule list moves from the catalog test into `review_funcs.go`.
- `standard_rules_live_test.go` checks ten cases against a real Claude model, and skips without `AIREVIEW_LIVE_CLAUDE_API_KEY`.

Closes BYT-10370

## Test plan

- `go test ./backend/plugin/aireview/ ./backend/runner/reviewrun/`
- `TestReviewLiveStandardRules` on the final prompt: claude-sonnet-5-5 30/30 and claude-haiku-5-5 20/20. claude-sonnet-5 passes 38/40: it reports a missing table while WALK_THROUGH is off in 2 of 4 runs. `TestReviewLiveClaude` still passes.
- golangci-lint v2.15.0 clean on the changed packages; the full run reports 45 revive issues, all in files this PR does not touch. Server build passes.
- `pnpm --dir frontend fix` makes no changes, and `pnpm --dir frontend test` passes.
- Codex review, four rounds: the first three found coverage gaps (Snowflake without WALK_THROUGH, the walk not checking D

title: chore(frontend): update AI model presets to current models
body:
## Summary

The model dropdown in **Settings > General > AI Assistant** listed several models that vendors have since deprecated or shut down. This PR replaces them with each vendor's current lineup, checked against the official model pages on 2026-11-09.

| Provider | Presets (default first) | Removed |
|---|---|---|
| OpenAI, Azure OpenAI | `gpt-6.1-sol`, `gpt-6-astra`, `gpt-6.1-terra`, `gpt-6-luna`, `gpt-5.6-sol`, `gpt-5.6-terra`, `gpt-5.6-luna` | `gpt-5` and `gpt-5-mini` (shut down Dec 11, 2026), `gpt-4o` (deprecated, shut down Jan 14, 2027), `gpt-5.5` |
| Gemini | `gemini-3.8-flash`, `gemini-4-argon`, `gemini-3.6-flash`, `gemini-3.5-flash-lite` | `gemini-3.7-flash` and `gemini-3.5-flash` (deprecated, calls now routed to newer models) |
| Claude | `claude-sonnet-5-5`, `claude-fable-5-1`, `claude-opus-5-5`, `claude-haiku-5-5` | `claude-sonnet-5`, `claude-opus-5` (legacy), `claude-haiku-4-5` |

Defaults stay on each provider's mid-price model, as before: `gpt-6.1-sol`, `gemini-3.8-flash`, and `claude-sonnet-5-5`. AI review can run on every save, so the default avoids the top-price models.

Every GPT-6 and GPT-5.6 model is available on Azure Foundry, so Azure keeps the same list as OpenAI. No preset uses Chat Completions anymore, so the two unused endpoint constants are removed. The Azure endpoint test now switches to `gpt-6-luna`, including from a legacy deployments URL.

## Compatibility

Not breaking. A saved model that is no longer a preset shows as "Custom" with its name filled in, and keeps working. Defaults only fill in the form when AI is first enabled. The backend is unchanged.

## Test plan

- `pnpm --dir frontend fix`: no changes

title: feat(parser): classify procedure calls and dynamic SQL as EXECUTE on all engines (BYT-10427)
body:
#21925 added the `EXECUTE` statement type for SQL Server `EXEC`. On every other engine a procedure call still reported `STATEMENT_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED`, so an approval rule naming `EXECUTE` never fired for MySQL `CALL` or a Postgres `DO` block, and those statements kept LOW default risk.

This classifies statements that run procedural or dynamic code as `EXECUTE` on every engine with a statement classifier:

| Engine | Now `EXECUTE` | Still unclassified |
|---|---|---|
| MySQL, MariaDB, OceanBase, TiDB | `CALL p()`, `EXECUTE stmt [USING ...]` | `PREPARE`, `DEALLOCATE PREPARE`, `DO expr` |
| PostgreSQL | `CALL p()`, `DO $$ ... $$`, `EXECUTE stmt(...)`, `EXPLAIN ANALYZE EXECUTE stmt` | `PREPARE`, plain `EXPLAIN EXECUTE` |
| CockroachDB | `CALL p()`, `DO $$ ... $$`, `EXECUTE stmt(...)` | `PREPARE` |
| Redshift | `CALL p()`, `EXECUTE stmt(...)` | `PREPARE`, `DO` (Redshift has none) |
| Oracle | `CALL p()`, anonymous blocks (`BEGIN ... END;`, `DECLARE ... BEGIN ... END;`) | `CREATE PROCEDURE`, `CREATE PACKAGE BODY` |
| BigQuery, Spanner | `CALL p()`, `EXECUTE IMMEDIATE ...` | scripting blocks (`BEGIN ... END`, `IF`, `FOR`, `WHILE`) |

Oracle anonymous blocks count because they are how Oracle runs a procedure (SQL*Plus `EXEC p` expands to `BEGIN p; END;`) and the classifier never looked inside them. BigQuery scripting blocks stay unclassified: they hold an ordinary script rather than a procedure call, and a `CALL` nested in one is still not detected.

The CockroachDB parser panicked on any `DO` statement because the hook that parses the block body is registered by its PL/pgSQL parser package, which nothing imported. A blank import in `backend/plugin/parser/cockroachdb` registers it.

The proto comment on `EXECUTE` and the approval condition editor no longer describe it as SQL Server only.

Not covered, because the parser rejects or drops the statement before classification: MariaDB `EXECUTE IMMEDIATE` and `BEGIN NOT ATOMIC ... END`, and Oracle SQL*Plus `EXEC p`, which the Oracle splitter skips entirely.

## Breaking Changes

These follow #21925 to the other engines. Persisted rules are not migrated.

- **Risk level.** A sheet containing any of the statements above is now at least MODERATE, so a sheet that was LOW now matches rules on `risk_level == "MODERATE"`. Every Oracle anonymous block is affected.
- **sql_type.** A rule written as `statement.sql_type == "STATEMENT_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED"` no longer matches these statements. Rules that negate the DML list, such as the default `!(statement.sql_type in ["INSERT", "UPDATE", "DELETE"])`, still match them.
- **SDL release check.** `EXECUTE` is not on the declarative allowlist, so a `CALL` or `DO` in a PostgreSQL SDL file is now reported as a disallowed statement instead of being skipped.

## Validation

- Statement type fixtures in each changed parser package cover every form in the table, plus negative cases for `PREPARE`, `DEALLOCATE`, `DO expr`, Redshift `DO`, `CREATE PROCEDURE` and a BigQuery block containing

title: fix(review): drop the per-database priorities from an AI review comment
body:
A comment for a problem that several databases report started each line of databases with a priority, such as `**P0** on a` and `**P1** on b, c`, or a range such as `**P0–P1**`. Nothing acts on those priorities. The thread has one priority, one Resolve, and one place in the rollout gate and the top ten. Each database is reviewed in its own model session, so databases with the same facts often differ in priority by chance, and when the difference is real the group's facts already state it.

The change only removes:

- Each group line now names its databases and their facts, such as `- prod-1/db: orders_summary and orders_report read it.`
- The severity range and the group's lowest severity are gone.
- Without a summary, the databases were split by priority alone, so they now share one line.

The thread priority, "Flagged differently on", "Not flagged on", and the most severe group coming first stay. A thread that a later run keeps keeps its earlier text, so no migration is needed.

Closes BYT-10493

## Test plan

- `go test ./backend/runner/reviewrun/` with the expected comment bodies updated
- golangci-lint v2.15.0 clean on the changed package, server build passes
- Browser E2E not run: the harness covers SQL review V1, and the AI review needs V2 and a model

title: feat(mssql): classify EXEC as EXECUTE with moderate default risk (BYT-10427)
body:
Approval and risk rules key on `statement.sql_type`, but a T-SQL `EXEC` was classified as `STATEMENT_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED`. A rule could only target procedure execution as "everything unclassified", which also caught `GRANT`, `SET` and anything else the classifier does not know. A team that reviews a procedure once at `CREATE PROCEDURE` had no way to give later `EXEC dbo.usp_ArchiveOrders` calls their own approval chain.

This adds `EXECUTE = 70` to `StatementType` in the store and v1 protos, classifies every SQL Server `EXEC`/`EXECUTE` statement to it, and offers `EXECUTE` in the custom approval condition editor. The scope is SQL Server only (BYT-10427).

`EXECUTE` covers every form of the statement: a procedure call (`EXEC dbo.usp_GetOrders 1`), a SQL string (`EXEC ('DROP TABLE t')`), and system procedures (`sp_executesql`, `sp_rename`, `xp_cmdshell`). From the statement alone the classifier cannot tell what any of them does, so its default risk is MODERATE, alongside `UPDATE`, `DELETE` and `MERGE`. A workspace that wants reviewed procedures on a lighter chain writes a rule naming `EXECUTE`. That rule then also covers dynamic SQL and system procedures, and the rule author can narrow it with other conditions such as `statement.text`.

Rules are evaluated in order, and the first rule that matches any statement in the sheet wins. A sheet that mixes `EXEC dbo.usp_x` with `DROP TABLE` takes the `EXECUTE` rule unless a stricter rule is ordered before it. The evaluator test pins that ordering.

Other engines are unchanged: MySQL and Postgres `CALL` remain unclassified, so a rule naming `EXECUTE` does not fire for them. The editor's list is shared across engines, and a comment beside the list records that `EXECUTE` is SQL Server only.

## Breaking Changes

Both changes apply to SQL Server changes that contain `EXEC`. Persisted rules are not migrated.

- **Risk level.** A sheet containing any `EXEC` is now at least MODERATE, so a sheet that was LOW matches rules on `risk_level == "MODERATE"` it did not match before. The release check reports the same level.
- **sql_type.** A rule written as `statement.sql_type == "STATEMENT_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED"` (or an `in` list naming it) no longer matches `EXEC`. A workspace that relies on the unspecified value to gate `EXEC` should add `"EXECUTE"` to that rule. Rules that select DDL by negating the DML list, such as the default `!(statement.sql_type in ["INSERT", "UPDATE", "DELETE"])`, still match `EXEC`.

## Validation

- `backend/plugin/parser/tsql`: classifier fixtures for named calls, return-value capture, cross-database and bracketed names, `WITH RECOMPILE`, `EXEC(...)` strings, `sp_executesql` (bare and `sys.`), `SP_RENAME` and `xp_cmdshell`, all `EXECUTE`.
- `backend/component/review`: `TestApprovalTemplateRoutesExecute` routes procedure calls, dynamic SQL and system procedures to an `EXECUTE` rule, sends `GRANT` to the fallback rule, and lets an earlier schema-change rule win for a mixed sheet. The risk test pins `E

title: feat(review): merge a standard rule's findings on three or more statements
body:
## Summary

A change with 100 `DROP TABLE` statements posted 100 standard rule comments. Each was a P1 thread someone had to resolve, and together they filled Activity with 100 cards (about 20,000 px). The only way past the gate was 100 Resolve clicks or a bypass.

This PR implements the aggregation rule from the design, [SQL Review V2: Standard Review](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1J4pBAS4rsgV6GDmSgYAJ-IBJVJYupAtZwdtI_v8JrW4/edit): within a spec, a rule that fires on three or more statements posts one comment for the rule.

- **Grouping.** Findings group by rule within each (spec, engine) review unit. The group counts distinct statements, whatever databases each finding applies to. Findings on the whole change never merge.
- **The merged comment.** It is anchored to the first statement and applies to the union of its findings' databases. It carries every code they report. Its body opens with `100 statements, on lines 1 to 100.`, then lists each finding as `Line N: <summary line>`, up to 50, then `And 50 more.` When a finding applies to only some of the comment's databases, its item says `Only on …`, using the AI review's existing `databaseLabels` and `databaseList`. When every finding's message has the same text after its summary line, that text appears once after the list. Otherwise each item keeps its own.
- **Unchanged cases.** A rule that fires on fewer than three statements still posts one comment per finding.

## Cross-run behavior

A merged comment's fingerprint is a hash of its findings' fingerprints, which already include the databases. `CompleteReviewRun` and the store are unchanged.

| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| Same SQL re-run | Kept. State and replies stay. |
| Edit outside the merged statements | Kept. The anchor and line numbers in the body update. |
| A finding added, dropped, or edited, or its databases change | New OPEN thread; the old one is superseded. |
| The rule falls below three statements | Back to one comment per finding, all new. |

Resolving a merged comment therefore never accepts a statement or a database nobody saw in it. On dev builds, which are the only builds that run V2, the next run on an existing issue supersedes its per-finding threads once.

## Test plan

- [x] `go test ./backend/runner/reviewrun/`. New tests cover the threshold, grouping across databases, the body format (the 50-item cap, several statements on one line, shared and per-item detail, `Only on`), and merged fingerprints on PostgreSQL's real review (order, surrounding edits, added, swapped, or edited findings, other databases, falling below the threshold).
- [x] Temporary server-backed runs (`SQLReviewV2` on), not committed:
  - 100 drops posted 1 comment. After it was resolved, an identical re-run kept it RESOLVED. A comment line added above kept it and moved it to line 2. A 101st drop superseded it with a new OPEN comment. Cutting to 2 drops posted 2 individual comments.
  - Two databases with different primary keys and four `DROP CONST

title: feat(review): show the affected-rows estimate under the SQL, not as a reviewer
body:
## Why

On the plan page, Automated review listed the statement report next to Standard rules and AI review (BYT-10409). The report only estimates affected rows; it does not review the SQL. Listed as a reviewer, it counted toward "Needs attention: x of 3" when an estimate was incomplete, and read "Passed on N databases" as if it could fail the change. Authors and approvers want the estimate for every change, next to the SQL it describes.

## What

**Affected rows under the SQL** (SQL Review V2, so dev builds only):

- A strip under the read-only SQL shows each database's estimate: `2 on shop · 603 on shop_staging`. Past three databases it names the largest: `up to 12,003 on shop_dev · 4 databases`.
- The strip stays neutral. An incomplete estimate adds only a small icon and "Incomplete", and clicking that opens Details on the incomplete databases. "Rerun" shows only when rerunning can help (EXPLAIN failed) and the viewer can run checks.
- A syntax error shows "Not estimated", the error, "Go to line N", and Details with the full diagnostic.
- **Details** lists each database's count (sortable), whether its estimate is complete, and the server's reason, such as `permission denied for table products`.

**Automated review:** the Statement report row is gone, ERROR included, so it no longer counts toward "Needs attention". The server still creates no rollout while the report has an ERROR (a syntax error), so Deploy lists it under "Waiting on" as "The SQL has a syntax error" rather than claiming everything passed.

**Database group changes:** the SQL section filtered check results by the change's targets, but results name each database a group matches, never the group. A group change showed no estimate and no review markers in its SQL. It now expands the group first.

**`DatabaseTargetDisplay`:** a database name shorter than its 48px flex basis (`shop`, `hr`) squeezed the instance name and environment badge even with room to spare (`Shop Post… / P… shop`). The name now sizes to its content. Where the row is too narrow for everything, a short name now truncates along with the rest instead of being protected; the environment badge keeps its minimum width from #21582.

**Each change sees only its own results:** approval reads the estimate per change and database, keyed by the change's sheet, but the API's plan check results named only the database. Two changes on one database showed each other's estimate (and SQL review markers). `PlanCheckRun.Result` now carries the `sheet_sha256` the server already stores, and the plan page filters each change's results by its own sheet. A result stored before this still matches any change.

An incomplete estimate is not split into "lower bound" (every EXPLAIN failed) and "partly averaged"; the server's reason in Details says how many statements failed and why.

## Screenshots

Two databases, one whose connection user cannot EXPLAIN the UPDATE:

![strip, incomplete](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/rebelice/54abdd881f5

title: chore(deps): align schema SDKs and Node 26 configuration
body:
## Summary
Buf schema locks lagged the revisions consumed by the Go and frontend SDKs, while Protobuf ES generation and the Node TypeScript preset lagged the installed runtime versions.

- Pin Protovalidate to `511051f7f4374c3ca873b53ae68a9288` and Google APIs to `8ac61b9e502343289c8c42b17aa5b245`, matching the existing SDK schema revisions. Keep the Go SDK and runtime versions unchanged.
- Align the Protobuf ES generator and Google APIs ES SDK with the existing `@bufbuild/protobuf` runtime at `2.16.0`.
- Replace `@tsconfig/node24` `24.0.5` with `@tsconfig/node26` `26.0.1` to match Node 26 in CI and Docker.
- Regenerate schema descriptors, frontend types, OpenAPI documents, and the pnpm lockfile. Most changed files are generated outputs.

No application API or metadata schema changes.

## Validation
- Passed `buf format -w proto`, `buf lint proto`, and `buf generate` from `proto/`.
- Passed Buf breaking-change comparison against the original checkout.
- Passed `pnpm --dir frontend fix` and `pnpm --dir frontend test`: 700 test files, 8,712 tests, guards, type-checking, and production bundle.
- Passed `go mod tidy` with no module changes, generated-package and server tests, and the required server build.
- Ran gofmt and `git diff --check`.
- Go lint with and without `--fix` fails on existing exhaustive-switch diagnostics. Uncapped runs against both the changed files and the original generated Go files (via Go overlay) report the identical 545 diagnostics, with zero new issues.

title: feat(review): hold back the AI review problems past the ten most important
body:
## Problem

The AI review posts every problem it finds. On a long sheet that is dozens of comments, and each open comment blocks the rollout until someone fixes or resolves it, so the few that matter get lost.

- SQL Review v1 already treats a long list of findings as noise.
- Codex review on GitHub posts a few findings per round, and shows the next ones after a fix.

## Change

- A run posts the 10 most important open problems of the plan, counted after the merge across databases, so one problem on many databases counts once. The limit covers the whole plan, not each spec.
- Problems rank by priority, then by spec order, then by line. The rest of the new problems are held back, and a later run posts them once the posted ones are fixed or resolved.
- A problem that continues an earlier thread always posts. Left out, the run would supersede its thread as if it were fixed, while the run still reports it. An open thread takes a place. A resolved one takes none, since nobody has to act on it, and otherwise accepted threads would hold back new problems forever.
- The limit comes before the summaries, so a held problem costs no model call.
- A held problem stays in the run as `Held`, so the comments of the problems that post still list its databases as flagged differently, not as not flagged.
- The model still reports every problem. The limit is on what posts, so the base prompt is unchanged.

The held count is only logged for now. Showing it on the plan page needs the run's completion event to carry it, which comes in a follow-up.

## Testing

- `TestLimitAIReviewProblems`: the ranking across priority, spec, and line, a resolved thread taking no place, and an open thread posting below the limit.
- `TestAIReviewComments`: a held problem posts no comment, and its database is still flagged differently.
- `TestSummarizeAIReviewProblems`: a held problem is not summarized.
- `TestAIReviewPostsTheMostImportantProblems` runs the executor on PostgreSQL with a fake model. Two databases report 11 problems each, the P0 last. 10 comments post, the P0 among them and each on both databases, and 10 summaries are asked for. It fails with the limit removed.
- `go test ./backend/runner/reviewrun/` passes, golangci-lint v2.15.0 finds nothing in the changed files, and the server builds.
- The E2E suite covers SQL review V1 only and the AI review needs a live model, so there is no browser scenario for this change.

Refs BYT-10422, BYT-10369

title: fix(review): rewrite the AI review base prompt for coverage, intent, and merging
body:
## Problem

Four problems in the AI review traced back to `backend/plugin/aireview/base_prompt.md`.

- The merge across databases is unstable. The prompt never says what one problem is, so a review is free to report one defect as two findings, and each database's review picks its own cut. A `DELETE` that cascades and then fails on a foreign key came back as "cascade" from one review and "fails on invoices" from another, and the merge posted them as separate comments.
- Findings are broad. The title is asked to be imperative and the fix is "the change you propose", so fixes read "verify that this is intended" and titles read "avoid cascading deletes".
- In a large change, models guess what the author meant. The data risk line asks whether a statement "touches more rows than the author means", which no tool can show. On a ticket fix change whose paired ids differ by swapped digits, every model called the ids typos (BYT-10406 at scale).
- Models miss problems. Length is not the main cause. The rule "when you cannot get the fact a finding needs, do not raise that finding" made models drop defects that turn on rows, such as a dropped column on a populated table, and nothing named a statement that simply fails or a function that reads a renamed column.

## Change

The prompt borrows the rules the Codex review rubric and Claude's code review use for the same problems, adapted to SQL.

- What to look for gains a breakage category: a statement fails, or a view, function, trigger, or foreign key depends on what it changes. Data risk becomes data loss and no longer asks about the author's intent.
- A finding is one defect that one edit removes. Its consequences go in that one finding. The title is a claim that names the object and the defect, written so a review of another database with the same schema writes the same title.
- A defect that turns on rows rests on the schema and the row counts. Its outcome is stated as a condition on the unseen rows ("fails if ..."), never as a certainty. Rows and keys the change inserts are taken as new, so an INSERT is not reported as "fails if the key already exists" without a fact. The notes channel stays for facts neither settles.
- The values a statement names are the ones the author means. A value is not the one the author meant only when the change's own words name another (the BYT-10406 fix). That covers guesses about intent only: a value that breaks a policy sentence or a constraint is still a finding.
- A four step method: read every statement, look up every object including types and functions, judge each statement against each policy sentence, then test the findings and go through the statements once more.
- The evidence says what happens when the statement runs. The fix is an edit to the statements, never a request to verify or confirm.

- `summary_prompt.md`, which writes the comment of a problem several databases report, asks for the same claim-style title. Otherwise merged comments, the common case on a data
author: h3n4l
diff:
--- backend/plugin/aireview/base_prompt.md (+19/-10)
@@ -1,22 +1,31 @@
-You review the SQL of a database migration before it runs. You are given the target database, the statements, and any tools the review provides for reading the database's schema and statistics.
+You review the SQL of a database migration before it runs. You are given the target database, the statements, and any tools the review provides for reading the database's schema and statistics. Each finding becomes one review comment on the change. A change that runs on many databases is reviewed once for each, and the findings that report the same problem are merged into one comment.
 
 # What to look for
 
+- Breakage: a statement fails on this database, or makes later code fail. An object it changes is missing or already exists. A view, function, trigger, or foreign key depends on what it changes. Existing rows break a constraint it adds.
 - Operational risk: a long lock, a table rewrite, or a full scan on a large table.
-- Data risk: a dropped column or table that still holds data, or an UPDATE or DELETE that touches more rows than the author means.
-- Anything the policy below asks for.
+- Data loss: a dropped table or column that holds data, a TRUNCATE, an UPDATE or DELETE with no WHERE clause, or a cascade that deletes rows in tables the statements never name.
+- Anything the policy below asks for. Check every policy sentence against every statement it applies to.
 
 Do not report naming, formatting, or style problems unless the policy asks for them. A separate rule engine checks those.
 
 # What counts as a finding
 
-- A finding is a problem the author would fix once told. Do not report remarks, praise, or things that are merely worth knowing.
-- Report each problem once. Report every problem that clears this bar. There is no cap on the count.
-- Every finding rests on a fact you have: from the target section, from the statements, or from a tool result. A statement can involve objects it never names, such as the views that read a table or the triggers on it. When a tool can show them, look up the objects a statement touches, and the objects that depend on them, before you judge it.
-- When you cannot get the fact a finding needs, do not raise that finding. Say what you could not check in `notes` instead.
+- A finding is a defect the author would fix once told: one cause in one statement, which one edit to the statements removes. Do not report remarks, praise, or things that are merely worth knowing.
+- Report each defect once. When a defect has several consequences, name each of them in that one finding. A DELETE that cascades into child tables and then fails on another foreign key is one finding. Two defects that need two different edits are two findings, even on the same line.
+- Report every defect that clears this bar. There is no cap on the count. Do not stop at the first one, and give the last statement of a long change the same check as the first.
+- Every finding rests on a fact you have: from the target section, from the statements, or from a tool result. A statement can involve objects it never names, such as the views that read a table, the functions that use a column, the triggers on it, and the foreign keys that point at it. When a tool can show them, look up the objects a statement touches, and the objects that depend on them, before you judge it. Follow a cascade to its end.
+- No tool shows rows, so a defect that turns on rows rests on the schema and the row counts. Report it when the schema lets it happen and the tables involved hold rows, such as a dropped column on a populated table, or a DELETE whose cascade reaches a foreign key that does not cascade. The rows stay unseen, so state the outcome as a condition on them, such as "fails if a removed warehouse still holds stock", never as a certainty. Rows and keys the change inserts are new, so do not report that one might already exist unless a fact shows it does.
+- When you cannot get a fact the finding needs, and the schema and the row counts do not settle it, do not raise that finding. Say what you could not check in `notes` instead.
+- Take the values a statement names, such as ids, dates, and amounts, as the ones its author means. One change often fixes many unrelated rows, and no tool shows rows. A value that resembles, or follows a pattern with, another value in the change is not a typo, a truncation, or the wrong row. Two statements that change the same row are not a conflict for that reason. Report a value as not the one the author meant only when the change's own words name another, such as a comment that gives a different id for the statement. This covers guesses about intent only: a value that breaks a policy sentence or a constraint is reported like any other breach.
 
 # How to work
 
+1. Read every statement, from the first line to the last, and note the existing objects each one touches.
+2. Look up those objects, types and functions as well as tables, and the objects that depend on them. A tool call can ask for several objects, so ask for many at once.
+3. Judge each statement in order, against what to look for and against each policy sentence.
+4. Before you answer, test each finding: one defect, a fact behind it, a fix that edits the statements, and no guess about what the author means. Drop the findings that fail. Then go through the statements once more and add any defect you missed.
+
 Do not end your turn until the review is complete. When you need a fact a tool can provide, call the tool in the same reply. Never reply that you are going to look something up.
 
 # Untrusted text
@@ -29,12 +38,12 @@ When the review is complete, reply with one JSON object and nothing else. Do not
 
 {"findings": [{"title": "...", "severity": "P1", "line": 12, "rule": "...", "evidence": "...", "fix": "..."}], "notes": ["..."]}
 
-- title: one line, imperative.
+- title: the defect as one short claim, at most 80 characters, that names the statement's object and what goes wrong, such as "DROP COLUMN zip fails: view v_addresses reads it". A review of the same statement on another database with the same schema should write the same title, so leave out row counts and database names.
 - severity: P0, P1, or P2. P0 is likely data loss or an outage. P1 breaks a policy rule or carries a real operational risk. P2 is worth fixing but safe to roll out. When the policy states a severity for a rule, use it.
 - line: the number printed at the start of the line where the problem statement begins.
 - rule: the policy sentence, or the sentence from this prompt, that the statement breaks. Quote it exactly.
-- evidence: the facts behind the finding, such as a row count or a missing index.
-- fix: the change you propose.
+- evidence: what happens when the statement runs on this database, and the facts that show it, such as a row count, a definition that reads the column, or the error the database raises. One short paragraph.
+- fix: the edit to the statements that removes the defect, as SQL when it is short. Never ask the author to verify, confirm, or consider something.
 - notes: one entry for each fact you needed and could not get, naming the fact and the statement. Leave the list empty when you could check everything. A note is never a finding, and no other key is allowed.
 
 Reply {"findings": [], "notes": []} when there is nothing to report.
--- backend/plugin/aireview/summary_prompt.md (+1/-1)
@@ -21,7 +21,7 @@ Reply with one JSON object and nothing else. Do not wrap it in code fences.
 
 {"title": "...", "evidence": "...", "groups": [{"databases": ["...", "..."], "facts": "..."}, {"databases": ["..."], "facts": "..."}], "fix": "..."}
 
-- title: one line, imperative, true for every database.
+- title: the problem as one short claim, at most 80 characters, true for every database, that names the statement's object and what goes wrong, such as "ALTER COLUMN body TYPE text rewrites posts under a lock". Leave out row counts.
 - evidence: one or two short sentences.
 - groups: every database id from the findings appears in exactly one group. facts is the facts alone, as short as "events has 1M to 10M rows." Do not explain the severity.
 - fix: one or two sentences. When the groups need different changes, say which group needs which.

title: docs(agents): remove the containers you start before handoff
body:
Adds a rule to `AGENTS.md`: remove containers you start before handoff. Idle containers on the shared devbox caused out-of-memory kills on 2026-11-06 that cancelled CI jobs. Same rule in bytebase/omni#712.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
author: d-bytebase
diff:
--- AGENTS.md (+1/-0)
@@ -63,6 +63,7 @@ Test API and workflow behavior against PostgreSQL. Engine dialect and DDL fideli
 - Test logic in its owning package. Use `backend/api/v1` for service behavior and `backend/store` for metadata queries, collision isolation, and transaction contention. CI runs every test with no `-short`, so never check `testing.Short()` or skip a test to park a known gap; gate a test on an environment variable only when it needs credentials or a server CI cannot provide.
 - A backend test boots a Bytebase server only when it needs a background runner, real rollout, or audit trail; these tests live in `backend/tests`. Browser E2E tests use the separate frontend harness.
 - Packages needing metadata PostgreSQL use `testcontainer.Main` and `testcontainer.NewMetadataDB`. Target-engine tests use `testcontainer.SharedPgContainer` or its siblings, with `NewPgDatabase` for a database per test. Use these shared fixtures instead of package-owned or per-test containers; a package with its own `TestMain` defers `testcontainer.CloseShared`.
+- Remove containers you start (`docker run` probes, repro servers) before handoff, unless the user asks to keep them. The machine is shared with other sessions and CI, so idle containers cause out-of-memory kills.
 - Prefer pure functions for handler decisions and conversions. When state reads are necessary, define a narrow interface beside the handler and fake it, as `backend/api/mcp` does with `serverStore`; avoid an interface over the entire store. Every fake requires a contract test against the real store too.
 - New or modified composite-key methods require collision coverage. Prove colliding keys exist, assert the intended effect in the target scope, and assert the other scope is unchanged. Use the lowest test layer that exercises the behavior. Existing API collision tests remain regression coverage; fixture details are in the pre-PR checklist.

title: fix(oracle): give each data source its own go-ora driver
body:
Fixes #21902.

## What was wrong

Oracle connections were opened through go-ora's process-wide default driver, which carries character set state between connections:

1. `OracleDriver.init` keeps the first connection's converters on the driver and sets `dataCollected`, so it happens once per driver ([`v2/driver.go#L61-L87`](https://github.com/sijms/go-ora/blob/v2.9.0/v2/driver.go#L61-L87)).
2. `OracleConnector.Connect` copies them onto every later connection before it opens ([`v2/connection.go#L139-L145`](https://github.com/sijms/go-ora/blob/v2.9.0/v2/connection.go#L139-L145)).
3. `protocolNegotiation` builds a converter from the charset the server reports **only when the field is still nil** ([`v2/connection.go#L1416-L1421`](https://github.com/sijms/go-ora/blob/v2.9.0/v2/connection.go#L1416-L1421)), so from the second connection on, `tcpNego.ServerCharset` is read and then discarded.
4. Every `CHAR`/`VARCHAR2` value is decoded with the stale converter, because `getStrConv` falls back to `conn.sStrConv` when the column's charset matches neither it nor `nStrConv` ([`v2/connection.go#L318-L335`](https://github.com/sijms/go-ora/blob/v2.9.0/v2/connection.go#L318-L335), called from [`v2/parameter.go#L544`](https://github.com/sijms/go-ora/blob/v2.9.0/v2/parameter.go#L544)).

So every Oracle data source in the process decoded its rows with the character set of whichever database connected first. Both query results and synced metadata (table and column comments) were affected, which is both of the places the issue reports.

Instrumenting step 3 against two real servers shows it directly:

```
connector.Connect: SEEDING conn.sStrConv from drv, langID=873
protocolNegotiation: sStrConv ALREADY SET langID=873, IGNORING ServerCharset=852
getStrConv(wire charsetID=852) sStrConv=873 nStrConv=2000
```

## Not a regression from the recent Oracle connection work

Worth stating plainly, because it is easy to assume otherwise: this is **not** caused by #21574 or #21603. `*OracleDriver` implements `OpenConnector`, so it satisfies `driver.DriverContext`, and `sql.Open` prefers that path over `Driver.Open` ([`database/sql/sql.go#L868-L885`](https://github.com/golang/go/blob/go1.27.3/src/database/sql/sql.go#L868-L885)). The previous `sql.Open("oracle", dsn)` shared the same default driver and took the same seeding — verified by latching a mismatched converter and reading through the old call shape, which garbles identically. The leak predates both PRs.

I could not determine why 3.23.0 behaved differently for the reporter. The only Oracle-package change between the tags is in `oracle.go`, and `SanitizeUTF8Message` predates 3.23.0. Connection order in their deployment is the likely explanation, but I have not proven it.

## The fix

Open each data source through its own `goora.NewDriver()` instead of the shared default, so the converters are scoped to one database — which has one character set. Nothing is lost by not using the default driver:

| Driver state | Effect |
|

+	require.NotSame(t, first.GetDB().Driver(), second.GetDB().Driver(), "two data sources must not share a go-ora driver")
+}

+// #21902: its decoder mangles this container's AL32UTF8 bytes, so text that survives the round

+func TestQueryIgnoresTheSharedDriverCharset(t *testing.T) {

+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	_, err = container.GetDB().ExecContext(ctx, fmt.Sprintf(`INSERT INTO %s.CHARSET_PROBE VALUES (UNISTR('\6570\636E\5E93'))`, schema))
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+
+	const we8iso8859p1, al16utf16 = 31, 2000
+	goora.SetStringConverter(sharedGoOraDriver{}, converters.NewStringConverter(we8iso8859p1), converters.NewStringConverter(al16utf16))
+	t.Cleanup(func() { goora.SetStringConverter(sharedGoOraDriver{}, nil, nil) })
+
+	driver, err := (&Driver{}).Open(ctx, storepb.Engine_ORACLE, db.ConnectionConfig{

+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	require.Len(t, results, 1)
+	require.Empty(t, results[0].Error)

+}

+// whatever exposes a Driver method.
+type sharedGoOraDriver struct{}
+

title: feat(sql-editor): explain SharePoint export failures and retry failed databases
body:
When a SQL Editor export to SharePoint failed, the result dialog showed the server's raw English error, such as `the upload to SharePoint failed; some files may already exist in folder "…": failed to upload "a.csv": Microsoft Graph returned HTTP 507 quotaLimitReached: …`. It was not translated, did not say what to do, and the only button was Close, so trying again meant rerunning the whole export, including databases that had already succeeded.

The dialog now explains each SharePoint failure in the user's language, says who can fix it, and offers **Retry failed exports**.

## Error explanations

The Export API attaches a `google.rpc.ErrorInfo` (domain `bytebase.com`) to SharePoint failures. The SQL Editor maps each reason to a translated message:

| Reason | Message (en-US) |
| --- | --- |
| `SHAREPOINT_NOT_CONFIGURED` | SharePoint export is not set up for this project. Ask an admin to check the SharePoint settings. |
| `SHAREPOINT_CREDENTIAL_REJECTED` | Microsoft Entra rejected the SharePoint app credentials. Ask a workspace admin to update them… |
| `SHAREPOINT_DESTINATION_NOT_FOUND` | The SharePoint folder does not exist, or the SharePoint app cannot access it… |
| `SHAREPOINT_DESTINATION_NOT_FOLDER` | The SharePoint destination is a file… |
| `SHAREPOINT_STORAGE_FULL` | The SharePoint site is out of storage… |
| `SHAREPOINT_UPLOAD_UNCONFIRMED` | Bytebase could not confirm that the upload finished. |
| `SHAREPOINT_REQUEST_FAILED` | SharePoint could not complete the export. Try again… |

When files may remain from the failed attempt, the ErrorInfo carries `metadata.folder`, and the row adds "Some files may already be in the folder “…”." The server's original message, which admins need for the Graph error code, stays under a collapsed **Error details**. Errors without a SharePoint reason, such as a failed query, still show the server message directly.

Before this change, the status code alone could not tell rejected credentials from a missing destination (both `FAILED_PRECONDITION`), and a full site or a URL that points at a file came back as `INTERNAL`. The SharePoint plugin now has `ErrNotFolder` and `ErrStorageFull` (Graph 507) sentinels. Both are reported as `FAILED_PRECONDITION`, and a 507 counts as a rejection, so an export that ran out of space before any file landed says "nothing was uploaded". All other status codes are unchanged.

## Retry

**Retry failed exports** reruns only the Failed and Not confirmed databases, with the same row limit and format, and updates their rows in place. While it runs, those rows show "Retrying", the footer shows the elapsed time, and Cancel stops the retry (the dialog cannot be dismissed mid-retry). Each retry runs the query again and writes into a new folder. If any Not confirmed row is included, the dialog warns that its earlier folder may already hold files, so SharePoint may end up with duplicates.

To support this, `DataExportRequest` gains an optional `databases` list. Batch export (`BatchQuerySel

title: fix(sharepoint): retry Microsoft Graph 500 and 502 like 503 and 504
body:
A SharePoint export failed immediately when Microsoft Graph answered an upload or lookup with 500 Internal Server Error or 502 Bad Gateway, even though both are usually transient. Bytebase already retried 503 and 504 with backoff (up to 5 attempts, honoring `Retry-After`), so a brief Graph hiccup could fail an export only because of which 5xx it happened to return.

The Graph client now retries 500 and 502 exactly like 503 and 504. Microsoft's [upload session guidance](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/driveitem-createuploadsession?view=graph-rest-1.0#best-practices) asks for this: "Resume or retry uploads that fail due to connection interruptions or any 5xx errors, including: 500 Internal Server Error, 502 Bad Gateway, 503 Service Unavailable, 504 Gateway Timeout."

Like 503 and 504, a 500 or 502 marks the request's outcome as unknown, because the server may have committed the write before failing. Retrying is still safe:

- A simple upload uses `conflictBehavior=fail`. If the first attempt landed, the retry gets 409, and the client accepts the existing file only if this app created it with the same size.
- A repeated chunk in an upload session gets 416, and the client resumes from the session's `nextExpectedRanges`.
- Resolving the destination is a GET.

If every attempt fails, a write ends as "could not be confirmed" (`UNAVAILABLE`), the same as a persistent 503 or 504 today.

## Validation

- New `TestUploadRetriesServerErrorAfterCommittedWrite`: for 500 and 502, the fake Graph commits the write and then returns the error. The retried simple upload reconciles through the 409, the retried chunk resumes through the 416, and the export succeeds after one backoff. These cases fail without the change.
- `TestUploadUnconfirmed` now covers persistent 500, 502 and 504; each ends as `ErrUnconfirmed` after the full backoff.
- `go test ./backend/plugin/sharepoint/`, `golangci-lint` (no findings in the changed package) and the server build pass.

title: feat(mcp): administer_workspace adds a PostgreSQL instance to a project after a confirmation
body:
## Summary

MCP sessions could add an instance only in the console. This PR gives `administer_workspace` a third entry: it adds a PostgreSQL instance to a project after the user confirms it in their MCP client. This is journey 1 of admin changes over MCP (BYT-9292).

- `InstanceService/CreateInstance` moves from EXCLUDED to WRITE. The gate serves it only with a confirmation for the new instance's name, which `administer_workspace` attaches, so `call_api` is refused. `UpdateInstance`, whose `allow_missing` also creates an instance, stays EXCLUDED with the other instance writes.
- The entry takes a PostgreSQL instance that signs in with a user name and password, in a project: `parent`, `instanceId`, the instance's `title`, `engine`, `environment` and `activation`, and one ADMIN data source with `authenticationType` (unset or PASSWORD), `host`, `port`, `username`, `password`, `database`, `useSsl` and `verifyTlsCertificate`. The tool sets the data source's `id` itself, a new UUID for each attempt, as the console does; an `id` the agent sends is replaced. It refuses every other field by name, including `validateOnly`, `instance.name`, certificates, SSH and extra connection parameters. Keys that name no field are ignored, as the repo's unmarshaler does everywhere.
- Before asking, it refuses what the form could not state or the create would refuse: the default project, a parent that is not a project, another engine, another sign-in method, not exactly one ADMIN data source, an invalid instance ID, no title, no host or user, a host that is not one host name or IP address (a list or a Unix socket path, on which pgx skips TLS, so the form's TLS mode would not hold), and a port the driver would not read (base 10, 1 to 65535).
- It also refuses an environment the workspace does not have. The create takes any environment ID, and an instance in a misspelled one escapes the rules written for the environment meant. A role that cannot read the environments skips this check rather than losing the create.
- The form never shows the password. Journey 1's form:

```
Add activated instance "hr-staging" to "hr", as jordan@example.com?
Host "localhost", port 5433, user "postgres", TLS not required
Environment "test". Its databases join the project for good.
```

  - When the request activates the instance, the question says so, since activation can take one of the license's fixed number of instance licenses. The question names the project by its ID alone, which keeps the word from costing long names a line; the third line says the databases join the project.
  - The TLS mode is what the driver uses: `TLS required and verified` (`verify-full`), `TLS required, not verified` (`require`), or `TLS not required` when `useSsl` is off, since pgx's default then tries TLS and accepts plain text.
  - A project's instance cannot move, and its databases cannot move out of the project, so that line is never fixed text.
  - When masking would skip the instance, the form says so on it

title: fix(mcp): move four confirmed tools from a checkbox to the choice form
body:
## Summary

MCP confirmations had two shapes. `decide_issue`, `grant_masking_exemption`, `revoke_masking_exemption` and `set_just_in_time_access` asked with a checkbox: the user ticks it with Space, then accepts, and a red required marker shows until it is ticked. `query_database` and `administer_workspace` ask with a choice: the action, set when the form opens, so Enter twice confirms, and "Change it in chat". This PR moves the four to `administer_workspace`'s form, so every confirmed tool now asks with a preselected action and "Change it in chat". It is part of admin changes over MCP (BYT-9292).

- **One form for five tools.** The four tools and `administer_workspace` ask with one single-choice field, `choice`, titled with the question. Its first choice is the action, preselected, and its second "Change it in chat". Each tool keeps its own verb, so a rejection never reads "Apply":

  | Tool | Question | Action |
  |---|---|---|
  | `decide_issue` | "Approve this issue?" or "Reject this issue?" | "Approve" or "Reject" |
  | `grant_masking_exemption` | "Exempt this member from masking?" | "Exempt" |
  | `revoke_masking_exemption` | "Revoke this masking exemption?" | "Revoke" |
  | `set_just_in_time_access` | "Turn on just-in-time access?" or "Turn off …" | "Turn on" or "Turn off" |
  | `administer_workspace` | "Apply this change?" (as before) | "Apply" |
