title: feat(mcp): administer_workspace changes the approval rules for database changes after a confirmation
body:
## Summary

MCP sessions could not change any workspace setting. `SettingService/UpdateSetting` was FORBIDDEN, because the same method writes the MCP ceiling, the mail relay and the AI endpoint. This PR adds the `administer_workspace` tool. It changes one setting, the approval rules for database changes, and only after the user confirms the change in their MCP client. This is part of admin changes over MCP (BYT-9292).

- `UpdateSetting` moves from FORBIDDEN to WRITE. The gate serves it only with a confirmation for the setting it names, as it serves `ApproveIssue`, `RejectIssue`, `UpdateProject` and `UpdatePolicy`. `call_api` cannot attach a confirmation, so it is refused for every setting. The refusal names the tool for the approval rules and the console for every other setting.
- The tool takes an `operationId` and a request `body`, as `call_api` does. It accepts `SettingService/UpdateSetting` for `settings/WORKSPACE_APPROVAL` only. It reads the rules before it asks, so it needs `bb.settings.get` as well as `bb.settings.set`, as the console's approval page does. It refuses a field the form does not state: `update_mask`, `allow_missing`, `validate_only`, and a condition's title, description and location, which nothing in the product writes. A stored rule that holds one of those is refused too, because the write would drop it, and the refusal points to the console page. The tool also refuses a request with no rule list, and an added or changed rule whose approver is not a role name such as `roles/workspaceDBA`: an approval check matches a step's role by its exact name, so no one could approve such a step.
- The tool reads the stored rules and compares the rules for database changes by their condition. The rules of every other source must come back as stored, in their order.
- The form's message gives one line per changed rule, approvers first: added, removed, approvers changed, moved, renamed or description changed. A kept rule that changes in several ways gets one line that names each change. A predefined role shows by its display name, and any other value as written. An added rule's line gives its place when another rule follows it, since the first matching rule decides.
- The message fits the four lines of 70 columns that the other confirmed tools use, and names the user's own issues that await approval. A change that does not fit is refused before asking, with a link to the console page. The form's description lists the rules for database changes in the order an approval check tries them, and says that the fallback rules decide when none matches, and that a change no rule matches needs no approval.
- The write is locked. The confirmation carries a digest of the stored rules the user saw. The handler writes through `UpdateSettingAtomic` and returns FailedPrecondition when the rules under the row lock differ, so an edit another admin made after the question is kept. title: feat(plan): show what a release did to each database on the plan page
body:
Implements [docs/design/release-plan-page.md](https://github.com/bytebase/bytebase/blob/main/docs/design/release-plan-page.md) (design PR #21680): the plan page of a release-backed plan, the one bytebase-action creates from a GitOps merge.

## What a reader sees now

- **Each task is one list of files (the spine).** Before the run, from a state stored at rollout creation: the files it will apply, and the files the database already has folded under one line. After a run, from its log: the files the run reached, with task-level steps beside them, the error on the failed file, and nothing after it. Long lists load in place, 20 at a time; a failed or running file always stays shown.
- **A version that runs a second time says so.** "Will apply again · revision deleted" before the run, "Applied again" after it; an info icon names who deleted the earlier revision and when, or says it was deleted after the rollout was created.
- **Every task is folded on load to one line that says what happened** ("2 to apply · 1 already applied", "All 3 applied", the failed version and its error). The whole header line folds and unfolds the card; the checkbox and buttons keep their own click. The page opens on the stage with the latest failed task, else the running one, else the last.
- **Changes lists the release's files** newest first, like a repository's file list, grouped by day and month only for timestamp versions, with no per-database status.
- **A read-only file viewer** draws the error on the failed statement and links to the file at its commit. It docks as the page's right half at 1280 px and wider, a sheet below.
- **A details block under the title**: source (PR or commit title, author, `repo@sha`, branch), trigger, release, review and progress; it folds.
- **Skip asks for a reason on release tasks**, shows each task's status and error, and a skipped task says who skipped it and when. A deployed plan with a skipped task reads "Deployed, 1 task skipped".
- **The Revisions link** shows once a run applied at least one file, failed or not.

## Changes by layer

- **Backend and proto.** Rollout creation stores each versioned task's file state (`Task.DatabaseUpdate.release_state`): the versions it will apply, with the deleted revision's deleter and time when one existed, and the count already applied, by the executor's own rule (a live `VERSIONED` revision of that version). One `ListRevisions` query per target, bounded by the release's file count. `BatchSkipTasks` records the skipper and skip time (`Task.skipper`, `Task.skip_time`, output only). `Release.VCSSource` gains commit SHA, branch, commit title, author and pull request. All proto changes are additive.
- **bytebase-action.** Reads the commit SHA, source branch, commit title, author and pull request from GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Bitbucket Pipelines and Azure Pipelines, from environment variables and GitHub's event payload only. `--source-title`, `--source-url`, `--source-author` and `--source-ref` cover ot

title: fix(pg,cockroachdb,redshift)!: quote the host, port and sign-in values in the connection string
body:
## Summary

The PostgreSQL, CockroachDB and Redshift drivers paste a data source's host, port and sign-in values into a pgx keyword/value connection string without quoting them. pgx ends an unquoted value at whitespace, reads the rest as more keywords, and keeps the last value of each. So a port of `5432 host=other.example.com` connects to `other.example.com`, while the instance still shows the host it was given. This was found while designing admin changes over MCP (BYT-9292). A confirmation form there will show the host and port the user approves, and it must show where Bytebase really connects.

- `util.QuotePGValue` trims a value and quotes it, escaping `'` and `\`. The fields that hold one value now go through it: the host and port for PostgreSQL, CockroachDB and Redshift; the host, port, user and IAM token for RDS sign-in; the user for Cloud SQL sign-in; and CockroachDB's routing option.
- `util.PGHostPort` builds the host and port, and refuses a blank host or port. Quoted, an empty host would make pgx use its default, a Unix socket directory on the Bytebase server, and an empty port would make it use 5432.
- Extra connection parameters are unchanged. They are written in libpq syntax, and a test pins that a value quoted that way still arrives unquoted.

## Breaking Changes

- A stored host or port that carries options stops connecting, such as a port of `5432 sslmode=require` or a host followed by more keywords. The console's port field takes digits only, but its host field, the API and Terraform take any text.
- A blank or whitespace-only port is refused. PostgreSQL and CockroachDB already refused an empty one, but a port of only spaces connected to 5432, and so did a Redshift data source with no port.
- Surrounding whitespace in a value is still ignored, as before.

## Notes for review

- This PR keeps each host, port and sign-in field one value. An extra parameter can still set any keyword, host and port included, as on main. So the server can still be made to open a file path that a caller names: pgx opens the `sslrootcert`, `sslcert`, `sslkey`, `passfile` and `servicefile` paths while it parses.
- `TestCloudSQLIAMDialerClosesWhenOpenFails` made `Open` fail with a username containing spaces, which failed only because of this defect. It now uses a NUL byte, which pgx refuses anywhere in a connection string, and still checks that the connector closes. `TestGetCloudSQLConnectionConfigKeepsTheUserWhole` covers the username with spaces.
- Other engines do not build a pgx keyword/value string and are not checked here.

## Test plan

- [x] `TestGetPGConnectionConfigKeepsEachValueWhole`: a port naming another host, or a CA file, fails to parse; a host carrying options stays one host; a blank host or port is refused; an extra parameter keeps libpq syntax. All but the whitespace and libpq cases fail on main.
- [x] `TestGetRDSConnectionConfigKeepsTheUserWhole` and `TestGetCloudSQLConnectionConfigKeepsTheUserWhole`, offline with fake credentials: t

title: fix(iam)!: validate every binding that gains a member
body:
## Summary

`SetIamPolicy` validated only the bindings whose role and condition were new. A binding whose role and condition matched a stored one skipped every check, even when the request added members to it. So, with a maximum role expiration set, a member added to a stored binding could carry an expiry past the maximum, or none at all. In SaaS mode, `allUsers` could be added to a stored binding although a new binding refuses it. This was found while designing admin changes over MCP (BYT-9292), where a confirmed role grant goes through this check.

- A binding is now validated when it gains a member. Stored members are converted to the request's form (`users/…` to `user:…`) before the comparison.
- The comparison runs inside the write's row lock, through `ValidateReplaced`, against the policy the write replaces. A policy read before the write could change before the write landed. Both the project and the workspace handler use it, and the project handler now returns the check's own status, as the workspace handler already did.
- `allUsers` is checked among the added members only. A binding that already holds it can still keep, lose or gain other members.
- A binding sent back as it was stored, or with fewer members, is not validated again. A policy saved as it was keeps saving, even when a stored binding no longer meets today's rules.
- Bindings are matched by a struct of role and condition. A missing condition now matches an empty one, as the converters store and return them. A condition can no longer match another binding's through their joined text, which let a crafted condition replace a stored one with no check.
- Project and workspace `SetIamPolicy` share the check. As before, the condition and expiry checks apply to project bindings only.

## Breaking Changes

- With a maximum role expiration set, adding a member to a stored project binding for any role but project owner is refused when the binding's expiry exceeds the maximum or it has none. Before, the member joined with the old expiry, or with none. Granting the member a binding within the maximum still works, and the console's member form already asks for an expiry within the maximum.
- In SaaS mode, adding `allUsers` to a stored binding is refused, as it already was for a new binding.
- Both reach every caller of `SetIamPolicy`: the console, the API and Terraform.

## Notes for review

- An approved role request writes through `store.PatchIamPolicy` and does not run this check. Its expiry is checked when the issue is created. Not changed here.
- A stored binding with no condition, as workspace creation and `PatchWorkspaceIamPolicy` write it, now matches the empty condition `GetIamPolicy` returns for it. Sending it back no longer validates it in full.
- The handlers no longer read the policy before the write. The check reads it under the lock.

## Test plan

- [x] `TestBindingsGainingMembersAreValidated` (pure, no database): a stored binding sent back as it was, or losing a member, sa

title: feat(review): keep a standard rule finding's thread across runs
body:
## Summary

Fixes BYT-10385. Every completed rule review run resolved all earlier results of its reviewer and posted all of its findings again. A re-run, whether from a SQL edit, Run checks, or a stale approval input, therefore resolved threads people were discussing, and brought back as new OPEN threads findings a person had already resolved. Those new threads held the rollout again.

Now a finding the run reports again keeps its thread and is not posted twice:

| Earlier result | Next run | Result |
|---|---|---|
| OPEN or resolved by a person | reports it again | kept: state, replies, and `updated_at`; its anchor moves to the statement in the SQL the run reviewed |
| any state | no longer reports it | resolved and marked superseded, as before |
| superseded | reports it again | a new OPEN thread |
| — | a new finding | a new OPEN thread |

**Backend**
- **Fingerprint** (`rule_review.go`): a hash of the spec, engine, rule, and databases, plus three things from omni (bytebase/omni#620, bytebase/omni#624, bumped in #21887):
  - the finding's codes, such as `WH101`;
  - its statement's body, the statement without the blank lines and comments around it;
  - the finding's range within that body.

  The message is left out, so omni rewording it keeps the thread. Editing other statements, inserting lines, or adding a comment above the statement also keeps it; editing the statement itself, or changing its databases, makes a new finding. Two findings of one code in one statement, such as `x = NULL OR y = NULL`, stay apart by where they stand, and identical statements by their order. It is stored in the store proto's `ReviewMetadata.fingerprint`, not in the v1 API.
- **Reconciliation** (`CompleteReviewRun`): in the existing completion transaction. A re-run does not stop the execution it supersedes, so two completions of one slot can overlap. Each locks every root it may update, in primary-key order, before updating any, so they cannot deadlock.
- **Anchors follow their statement:** a kept result takes the anchor of the result that repeats it. Equal fingerprints mean equal statement text, so the thread moves to the same statement in the SQL the run reviewed.
  - Without this, a kept thread stayed anchored on an earlier sheet, and the editor only places a thread where its lines are byte for byte the same.
  - Appending a statement adds a newline to the old last line, so that line's open finding dropped out of the editor while it still held the rollout.
  - The "immutable after creation" note on `statement_anchor` now names this exception, in both protos.
- **Run record:** each DONE run posts a creatorless `ReviewRunCompletion` event with its attempt and how many results it posted, kept, and superseded. Each result carries the `attempt` of the run that posted it, and a kept result keeps its attempt. Both are added to the v1 `IssueComment` as output-only fields. A FAILED run records nothing, as before.
- **AI review:** its results carry no fingerprint, so a

title: perf(export): mask exports once and cut SharePoint export round trips
body:
Exporting a masked column could produce a different value than SQL Editor shows, and SharePoint exports spent most of their time waiting on Graph round trips. This PR fixes the first and cuts the second.

## Masking applied twice

`queryRetry` already masks the results, and `doExport` masked them again. Masking is not idempotent for every algorithm: an MD5-masked column was exported as the hash of its hash. For example, Query returned `9bdabc…` while the export of the same statement held `e96007…`. Export now masks once, which also saves 0.2–0.4 s on large exports. `TestSQLExportMatchesQueryMasking` exports an MD5-masked column and compares it with the Query result; it fails without the fix.

## Fewer Graph round trips per SharePoint export

Each export used to make three sequential Graph calls before uploading anything: resolve the destination URL (about 0.4 s), create the export folder (about 0.5 s), then upload the files.

- Files are uploaded by path (`<destination>:/<folder>/<file>`), so the first upload creates the export folder. The returned folder link is built from the destination's web URL.
- `Client.ResolveRecent` reuses a resolution of the same URL made within the last minute, so a batch export resolves its destination once. Saving a project destination still calls `Resolve`, which always asks Graph.
- If SharePoint rejects an upload into a reused resolution as not found or inaccessible, `Upload` drops the cached resolution, resolves the URL again and retries once, so a folder recreated at the same URL still receives the export.
- Upload sessions send 20 MiB chunks instead of 5 MiB. Each chunk pays a fixed round trip; larger chunks measured no faster and resend more after a stalled request.

ADR 0007 is amended for the one-minute reuse. Three behaviors change:

- **Rename:** for up to a minute after the destination folder is renamed, an export uploads into the renamed folder and returns a link to the old path.
- **Empty folder:** a failed upload can leave an empty export folder, since the first upload creates it. A rejected request creates nothing, so a missing or inaccessible destination still reports that nothing was uploaded.
- **Name collision:** an export folder name that collides with an existing file reads as "destination not found". The random export ID in the name makes this practically impossible.

## Expected effect

These figures come from prototypes of the same changes, timed against a real SharePoint tenant from a client with high latency to Microsoft Graph (medians of interleaved runs). Absolute times will be lower closer to Microsoft's region. The large-export prototype also had a per-chunk stall timeout that this PR does not include; on its own it showed no measurable gain.

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Single 1 MB export | 2.3 s | 1.1 s |
| 10-database batch (still serial) | 20.5 s | 9.6 s |
| 120 MB export | 29.3 s | 18.8 s |
| 241 MB export | 43.4 s | 31.8 s |
| 482 MB export | 84.2 s | 66.9 s |

title: fix(mcp)!: correct misleading MCP tool text and name the session's workspace
body:
## Summary

Four pieces of MCP tool text misled an agent in the UCG-1 baseline run (BYT-10295). Each now says what the product does (BYT-9292).

- **Masking exemption form.** It said "Unmasked in query and export results". In the run, the user accepted it on a workspace with no masking configured, where the exemption changed nothing at the time. The effect line now reads "Bypasses masking here, with no expiry; adds no masking.", and the tool description says the member bypasses the masking that applies to the covered data, including masking set up later, and that an exemption does not set up masking itself. - **`get_schema` row count.** It reported the last metadata sync's estimate as `rowCount`. On tables loaded just before the sync it read 0, and the agent told the user the masking could not be tested with a query; the tables hold 1,000 and 9,488 rows. title: fix(mcp): name what MCP cannot do in search_api
body:
## Summary

`search_api` used to leave out every operation no MCP mode serves, and said nothing about it. This PR makes discovery name what MCP cannot do, why, and where to do it instead: the Bytebase console (BYT-9292). It is stacked on #21863.

- **Why.** In the UCG-1 baseline run (BYT-10295), `search_api(service="SettingService")` answered "No endpoints found for service: SettingService", which reads as "Bytebase has no settings". The agent guessed an operation that does not exist, never met the refusal that names the console, and never learned that workload identities exist. Detail mode was inconsistent the other way: asked for a hidden operation by ID, it returned the full schema with no word that MCP refuses it.
- **The service list** gains a "Not available over MCP" section: each service no MCP session can call, with its description and the gate's reasons. Workload identities appear there as "manages workload identities for external CI/CD integrations".
- **A service listing** adds the operations no MCP session can call, grouped by the gate's reason. A service with none served says so.
- **Detail mode** on such an operation gives the reason and no schema.
- **`GetSetting`** names the four settings an MCP session reads and says the user's own permissions still apply, from the same list the gate enforces. It also says that a setting the workspace has never saved answers "setting ... not found", and that the built-in semantic types `bb.default` and `bb.default-partial` always exist although the read does not list them. A new workspace saves no semantic types, so without this an agent would report that the workspace has none.
- **Bytes fields** show as `string (base64-encoded bytes)`. An agent got a 400 sending `CheckRelease`'s statement as plain text.

These operations are still never offered: they stay out of the served listings and the keyword index, and the listings and detail mode never show their schema. They still resolve by operation ID, so `call_api` meets the gate's refusal. The tool description says the results name what no MCP session can do, whatever the workspace's MCP mode and the user's permissions.

## Notes for review

- **One source for the reasons.** The reason-to-sentence table moves verbatim from `backend/api/v1/mcp_gate.go` to `backend/api/auth/mcp_denial.go`, beside `MCPClassIsRefused`, which lives in `auth` because the gate and the index must agree. The gate's refusal text does not change; its fallback wording stays pinned by literal strings. `git diff --color-moved` shows the move.
- `auth` reads both MCP annotations of a procedure in one call, and returns the readable settings as resource names for the gate and for search.
- Claude Code shows the model a tool's `structuredContent` and drops its text when both exist. `search_api` returns text only, so the text is what the model reads.
- "Unknown service" and "Unknown operationId" make no claim that Bytebase lacks the name. Lookups match exactly, so a qualified name su

body:
## Summary

An MCP session can now read four workspace settings through `SettingService/GetSetting`: the approval rules (`WORKSPACE_APPROVAL`), the environments (`ENVIRONMENT`), the semantic types (`SEMANTIC_TYPES`) and the data classification (`DATA_CLASSIFICATION`). This holds in Read-only and Read-write. Every other setting, `ListSettings` and every settings write stay refused (BYT-9292).

- **Why.** In the UCG-1 baseline run (BYT-10295), an agent asked to set up approvals could not read the approval rules, so it never saw the default Fallback Rule. Its plan, applied to a fresh workspace, still made changes in test wait for the project owner.
- **The user's own permissions still apply.** The gate checks only the setting name. The handler already checks a permission for each setting: `ENVIRONMENT` needs `bb.settings.getEnvironment`, which workspace members hold, and the other three need `bb.settings.get`, which only Workspace Admin and DBA hold. A member's agent reads the environments and gets the handler's permission error for the rest. `GetSetting`'s permission line now names the permission for each setting, because `search_api` shows it to agents.
- **No masking salt.** A semantic type with MD5 masking carries a salt, which keeps masked values from being enumerated offline. `GetSetting` blanks it for an MCP session. The console still receives it, because its semantic-type editor writes the whole setting back; BOT-78 tracks blanking it for every caller, with the stored salt carried forward on update.
- **Every other setting name is refused at the gate**, with a reason that lists the four readable settings. The list lives in `backend/api/auth`.
- **The in-console agent still asks first.** It runs every READ method without asking, but a console call reaches neither the four-setting rule nor the salt strip. title: fix(deps): pin the pgx fork at its master tip
body:
Dependency hygiene only. Two lines of `go.mod` / `go.sum`, no code change.

The pin named `d3c6cdda`, the v5.12.0 rebase, which is an **ancestor** of the fork's
`master` rather than its tip. Pinning an ancestor still resolves, but it means the
default branch and the shipped commit can drift: a later rebase would start from
whatever `master` happens to be, not from what Bytebase runs. This points the pin at
`master`'s tip so those are the same commit.

## This changes no code

- `diff -r` between the two module trees in the module cache is **empty**.
- Both fork patches are present at the new pin: `ColumnTypePrecisionScale`
  (`stdlib/sql.go:704`) and the timestamptz session `TimeZone` conversion
  (`stdlib/sql.go:857`).
- `TestConvertValueTimestampFromDriver` passes unchanged, including its
  `Zone == "CST"` / `Offset == 28800` assertions. Nothing in the test suite moved.

The fork's `master` reached this state via bytebase/pgx#4, which reverted
bytebase/pgx#3 so that `master` matches the shipped commit again.

## Not in this PR

The v5.11 → v5.12 upgrade itself already landed in #21840. This PR adds no new
dependency version.

Removing the fork's time zone patch — and with it, deciding where `timestamptz`
should be rendered — is deliberately **not** here. That design question is open, and
the POSIX `TimeZone` failure behind it is real and still unfixed: an instance whose
session `TimeZone` is `+08:00` or `EST5EDT,M3.2.0/2,M11.1.0/2` fails every
`timestamptz` read, because the patch calls `time.LoadLocation` on that string. It is
pre-existing, not a regression, and it belongs with the time zone work.

## Verification

- `gofmt` clean; `golangci-lint` v2.15.0 → `0 issues`; server build OK.
- `./backend/store/...` and `./backend/plugin/db/{pg,redshift,cockroachdb}` pass.
- The four `backend/tests` sample-instance tests pass.

title: fix(deps): update go-redis to v9.23.0, keeping its new defaults off
body:
Updates `github.com/redis/go-redis/v9` from v9.21.0 to v9.23.0, keeps two of the new release's defaults off, and fixes the SQL editor's "Run commands on: All nodes" option, which returned no rows.

`backend/plugin/db/redis` is the only package that imports go-redis, so the bump reaches nothing else.

## Compatibility with existing Redis servers

The driver was driven against real servers, comparing **this branch against `main` as it ships today** (go-redis v9.21.0 with the current driver) rather than only swapping the library. 43 scenarios pass on both, and the only difference anywhere is the ALL_NODES row count below, which is the bug fix.

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Servers | Redis 3.2, 4.0, 5.0, 6.0, 6.2, 7.0, 7.2, 7.4, 8.0, 8.10; Valkey 7.2 and 8; KeyDB; Dragonfly |
| Topologies | standalone; Sentinel with three sentinels, master auth and a forced failover; a real cluster of three masters each with a replica |
| Transports | plain TCP; TLS encrypt-without-verify (the data-source default), TLS verified against a custom CA, and mutual TLS with a client certificate; SSH tunnel |
| Auth | none, `requirepass`, ACL user and password, an ACL user without administrative rights, and a wrong password or unknown CA still rejected |
| Managed-provider shapes | `CONFIG` removed with `rename-command`, exercising the sync's fail-open path |
| Behavior | non-zero DB selection asserted against the server's own `-n <db> DBSIZE`, `redis.Nil` rendered as NULL, per-command `WRONGTYPE` preserved, `TTL`/`TYPE`/`LRANGE`/`HGETALL` rendering, 700 KiB value, multi-MiB pipelines in both directions, version and database discovery |
| Load | 30 concurrent open/ping/execute/query/close requests against `maxclients 40`, no failures |

On the cluster, a 60-key pipeline spans all three masters, so go-redis splits it per node; the replies still come back in the order the statements were written. A sentinel failover was forced and the same driver followed the promotion and resumed reading and writing immediately.

`HELLO` only exists from Redis 6, and v9.23.0 leaves the `HELLO` → legacy `AUTH` → RESP2 fallback unchanged, so the pre-6 servers behave as they did.

The matrix was run against stock v9.23.0 as well, before the two options below were set, so the bump on its own is not what either of them guards against: the new pipeline pool runs the same `initConn` handshake, and pipelined writes still landed in the configured database rather than DB 0 on every server. The options are about cost and failover timing, not correctness.

## Pipelines stay on the main pool

v9.22.0 ([redis/go-redis#4002](https://github.com/redis/go-redis/pull/4002)) gives every client a dedicated pipeline connection pool. `Execute` and `QueryConn` both use `Pipelined`, so it applies to every Redis query and change task. A driver is opened per request and runs a single pipeline on it, so the second pool has no contention to relieve and only adds a connection and its handshake:

+// RedisClusterSlots is the number of hash slots a Redis cluster partitions keys
+// into; the single node getRedisClusterContainer starts owns all of them.
+const RedisClusterSlots = 16384
+
+// getRedisClusterContainer starts a one-node Redis cluster. Cluster clients
+// follow the addresses CLUSTER SLOTS reports, so the node is told to announce
+// the host-mapped address rather than its address inside Docker, which a test
+// outside Docker cannot reach.
+func getRedisClusterContainer(ctx context.Context) (retC *Container, retErr error) {
+	c, err := start(ctx, testcontainers.ContainerRequest{
+		Image: "redis:7.2-alpine",
+		Cmd: []string{
+			"redis-server", "--cluster-enabled", "yes",
+			"--cluster-config-file", "/tmp/nodes.conf", "--cluster-node-timeout", "5000",
+		},
+		WaitingFor: wait.ForLog("Ready to accept connections").WithStartupTimeout(3 * time.Minute),
+	}, spec{port: "6379/tcp"})
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, err
+	}
+	defer func() {
+		if retErr != nil {
+			c.Close(ctx)
+		}
+	}()
+
+	if _, err := redisCLI(ctx, c, "config", "set", "cluster-announce-ip", c.host); err != nil {
+		return nil, err
+	}
+	if _, err := redisCLI(ctx, c, "config", "set", "cluster-announce-port", c.port); err != nil {
+		return nil, err
+	}
+	if _, err := redisCLI(ctx, c, "cluster", "addslotsrange", "0", strconv.Itoa(RedisClusterSlots-1)); err != nil {
+		return nil, err
+	}
+	// Owning every slot is not enough on its own: the node reports state fail
+	// until its cluster cron has taken the new slots into account.
+	ticker := time.NewTicker(200 * time.Millisecond)
+	defer ticker.Stop()
+	timeout := time.After(2 * time.Minute)
+	for {
+		info, err := redisCLI(ctx, c, "cluster", "info")
+		if err != nil {
+			return nil, err
+		}
+		if strings.Contains(info, "cluster_state:ok") {
+			return c, nil
+		}
+		select {
+		case <-ticker.C:
+		case <-timeout:
+			return nil, errors.Errorf("redis cluster did not reach state ok: %s", info)
+		case <-ctx.Done():
+			return nil, ctx.Err()
+		}
+	}
+}
+
+// redisCLI runs redis-cli inside the container, which keeps the cluster
+// bootstrap off the host and out of this package's dependencies. Exec output is
+// a multiplexed Docker stream, so Multiplexed decodes it into plain text.
+func redisCLI(ctx context.Context, c *Container, args ...string) (string, error) {
+	code, reader, err := c.container.Exec(ctx, append([]string{"redis-cli"}, args...), tcexec.Multiplexed())
+	if err != nil {
+		return "", errors.Wrapf(err, "exec redis-cli %s", strings.Join(args, " "))
+	}
+	out, err := io.ReadAll(reader)
+	if err != nil {
+		return "", errors.Wrapf(err, "read redis-cli %s output", strings.Join(args, " "))
+	}
+	if code != 0 {
+		return "", errors.Errorf("redis-cli %s exited %d: %s", strings.Join(args, " "), code, out)
+	}
+	return string(out), nil
+}

title: feat(review): switch a dev build between SQL Review V1 and V2
body: ## Summary On a dev build SQL Review V2 replaces V1: the workspace SQL Review page only shows the V2 standard rules, and the plan checks skip V1's SQL review on every engine V2 covers. So a fresh local workspace had no way to test V1. This adds a V1/V2 switch to the workspace SQL Review page, on dev builds only. ## Changes 1. **Plan checks (`backend/runner/plancheck`)**: under `Profile.SQLReviewV2` (dev builds), V1's SQL review advice is skipped only where the project's effective review rule policy leaves a standard rule on. A project whose standard rules are all off gets V1's advice, as on a release build. The rule review already completes with no findings for such a project, so the same SQL is never reviewed by both. Release builds are unchanged, since V2 is off there. 2. **Workspace SQL Review page**: on the Vite dev server (`isDev()`), a "SQL Review version" switch sits above the page. After a confirmation: - **V1** saves the workspace standard rules with every rule off, so the plan checks run V1. - **V2** turns every workspace standard rule on, as a new workspace has. - The browser's choice goes to localStorage, which `sqlReviewV2Enabled()` now reads, and the page reloads, since the gate is read outside React state. - V1 review configs are left as they are; while V2 is on, the plan checks ignore them. ## Notes for reviewers - Everything is behind the dev-build switches. `isDev()` is a build-time constant, so a release bundle never renders the switch or reads the stored choice, and the backend change only runs under `Profile.SQLReviewV2`. - Side effects on dev builds: - Turning every rule off on the V2 page now also hands that project to V1. - A project that customizes its own standard rules stays on V2 after switching to V1. - Switching to V1 does not lift V2's rollout hold: open threads still hold the automatic rollout. - Switching overwrites the workspace's standard rule selection; switching back to V2 turns every rule on. ## Test plan - [x] `go test ./backend/runner/plancheck/`, with the new `TestCombinedExecutorHandsSQLReviewToV1WhereEveryRuleIsOff` (workspace rules all off → V1; a project's own rules win; a list without SYNTAX counts as off). - [x] `pnpm --dir frontend test`: 684 files, 8435 tests, including the new `SQLReviewVersionSwitch.test.tsx` and `featureGates.test.ts` cases. - [x] golangci-lint reports nothing in the changed files; the server builds. - [x] Browser, dev backend with a dev-mode frontend bundle: with V2, `DELETE FROM t;` gets a standard rule finding and the plan checks have no SQL review advice. After switching to V1, the same SQL gets V1's ERROR from the V1 config attached to the environment. Switching back turns all 11 rules on. - [x] `plan-detail/plan-detail-checks.spec.ts` on the release-like e2e build (`build-server.sh`, V1): 6/6 passed, so the V1 path is unchanged. ## Screenshots | V2 (default) | Switch to V1 | | --- | --- | |

i18next/react-i18next (react-i18next) ### [`v17.1.10`](https://redirect.github.com/i18next/react-i18next/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#17110) [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/i18next/react-i18next/compare/v17.1.9...v17.1.10) - fix(Trans): markup inside an interpolated value is no longer parsed as translation markup. `Trans` interpolates `values` (and `count`, values in `tOptions`, or the whole string when there are no children) before it parses the string. With `interpolation.escapeValue: false`, or with an i18nFormat plugin (i18next-icu, i18next-mf2, i18next-fluent), which inserts values without escaping whatever `escapeValue` says, a value like `<0 href="https://example.com">x` was rendered as component 0 with that `href`, overriding the props of the component, and `x` in a value became a real ``. `Trans` now escapes the values for this `t()` call (with a plugin, the string values in `values`) and decodes the entities after parsing, so such a value renders as text, and a `"` in a value no longer closes an attribute like ``. `{{- var}}` stays the explicit way for a translator to insert a value unescaped. As with `shouldUnescape`, entities written in these translations (for example `&`) are now decoded instead of shown literally. Output with `escapeValue: true` and no plugin, with i18next-icu `escapeVariables: true`, and with children and no `values` or `count` is unchanged. - fix(IcuTrans): the same for `IcuTrans` with `escapeValue: false` or an i18nFormat plugin: a value like `<0>x` no longer becomes the first component, and a value containing an entity like `&` is no longer decoded a second time.

title: fix(deps): migrate to opensearch-go v5 and disable its new node discovery
body:
Updates `github.com/opensearch-project/opensearch-go` from v4.8.1 to v5.1.3, and migrates the call sites, since Go treats major versions as distinct modules.

Renovate opened this as a one-line `require` addition, which left every import on `/v4`: the binary kept using v4 and `go mod tidy` removed v5 again as unused, which is what failed `go-tests`.

## The important finding: v5 abandons the endpoint it was given

`opensearchapi.NewClient` in v5 injects a default router, and `opensearch.NewClient` then turns on node discovery, unless told otherwise. v4 did neither. The client calls `GET /_nodes/http` and from then on sends requests to each node's **published** address rather than the address it was configured with.

This driver builds the OpenSearch client only for `AWS_RDS_IAM` authentication, i.e. only against managed domains, where a single endpoint fronts the nodes. There the published addresses are not reachable from outside, and SigV4 is bound to the configured host, so the discovered addresses are wrong twice over.

Reproduced against a container started with `http.publish_host` set to an unroutable address, which is how a fronted domain looks to a client:

| client | result |
| --- | --- |
| v4.8.1 | passes in 1.5s |
| v5.1.3 defaults | **blocks 133s**, then `dial tcp 10.255.255.1:9200: connect: connection timed out` |
| v5.1.3 + the guard in this PR | passes in 1.5s |

A healthy local single node hides this, because it publishes a reachable address. The guard is two lines on `opensearch.Config` (`DiscoverNodesOnStart: new(false)`, `DiscoverNodesInterval: -1` — `0` now means 30s whenever a router is in use), and it was mutation-checked by removing it and watching the failure return.

### Configuring host and port does not prevent it

Worth stating explicitly, because it is the natural assumption: the configured address is the *seed* discovery bootstraps from, not a pin. Discovery is not a fallback for an address the operator left unset — this driver always builds `Addresses` from `DataSource.Host` and `DataSource.Port`, so there is no unset case. With a fully specified host and port, v5 still replaced it:

| case (host and port always explicitly configured) | `_nodes/http` | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| v5 defaults, nodes API answers | asked once | **fails**, dials the published `10.255.255.1:9200` |
| v5 defaults, nodes API refused `403` | asked once | ok in 30ms, keeps the configured address |
| v5 + the guard in this PR | never asked | ok in 10ms |

So the breakage is conditional on whether the domain answers the nodes API, not on how completely it was configured. A domain whose credentials lack `cluster:monitor/nodes/info` is unaffected, because discovery fails and the seed is kept. Which behavior a given managed domain has was not determined here, and that uncertainty is the argument for the guard: the bad branch costs a multi-minute hang on every connection, and the guard removes the question for two lines.

title: test(frontend): cut 92k pointless fake-timer ticks from the clock test
body:
Preventive follow-up to the two cases cut earlier today (`mssql-plan` at 3073ms, `ToolCallCard` at 1684ms, both now on main): sweep the rest of the suite for cases slow enough to time out when the shared runner is loaded, and cut the ones whose cost buys nothing.

Swept all 676 files / 8384 cases with `vitest run --reporter=json` on a **genuinely idle** box (load 0.59, both CI runners at 0% — the first such window in this session; earlier attempts sat at load 35–91 and were discarded).

## What the sweep found

38 cases exceed 1.5s on an idle box, but **only one is an oversized fixture**. The rest split into two classes that a fixture trim cannot touch, so this PR changes one case and explains the others.

The classes are separable by measurement, not guesswork: re-running candidates under heavy foreign load (runners at 1701%) shows sleep-bound cases pinned to their wall-clock wait while CPU-bound ones inflate ~5x.

| case | idle | under load | class |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `AgentChat` "Issue comment editor never receives the draft" | 3100ms | 3069ms | sleep-bound (flat) |
| `AgentChat` "existing access drawer rejects the draft" | 3085ms | 3078ms | sleep-bound (flat) |
| `authInterceptor` "startup exhaustion … (silent=false)" | 1519ms | 1516ms | sleep-bound (flat) |
| `authInterceptor` "startup exhaustion … (silent=true)" | 1518ms | 1512ms | sleep-bound (flat) |
| `useTimeReading` "deadline beyond the platform timer ceiling" | 778ms | 4055ms | CPU-bound (5.2x) |
| `domTree` "drops plain text … when the tree budget is hit" | 1161ms | 5528ms | CPU-bound (4.8x) |

A case dominated by real `setTimeout` sleeps does not stretch under contention, so it is not a timeout risk however long it looks.

## Fixed

| case | isolated before | isolated after | in-suite before | in-suite after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `useTimeReading.test.tsx` "waits quietly for a deadline beyond the platform timer ceiling" | 620ms | **170ms** | 778ms | **312ms** |

The clock re-arms every `RESYNC_MS` (60s) however far the deadline is, so a 90-day deadline made `advanceTimersByTime` drive **129,600** `tick()` iterations to assert one render. A day past the 32-bit ceiling is still past it and needs 37,231. Peak observed before the fix was 4055ms under contention.

**Mutation-checked:** removing the `Math.min(..., RESYNC_MS)` clamp fails this case both before and after the change, on `expect(setTimeout).not.toHaveBeenCalled()` (setTimeout fires 1000 times without the clamp). The assertions are unchanged.

## Deliberately left

**Sleep-bound — load-insensitive, so not timeout risks.** The waits are production behavior, not fixtures:
- `AgentChat` ×3 (3100 / 3085 / 1532ms): `waitForDeliveredIssueCommentDraft` and `waitForDeliveredAccessDraft` poll `60 × 50ms = 3000ms` before giving up; these cases cover the give-up path, so they must exhaust it.
- `authInterceptor` ×2 (1519 / 1518ms): `STARTUP_RETRY_DELAY_MS` 250 × attempts (1+2) × 2 outages = 1500ms of real backoff.

title: fix(sync): refuse a schema dump read from an older state
body:
## The lost update

`GetDatabaseSchema` serves `db_schema.raw_dump`, and only the schema syncer writes
it. `UpsertDBSchema` row-locks its own write but stamps no version, so whichever
sync commits last owns the dump — however old the schema it read.

Two syncs routinely overlap. A migration task runs its own
`SyncDatabaseSchemaToHistory` as soon as the statement lands, while the queued
syncer drains the database queue on its own tick. When the queued sync's live read
predates the migration and its write commits after the task's, the stored dump
reverts to the pre-migration schema while the task is `DONE`. Outside tests that
leaves the database's schema view a revision behind until something syncs it again
— with no sync interval configured, a manual sync.

`TestTenantBackfill` hit this as a flake, fixed on the test side in #21831. This is
the product-side follow-up that PR named.

## The guard

`db_schema.synced_at timestamptz` records when the sync that produced `metadata`
and `raw_dump` *started reading* the live database — `doSyncDatabaseSchema` takes
the timestamp immediately before `driver.SyncDBSchema` and `driver.Dump`, not when
the row is written, so it describes the age of the schema in that same row.

The conflict clause then refuses a write whose read predates the stored one:

```sql
ON CONFLICT(instance, db_name) DO UPDATE SET ...
WHERE db_schema.synced_at IS NULL OR db_schema.synced_at <= EXCLUDED.synced_at
```

- **Existing rows** are backfilled from `db.metadata`'s `lastSyncTime` where it is
  set, and left `NULL` otherwise, which the predicate treats as older than
  anything. The column is nullable rather than `NOT NULL DEFAULT now()`: a default
  would stamp every pre-existing row with the upgrade time, which is neither when
  that schema was read nor anything the deployment recorded. Details below.
- **A refused write** returns `(false, nil)`, not an error. It is an ordinary
  outcome — the row already holds a newer schema — and the only caller logs it at
  debug. Equal stamps still store: "not older" rather than "strictly newer", so a
  second read within the same microsecond is not thrown away.
- **Clock skew** is the known limit. The stamp is a wall clock, so two stamps are
  only comparable to within the skew between the nodes that took them. The overlap
  this fixes is same-process in the common case (the migration task's sync against
  the syncer's queue), so a `nextval` sequence was not worth the extra round trip
  per sync and the new sequence object.

### How existing rows are treated

The migration backfills `synced_at` from `db.metadata`'s `lastSyncTime`, joined on
the whole key of both tables:

```sql
UPDATE db_schema
SET synced_at = LEAST((db.metadata ->> 'lastSyncTime')::timestamptz, now())
FROM db
WHERE db.instance = db_schema.instance
  AND db.name = db_schema.db_name
  AND jsonb_typeof(db.metadata -> 'lastSyncTime') = 'string';
```

A row with a dump and no stamp reads as inconsistent, and `lastSyncTime` is the

+			name TEXT NOT NULL,
+			metadata JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
+			PRIMARY KEY (instance, name)
+		);
+		CREATE TABLE db_schema (
+			instance TEXT NOT NULL,
+			db_name TEXT NOT NULL,
+			raw_dump TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
+			PRIMARY KEY (instance, db_name)
+		);

+			-- fractional digits, more than timestamptz keeps.
+			('prod', 'synced', '{"lastSyncTime":"2026-10-28T04:05:06.123456789Z","syncStatus":"SYNC_STATUS_OK"}'),
+			('prod', 'whole-second', '{"lastSyncTime":"2026-10-28T04:05:06Z"}'),
+			('prod', 'never-synced', '{"syncStatus":"SYNC_STATUS_OK"}'),
+			-- A clock that ran ahead, so the recorded time is in the future.
+			('prod', 'clock-ahead', '{"lastSyncTime":"2099-01-01T00:00:00Z"}'),
+			-- Same database name in another instance: db_schema is keyed by
+			-- (instance, db_name) and the backfill joins on the whole key.
+			('staging', 'synced', '{"lastSyncTime":"2026-10-20T01:02:03Z"}');

+			('prod', 'synced', 'prod dump'),

+			('prod', 'never-synced', 'unstamped dump'),
+			('prod', 'clock-ahead', 'clock ahead dump'),

+	require.NoError(t, err)

+		databaseName string

+	}{
+		{instance: "prod", databaseName: "synced", want: "2026-10-28T04:05:06.123457Z"},
+		{instance: "prod", databaseName: "whole-second", want: "2026-10-28T04:05:06Z"},
+		{instance: "prod", databaseName: "never-synced"},
+		{instance: "prod", databaseName: "clock-ahead", wantClamped: true},

+			tc.instance, tc.databaseName).Scan(&syncedAt))

This PR contains the following updates:

| Package | Change | [Age](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | [Confidence](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) |
|---|---|---|---|
| [react-arborist](https://react-arborist.netlify.app) ([source](https://redirect.github.com/jameskerr/react-arborist)) | [`^3.5.0` → `^4.0.0`](https://renovatebot.com/diffs/npm/react-arborist/3.16.0/4.0.1) | ![age](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/age/npm/react-arborist/4.0.1?slim=true) | ![confidence](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/confidence/npm/react-arborist/3.16.0/4.0.1?slim=true) |

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>jameskerr/react-arborist (react-arborist)</summary>

### [`v4.0.1`](https://redirect.github.com/jameskerr/react-arborist/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#Version-401)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/jameskerr/react-arborist/compare/v4.0.0...v4.0.1)

**Fixes**

- Dragging no longer makes the drag preview lag behind the pointer: hovers reach the store at most once per animation frame, and only rows whose drop highlight changes re-render. (The internal `tree.state.nodes.drag.destinationParentId` / `destinationIndex` fields moved to `tree.state.dnd`; use `tree.dragDestinationParent` / `tree.dragDestinationIndex` instead.) ([#​385](https://redirect.github.com/jameskerr/react-arborist/issues/385))

### [`v4.0.0`](https://redirect.github.com/jameskerr/react-arborist/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#Version-400)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/jameskerr/react-arborist/compare/v3.16.0...v4.0.0)

**Breaking Changes**

- `react-dnd` and `react-dnd-html5-backend` are now **peer dependencies** instead of
  bundled dependencies — install them alongside react-arborist (`npm install
  react-arborist react-dnd react-dnd-html5-backend`). This fixes a global singleton
  conflict ([#​319](https://redirect.github.com/jameskerr/react-arborist/issues/319)) where apps that also used react-dnd ended up with two independent
  copies of the library, causing drag-and-drop to silently break or throw "Cannot have
  two HTML5 backends at the same time." Both peers must be v16 (`^16`), and both are
  required even when you pass your own `dndBackend` / `dndManager`, because the drag
  preview calls into `react-dnd-html5-backend` on every drag. react-dnd v16 is ESM-only,
  and react-arborist now ships a single ESM build too (the CommonJS `dist/main` build is
  gone), so `import` and `require` load the same copy instead of two copies with
  separate React contexts. `require("react-arborist")` from CommonJS relies on
  `require(esm)`, unflagged from Node **22.12** — now the `engines.node` floor, which
  package managers check at install time, so installing v4 requires Node ≥ 22.12 even
  for bundler and browser consumers. CommonJS TypeScript projects on Node module
  resolution need `module: "nodenext"` (TypeScript ≥ 5.8) or `"node20"` (TypeScript
  ≥ 5.9); `"node16"` and `"node18"` report TS1479. Jest users must add
  `rea

### Release Notes

### [`v15.0.3`](https://redirect.github.com/markdown-it/markdown-it/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#1503---2026-10-16)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/markdown-it/markdown-it/compare/15.0.2...15.0.3)

##### Changed

- Updated dependencies.

##### Fixed

- Enforce the 999 Unicode code point limit for reference definition labels,
  partially addressing [#​1213](https://redirect.github.com/markdown-it/markdown-it/issues/1213).
- Require whitespace before multiline reference titles.

##### Security

- Fixed quadratic complexity when parsing multiline reference definitions.
- Fixed quadratic complexity when parsing unclosed inline HTML comments,
  processing instructions, declarations and CDATA sections.

### [`v15.0.2`](https://redirect.github.com/markdown-it/markdown-it/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#1502---2026-09-11)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/markdown-it/markdown-it/compare/15.0.1...15.0.2)

##### Security

- Fixed quadratic complexity in smartquotes when quote types don't match, [#​1209](https://redirect.github.com/markdown-it/markdown-it/issues/1209).
  Also limited the smartquotes stack to 1000 unmatched openers.

### [`v15.0.1`](https://redirect.github.com/markdown-it/markdown-it/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#1501---2026-08-27)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/markdown-it/markdown-it/compare/15.0.0...15.0.1)

##### Changed

- doc: replace oxide theme with custom one.

##### Fixed

- Fixed code span parsing after lookaheads for unclosed link and image labels, [#​1201](https://redirect.github.com/markdown-it/markdown-it/issues/1201).
- Preserve spaces in code spans whose content consists only of spaces, [#​1180](https://redirect.github.com/markdown-it/markdown-it/issues/1180).
- Preserve brackets around IPv6 address literals when normalizing links, [#​1204](https://redirect.github.com/markdown-it/markdown-it/issues/1204).

- Fixed quadratic complexity in scheme backscan (inline linkify rule).

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/markdown-it/markdown-it/compare/14.3.3...15.0.0)

- Exposed parser internals classes as static properties on `markdownit`.

title: fix(deps): rebase the pgx fork onto v5.12.0 and update the replacement
body:
Renovate opened this as a bare `require` bump, which was a no-op. Rather than close it, this PR now carries the change that makes the bump real: Renovate's commit is kept as-is and the fork rebase is layered on top.

## Why the version bump alone changed nothing

`go.mod` replaces `github.com/jackc/pgx/v5` with the `bytebase/pgx` fork, and the replacement is **unversioned**, so it shadows every requested version. Bumping the `require` line alone changes nothing a build compiles. The tells were all there: the original diff touched only `go.mod` and not `go.sum` (the upstream module has no `go.sum` entry at all), Snyk reported "No manifest changes detected", and CI went green because nothing differed.

The fork had sat at upstream `1abf7d90` — v5.7.2 era, February 2025 — while the `require` line climbed through v5.7.6, v5.8.0, v5.10.0 and v5.11.0. About 21 months of drift, invisible in every one of those PRs.

## What this does

Rebases the fork onto v5.12.0 ([bytebase/pgx#2](https://github.com/bytebase/pgx/pull/2), merged as a fast-forward onto `master`) and points the replacement at it, so the `require` line and the compiled code finally agree.

The fork keeps its two `stdlib/sql.go` patches, both load-bearing for Postgres/Redshift/CockroachDB query results:

- `ColumnTypePrecisionScale` reports the type modifier as the `scale` for timestamp/timestamptz. `backend/plugin/db/pg/query.go` reads it through `sql.ColumnType.DecimalSize` (`scale == -1 → 6`). Unpatched upstream returns `(0, 0, false)`, which would truncate fractional seconds.
- timestamptz values are converted into the session `TimeZone`. Unpatched, the location comes back as `Local`.

Upstream moved the per-type conversion out of `Rows.Next` into the `rowValueFunc` closures built by `initValueFuncs`; the timezone patch moves with it. `git diff v5.12.0` on the fork is those two patches and nothing else.

## Security

v5.12.0 fixes two high-severity advisories. Neither reaches Bytebase, so this is correctness and currency work rather than an urgent patch:

- **GHSA-j38q-h3ph-jjpq**, SQL injection in simple-protocol batches. Affects all v5 before v5.12.0, so the fork was in range, but it requires `SendBatch`, which this repo never calls.
- **GHSA-95fj-3fxw-g62g**, `require_auth` / `channel_binding=require` bypass. Introduced in v5.9.0, after the version the fork was pinned to.

Worth being explicit about the thing that made the bare bump worse than inert: merging it on its own would have left `go.mod` reading v5.12.0 — the version both advisories are fixed in — while the build kept running v5.7.2-era code.

## Behavior changes in v5.12.0

Checked each documented change against our usage. None applies: no `pgxpool` (the `MinConns` timeout and `Acquire` cancellation changes), no `sslcertmode` / `require_auth` / `channel_binding` configuration (the new `sslcertmode` default `allow` preserves prior behavior), no `NamedArgs`, and no custom `BatchResults` implementation needing the new `Tx` meth

 		require.Equal(t, test.expected, got)
 	}
 }
+
+// TestConvertValueTimestampFromDriver reads timestamps through the driver rather than
+// from a constructed time.Time, covering the two behaviors Bytebase's pgx fork adds and
+// upstream does not: timestamptz values arrive in the session time zone, and
+// ColumnType.DecimalSize reports the column's fractional-second scale. A pgx upgrade
+// that loses either patch fails here instead of silently changing query results.
+func TestConvertValueTimestampFromDriver(t *testing.T) {
+	const (
+		sessionZone   = "Asia/Shanghai"
+		sessionOffset = 8 * 60 * 60
+	)
+
+	ctx := context.Background()
+	_, db := testcontainer.NewPgDatabase(t)
+
+	// SET applies to one session, so hold a single connection for the query.
+	conn, err := db.Conn(ctx)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	defer func() { require.NoError(t, conn.Close()) }()
+	_, err = conn.ExecContext(ctx, "SET TimeZone TO '"+sessionZone+"'")
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+
+	rows, err := conn.QueryContext(ctx, `SELECT
+		'2026-03-04 05:06:07.891234+00'::timestamptz    AS tz_default,
+		'2026-03-04 05:06:07.891234+00'::timestamptz(3) AS tz_scale3,
+		'2026-03-04 05:06:07.891234'::timestamp         AS ts_default`)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	defer rows.Close()
+
+	columnTypes, err := rows.ColumnTypes()
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	require.Len(t, columnTypes, 3)
+
+	require.True(t, rows.Next())
+	dest := make([]any, len(columnTypes))
+	for i, columnType := range columnTypes {
+		dest[i] = makeValueByTypeName(columnType.DatabaseTypeName(), columnType)
+	}
+	require.NoError(t, rows.Scan(dest...))
+	require.NoError(t, rows.Err())
+
+	values := make(map[string]*v1pb.RowValue, len(columnTypes))
+	for i, columnType := range columnTypes {
+		values[columnType.Name()] = convertValue(columnType.DatabaseTypeName(), columnType, dest[i])
+	}
+
+	tzDefault := values["tz_default"].GetTimestampTzValue()
+	require.NotNil(t, tzDefault)
+	require.Equal(t, "CST", tzDefault.Zone)
+	require.EqualValues(t, sessionOffset, tzDefault.Offset)
+	require.EqualValues(t, 6, tzDefault.Accuracy)
+	require.Equal(t, "2026-03-04T05:06:07.891234Z", tzDefault.GoogleTimestamp.AsTime().Format(time.RFC3339Nano))
+
+	// Postgres rounds the fixture's .891234 to .891 for timestamptz(3).
+	tzScale3 := values["tz_scale3"].GetTimestampTzValue()
+	require.NotNil(t, tzScale3)
+	require.Equal(t, "CST", tzScale3.Zone)
+	require.EqualValues(t, sessionOffset, tzScale3.Offset)
+	require.EqualValues(t, 3, tzScale3.Accuracy)
+	require.Equal(t, "2026-03-04T05:06:07.891Z", tzScale3.GoogleTimestamp.AsTime().Format(time.RFC3339Nano))
+
+	// timestamp without time zone carries no zone, so it is not shifted.
+	tsDefault := values["ts_default"].GetTimestampValue()
+	require.NotNil(t, tsDefault)
+	require.EqualValues(t, 6, tsDefault.Accuracy)
+	require.Equal(t, "2026-03-04T05:06:07.891234Z", tsDefault.GoogleTimestamp.AsTime().Format(time.RFC3339Nano))
+}

### [`v15.9.0`](https://redirect.github.com/sql-formatter-org/sql-formatter/releases/tag/v15.9.0): 15.9.0

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/sql-formatter-org/sql-formatter/compare/v15.8.2...v15.9.0)

#### Parsing improvements

- Support `\restrict` and `\unrestrict` commands found in SQL created by `pg_dump` ([#​935](https://redirect.github.com/sql-formatter-org/sql-formatter/issues/935)) (thanks to sophalter)
- Treat a reserved word after `AS` as an alias ([#​801](https://redirect.github.com/sql-formatter-org/sql-formatter/issues/801), [#​972](https://redirect.github.com/sql-formatter-org/sql-formatter/issues/972)) (thanks to Christopher Pruijsen)
- Support `%` as the modulo operator in SingleStoreDB ([#​578](https://redirect.github.com/sql-formatter-org/sql-formatter/issues/578), [#​971](https://redirect.github.com/sql-formatter-org/sql-formatter/issues/971)) (thanks to Max Freedom Pollard)

#### Formatting improvements

- Keep a space when densing `-` before a negative operand (thanks to Sarath Francis)
- Keep spaces around PostgreSQL `OPERATOR()` with `denseOperators` ([#​958](https://redirect.github.com/sql-formatter-org/sql-formatter/issues/958)) (thanks to Sarath Francis)
- Remove extra space after `BETWEEN _ AND _` expression ([#​959](https://redirect.github.com/sql-formatter-org/sql-formatter/issues/959)) (thanks to Sarath Francis)
- Keep DuckDB array-slice colon dense inside `[]` ([#​960](https://redirect.github.com/sql-formatter-org/sql-formatter/issues/960)) (thanks to Vincent Gao)

#### Performance

- Avoid quadratic accumulation when parsing long SQL expression lists ([#​840](https://redirect.github.com/sql-formatter-org/sql-formatter/issues/840), [#​963](https://redirect.github.com/sql-formatter-org/sql-formatter/issues/963)) (thanks to Alex Coleman)

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>i18next/i18next (i18next)</summary>

### [`v26.6.0`](https://redirect.github.com/i18next/i18next/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#2660)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/i18next/i18next/compare/v26.5.12...v26.6.0)

- feat(types): new `strictInterpolationChecks` type option (default `false`). With `strictInterpolationChecks: true` in `CustomTypeOptions`, `t()` needs its options for a string with `{{variables}}`: for `'Hello {{name}}!'`, `t('greeting')` is a type error and `t('greeting', { name })` compiles. Left out, the variable reaches the UI as the raw `{{name}}` placeholder. This applies to string keys, selectors, selector arrays and `getFixedT`, and with `strictKeyChecks` also to `t(key, defaultValue)`. Without the flag nothing changes. With the flag on, a wrapper that passes on a key type (`(key: ParseKeys<'ns'>) => t(key)`, or a generic `K extends ParseKeys`) no longer compiles without options, as the variables of its string are not known there. `parseInterpolation: 'icu'` and `'mf2'` require their arguments as before. Thanks [@​Alex0007](https://redirect.github.com/Alex0007) ([#​2465](https://redirect.github.com/i18next/i18next/pull/2465)).
- fix(types): an array of selectors with a plural member now requires `count`, as a single selector does since v25.9.0. Without `count`, i18next skips the plural member at runtime, so `t([($) => $.item, ($) => $.plain])` returned the `plain` value while typed as the plural forms. An array of selectors with `defaultValue` now returns the literal values and the default value (`'a' | 'b' | 'x'`) instead of `string`. [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/remix-run/react-router/compare/react-router@8.5.0...react-router@8.5.1)

##### Patch Changes

- Fix `URIError: URI malformed` when an `ssr: false` dev server receives a URL path with a malformed percent-encoding ([#​15649](https://redirect.github.com/remix-run/react-router/pull/15649))

- Fix fetcher revalidation errors bubbling to the root error boundary instead of the nearest boundary above the route that owns the fetcher ([#​15676](https://redirect.github.com/remix-run/react-router/pull/15676))

  - Replace the current history entry when the `action` contains characters that get percent-encoded, such as spaces or non-ASCII characters
- Fix an unhandled promise rejection when the browser skips a `viewTransition` navigation, for example in a hidden tab ([#​15582](https://redirect.github.com/remix-run/react-router/pull/15582))
- Bubble rejected `lazy.Component` imports on loader-less routes to the nearest error boundary ([#​15658](https://redirect.github.com/remix-run/react-router/pull/15658))
  - Render the error boundary instead of a blank page

- Add `Workspace` component, for layouts of tabsets that users can rearrange by dragging tabs: between tabsets, within a tabset's list of tabs, or onto the edge of a tabset to split it. title: fix(test): wait for the schema dump in TestTenantBackfill
body:
## Problem

`TestTenantBackfill` reds unrelated PRs. On 2026-11-01 it failed on two dependency bumps
([#21794](https://github.com/bytebase/bytebase/pull/21794),
[#21796](https://github.com/bytebase/bytebase/pull/21796)) that an unversioned `replace`
makes no-ops, so the failure was already on `main`. The assertion comparing the two
tenants' schema dumps saw the new tenant missing exactly the column the backfill had just
added:

```diff
     "id" integer DEFAULT nextval('public.book_id_seq'::regclass) NOT NULL,
-    "name" text,
-    "author" text
+    "name" text
 );
```

## The race

`GetDatabaseSchema` serves `db_schema.raw_dump`, which only the schema syncer writes, and
`UpsertDBSchema` stamps no version — it row-locks the write itself, so whichever sync
*finishes* last owns the dump, however old the schema it read.

The competing writer is the async sync queue. `createDatabase` registers the database, and
the `SyncInstance` that registration runs hands newly discovered databases to
`SyncDatabasesAsync`; the syncer drains that queue on its own
`databaseSyncCheckerInterval` tick. When the tick lands on the backfill rollout, the queued
sync reads the tenant before the `ALTER TABLE` commits and upserts its pre-ALTER dump after
the migration task's own `SyncDatabaseSchemaToHistory` upserted the post-ALTER one. The
dump reverts while the task stays `DONE`, so `waitRollout` returning is not a
happens-before edge for the dump the test read next.

`LastSyncTime` is no use as a freshness signal either: `doSyncDatabaseSchema` writes it
*before* the upsert, and the reverting sync writes it too.

## The fix

`waitSchemaDump` syncs the database and reads its dump once per round, until the dump
reports the change just applied. The sync makes the dump current, and the loop outlasts a
queued write that reverted it. Every dump read in the test goes through it: the first
`CREATE TABLE`, step 1's baseline read, step 3's tenant check and step 6's comparison all
had the same exposure. The assertions are unchanged.

## Verification

Reproduced and proved with a `go test -overlay` copy of
`backend/runner/schemasync/syncer.go` that builds the inversion instead of waiting for it.
When a sync computes the pre-ALTER dump for the tenant, the overlay hands a copy to a
goroutine parked on a channel; the post-ALTER upsert closes that channel and waits for the
late write before returning.

- Overlay on the test before this change: `FAIL tenant_test.go:289` with the byte-exact
  diff above, every run.
- Overlay on the test after this change: `--- PASS: TestTenantBackfill (8.46s)`.

Gates on this branch:

- `gofmt -w` on both changed files — clean.
- `GOGC=off GOMEMLIMIT=10GiB golangci-lint run --fix -j 8 --allow-parallel-runners`, then
  again without `--fix` — `0 issues.` both passes, and `--fix` changed nothing. Run with
  v2.15.0, the version `ci.yml` pins on this base; v2.14.0 silently drops this base's
  renamed `exhaustive.explicit-exhaustive` setting and reports 50 iss

### [`v2.11.1`](https://redirect.github.com/qax-os/excelize/releases/tag/v2.11.1)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/xuri/excelize/compare/v2.11.0...v2.11.1)

We are pleased to announce the release of version 2.11.1. Featured are a handful of new areas of functionality and numerous bug fixes.

A summary of changes is available in the [Release Notes](https://redirect.github.com/xuri/excelize/releases/tag/v2.11.1). A full list of changes is available in the [changelog](https://redirect.github.com/xuri/excelize/compare/v2.11.0...v2.11.1).

#### Release Notes

The most notable changes in this release are:

##### Breaking Change

- Upgraded requirement: Go language version is Go 1.26.0 or later, due to upgrading dependency package `golang.org/x/crypto`

##### Security

- Fixed a panic when getting a cell value with a negative shared string index (CVE-2026-104819), related security advisory GHSA-48hm-4h8j-58fg
- Fixed a `GetPivotTables` panic on invalid pivot table field indices (CVE-2026-107211), related security advisory GHSA-mx22-3794-2vpv
- Fixed an unbounded row number in the rows iterator (CVE-2026-107212), related security advisory GHSA-jw42-f3rr-4cc3
- Fixed a `GetSlicers` panic when getting slicers from a worksheet without a drawing part (CVE-2026-107213), related security advisory GHSA-r7x5-4969-99p7
- Fixed a panic when decrypting a malformed workbook (CVE-2026-107214), related security advisory GHSA-2j4c-ffch-9f23
- Fixed unbounded `EncryptionInfo` and `EncryptedPackage` stream sizes being allocated when decrypting a workbook (CVE-2026-107215), related security advisory GHSA-x2q3-8cjh-766f
- Fixed a `CalcCellValue` stack overflow caused by circular ANCHORARRAY formula references (CVE-2026-107216), related security advisory GHSA-wp2g-vpjj-g53r
- Fixed `ColumnNameToNumber` and `JoinCellName` accepting invalid column names, which caused integer overflow (CVE-2026-107217), related security advisory GHSA-c85p-xxjj-2r75
- Fixed Unicode handling and count overflow in the LEFT, LEFTB, RIGHT, and RIGHTB formula functions (CVE-2026-107218), related security advisory GHSA-8jjq-8j9w-m2v6
- Fixed an unbounded spin count when deriving the agile decryption key (CVE-2026-107219), related security advisory GHSA-jrfj-fhj2-jjvm
- Fixed a panic on a worksheet with an empty merged cell reference (CVE-2026-107220), related s

### [`v4.10.4`](https://redirect.github.com/bmatcuk/doublestar/releases/tag/v4.10.4): Preserves segment position across alternatives

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/bmatcuk/doublestar/compare/v4.10.3...v4.10.4)

Fixes patterns like `x{**/a,b}` which *should* be treated like `x*/a` and `xb` because the doublestar appears mid-pattern.

#### What's Changed

- fix: preserve segment position across brace alternatives by [@​yuefdev](https://redirect.github.com/yuefdev) in [#​125](https://redirect.github.com/bmatcuk/doublestar/pull/125)

### [`v4.10.3`](https://redirect.github.com/bmatcuk/doublestar/releases/tag/v4.10.3): Handles character ranges when using WithCaseInsensitive

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/bmatcuk/doublestar/compare/v4.10.2...v4.10.3)

Character ranges, such as `[a-z]` would *not* match things like `A` when using `WithCaseInsensitive`. This release fixes that.

Thanks to [@​bensynapse](https://redirect.github.com/bensynapse) for bringing this to my attention.

**Full Changelog**: <https://github.com/bmatcuk/doublestar/compare/v4.10.2...v4.10.3>

### [`v4.10.2`](https://redirect.github.com/bmatcuk/doublestar/releases/tag/v4.10.2): Better support for Windows "Junctions"

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/bmatcuk/doublestar/compare/v4.10.1...v4.10.2)

+package trino
+
+import (
+	"context"
+	"testing"
+
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
+
+	storepb "github.com/bytebase/bytebase/backend/generated-go/store"
+	"github.com/bytebase/bytebase/backend/plugin/db"
+)
+
+func openTrino(t *testing.T, password string, useSSL bool) error {
+	t.Helper()
+	driver, err := (&Driver{}).Open(context.Background(), storepb.Engine_TRINO, db.ConnectionConfig{
+		DataSource: &storepb.DataSource{
+			Host:     "trino.example.com",
+			Port:     "8080",
+			Username: "bytebase",
+			UseSsl:   useSSL,
+		},
+		Password: password,
+	})
+	if driver != nil {
+		// Releases the custom HTTP client the SSL path registers globally.
+		t.Cleanup(func() { _ = driver.Close(context.Background()) })
+	}
+	return err
+}
+
+// trino-go-client refuses a password on a plaintext connection, so such a data
+// source cannot connect whatever we do. The guard exists for the message: it
+// names the setting to change instead of reporting a DSN parse failure.
+func TestOpenRefusesAPasswordWithoutSSL(t *testing.T) {
+	err := openTrino(t, "secret", false)
+	require.ErrorContains(t, err, "requires SSL to authenticate with a password")
+	require.NotContains(t, err.Error(), "secret", "the error must not carry the password")
+}
+
+func TestOpenAcceptsTheConfigurationsThatCanConnect(t *testing.T) {
+	for _, tc := range []struct {
+		name     string
+		password string
+		useSSL   bool
+	}{
+		{"password over SSL", "secret", true},
+		{"no password without SSL", "", false},
+		{"no password over SSL", "", true},
+	} {
+		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
+			err := openTrino(t, tc.password, tc.useSSL)
+			require.NoError(t, err)
+		})
+	}
+}

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>shopspring/decimal (github.com/shopspring/decimal)</summary>

### [`v1.6.0`](https://redirect.github.com/shopspring/decimal/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#Decimal-v160)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/shopspring/decimal/compare/v1.5.0...v1.6.0)

##### BEHAVIOR CHANGES

- `Decimal` implements `fmt.Formatter`. `%#v` prints Go code that recreates the value, like `decimal.New(314, -2)`, instead of the struct fields, and verbs that don't apply, like `%d`, print `%!d(decimal.Decimal=3.14)`. `%v`, `%s`, `%q`, `%x` and `fmt.Println` print the same as before [#​463](https://redirect.github.com/shopspring/decimal/pull/463)
- `Ln` rounds correctly, so some results change in the last digit: `Ln` of 10 to 5 places is `2.30259`, not `2.30258` [#​471](https://redirect.github.com/shopspring/decimal/pull/471)
- `ExpHullAbrham` returns `overallPrecision` significant figures for every input. Negative inputs used to lose digits or return 0, like `-50` at precision 10, and large inputs returned extra digits [#​429](https://redirect.github.com/shopspring/decimal/pull/429) [#​470](https://redirect.github.com/shopspring/decimal/pull/470)
- `Scan` converts `float32` with `NewFromFloat32`, so `54.33` stays `54.33` instead of becoming `54.33000183105469`. NaN and infinite floats return an error instead of panicking [#​469](https://redirect.github.com/shopspring/decimal/pull/469)
- On Go 1.10 to 1.12, `NewFromFloat` can pick a different shortest form in rare cases ([golang/go#29491](https://redirect.github.com/golang/go/issues/29491)). It still converts back to the same float [#​431](https://redirect.github.com/shopspring/decimal/pull/431)

##### FEATURES

- Add BSON Decimal128 support for `Decimal` and `NullDecimal` with the official MongoDB Go driver v2, without a new dependency [#​460](https://redirect.github.com/shopspring/decimal/pull/460)
- Add `%f` formatting with precision, width and flags, like `%.2f` and `%08.2f` [#​463](https://redirect.github.com/shopspring/decimal/pull/463)
- Add `Normalize`, which strips trailing zeros so equal decimals also match with `reflect.DeepEqual`, testify and gomock [#​464](https://redirect.github.com/shopspring/decimal/pull/464)
- Add `Sqrt` and `SqrtRound` [#​465](https://redirect.github.com/shopspring/decimal/pull/465)
- Add `Root` and `RootRound` for n-th roots [#​473](https://redirect

:warning: This release raises the minimum required Go version to 1.26 and includes breaking API changes in `api/prometheus/v1` (see the \[CHANGE] entries below). :warning:

#### 1.25.0 / 2026-10-07

- \[CHANGE] Minimum required Go version is now 1.26, only the two latest Go versions (1.26 and 1.27) are supported from now on. [#​2138](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/client_golang/issues/2138)
- \[CHANGE] api/prometheus/v1: `Query`, `QueryRange`, `Series`, `LabelNames`, and `LabelValues` now return `Infos` annotations in addition to `Warnings`, matching the Prometheus server's info annotations. This changes the signatures of these methods and of `api.Client`'s `Do`/`DoGetFallback`; custom API client implementations must be updated. [#​1963](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/client_golang/issues/1963)
- \[CHANGE] api/prometheus/v1: Rework `TSDBBlocks` result types to align with the Prometheus server's `tsdb.BlockMeta`: `TSDBBlocksResult` now contains `Blocks []TSDBBlockMeta` directly instead of mirroring the full API envelope, nested types are renamed (`TSDBBlockMeta`, `TSDBBlockStats`, `TSDBBlockMetaCompaction`), stat fields are `uint64` with `omitempty` tags, and the optional compaction `parents` field is included. [#​1928](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/client_golang/issues/1928)
- \[FEATURE] testutil: Add `GatherAndFormat` to encode a subset of metrics from a Gatherer. [#​2091](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/client_golang/issues/2091)
- \[FEATURE] promhttp: Add `HandlerOpts.AcceptedFormats` to customize the formats negotiated from the incoming `Accept` header, enabling opt-in to experimental formats such as OpenMetrics 2.0 without changing default negotiation. [#​2146](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/client_golang/issues/2146)
- \[ENHANCEMENT] promhttp: Negotiated metrics responses now include a `Vary` header. [#​2142](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/client_golang/issues/2142)
- \[ENHANCEMENT] prometheus: Regenerate the default runtime collector metrics for Go 1.25 and Go 1.26. [#​2090](https://redire

Fixes some things, performance boost on indexing too from [@​Tjmstudios](https://redirect.github.com/Tjmstudios)

### [`v0.42.1`](https://redirect.github.com/pb33f/libopenapi/compare/v0.42.0...v0.42.1)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pb33f/libopenapi/compare/v0.42.0...v0.42.1)

### [`v0.42.0`](https://redirect.github.com/pb33f/libopenapi/releases/tag/v0.42.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pb33f/libopenapi/compare/v0.41.8...v0.42.0)

This release improves reference resolution, bundling, and schema comparison across OpenAPI and Swagger documents. It fixes missing schema fields, incomplete bundles, incorrect circular-reference paths, and recursive comparisons that could panic or stall. It also fixes a shared-index race affecting Vacuum when multiple documents use the same cached filesystem.

Compatibility has been verified against unmodified Vacuum and openapi-changes, including full test suites, targeted race checks, and CLI runs across six real-world specifications. Linux, Windows, and the full library race suite pass, with 100% project and patch coverage. Benchmarks show faster indexing and comparison overall, though gains vary by specification and operation.

- Reference handling: resolve external schemas and Swagger path items in their owning documents; preserve aliases, discriminator mappings, and encoded paths during bundling.
- More accurate comparisons: count allOf breaking changes once and include changes inside retargeted references. Reports and change totals can differ from earlier releases.
- Bounded alias expansion: excessive YAML alias expansion now returns an error. Set AllowExcessiveAliases for trusted documents that require it; cycle detection remains enabled.
- Clearer cycle failures: reference-only cycles now return build errors instead of incomplete models or hangs.
- Go compatibility note: empty schema-change maps may now be nil. Reading and iterating remain safe; initialize them before writing directly.

[@​CaliLuke](https://redirect.github.com/CaliLuke) [@​josephaxisa](https://redirect.github.com/josephaxisa) [@​madesst](https://redirect.github.com/madesst)
