[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/opensearch-project/opensearch-go/compare/v4.8.0...v4.8.1)

### opensearch-go v4.8.1

> ## CRITICAL UPGRADE RELEASE NOTE - v5 has substantially expanded error handling capabilities compared to v4.
>
> **v5.0.0 is out, and v4 is now in maintenance mode.** v4.8.1 is a maintenance release: it does not add features. The v4 -> v5 upgrade changes runtime error-handling behavior and is *NOT* a drop-in replacement across major versions. If you use this client, read this now - even if you are only upgrading to v4.8.1.
>
> v4 only returns transport-level errors; partial failures (e.g. failed bulk items, failed shards, unconfirmed replica writes) are reported inside the response body, not as Go `error` values. **In v5, those partial failures are returned as errors by default.** Code that compiles and passes against v4 can behave differently against v5 without any code change.
>
> Upgrading between v4 releases (any `<v4.8.1` to any `v4.X.X`) does **not** change the default error-handling semantics. See [`guides/error_handling.md`](https://redirect.github.com/opensearch-project/opensearch-go/blob/v4.8.1/guides/error_handling.md) for how to adopt the v5 behavior on v4 before you upgrade, and the [v4 to v5 migration guide](https://redirect.github.com/opensearch-project/opensearch-go/blob/v5.0.0/opensearchapi/UPGRADING_V4_TO_V5.md) for the full API delta.

v4.8.1 is a dependency patch on top of v4.8.0. No client code changed.

Its main purpose is the Go toolchain. The root module and `cmd/osgen` now declare `go 1.26.0` with `toolchain go1.26.9`, so builds in this repository use a Go release with the standard library CVE fixes from 1.26.9 (13 advisories that affect 1.26.8, 10 of them reachable from this code). The minimum Go version for building against v4 drops from 1.26.8 to 1.26.0. A `toolchain` line does not apply to modules that depend on this one, so build your own binaries with Go 1.26.9 or newer to get the fixes.

**Full Changelog**: <https://github.com/opensearch-project/opensearch-go/compare/v4.8.0...v4.8.1>

**`4.8.1` Dependencies**

- Set `go 1.26.0` with `toolchain go1.26.9` in

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk (github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk)</summary>

### [`v1.8.0`](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk/releases/tag/v1.8.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk/compare/v1.7.0...v1.8.0)

***This release is equivalent to v1.8.0-pre.2. Thank you to those who tested the pre-release.***

In this release we introduce several fixes and improvements on top of [v1.7.0](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk/releases/tag/v1.7.0). It adds no new protocol revision: the supported set is unchanged, and `2026-07-28` remains the newest version the SDK negotiates.

The bulk of the work is hardening the transports against resource exhaustion, closing session leaks, deadlocks and teardown hangs found by users running the new protocol at scale, and giving servers explicit control over which protocol versions they advertise.

Two behavior changes are guarded by new `MCPGODEBUG` flags; see the section below.

#### Hardening against resource exhaustion

Every decoding path that buffers incoming input is now bounded. JSON payloads are rejected past 1000 levels of nesting, before the parser recurses. Both SSE readers cap the bytes buffered for a single event via `MaxEventSize` on `SSEClientTransport` and `StreamableClientTransport`, and the stdio transport caps a single JSON-RPC frame via `StdioTransport.MaxLineLength`.

On the OAuth side, dynamic client registration responses are bounded to 1 MB, and the discovery code now validates metadata documents rather than trusting them.

- internal/json: json nesting depth check by [@​yarolegovich](https://redirect.github.com/yarolegovich) ([#​1200](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk/pull/1200))
- mcp: add an sse event size cap by [@​yarolegovich](https://redirect.github.com/yarolegovich) ([#​1205](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk/pull/1205))
- mcp: add a max request body size of the old transport by [@​yarolegovich](https://redirect.github.com/yarolegovich) ([#​1224](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk/pull/1224))
- oauthex: bound dcr read to 1mb by [@​yarolegovich](https://redirect.github.com/yarolegovich) ([#​1206](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk/pull/1206))
- oauthex: oauth discov

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>labstack/echo (github.com/labstack/echo/v5)</summary>

### [`v5.4.4`](https://redirect.github.com/labstack/echo/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#v544---2026-10-29)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/labstack/echo/compare/v5.4.3...v5.4.4)

**Proxy identity hardening**

- Preserve the derived upstream `X-Real-IP` after hop-by-hop header stripping. A client can no longer remove that header with `Connection: X-Real-IP`, including duplicate or mixed-case nominations and WebSocket upgrades.
- Capture the client identity once and preserve it across retries and balancer request replacement. Default and custom transports and extractors remain supported.
- Add permanent regressions for HTTP forwarding, raw WebSocket upgrades, header nominations, and stateful extraction during request-swapping retries. Implementation: [#​3200](https://redirect.github.com/labstack/echo/pull/3200).

v5 already uses the connection peer by default. This release adds proxy header protection and does not change client-IP configuration or the affected ranges of the earlier default-IP CVEs. A missing identity header can affect an upstream that falls back to an untrusted source; no new client-IP migration, public API, dependency, or minimum Go-version change is introduced.

### [`v5.4.3`](https://redirect.github.com/labstack/echo/releases/tag/v5.4.3)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/labstack/echo/compare/v5.4.2...v5.4.3)

#### Security

Upgrade to v5.4.3 to fix a static route-guard bypass involving encoded empty path segments in non-default path-matching or unescaping configurations. The confirmed impact is access to protected files inside a static root. The fix validates raw and decoded request paths and wildcard boundaries, including singly and doubly encoded leading slashes and guarded directory indexes.

Advisory: <https://github.com/labstack/echo/security/advisories/GHSA-v97q-3xf5-rj74>

#### Fixes

- Decode path parameters only once when `UnescapePathParamValues` is enabled, preserving literal percent-containing values.
- Correct `UseEscapedPathForMatching` documentation without changing its behavior.
- Preserve correctly escaped filenames and static prefixes such as `/assets*`.

Thanks to MyWorld319 for the static bypass report and alexreid for the parameter-decoding report.

#### Documentation

- Publish v4 support dates and the Echo Support offer ([#​3193](https://redirect.github.

-			// Only mark an asset immutable once we've confirmed it exists. In an HA

+			// Mark an asset immutable only once the response is known to be a
+			// success. In an HA rolling deploy an older replica can 404 a new
+			// hashed asset briefly, and the static handler rejects a path with a
+			// dot or empty segment outright, so a year of cached "does not exist"
+			// has to be impossible. Reading the status rather than re-deriving the
+			// file from the path also leaves echo's path rules to echo: deciding
+			// from a cleaned path is what put the header on those 404s.
+			//
+			// 304 keeps the directive so a revalidating CDN does not shorten its

### [`v2.33.0`](https://redirect.github.com/grpc-ecosystem/grpc-gateway/releases/tag/v2.33.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/grpc-ecosystem/grpc-gateway/compare/v2.32.0...v2.33.0)

##### Notice to all users

This release contains a security fix that changes the behavior of header parsing in the gateway. As part of fixing [#​7281](https://redirect.github.com/grpc-ecosystem/grpc-gateway/issues/7281), the decision was made to stop automatically adding client headers with the `Grpc-Metadata-` prefix into the grpc metadata by default. This behavior can be restored using the new mux option `WithLegacyHeaderMatching`. See <https://grpc-ecosystem.github.io/grpc-gateway/docs/operations/security_considerations/#request-headers-become-grpc-metadata-under-a-prefix> for more information.

##### Changes

- reject non-decimal float spellings in query and path params by [@​itecz26](https://redirect.github.com/itecz26) in [#​7512](https://redirect.github.com/grpc-ecosystem/grpc-gateway/pull/7512)
- docs: link example repositories in README by [@​wangyusheng1985](https://redirect.github.com/wangyusheng1985) in [#​7517](https://redirect.github.com/grpc-ecosystem/grpc-gateway/pull/7517)
- docs: update outdated local proxy documentation ([#​912](https://redirect.github.com/grpc-ecosystem/grpc-gateway/issues/912)) by [@​Asthenia0412](https://redirect.github.com/Asthenia0412) in [#​7521](https://redirect.github.com/grpc-ecosystem/grpc-gateway/pull/7521)
- reject field\[key] syntax for non-map fields in query params by [@​itecz26](https://redirect.github.com/itecz26) in [#​7522](https://redirect.github.com/grpc-ecosystem/grpc-gateway/pull/7522)
- keep remote address in x-forwarded-for when a client value is invalid by [@​itecz26](https://redirect.github.com/itecz26) in [#​7531](https://redirect.github.com/grpc-ecosystem/grpc-gateway/pull/7531)
- let WithMetadata annotators override client-forwarded metadata by [@​itecz26](https://redirect.github.com/itecz26) in [#​7532](https://redirect.github.com/grpc-ecosystem/grpc-gateway/pull/7532)
- try GET first for path length fallback so it isn't lost to map order by [@​cvas22](https://redirect.github.com/cvas22) in

##### Improvements

- Improve TypeScript types  [`cf2297d`](https://redirect.github.com/sindresorhus/emittery/commit/cf2297d)
  - `Emittery.mixin()` now returns a class type that includes the emittery property and the mixed-in methods
  - The iterators from `.events()` and `.anyEvent()` now type `next()` and `return()` precisely, instead of `any`
  - `Emittery.listenerAdded` and `Emittery.listenerRemoved` are now accepted everywhere the runtime accepts them, like `.on()`, `.events()`, and `.listenerCount()`
  - `.emit()` without data now works on an untyped emitter
  - `.bindMethods()` now accepts any object, including a class instance
  - `methodNames` for `Emittery.mixin()` and `.bindMethods()` now only accepts real method names. A list typed as `string[]` needs `as const` or the new `EmitteryMethodName` type.

##### Fixes

- Fix async iterators hanging forever when `next()` is called concurrently  [`7157da9`](https://redirect.github.com/sindresorhus/emittery/commit/7157da9)
- Fix a rejected event data promise causing an unhandled rejection when an iterator never reads it  [`7157da9`](https://redirect.github.com/sindresorhus/emittery/commit/7157da9)

- Fix `listenerAdded` and `listenerRemoved` firing when nothing changed  [`4987e5f`](https://redirect.github.com/sindresorhus/emittery/commit/4987e5f)

title: fix(members): keep the member drawer's binding tables inside their cards
body: Design doc and implementation: [`docs/design/member-drawer-binding-tables.md`](https://github.com/bytebase/bytebase/blob/worktree-byt-10364-member-drawer-columns/docs/design/member-drawer-binding-tables.md) ([BYT-10364](https://linear.app/bytebase/issue/BYT-10364)). **Each role card's table keeps a fixed column layout fitted to the card, so every card opens with the same columns; a name too long for its column ends in an ellipsis and shows in full on hover, and the user can widen a column, in that card only.** Expiration moves from a column to the card's header, because it belongs to the binding, not to a row. ## Why On a project's Members page, Edit on a member opens a drawer with one card per role binding, and each card lists the binding's databases, schemas and tables: - The table had no fixed layout, so a long schema or table name pushed Table and Expiration past the card, and the whole drawer body scrolled sideways. - Each card sized its columns from its own rows, so the headers sat at a different x in every card. - The truncation in `MemberDatabaseResourceName` never applied, because an auto-layout cell grows to fit. - The binding's one expiration was repeated on every row, in the column that overflowed first. #21699 proposed wrapping long names instead. This PR follows the plan list and Access grants tables: fixed columns, cut names with the full value on hover, and resizable columns. ## What the doc decides - **D1.** Each card's table is `table-fixed`, with Database, Schema and Table spread across the card's width on open (`distributeColumnWidths` + `fillableWidth`, as Access grants does). A column dragged past the card scrolls that card only. - **D2.** Columns resize per card; widths are not shared between cards or kept after the drawer closes. - **D3.** Schema and Table use `EllipsisText`, which shows a tooltip only when the name is cut. The Database cell cuts the instance title and the database name separately, as `DatabaseTargetDisplay` does. - **D4.** Expiration moves to the card header ("Expiration" and the time, or "Never"), using existing strings. - **D5.** The edit-member sheet goes from `medium` (640px) to `wide` (832px), the UX contract's tier for a sheet with nested tables. ## Screenshots From an e2e build of `main` (before) and of this branch (after): a member with Project Developer and a SQL Editor User binding scoped to a long schema and three tables. | Before | After | | --- | --- | | | | **Hovering a cut table name shows it in full:** ## Testing - `MemberBindingResourceTable.test.tsx` (new): Database, Schema and Table headers with no Exp
author: zchpeter
diff: --- docs/design/member-drawer-binding-tables.md (+109/-0) @@ -0,0 +1,109 @@ +# Member drawer binding tables + +Status: implemented in this PR · 2026-11-01 · [BYT-10364](https://linear.app/bytebase/issue/BYT-10364) + +On a project's Members page, Edit on a member opens a drawer with one card per role binding, and +each card lists the binding's databases, schemas and tables in a table. A long name widens its +column until the table runs out of the card, and every card lines its columns up differently. +**Each card's table keeps a fixed column layout fitted to the card, so every card opens with the +same columns; a name too long for its column ends in an ellipsis and shows in full on hover, and +the user can widen a column, in that card only.** Expiration moves from a column to the card's +header, because it belongs to the binding, not to a row. + +## Problem + +Verified on `main` at `cbaf903ae6`, in `EditMemberRoleDrawer` (`frontend/src/routes/workspace/MembersPage.tsx`): + +- **Columns size to their content.** The table has no fixed layout, so the browser sizes each + column from its longest value. A long schema or table name pushes Table and Expiration past the + card's edge, and the whole drawer body scrolls sideways. +- **Every card has its own geometry.** Each card sizes its columns from its own rows, so the + Database, Schema, Table and Expiration headers sit at a different x in every card. +- **Truncation does nothing.** `MemberDatabaseResourceName` truncates the instance and database + names, but an auto-layout cell grows to fit them, so nothing is ever cut. +- **Expiration repeats on every row.** `getSingleBindingRows` copies the binding's one + `expiredTime` onto each resource row, so a binding with ten tables shows the same expiration ten + times, in the column that overflows first. +- **The drawer is narrower than the contract's tier.** It uses sheet width `medium` (640px); the UX + contract gives `wide` (832px) to a sheet with nested tables. + +## Principle + +> A role card reads like the other tables in Bytebase, the plan list and Access grants: fixed +> columns that fit the space, long identifiers cut with the full value on hover, and columns the +> reader can widen. Nothing a card shows changes another card. + +## Decisions + +**D1 · Fixed columns, fitted to the card.** Each card's table uses `table-fixed` with Database, +Schema and Table columns. On open, the columns are spread across the card's width with +`distributeColumnWidths` and `fillableWidth` from `useColumnWidths`, as Access grants does, so +every card opens with the same columns and no card scrolls. The table sits in an `overflow-x-auto` +box inside the card, so a width the user drags past the card scrolls that card only. Rejected: +wrapping long names in fixed columns (#21699); it shows every name in full but gives rows uneven +heights and is not how Bytebase's other identifier tables read. + +**D2 · Columns resize per card, and the widths are not kept.** Every column has the shared resize +handle. Dragging it changes that card only; widths reset when the drawer opens again. Rejected: one +set of widths shared by every card; a reader reviews one binding at a time, and sharing would tie +every card to state held by the drawer for no task the drawer serves. + +**D3 · A cut name shows in full on hover.** Schema and Table cells use `EllipsisText`, which adds +the tooltip only when the value is cut. The Database cell keeps its engine icon, instance title and +database name, each an `EllipsisText` of its own, as `DatabaseTargetDisplay` does, so the database +name stays partly visible beside a long instance title and hovering either shows it in full. `*` +(every database, schema or table) never needs a tooltip. + +**D4 · Expiration goes to the card header.** The header row reads: role title, the Expired badge +when expired (as today), then on the right "Expiration" and the value the column showed, the +`operational` timestamp or "Never", before the delete button. The table loses its Expiration +column. The strings already exist (`common.expiration`, `project.members.never-expires`). + +**D5 · The drawer moves to sheet width `wide`.** The edit-member sheet goes from `medium` (640px) to +`wide` (832px), the contract's tier for a sheet with nested tables. The grant sheet the drawer +opens on top, and the workspace member sheet, keep their widths. + +## States + +| Binding scope | Name length | Card shows | +|---|---|---| +| Every database | — | One row: `*`, `*`, `*`. | +| A database | Fits | Engine icon, instance › database; Schema and Table `*`. | +| A database, schema and tables | Fits | One row per table, database and schema repeated, nothing cut. | +| Any | A name longer than its column | The name ends in `…`; hovering it shows the full value. | +| Any | A column dragged wider than the card | That card's table scrolls sideways; other cards unchanged. | + +| Expiration | Header right side | +|---|---| +| None | "Expiration Never" | +| A future time | "Expiration" and the time, `operational` form | +| A past time | Expired badge after the role title, struck-through title, dimmed card (as today), and the time | + +At phone width the sheet is the screen's width; columns shrink to fit, no column below its minimum +width, and a card whose minimum widths don't fit scrolls sideways. + +## Scope + +| File | Change | +|---|---| +| `frontend/src/routes/workspace/MemberBindingResourceTable.tsx` | New: one card's table (D1–D3). | +| `frontend/src/routes/workspace/MemberDatabaseResourceName.tsx` | A tooltip on the instance title or database name when it is cut (D3). | +| `frontend/src/routes/workspace/MembersPage.tsx` | Uses the new table, moves expiration to the header (D4), sheet `wide` (D5). | + +Tests: + +- `MemberBindingResourceTable.test.tsx`: Database, Schema and Table headers and no Expiration; a + row per resource and `*` for an unscoped binding; dragging a column in one table leaves another + table's widths unchanged. +- `MemberDatabaseResourceName.test.tsx`: the full instance title or database name on hover when it + is cut, no tooltip when it fits. +- `MembersPage.test.tsx`: each card's header shows its expiration once, "Never" or the time. +- `tests/e2e/project-members/project-members.spec.ts`: with a long schema and table name, every + card's columns line up and stay inside the card on open, hovering a cut table name shows it in + full, and dragging a column in one card leaves the other cards' columns where they were. + +## Not in this PR + +- Grouping a binding's tables under one database and schema row (the issue's second open point). +- Reading a cut name on a touch screen, where there is no hover. +- The workspace member sheet and the grant sheet. --- frontend/src/routes/workspace/MemberBindingResourceTable.test.tsx (+85/-0) @@ -0,0 +1,85 @@ +import { fireEvent, render, screen, within } from "@testing-library/react"; +import { describe, expect, test, vi } from "vitest"; +import type { DatabaseResource } from "@/types"; +import { MemberBindingResourceTable } from "./MemberBindingResourceTable"; + +vi.mock("react-i18next", () => ({ + useTranslation: () => ({ t: (key: string) => key }), +})); + +vi.mock("./MemberDatabaseResourceName", () => ({ + MemberDatabaseResourceName: ({ + resource, + }: { + resource?: DatabaseResource; + }) => {resource?.databaseFullName ?? "*"}, +})); + +const columnHeaders = () => + screen.getAllByRole("columnheader").map((th) => th.textContent); + +describe("MemberBindingResourceTable", () => { + test("lists database, schema and table, one row per resource, without an expiration column", () => { + render( + + ); + + expect(columnHeaders()).toEqual([ + "common.database", + "common.schema", + "common.table", + ]); + const rows = screen.getAllByRole("row").slice(1); + expect(rows.map((row) => within(row).getAllByRole("cell").map((c) => c.textContent))).toEqual([ + ["instances/prod/databases/hr", "public", "employee"], + ["instances/prod/databases/hr", "audit", "*"], + ]); + }); + + test("dragging a column edge widens that column in its own table only", () => { + const { container } = render( + <> + + + + ); + const [first, second] = Array.from(container.querySelectorAll("table")); + const colWidths = (table: HTMLTableElement) => + Array.from(table.querySelectorAll("col")).map((col) => col.style.width); + const before = colWidths(first); + expect(colWidths(second)).toEqual(before); + + const schemaHeader = within(first).getByRole("columnheader", { + name: "common.schema", + }); + const handle = schemaHeader.lastElementChild as HTMLElement; + fireEvent.mouseDown(handle, { clientX: 100 }); + fireEvent.mouseMove(document, { clientX: 180 }); + fireEvent.mouseUp(document); + + expect(colWidths(first)).toEqual([ + before[0], + `${Number.parseInt(before[1]) + 80}px`, + before[2], + ]); + expect(colWidths(second)).toEqual(before); + }); + + test("an unscoped binding is one row of *", () => { + render(); + + const rows = screen.getAllByRole("row").slice(1); + expect(rows.map((row) => within(row).getAllByRole("cell").map((c) => c.textContent))).toEqual([ + ["*", "*", "*"], + ]); + }); +}); ... 6 more files truncated

### [`v4.1.7`](https://redirect.github.com/go-jose/go-jose/releases/tag/v4.1.7)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/go-jose/go-jose/compare/v4.1.6...v4.1.7)

#### Fixed Security Issues

- Thumbprint: reject invalid RSA key ([#​317](https://redirect.github.com/go-jose/go-jose/issues/317)) - [GHSA-r39w-98wm-9pp6](https://redirect.github.com/go-jose/go-jose/security/advisories/GHSA-r39w-98wm-9pp6)
- json: backport stdlib fix for embedded unexported field ([#​318](https://redirect.github.com/go-jose/go-jose/issues/318)) - [GHSA-27pc-rm86-68pq](https://redirect.github.com/go-jose/go-jose/security/advisories/GHSA-27pc-rm86-68pq)
- Detect if headers are set by presence in the map ([#​319](https://redirect.github.com/go-jose/go-jose/issues/319)) - [GHSA-p9j4-2j95-j4rv](https://redirect.github.com/go-jose/go-jose/security/advisories/GHSA-p9j4-2j95-j4rv)
- limit RSA size in certificate verify ([#​315](https://redirect.github.com/go-jose/go-jose/issues/315)) - [GHSA-v6h2-qj3f-2h6v](https://redirect.github.com/go-jose/go-jose/security/advisories/GHSA-v6h2-qj3f-2h6v)
- Limit recipients and signatures in JWE/JWS ([#​316](https://redirect.github.com/go-jose/go-jose/issues/316)) - [GHSA-c67m-wr4h-2ccg](https://redirect.github.com/go-jose/go-jose/security/advisories/GHSA-c67m-wr4h-2ccg)

#### Fixed

- jwk: fix bug in x5c parsing ([#​311](https://redirect.github.com/go-jose/go-jose/issues/311))
- reject base64-encoded "null" in protected headers ([#​309](https://redirect.github.com/go-jose/go-jose/issues/309))

#### Deprecated

- deprecate ParseEncrypted / ParseSigned ([#​222](https://redirect.github.com/go-jose/go-jose/issues/222))

### [`v4.1.6`](https://redirect.github.com/go-jose/go-jose/releases/tag/v4.1.6)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/go-jose/go-jose/compare/v4.1.5...v4.1.6)

#### Fixed Security Issues

This release contains a fix for <https://github.com/go-jose/go-jose/security/advisories/GHSA-mgcc-cww5-fp2q>

#### Breaking Changes

The fix for <https://github.com/go-jose/go-jose/security/advisories/GHSA-mgcc-cww5-fp2q> involves capping the size of the RSA modulus of keys accepted by JWK parsing. This limit is 4096 bits. If you need this to be higher, set `MaxRSAModulusBits` before performing any JWK parsing.

#### Changed

- Reject mismatched JWE CE

 		return nil, errors.Errorf("failed to fetch JWKS: HTTP %d", resp.StatusCode)
 	}
 
-	var jwks jose.JSONWebKeySet
-	if err := json.NewDecoder(resp.Body).Decode(&jwks); err != nil {
+	var raw struct {
+		Keys []json.RawMessage `json:"keys"`
+	}
+	if err := json.NewDecoder(resp.Body).Decode(&raw); err != nil {
 		return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to decode JWKS")
 	}
 
-	return &jwks, nil
+	// Decode one key at a time: go-jose refuses a key whose RSA modulus exceeds
+	// jose.MaxRSAModulusBits, and decoding the set in one call would let such a
+	// key cost us the rest of it, including the one the token was signed with.
+	jwks := &jose.JSONWebKeySet{}
+	for i, rawKey := range raw.Keys {
+		var key jose.JSONWebKey
+		if err := json.Unmarshal(rawKey, &key); err != nil {
+			slog.Warn("Skipping a JWKS key go-jose cannot parse",
+				slog.String("jwksURL", jwksURL),
+				slog.Int("index", i),
+				log.BBError(err),
+			)
+			continue
+		}
+		jwks.Keys = append(jwks.Keys, key)
+	}
+	// Dropping every key an issuer published is not the same as it publishing
+	// none: erroring keeps the emptied set out of the cache, so a fixed issuer
+	// is picked up on the next call rather than after cacheDuration.
+	if len(jwks.Keys) == 0 && len(raw.Keys) > 0 {
+		return nil, errors.New("failed to decode JWKS: no key could be parsed")
+	}
+
+	return jwks, nil
 }

+// The modulus is fabricated, not generated: JWK parsing reads only n and e, and
+// generating a key above jose.MaxRSAModulusBits would dominate the test.
+func rsaJWKJSON(t *testing.T, kid string, modulusBits int) string {
+	t.Helper()
+	modulus := new(big.Int).SetBit(new(big.Int).Lsh(big.NewInt(1), uint(modulusBits-1)), 0, 1)
+	require.Equal(t, modulusBits, modulus.BitLen())
+	return fmt.Sprintf(`{"kty":"RSA","kid":%q,"alg":"RS256","use":"sig","n":%q,"e":%q}`,
+		kid,
+		base64.RawURLEncoding.EncodeToString(modulus.Bytes()),
+		base64.RawURLEncoding.EncodeToString(big.NewInt(65537).Bytes()),
+	)
+}

title: fix(deps): point the gh-ost fork at upstream v1.1.11
body:
Renovate opened this to bump the `require` line to v1.1.11. On its own that is a
no-op — the `replace` below it shadows the line entirely, `go.sum` holds no
upstream gh-ost entries, and the version on it is never compiled, which is why
the previous monthly bumps were closed rather than merged.

A second commit makes it real: it repoints the `replace` at the Bytebase fork
rebased onto upstream `v1.1.11` (bytebase/gh-ost2#10). The old pin,
`v1.1.7-0.20260512035759-ca2794d6ebea`, sat on upstream `v1.1.8` and so shipped
none of upstream's MariaDB support, the migration-state data-race fixes, or the
binlog decode optimisation that skips rows for unrelated tables.

Renovate's commit is kept as-is (rebased onto current `main`) so the `require`
line and the `replace` finally agree. Note that this branch now carries a
non-Renovate commit, so Renovate will stop rebasing it.

Why it matters beyond tidiness: gh-ost dispatch is directive-based with no engine
gate — `backend/runner/taskrun/database_migrate_executor.go:125` routes to
`runGhostMigration` whenever `ghost.IsGhostEnabled(sheet.Statement)` holds, on any
instance — and SQL Review registers an online-migration advisor for MariaDB at
`backend/plugin/advisor/mariadb/rule_online_migration.go:25` that recommends
gh-ost. MariaDB and OceanBase gh-ost runs were therefore reachable on a build
that predated upstream's MariaDB work.

## What the fork branch carries

Eight Bytebase patches, one per commit, each reapplied by hand against upstream's
current code (upstream renamed every receiver). The preserved and dropped lists,
with reasons, are in bytebase/gh-ost2#10.

One patch is **dropped** with a behavior change here worth a look: `chore: no need
to set tx isolation level`. Upstream's new `mysql.OpenDB` strips the
`transaction_isolation` DSN parameter and issues the portable `SET SESSION
TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL` statement instead, exactly because that variable is
absent on MariaDB < 11.1 and `tx_isolation` is gone from MySQL 8.0+ — the
incompatibility the patch worked around. Confirmed against live servers: the raw
DSN parameter gets `Error 1193: Unknown system variable 'transaction_isolation'`
on MariaDB 10.11 and succeeds through `OpenDB` on both 10.11 and 11.4. The
consequence is that gh-ost had been running at the server's default isolation
level since the patch landed in 2024 and now gets the REPEATABLE-READ that
upstream intends.

It also carries one fix that is not a carried-forward patch. **Without it this
bump hangs every gh-ost migration that MySQL can apply instantly**, which is all
of them that qualify, since `defaultConfig.attemptInstantDDL` is `true`. The
rebase first failed `TestGhostSchemaUpdate` here while `main` passed it 3/3 in
~23s; a focused reproduction in gh-ost pinned it to a three-goroutine cycle after
`--attempt-instant-ddl` short-circuits the migration:

- the changelog listener parks on the unbuffered `GhostTableMigrated` send, which
  that path returns without reading;
- `not

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>cure53/DOMPurify (dompurify)</summary>

### [`v3.4.17`](https://redirect.github.com/cure53/DOMPurify/releases/tag/3.4.17): DOMPurify 3.4.17

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/cure53/DOMPurify/compare/3.4.16...3.4.17)

- Fixed an issue with `IN_PLACE`, `SAFE_FOR_TEMPLATES` and shadow roots, thanks [@​manus-pi](https://redirect.github.com/manus-pi)
- Fixed `IN_PLACE` handling of nodes that hooks or custom elements tough during sanitization, thanks [@​uttej-badwane](https://redirect.github.com/uttej-badwane)
- Fixed the SMIL `attributeName` guard in XHTML mode, thanks [@​Koukyosyumei](https://redirect.github.com/Koukyosyumei)
- Hardened several smaller edge cases (namespaces, literal-text elements, `isValidAttribute()`), thanks [@​artiphishell](https://redirect.github.com/artiphishell)
- Added a purify-edge test runner as a compatibility check, thanks [@​anzal1](https://redirect.github.com/anzal1)
- Clarified the `IN_PLACE` documentation in the README about possible risks
- Updated several dependencies

### [`v3.4.16`](https://redirect.github.com/cure53/DOMPurify/releases/tag/3.4.16): DOMPurify 3.4.16

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/cure53/DOMPurify/compare/3.4.15...3.4.16)

- Fixed a problem with `IN_PLACE` node removal when working with hooks, thanks [@​manus-pi](https://redirect.github.com/manus-pi)
- Fixed a problem with `IN_PLACE` sanitization and raw-text roots, thanks [@​h-t-m](https://redirect.github.com/h-t-m)
- Fixed a problem with ESM default exports landing in CommonJS declarations, thanks [@​ssi02014](https://redirect.github.com/ssi02014)
- Migrated from `rollup` to `rolldown` because performance, thanks [@​ssi02014](https://redirect.github.com/ssi02014)
- Bumped several dependencies where possible

### [`v3.4.15`](https://redirect.github.com/cure53/DOMPurify/releases/tag/3.4.15): DOMPurify 3.4.15

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/cure53/DOMPurify/compare/3.4.14...3.4.15)

- Added better clobbering hardening when XML content is involved, thanks [@​gnyselcuk](https://redirect.github.com/gnyselcuk)
- Added several smaller hardening and edge-case improvements, thanks [@​leechristensen](https://redirect.github.com/leechristensen)
- Bumped several dependencies where possible

</details>

These methods already put a space between arguments, so such a space prints twice.

  ```js

  ```

   - `bidichk`: from 0.3.3 to 0.3.4

##### What's Changed

##### Bugfixes

- Stop draining gRPC response body after rejecting a message by [@​stefanvanburen](https://redirect.github.com/stefanvanburen) in [#​1005](https://redirect.github.com/connectrpc/connect-go/pull/1005)
- Keep sending unary request bodies after an early response by [@​stefanvanburen](https://redirect.github.com/stefanvanburen) in [#​1008](https://redirect.github.com/connectrpc/connect-go/pull/1008)
- Report truncated envelopes as internal errors by [@​stefanvanburen](https://redirect.github.com/stefanvanburen) in [#​1015](https://redirect.github.com/connectrpc/connect-go/pull/1015)
- Fix removing all compressors on unary Connect clients by [@​emcfarlane](https://redirect.github.com/emcfarlane) in [#​1016](https://redirect.github.com/connectrpc/connect-go/pull/1016)
- Reject a negative Connect-Timeout-Ms instead of expiring the context by [@​emcfarlane](https://redirect.github.com/emcfarlane) in [#​1017](https://redirect.github.com/connectrpc/connect-go/pull/1017)
- Set Connect-Timeout-Ms when less than a millisecond remains by [@​emcfarlane](https://redirect.github.com/emcfarlane) in [#​1018](https://redirect.github.com/connectrpc/connect-go/pull/1018)
- Improve http2 client disconnect error handling by [@​emcfarlane](https://redirect.github.com/emcfarlane) in [#​1019](https://redirect.github.com/connectrpc/connect-go/pull/1019)
- Return the end-stream error when the body read fails after it by [@​stepan-romankov](https://redirect.github.com/stepan-romankov) in [#​1014](https://redirect.github.com/connectrpc/connect-go/pull/1014)
- Guard against typed nil \*connect.Error by [@​emcfarlane](https://redirect.github.com/emcfarlane) in [#​1020](https://redirect.github.com/connectrpc/connect-go/pull/1020)
- Enforce read max limit on unary errors by [@​emcfarlane](https://redirect.github.com/emcfarlane) in [#​1022](https://redirect.github.com/connectrpc/connect-go/pull/1022)
- Send a minimal end of stream when over WithSendMaxBytes by [@​emcfarlane](https://redirect.github.com/emcfarlane) in [#&#8203

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>grpc/grpc-go (google.golang.org/grpc)</summary>

### [`v1.85.0`](https://redirect.github.com/grpc/grpc-go/releases/tag/v1.85.0): Release 1.85.0

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/grpc/grpc-go/compare/v1.84.0...v1.85.0)

### New Features

- stats: Expose the effective client authority (sent on the wire as the HTTP/2 `:authority` header) in client `stats.OutHeader` events. ([#​9296](https://redirect.github.com/grpc/grpc-go/issues/9296))
  - Special Thanks: [@​aryansk](https://redirect.github.com/aryansk)
- metadata: Add `ValueFromOutgoingContext`, which reads a single metadata value from outgoing context without copying the entire outgoing metadata into a new map. ([#​9282](https://redirect.github.com/grpc/grpc-go/issues/9282))
  - Special Thanks: [@​yuyangguo42](https://redirect.github.com/yuyangguo42)

### Bug Fixes

- transport: Refine control buffer throttling to only count peer-induced control frames, raise the default `GRPC_GO_EXPERIMENTAL_CONTROL_BUFFER_THROTTLE_LIMIT` from 100 to 10,000, and close client connections if reads remain throttled for `10s`. ([#​9563](https://redirect.github.com/grpc/grpc-go/issues/9563))
- server: Ensure `Stop()` forcefully terminates the server while `GracefulStop()` is waiting for active handlers to complete. ([#​9394](https://redirect.github.com/grpc/grpc-go/issues/9394))
  - Special Thanks: [@​stanhu](https://redirect.github.com/stanhu)
- server: Unconditionally increment the highest-seen stream ID on when handling `HEADERS` frames to comply with [RFC 7540 §5.1.1](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7540.html#section-5.1.1). Previously, truncated `HEADERS` frames left the connection in an inconsistent state and allowed stream IDs to be reused by clients without resulting in a protocol error. ([#​9414](https://redirect.github.com/grpc/grpc-go/issues/9414))
- server: Terminate streams immediately when a `HEADERS` frame includes the `EndStream` bit. Previously, this caused server handlers to hang when reading a message. ([#​9391](https://redirect.github.com/grpc/grpc-go/issues/9391))
- server: Reject requests missing both `:authority` and `Host` headers with HTTP 400 and status `Internal`. ([#​9365](https://redirect.github.com/grpc/grpc-go/issues/9365))
- xds: Fix a bug where route header matchers with non-lowercase names failed to match routes. ([#​9353](https://redirect.github.com/grpc/

title: test(backend): keep one subtest's sync from deleting another's database
body:
## The flake

`TestSQLQueryStopOnError` failed in [CI run 41275973273](https://github.com/bytebase/bytebase/actions/runs/41275973273/job/124758123457) on a database its own `createDatabase` call had just created, taking out an unrelated dependency bump:

```
=== NAME  TestSQLQueryStopOnError/All_statements_succeed
    sql_stop_on_error_test.go:92:
        Error: Received unexpected error:
               not_found: database "instances/instance-.../databases/TestStopOnError4" not found
```

A re-run of the same commit was green.

## Why it happened

Not a missing wait before the sync. `registerDatabase` already held a per-instance lock around `GetInstance` → `UpdateInstance(sync_databases)` → `SyncInstance`, so those were ordered. It was a lost update to the sync list.

`Syncer.SyncInstance` marks deleted every `db` row the instance's `sync_databases` list leaves out. `registerDatabase` rebuilt that list as *the list `GetInstance` returned, plus my name*, and the server serves instances from a plain LRU with no generation guard (`backend/store/instance.go`, and test servers run with the cache on). A reader whose `SELECT` straddles another subtest's commit can put the pre-update copy back into the cache after `store.UpdateInstance`'s own refill. The next subtest then reads a list missing a sibling, writes it back, and its sync takes that sibling's database away mid-test.

That is the observed failure: subtest 4 finished registering, subtest 5 took the lock with a stale list, 4's row was marked deleted, and 4's next call returned not-found. It reads as "not found" rather than "was deleted" because `findDatabaseForResource(..., showDeleted=false)` filters the row out entirely.

Separately, each subtest did `err = ctl.createDatabase(...)`, assigning the `err` declared in the parent test body. Four parallel subtests wrote and read one variable, so one could assert on another's failure.

## The fix

- `registerDatabase` writes `sync_databases` from a per-instance record this process owns, seeded from the instance's own list and never from a read of the instance. No write can drop a database another subtest registered.
- `createDatabase` now goes through `waitDatabaseRegistered`, which re-syncs until `GetDatabase` reports the resource `ACTIVE` — bounded at three attempts, no sleep. That gives `createDatabase` the guarantee its callers assume, and covers the remaining case where the `SyncInstance` handler's own instance snapshot was stale.
- `err :=` in both tests in `sql_stop_on_error_test.go`.
- `backend/tests/database_test.go` pins the invariant: an out-of-band write of `sync_databases` that misses an earlier database must not unregister it.

`registerDatabase` keeps its old contract for `createDatabaseByRollout`, which registers a name *before* the rollout creates the database and so must not wait for a resource.

## Sibling tests

`TestWebhookIntegration` creates one instance and calls `createDatabase` from four parallel subtests the same way — same e

+// database.

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>connectrpc/validate-go (connectrpc.com/validate)</summary>

### [`v0.9.0`](https://redirect.github.com/connectrpc/validate-go/releases/tag/v0.9.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/connectrpc/validate-go/compare/v0.8.0...v0.9.0)

#### What's Changed

This release brings back the connect-go v1 API that v0.8.0 removed. `connectrpc.com/validate` now supports connect-go v1 and v2 at the same time, so you can upgrade services to connect-go v2 one at a time.

For connect-go v1, `Interceptor` and `NewInterceptor` are unchanged from v0.7.0:

```go
mux.Handle(userv1connect.NewUserServiceHandler(
      &userv1connect.UnimplementedUserServiceHandler{},
      connect.WithInterceptors(validate.NewInterceptor()),
))
```

For connect-go v2, use `NewServerInterceptor` and `NewClientInterceptor` as introduced in v0.8.0:

```go
server := connect.NewServer(validate.NewServerInterceptor())
userv1connect.RegisterUserServiceHandler(server, &userv1connect.UnimplementedUserServiceHandler{})
```

The options `WithValidator`, `WithValidateResponses`, and `WithoutErrorDetails` work with all three constructors. The public API is a superset of v0.7.0, so connect-go v1 users can upgrade from v0.7.x without code changes. The module now depends on both `connectrpc.com/connect` and `connectrpc.com/connect/v2`. See [#​59](https://redirect.github.com/connectrpc/validate-go/issues/59) for details.

**Full Changelog**: <https://github.com/connectrpc/validate-go/compare/v0.8.0...v0.9.0>

### [`v0.8.0`](https://redirect.github.com/connectrpc/validate-go/releases/tag/v0.8.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/connectrpc/validate-go/compare/v0.7.0...v0.8.0)

#### What's new for connect-go v2

This release of validate-go supports [connect-go v2](https://redirect.github.com/connectrpc/connect-go/releases/tag/v2.0.0). The module path stays `connectrpc.com/validate` but this version requires connect-go v2. v0.7.x is the last release series compatible with connect-go v1, so pin `connectrpc.com/validate@v0.7` if you're still on connect-go v1. Validation behavior, error codes, and error details are unchanged.

v2 separates server and client interceptors, so `NewInterceptor` splits into `NewServerInterceptor` and `NewClientInterceptor`. Interceptors now go on the `connect.Server` or `connect.Client`:

```diff
---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>pnpm/pnpm (pnpm)</summary>

### [`v12.16.1`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v12.16.1): pnpm 12.16.1

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v12.16.0...v12.16.1)

This release fixes `pnpm install` hanging on a cold store in workspaces that install Cargo crates, and `pnpm pack` shipping a file that `files` excludes by name.

##### Patch Changes

- `pnpm install` no longer hangs on a cold store in a workspace that also installs Cargo crates or a Rust toolchain.

- `pnpm pack` and `pnpm publish` now apply a `files` entry that names a file after the glob and directory entries, as npm does. A file excluded by name, such as `!dist/index.js`, stays out even when a later `dist/**` matches it. A file named by its path, such as `lib/secret.js`, ships even when a later `!lib/*.js` matches it.

- `pnpm install` no longer leaves a broken symlink in an injected workspace dependency when the package links to a file outside its published files and pnpm imports by hardlink. Installing a git dependency now skips internal directory symlinks when importing its files into the store.

- `pnpm install` now relinks a command that a workspace project renames into the projects that depend on it when `sharedWorkspaceLockfile` is `false` [pnpm/tasks#224](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/224).

- `pnpm install` and `pnpm rebuild` now refresh privately hoisted `.bin` shims in `node_modules/.pnpm/node_modules/.bin` after a dependency build replaces a script target with a native executable [#​17402](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17402).

- `pnpm install` now reads a package's manifest to decide its peer dependencies when it updates an existing lockfile, as it does when it resolves from scratch.

- Commands, `pnpm --version`, `pnpm self-update`, and invocations with unknown flags now apply the same `packageManager` and `devEngines.packageManager` settings when switching to the pinned pnpm version or recording it in `pnpm-lock.yaml`. `--c

title: fix(doris,starrocks): gate INTO OUTFILE and EXPLAIN ANALYZE off the AST
body:
## What

Adds the read-only-editor gates that `main`'s current omni pin requires.

This opened as a pin bump plus its gates, shipped together because the Doris gate does not compile without the pin and the StarRocks gate is only *needed* because of it. **#21737 has since bumped the pin on `main` by itself**, to `0d36648c` — a descendant of this branch's `b698d168`. Resolving that conflict took main's pin, so the bump is no longer part of this diff and only the gates remain.

That changes the urgency rather than the content: `main` today parses StarRocks `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` and has nothing stopping it over DML. The hole the gates close is live on `main`, not prospective.

## StarRocks: `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` is not a read over DML

The pin brings [bytebase/omni#574](https://github.com/bytebase/omni/pull/574), which replaces StarRocks' inherited Doris EXPLAIN modifier list with its own, so `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` now parses where it used to be a syntax error.

`ANALYZE` runs the statement rather than planning it, so the validator can no longer treat every `EXPLAIN` as a read. Measured with the pin bumped and the guard not yet in place:

| statement | classification |
|---|---|
| `EXPLAIN SELECT a FROM t` | accepted as read |
| `EXPLAIN ANALYZE SELECT a FROM t` | accepted as read |
| `EXPLAIN ANALYZE INSERT INTO t SELECT a FROM s` | **accepted as read** — a write on the read-only editor path |

`EXPLAIN ANALYZE` is now read-only only over a SELECT-family inner statement. StarRocks [aborts the INSERT transaction by default](https://docs.starrocks.io/docs/sql-reference/sql-statements/cluster-management/plan_profile/EXPLAIN_ANALYZE/), but the run still creates any partitions the rows need and those outlive the abort, so the abort is no licence to allow it. The plan-only modifiers (`VERBOSE`, `LOGICAL`, `COSTS`, `SCHEDULER`) never execute and stay readable over DML.

This applies to StarRocks the rule [bytebase/bytebase#21734](https://github.com/bytebase/bytebase/pull/21734) applies to MySQL, OceanBase and TiDB.

**Doris needs no equivalent case**: its `EXPLAIN` takes `ANALYZED` — a plan stage — and has no modifier that executes the query, so a guard there would be dead code.

## StarRocks: EXPLAIN was laundering exports past the gate (second commit)

Codex review flagged that the ANALYZE branch tested the inner node's *type* only, ignoring its `Into` clause. It was right, and the hole was wider than reported — the EXPLAIN path had its own copy of the read test, so **every** EXPLAIN shape accepted an export the bare statement refuses:

| statement | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `SELECT a FROM t INTO OUTFILE …` | refused | refused |
| `EXPLAIN SELECT … INTO OUTFILE …` | **accepted** | refused |
| `EXPLAIN VERBOSE SELECT … INTO OUTFILE …` | **accepted** | refused |
| `EXPLAIN ANALYZE SELECT … INTO OUTFILE …` | **accepted** | refused |
| `EXPLAIN ANALYZE (…)` / `((…))` export | **accepted** | refused |
| `EXPLAIN ANALYZE … UNION … INTO OUTFILE …` | **accepted** | r

title: fix(mysql,tidb,oceanbase): allow EXPLAIN ANALYZE over a read
body:
`EXPLAIN ANALYZE SELECT ...` was refused in the SQL editor with "Support read-only command statements only" on MySQL, TiDB and OceanBase, so profiling a query was impossible. Postgres already allows it. This brings the three into line — and, in the second commit, closes the export hole that writing the first one exposed.

## The distinction that matters

A plain `EXPLAIN` only plans, so it reads whatever it wraps, DML included. `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` **runs** what it wraps — `EXPLAIN ANALYZE DELETE` really deletes — so it is a read exactly when the wrapped statement is one. All three engines were taking the blunt option, `if stmt.Analyze { readOnly = false }`, which is safe but costs the legitimate case.

Postgres's validator already draws the line properly, and this copies it.

## The export gate

An `INTO OUTFILE` writes a file on the database server, so a query carrying one is not a read. Getting that right under `EXPLAIN` turned out to need more than reusing each engine's top-level test:

- **A set operation carries `INTO` on an arm**, never on the node the validator holds. `SelectIntoOpt` on the root of `SELECT 1 UNION SELECT a FROM t INTO OUTFILE '/x'` is nil, so TiDB classified that union as a read — with no `EXPLAIN` involved, on `main` today. Under `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` the same blind spot would have let the file actually be written, because `ANALYZE` executes.
- **MySQL and OceanBase were already safe here**: their `selectIntoTargets` searches the tree rather than the root. TiDB now does the same, through a visitor, so the three agree.
- **The two `EXPLAIN` forms are decided together.** TiDB's `explainReads` answers both, rather than having an `ANALYZE` path with a gate of its own that could drift from the top-level one. That drift is exactly the bug the first commit had.
- **A plain `EXPLAIN` over an export is refused too.** It does not run the statement, so nothing is written, but the editor must not label as a read what it refuses when asked directly.

## Measured across engines, after the change

The loosening — profiling a read becomes possible, every write form stays refused:

```
EXPLAIN SELECT count(*) FROM t WHERE a = 1              TI=ok      MY=ok      OC=ok      PG=ok
EXPLAIN ANALYZE SELECT count(*) FROM t WHERE a = 1      TI=ok      MY=ok      OC=ok      PG=ok
EXPLAIN ANALYZE SELECT a FROM t UNION SELECT a FROM s   TI=ok      MY=ok      OC=ok      PG=ok
EXPLAIN DELETE FROM t WHERE a = 1                       TI=ok      MY=ok      OC=ok
EXPLAIN ANALYZE DELETE FROM t WHERE a = 1               TI=REFUSED MY=REFUSED OC=REFUSED PG=REFUSED
EXPLAIN ANALYZE INSERT INTO t SELECT a FROM s           TI=REFUSED MY=REFUSED OC=REFUSED PG=REFUSED
EXPLAIN ANALYZE UPDATE t SET a = 1                      TI=REFUSED MY=REFUSED OC=REFUSED PG=REFUSED
```

The gate — every export shape refused, on both `EXPLAIN` paths and off them:

```
SELECT a FROM t INTO OUTFILE '/tmp/x'                   TI=REFUSED MY=REFUSED OC=REFUSED
SELECT 1 UNION SELECT a FROM t

title: chore(deps): bump omni to 073d42a9, parsing OceanBase's storage and index clauses
body:
Bumps `github.com/bytebase/omni` from `3f8520a4` (#570) to `073d42a9` (#573), three merges behind to current.

Only `go.mod` and `go.sum` change — no Bytebase code needed adapting.

## What it picks up

| omni PR | Effect here |
|---|---|
| [#573](https://github.com/bytebase/omni/pull/573) | OceanBase's storage, index and partition clauses parse |
| [#572](https://github.com/bytebase/omni/pull/572) | `mysql/review.ReviewOceanBase` removed — nothing here calls it |
| [#571](https://github.com/bytebase/omni/pull/571) | test-only |
| [#566](https://github.com/bytebase/omni/pull/566) | MariaDB: an unaliased `VALUES` subquery is named without MySQL's `ROW` |

## Why it matters

#573 is what users feel. A compatibility list from a customer had five OceanBase statements Bytebase rejected at parse time; four of them are this bump. The clause shapes are an index scope written as `LOCAL` or `GLOBAL`, a `BLOCK_SIZE` index option, and `ORGANIZATION INDEX` as a table option — all things OceanBase writes in its own `SHOW CREATE TABLE` output.

Verified both ends rather than assuming the merge was enough. The four statements fail to parse on the old pin and parse on this one:

```
old pin (3f8520a4)        new pin (073d42a9)
row 2  PARSE FAIL    →    PARSES
row 3  PARSE FAIL    →    PARSES
row 4  PARSE FAIL    →    PARSES
row 5  PARSE FAIL    →    PARSES
row 7  PARSE FAIL    →    still rejected
```

The fifth stays rejected deliberately: it is invalid on OceanBase itself, which answers 1064 for it on a live 4.3.5. omni#573 added a guard so both sides keep refusing it.

## Reviewer notes

**#572 removed an exported function.** `mysql/review.ReviewOceanBase` is gone. Checked before bumping: `runner/reviewrun/review_funcs.go` maps `Engine_OCEANBASE` to `oceanbasereview.ReviewOceanBase` and has since #21727, so there is no caller left. `go build ./...` confirms it.

**The OceanBase schema goldens do not move.** #573 changed how omni's `oceanbase/catalog` renders an index scope and a subpartition template, so `backend/plugin/schema/oceanbase` was the place to expect fixture churn. It is green with no re-record, so that rendering does not reach the DDL this repo generates.

## Verification

- `go mod tidy`: clean
- `go build ./...`: clean
- `go test` green: every package under `backend/plugin/parser/...`, `backend/plugin/schema/...` and `backend/plugin/advisor/...`, plus `backend/plugin/db/oceanbase` and `backend/runner/reviewrun`
- `gofmt` / `golangci-lint`: clean
- `go build -ldflags "-w -s"`: ok

Not a breaking change: no API, schema, proto, config, webhook or UI surface moves, and it only widens what the OceanBase parser accepts.

title: fix(doris,starrocks): let a session SET through the read-only editor path
body:
`SET time_zone = 'UTC'` in the SQL editor failed with **"Support read-only command statements only"** on Doris and StarRocks. It parses cleanly to `*ast.SetStmt`, but `isReadOnlyAST` had no case for that node, so it fell to the `default` arm and `validateQuery` answered false.

These two were the only engines refusing it. MySQL, Postgres, TiDB, OceanBase, Redshift and Snowflake all allow a SET, and this follows them.

## Why it mirrors MySQL and Postgres exactly

I started designing a rule that would refuse `SET GLOBAL`, then read what the second return value actually feeds. `isExplicitReadOnly` is **not** a permission gate — each driver's `QueryConn` reads it to choose between `QueryContext` and `ExecContext`. A SET returns no rows, so it has to be false, or the driver would try to read a result set that isn't there. MySQL and Postgres both express that as `hasExecute = true` and `return true, !hasExecute, nil`.

So scope is deliberately not distinguished: a global SET is permitted here exactly as it is for MySQL and Postgres, because this switch picks the execution path rather than the authorization. Checked the other half of that too — Doris and StarRocks both answer `false` to `EngineSupportQueryNewACL`, so their query ACL falls back to `bb.sql.select` for every statement type and nothing further gates this. `getQueryType` still classifies a SET as DDL, which is its documented safe upper bound and is unused on this path.

## Narrower than MySQL in one respect

Only variable assignment qualifies. `SET PASSWORD` and `SET DEFAULT STORAGE VAULT` are separate AST nodes and stay refused — which matches Postgres, where only `VariableSetStmt` is allowed. They administer the server rather than prepare a read. Easy to widen to MySQL's full list if that is preferred.

## Verification

Grounded on a real engine rather than on the grammar. Against Apache Doris 3.1.4, whose `VERSION()` is `5.7.99`, all nine SET spellings probed execute without error, global scope included.

End to end through the registry, for the exact reported statement:

```
DORIS      readOnly=true allQuery=false
STARROCKS  readOnly=true allQuery=false
```

Both test batteries are mutation-checked — five deliberate breakages each fail a case: accepting every node as a session SET, folding `SET PASSWORD` in with it, pinning the second return value back to `true`, dropping `UNSET VARIABLE`, and never setting `hasExecute`. The script cases are the load-bearing ones: `SET time_zone = 'UTC'; DROP TABLE t` is still refused, and a SET anywhere in a script makes the whole script need executing.

- `gofmt`: clean
- `golangci-lint run --fix -j 8`: 0 issues
- `go test` green: `parser/{doris,starrocks}`, `db/{doris,starrocks}`, `api/v1`

title: refactor(doris,starrocks): split the engines, and fix their changed-resource extraction
body:
Doris and StarRocks were already forked in omni, and each already had its own Bytebase parser plugin, but three couplings were left behind. This closes them, and in doing so fixes a bug that the split made visible.

## Changed-resource extraction was broken for both engines

`parser/mysql/resource_change.go` was registered for `DORIS` and `STARROCKS`, and it type-asserts every node to MySQL's `*OmniAST`. Both engines produce their own `omniAST`, so the assertion always failed:

```
DORIS      CREATE TABLE t (a INT) DISTRIBUTED BY HASH(a) BUCKETS 1;  EXTRACT ERR: expected OmniAST for MySQL
STARROCKS  ALTER TABLE t ADD COLUMN b INT;                           EXTRACT ERR: expected OmniAST for MySQL
MYSQL      CREATE TABLE t (a INT);                                   ok
```

`backend/runner/plancheck/statement_report_executor.go` calls this for every engine, so changed resources and affected rows have been unavailable for Doris and StarRocks DDL — not partial, erroring.

Each engine now extracts over its own AST. This is a port, not a copy: these engines name tables with `*ObjectName` (`Parts` holding `table`, `db.table` or `catalog.db.table`) where MySQL carries a `*TableRef` with a `Schema` field, and their `UPDATE`/`DELETE` name a single target with sources in `FROM`/`USING` rather than MySQL's table list. Materialized views are first-class here and get the same database-only treatment as views. `CREATE FUNCTION` is deliberately absent — its AST keeps the name inside `RawSignature`, so there is nothing to qualify by.

## Doris has its own driver

`db/starrocks` registered both engines against one driver and branched internally on `dbType`. `db/doris` is now a fork of it, following `db/oceanbase` (clean fork, no import of its origin).

Three of those branches carried no information — the driver only ever served these two engines, so `dbType == DORIS || dbType == STARROCKS` was always true. The rest were real and separated cleanly:

| | Doris | StarRocks |
|---|---|---|
| `UNIQUE_CHECKS`/`FOREIGN_KEY_CHECKS` dump bracket | emitted | dropped (no such session variables) |
| materialized views | `mv_infos()` table function | `information_schema.materialized_views` + sync-rollup filter |
| system-database exclusion | `information_schema`, `_statistics_` | plus `sys` |

Each driver also splits `DELIMITER` scripts with its own grammar; both were calling omni's MySQL splitter.

## MySQL's extractor no longer carries StarRocks code

`base.GetQuerySpan` assigns `gCtx.Engine` *after* looking up `spans[engine]`, and `mysql/query_span.go` registers only `MYSQL` and `MARIADB`, so the extractor's `Engine_STARROCKS` branches were unreachable from any production path once StarRocks forked. The `normalizeStarRocksCluster` flag was threaded through 120 sites to be read at exactly one.

They were not unreachable from *tests*, which is worth a reviewer's attention: two cases built a MySQL context and then overwrote `gCtx.Engine` by hand, and a golden fixture the harnes

+	defer func() { require.NoError(t, second.closeCloudSQL()) }()
+
+	// The network name keys a process-wide registry. Sharing one name let the
+	// second driver take over the first driver's pool and dial its own instance.
+	require.NotEqual(t, first.cloudSQLProtocol, second.cloudSQLProtocol)
+
+	firstConfig, err := mysql.ParseDSN(firstDSN)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	require.Equal(t, first.cloudSQLProtocol, firstConfig.Net)
+
+	secondConfig, err := mysql.ParseDSN(secondDSN)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	require.Equal(t, second.cloudSQLProtocol, secondConfig.Net)
+}
+
+func TestCloudSQLIAMNetworkNameDeregisteredOnClose(t *testing.T) {
+	ctx := context.Background()
+
+	driver := &Driver{}
+	dsn, err := driver.getCloudSQLConnection(ctx, cloudSQLIAMConnectionConfig(cloudSQLTestInstance))
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	require.NoError(t, driver.closeCloudSQL())
+
+	// The registration would otherwise pin the closed connector in the MySQL
+	// driver's process-wide map, one entry per driver ever opened.
+	pool, err := sql.Open("mysql", dsn)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	defer pool.Close()
+	err = pool.PingContext(ctx)
+	require.Error(t, err)
+	require.NotErrorIs(t, err, cloudsqlconn.ErrDialerClosed)
+}

title: refactor(oceanbase): give OceanBase its own schema plugin
body:
OceanBase has had its own omni parser since omni#559, but in Bytebase it still ran through `backend/plugin/schema/mysql`: the shared walk-through re-parsed every OceanBase statement from its own text because `mysqlparser.GetOmniNode` rejects an `omni/oceanbase/ast` node. omni#569 forked the remaining packages, so OceanBase can now have its own schema plugin.

## What moves

A new `backend/plugin/schema/oceanbase` registering exactly the eight features OceanBase has today, one of each:

```
GenerateMigration  GetDatabaseDefinition  GetDatabaseMetadata  GetFunctionDefinition
GetProcedureDefinition  GetTableDefinition  GetViewDefinition  WalkThroughWithContext
```

It follows `schema/tidb`, which is already a standalone per-engine package with its own copies of these files and no import of `schema/mysql`. Three more files came along because the compiler needs them: `system_versioning.go`, `database.go`, and `format_view_body.go` (which `GetViewDefinition` calls).

`schema/mysql` gives up those eight registrations in the same commit — the registry panics on a duplicate — and `walkThroughOmniNode` is deleted from both packages. The walk-through now reads its nodes through `oceanbaseparser.GetOmniNode`, and tags its metadata model `Engine_OCEANBASE` instead of `Engine_MYSQL` (behaviour-neutral today: `getIsDetailCaseSensitive` groups them).

Also here: `reviewrun` switches to `oceanbase/review.ReviewOceanBase`, and the `GetSDLDiff` registration point is removed — no engine registered it and nothing called it.

## No SDL for OceanBase

The fork omits `sdl_migration.go` and `get_multi_file_definition.go`, which also avoids `mysqlVersionFor` reading OceanBase's `5.7.25-OceanBase_CE-v4.3.5.6` as MySQL 5.7 and picking 5.7 collation and display-width defaults. `TestSDLRegistrationsAreMySQLOnly` stays in `schema/mysql` and still passes, so the decision is pinned by a test.

## A regression this found

Parsing OceanBase with its own parser exposed one. At the previous omni pin, the same synced view definition behaved differently in the two packages:

```
schema/mysql     (omni mysql/catalog):      <nil>
schema/oceanbase (omni oceanbase/catalog):  unexpected token (line 3, column 87)
```

That text is the canonical form an engine writes back for a view over a derived table joined to a table — what Bytebase reads when it syncs a view. `oceanbase/parser` was missing omni#560, which this pin (omni#570) adds. `TestGetDatabaseMetadataSyncedView` pins it so the pin cannot slip back.

That pin also makes OceanBase's parser stricter in one place, the other half of omni#560: a lone derived table, `LATERAL` table, or `JSON_TABLE` in parentheses is now a syntax error, as MySQL 8.0 and the sibling `mysql`, `mariadb` and `tidb` parsers already treat it. A statement of that shape that OceanBase review used to accept now fails it, which matches what the server does with it.

## Verification

- `golangci-lint` (CI's pinned version): 0 issues, and `--fix` changed nothing outsid

title: fix(db): release the Cloud SQL connector with the driver
body:
## Summary

#21721 reports a server with a Google Cloud SQL IAM instance growing in memory and goroutines until it is OOM-killed. `GetGCPConnectionConfig` builds a `cloudsqlconn.Dialer` on every driver open and nothing closed it. The connector reschedules an ephemeral certificate refresh for as long as it lives, so each orphaned dialer kept refreshing and holding its cache for the life of the process.

- **The connector lives and dies with the driver.** It is kept on the `Driver` and closed in `Close`, as the SSH client already was.
- **A failed `Open` releases it too.** `db.Open` discards a driver whose `Open` failed without calling `Close`, so a failing instance leaked one connector per attempt, needing no successful connection at all. `Open` now routes its failure through `Close`, which in turn had to tolerate a half-built driver (`d.db` can be nil).
- **MySQL registers its own network name.** It registered the dial function under the fixed name `"cloudsqlconn"`. That name keys a process-wide registry in go-sql-driver, so with two Cloud SQL IAM MySQL instances in use the last driver opened won, and the other instance's pool dialed the wrong host with no error. Each driver now uses `"cloudsqlconn-" + uuid` and deregisters it on `Close`, as the SSH path at `mysql.go:141` already did. A registration left behind also pins the closed connector in that map for good.
- **Postgres stops abandoning its pool when `Open` fails.** Routing the failure through `Close` picked this up: with `postgres_database_tenant_mode` set, the database-owner lookup runs after `sql.Open`, and a failure there leaked the connection pool, the pgx connection-string registration, and any SSH client. Plan checks and migrate tasks run that path.

## Notes for review

- Measured per-dialer cost, with real dialers and a throwaway credential: one that has never dialed costs 0 goroutines and ~0.02 MiB, while one that has dialed and is then orphaned parks 2 goroutines for as long as its refresh keeps retrying. So the growth tracks dialers that connected, not dialers that were built. The reporter's exact goroutine count is not reproducible here, since it depends on whether their refreshes are succeeding, but the mechanism and its unboundedness are confirmed.
- `NewDialer` also generates a 2048-bit RSA key, about 130 ms of CPU per driver open, plus an admin API round trip and a certificate fetch on first dial. #21721 suggests pooling one dialer per credential to avoid that. This PR does not: pooling needs credential-rotation and eviction semantics, and the leak is fixed without it.
- OceanBase carries a copy of the same Cloud SQL branch from the driver split in `c872cacaf7`, but Cloud SQL does not host OceanBase and `DataSourceForm.tsx` offers Cloud SQL IAM only for MySQL, Postgres, Spanner and BigQuery, so that branch is unreachable. Left untouched; removing it is a separate cleanup.
- The network name uses the full UUID rather than the SSH path's 8-character prefix, because a collisio

title: fix(mcp): state the write confirmation on the MCP Access page
body:
## Summary

The MCP Access page lists what each access mode allows. Its "Run DML and DDL statements" row did not mention the confirmation #21709 added, while the approval and masking-exemption rows state theirs ("Each decision is confirmed in the user's MCP client before it is made"). This PR adds it in all five locales and updates the row table in the access policy design doc to match.

The row's details now read:

> INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, CREATE, ALTER, DROP through queries, as far as the engine and the user's own permissions allow · Where the user's MCP client supports confirmations, a query that is not a read as far as the engine can check it runs only after the user confirms it · In other clients such a query can run without asking

## Why it reads this way

The design doc's "Keeping the rows true" asks every line to hold on each axis: mode, engine, effect, complement and method.

- **Engine.** "As far as the engine can check it" is the bound the request-access row already uses. On an engine with no query validator, nothing counts as a read, so every query asks.
- **Client.** The condition comes first. A client that declares no form runs the query at once (#21709), so an unconditional "only after" would be false there.
- **Operation.** The line says "query", the word the row's first item uses. A statement filed as an issue, through `propose_database_change` or the form's Create an issue, runs as a rollout task under the project's approval policy, with no confirmation in the client. The rollouts row covers that.
- **"Can run".** Through `call_api`, `SQLService/Query` refuses a possible write. Only `query_database` runs one without asking, in a client without the form.
- **Mode.** The row is served only under Read-write.

The doc gains one paragraph on why this row states its confirmation with a condition: `decide_issue` and the other confirmed tools refuse in a client without the form, while `query_database` runs the query.

The translations reuse each locale's existing words for the engine bound and for "query" from the row's first item. The consent page shows these details after Show details. The tests refer to locale keys, not text.

## Context

Follows #21709 (BYT-9292). The write-confirmation design's section 4 notes that the access policy design's DML and DDL row gains the confirmation, as its approval and exemption rows state theirs.

## Test plan

- [x] Each claim checked on main at `ad04e189a3`:
  - `SQLService/Query` refuses a possible write unless `query_database` confirmed that exact request (`backend/api/v1/sql_service.go:358`, `:388-389`), and `call_api` cannot confirm one (`backend/api/v1/mcp_sql_write.go:30-36`).
  - `SQLService/Export` refuses a possible write from an MCP session (`sql_service.go:1244`).
  - `query_database` runs the query at once when the client declared no form (`backend/api/mcp/tool_query.go:158-159`).
  - With no validator, nothing is a read (`nonReadReason`, `backend/api/v1/mcp_sql_clamp.go`).
  - Rollo

title: feat(helm-charts): pass --metrics-remote-access and --ha
body:
Closes #21722.

## Problem

`/metrics` has answered loopback clients only since 3.22.0 (`metricsAccessHandler`, `backend/server/metrics.go`), and the chart renders a closed argument list — `--data`, `--port`, `--external-url`, optionally `--enable-json-logging` — with no `extraArgs` and no env passthrough for flags. Chart 1.1.6 then added `bytebase.podAnnotations`, documented as useful for metrics scrapers, with a commented `prometheus.io/scrape` example. A scraper that finds the pod through those annotations gets a 404, and nothing in the chart can turn the gate off.

## Change

Two typed values under `bytebase.option`, matching the existing `enable-json-logging` shape:

- `metrics-remote-access` renders `--metrics-remote-access`.
- `ha` renders `--ha`.

Both default to `false`, so the rendered command is byte-identical until one is set.

`--ha` is here because the HA runbook requires the flag on every replica sharing a metadata database, and the chart gave no way to pass it. The flag turns off the in-process metadata cache (`store.New(ctx, pgURL, !profile.HA)`), so the replica this chart manages was keeping its cache and serving metadata that other replicas had already changed. `--saas` and `--memory-profile-threshold` are deliberately left out.

Docs:

- A "Scraping /metrics" section in the chart README with the `--set` one-liner and a values snippet, plus the caution the issue asked for: `/metrics` carries no authentication of its own, and an Ingress or HTTPRoute matching `/` publishes it to everything that reaches the route.
- The `podAnnotations` comment in `values.yaml` now says that annotations alone do not open `/metrics` and that `prometheus.io/port` must match `bytebase.option.port`.
- Parameter rows for both new values, and for `enable-json-logging`, which the table omitted.
- The HA runbook and README no longer claim the chart cannot pass `--ha`.

Chart 1.1.8, packaged into `docs/` via `scripts/package_helm.sh`.

## Verification

- `helm lint` passes.
- The container runs `/bin/sh -c` over one string, so rendering alone proves little. Extracted `args[0]` from the rendered StatefulSet, ran `sh -n` on it, then executed it with a fake `bytebase` on `PATH` that echoes its arguments: `argv: [--data] [/var/opt/bytebase] [--port] [8080] [--external-url] [...] [--ha] [--metrics-remote-access]`.
- Both argument branches covered: the plain one and `externalPg.escapePassword=true`, which prepends an `export PG_URL=` line.
- Defaults render neither flag; explicit `false` renders neither; both README examples work verbatim; `scripts/azure-marketplace/values-azure.yaml` renders unchanged.
- `bytebase --help` from a build of this tree lists `--metrics-remote-access` and `--ha` as boolean flags, matching how the chart renders them.
- The packaged tarball's digest matches its `index.yaml` entry, the file set is unchanged from 1.1.7, and `helm template` straight from `docs/bytebase-1.1.8.tgz` renders both flags.

No application code changed, so the Go

@@ -99,6 +99,29 @@ upgrade bytebase-release bytebase-repo/bytebase
 
 Bytebase migrates its metadata database at startup and opens its port only after the migration finishes, which can take a long time on a large metadata database. The chart sets only a readiness probe on `/healthz`, so the pod stays unready during the migration instead of being restarted. If you pass `--wait` or `--atomic` to `helm upgrade`, set `--timeout` above the expected migration time. Helm's default is `5m`, and `--atomic` rolls the release back to the previous Bytebase version when it expires, which does not support the migrated metadata database.
 
+## Scraping /metrics
+
+Since Bytebase 3.22.0, the Prometheus endpoint at `/metrics` answers loopback clients only. An in-cluster scraper gets a 404 until the server starts with `--metrics-remote-access`:
+
+```bash
+helm -n <YOUR_NAMESPACE> \
+--set "bytebase.option.metrics-remote-access"=true \
+upgrade <RELEASE_NAME> bytebase-repo/bytebase
+```
+
+`bytebase.podAnnotations` makes the pod discoverable, and needs this value set as well. Keep `prometheus.io/port` equal to `bytebase.option.port`:
+
+```yaml

title: feat(mcp): offer to file a possible write as an issue
body:
## Summary

#21709 asks the user before `query_database` runs a statement that may write, with two choices: Run now and Change it in chat. A user who wants the change reviewed first had to say so in chat. This PR adds a third choice, **Create an issue**, which files the request as a change issue, as `propose_database_change` does (BYT-9292).

- **The choice.** The form offers Run now (still the default), Create an issue, and Change it in chat. Create an issue appears only when the call carries the agent's title for the issue and names no schema, since a plan carries no schema and its rollout would run with the database's default one.
- **The title.** `query_database` takes `issueTitle`, which the agent writes from the conversation when it sends a statement that may write. The choice shows it, as `Create an issue titled "…"`, so the user sees the title it files. Bytebase generates no title, so a project that requires a manual title, the default since 3.14, gets the agent's title, as it does from `propose_database_change`. The description asks the agent to say what the change does without data values, since webhooks carry the title.
- **What it files.** The sheet, plan, plan checks and issue that `propose_database_change` creates, under the user's own permissions. It creates no rollout. Bytebase creates the rollout once the approval flow is done and the plan checks pass with no errors, and the environment's rollout policy decides when it runs.
- **What it reports.** The issue's name and link, and that nothing ran. When the plan checks did not pass, the result names the errors, since Bytebase then creates no rollout on its own. When they are still running after the tool's wait, it says so. The approval status is on the issue page. A new change issue reports it as checking until Bytebase finds the approval flow, and an approval comes later from another person, so the user asks the agent about it when they want to know.
- **The answer is checked like Run now's.** An issue can roll out with no approval when no rule applies, so the answer must be signed for this request and fresh. A changed database, or an answer older than 10 minutes, gets `STALE_CONFIRMATION`, and nothing is filed. An answer that picks Create an issue on a form that did not offer it files nothing. The signed state also covers the title, which decides whether the form offers the choice, what the choice shows, and what it files, so a second round that adds or changes the title gets `STALE_CONFIRMATION` too. A request that names a schema is never offered the choice, so its state covers no title. Query still checks only the statement's digest, since it never sees the title.
- **Tool description.** Besides `issueTitle`, `query_database` tells the agent to call `propose_database_change` when the user asks for an issue or a review. Since that tool takes no schema, the agent qualifies each name when the request named one.

## Notes for review

- `propose_database_change`'s sheet, plan and iss

title: feat(mssql): sync the default schema and synonyms, and pass the default schema to review
body:
## What

- **Default schema**: SQL Server's `SyncDBSchema` reads `SCHEMA_NAME()` into `DatabaseSchemaMetadata.default_schema`, and the rule review passes it as `review.Target.DefaultSchema`.
- **Synonyms**: the sync lists each schema's synonyms in `SchemaMetadata.synonyms`, with the server, database, schema, and object each stands for (`PARSENAME`).
- **omni** is pinned to `3de91a9a`, the merge commit of bytebase/omni#563, which adds those fields. Main pinned `0d36648c`; the move also brings in bytebase/omni#580 (MySQL-family tokens and comment closes).

## Why

- **Unqualified names go unchecked today.** SQL Review V2's SQL Server WALK_THROUGH judges no unqualified name while `DefaultSchema` is empty, and Bytebase never set it. So `ALTER TABLE t ...`, `TRUNCATE TABLE t`, and `CREATE TABLE t` of a taken name are checked only when written as `dbo.t`.
- **The synced value is the one the change sees.** Bytebase syncs and runs changes as the same admin data source, so `SCHEMA_NAME()` read in the sync is the schema the change's unqualified names land in. Checked on SQL Server 2022:
  - a `db_owner` user with `DEFAULT_SCHEMA = app` gets `app`, creates `CREATE TABLE newt` in `app`, and resolves an unqualified name in `app` first, then in `dbo`;
  - a sysadmin gets `dbo`, whatever its mapped user's default schema.
- **The synonyms come next.** DML resolves through synonyms, so the walk needs them before it can claim that a DML target does not exist. The omni change that reads them follows this PR.

## Tests

- `TestSyncDefaultSchemaAndSynonyms` (SQL Server container):
  - as `sa`, the default schema is `dbo`, and one-, two-, and four-part synonyms come back split;
  - as a `db_owner` login whose default schema is `app`, it is `app`.
- `TestRuleExecutorPassesTheSyncedDefaultSchema`: `CREATE TABLE t` on a database whose synced `dbo` holds `t` gets the WALK_THROUGH finding `an object named t already exists`, and none without a synced default schema. The test fails with the wiring line removed.
- Passed locally:
  - `go test ./backend/runner/... ./backend/plugin/db/mssql/ ./backend/api/v1/... ./backend/store/`
  - the server build
  - after merging main and moving the pin: `go test` on `backend/plugin/parser/{mysql,tidb,mariadb,oceanbase,tsql}/...`, `backend/plugin/db/mssql/...`, `backend/plugin/schema/...`, and `backend/runner/reviewrun/...`
- `golangci-lint` v2.14.0 reports no issue on the changed lines.
