## Summary

The e2e routine (#21633) had its first full local run on 2026-10-22: green on main `5f374e7` with 2 flaky tests. The run worked, but it showed where the routine's scripts record, classify or attribute the wrong thing. This PR fixes those gaps. Only `.claude/skills/e2e-routine/` changes.

| Gap the run found | Fix |
|---|---|
| The ledger recorded `634bde57`, a local overlay commit GitHub never had, so the next run's attribution baseline was unusable | The ledger records the main commit under test: the merge base when local commits touch only the e2e tree or `.claude/`. `ledger.sh record` refuses a SHA not on main, and `last-green` skips entries not on main |
| `attribute.py` treated an unknown baseline as "0 commits" and fell back to the area owner | Exits 2 when `--since` or `--head` is not a commit |
| `attribute.py` ignored commits to the spec itself, so it missed that #21631's locator broke `workspace-setup.spec.ts` | Scores commits to the spec and to `frontend/tests/e2e/framework/` as test changes; on that case it now names #21631 |
| A `test.fail()` lock that passed on some attempts was reported as an ordinary flake, quoting the expected error and no screenshot | A truth table in `references/triage.md` sorts every case: new `lock_unstable` bucket and LOCK-UNSTABLE class, timed-out locks are `failed` or `flaky`, and the error and evidence come from the attempt whose status differs from the expected one |
| Only failed rows were rerun alone, so a flaky row that fails every time in isolation (a broken locator) would be logged as noise | Phase 4 isolates flaky and lock-unstable rows too; a flaky row red in isolation is worked as failed. A strict-mode violation gets a spec-defect hint |
| SKILL.md's overlay recipe would revert main's changes to the suite | Removed, with the bootstrap prompt, now that the skill is on main |
| All checkouts shared `/tmp/e2e-routine/CURRENT`, so two local runs could take over each other's run directory | One results root per checkout |
| `build.sh` ran `pnpm --dir frontend` from the repo root, which picks pnpm 10 instead of the pinned 11 | Runs pnpm inside `frontend/`, lets it rebuild a `node_modules` another pnpm laid out, and preflight fails on a version mismatch |
| `run-suite.sh status` printed a stray `0` and counted Playwright call-log lines as tests | Counts only result lines; one output line |

title: feat(mcp): add request_access_grant and ask Claude Code users before access grants and exemptions
body:
# feat(mcp): add request_access_grant and ask Claude Code users before access grants and exemptions

Part of BYT-9292 user journey 1, after #21588, #21593, #21626 and #21627. This is PR 1 of 2 for the access-request tool design in `plans/2026-10-22-mcp-access-request-tool-design.md`.

We reran journey 1 the way a new user would, in Claude Code's default auto mode. The agent never got the names. Claude Code blocked its access request twice, and the user saw a notification, not a prompt they could approve.

Auto mode sends each MCP call that no permission rule matches to a classifier. Without an allow rule, its Permission Grant and PII Data Handling rules clear only when the user's own message names the action. In natural sessions, the classifier stopped the agent in three of four sessions: twice on the `call_api` `CreateAccessGrant` call, and once at its `search_api` lookup of the request's format. It blocked the agent's first `grant_masking_exemption` call in six of six. A blocked call shows a notification, not a prompt. To go on, the user has to find the call under `/permissions` → Recently denied and retry it, or ask again.

What changes:

- **A new tool, `request_access_grant`,** files an access grant through `CreateAccessGrant` for one database, named by its full resource name as `query_database` prints it. It takes the statement, an optional schema and container, unmask and export, a reason, and a required `durationHours`. The duration is sent as `ttl`, so the access starts at approval. The tool reads the database for the request's project, because a workspace instance's database name carries no project, and it sends no creator. Every check stays in the API: the name, just-in-time access, the workspace maximum expiration, the MCP ceiling, and the refusal of an MCP request that no person would approve.
- **Claude Code's `anthropic/requiresUserInteraction` flag on `request_access_grant` and `grant_masking_exemption`.** Claude Code then shows a permission prompt on every call, even in auto and bypassPermissions modes and despite allow rules, and the classifier does not decide. The prompt shows every input in full, with Yes and No only. Other clients ignore the key, and Bytebase's checks and approval do not depend on it. On the exemption tool the user answers Claude Code's prompt, then Bytebase's form. The form stays: it binds the exact change in Bytebase and covers clients without the flag.
- **`grant_masking_exemption` takes `columns`, a list, in place of `column`.** Several columns of one table become one exemption entry, written as the console writes it (`resource.column_name in [...]`), so one call shows one prompt and one form. In the live check the agent exempted the two name columns in two calls, so the user answered four dialogs. The form counts the columns before naming them, so a cut line still shows how many the exemption covers.
- **`call_api` keeps serving `CreateAccessGrant`,** for other clients and for the runs that the flag deni

title: fix(sql)!: require bb.sql.explain on every database a plan describes
body:
## Why

A plan names the tables it reads, but explain was checked only on the database the editor is connected to. An explain request had no query spans, and a typed `EXPLAIN` had a span with no source columns, so both ended at one database-level check. `EXPLAIN SELECT * FROM db_b.secret` on `db_a` yielded `db_b`'s plan to a user with explain on `db_a` alone. A typed `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` was classified as its inner statement and passed on `bb.sql.select` alone while still returning a plan.

This closes the last open item of `docs/design/query-plan-visualizer.md` §3.5; the access-grant leak closed in #21619.

## What

One rule: the databases a plan describes are the ones the statement's tables live in, whatever the statement is.

- Every query span now carries the tables its statement touches. The parsers already collected them for every statement type and then blanked the list for anything but a SELECT; PostgreSQL, MySQL, TiDB, Oracle, Snowflake, SQL Server and GoogleSQL keep it. `Results` stay empty for non-reads, so masking is unaffected.
- Explain requests get query spans like any other request, so the bare statements the driver wraps name the databases the plan describes.
- `checkExplainAccess` requires `bb.sql.explain` on the connected database and every tracked database the statement references, through the same per-target check writes use (`authorizeWriteTargets` at database level). A name is resolved as typed, and case-insensitively on engines that fold case, so `DB_B` reaches `db_b`. A database in another project fails closed, as it does for a write. Access grants do not apply. What the span cannot place in a tracked database — a system schema such as Oracle's `SYS` or Snowflake's `SNOWFLAKE`, a procedure call naming no table — is left to the connected database's check.
- SQL Server's access-table walker now visits INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, MERGE and ORDER BY, and Oracle's collector names DML targets, so a cross-database write under SHOWPLAN or `EXPLAIN PLAN` is checked on the target database too. Snowflake's walker still reads only queries, which is what Snowflake's EXPLAIN plans.
- A typed `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` carries `QuerySpan.ExplainAnalyze` (PostgreSQL, MySQL, TiDB) and, on the per-statement ACL engines, needs the executed statement's permission as well as explain. Engines outside that ACL (MariaDB, OceanBase, CockroachDB) are unchanged.
- A statement whose span names no table, such as `EXEC dbo.p` or `CALL p()`, is checked on the connected database alone, as every explain was before.
- The design doc's §3.5 and §6 are updated.

## Breaking Changes

Permission logic changes for explain:

- An explain of a statement that references another database now requires `bb.sql.explain` on that database too, and a database in another project is refused outright, as a write into one is. Users who could explain a cross-database read or write with explain on the connected database alone are now denied on the other database.
- A typed `EXPLAIN ANALYZE`

title: test(e2e): scope the setup own-instance assertion to the main page area
body:
## Summary

The own-instance step of `workspace-setup.spec.ts` ("first-run setup: skip, no project, own instance, then the sample") asserts that the project's Instances page shows a "Connect instance" button. #21631 changed that assertion to `page.getByRole("button", { name: "Connect instance" })`, but the page has two buttons with that name:

1. the page's primary **+ Connect instance** button (top right, `data-product-intro-target="create-instance"`), which the "Connect the instance" intro points at;
2. the **Connect instance** step in the Getting started bar at the bottom (`data-testid="setup-step-connect-instance"`, from #21594 / #21599).

Once the bar renders, the locator matches both and Playwright's strict mode fails the step:

```
Error: strict mode violation: getByRole('button', { name: 'Connect instance' }) resolved to 2 elements
```

This change scopes the locator to the main layout region (`#bb-layout-main`), which holds the page button but not the bar. The next assertion, on the "Connect the instance" intro, is unchanged. No product code changes.

## Evidence

Found by the e2e routine's local run on main `5f374e7782` (2026-10-22):

- Full suite (`--retries=2`): failed on attempt 1, passed on the retry, so it was reported as flaky.
- File alone, before this change (`--retries=0 --repeat-each=2`): **0/2**, same strict-mode error both times.
- File alone, after this change (`--retries=0 --repeat-each=3`): **3/3** green.
- The changed spec type-checks with `tsc --strict` (the frontend gate's `tsc` projects and Biome do not cover `tests/e2e`).

## Test plan

```bash
cd frontend && pnpm exec playwright test workspace-setup/workspace-setup.spec.ts --retries=0 --repeat-each=3 --reporter=list
```

title: feat(sql-editor): export to SharePoint and allow turning off download
body:
## Summary

Lets SQL Editor exports go straight to a SharePoint document library, and lets a workspace turn off Download, so governed workspaces can stop handing export files to users' machines. API design: [export destination API doc](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ND4XJmZDzMlQq7_n9W3nsk-rvJ--3SmJ0Ct4R4tgZsQ/edit). Product boundary: `docs/adr/0007-sharepoint-export-ownership-boundary.md`, evidence in BOT-156.

- **Export destinations** (`ExportDestination`: `DOWNLOAD`, `SHAREPOINT`): `DOWNLOAD` returns the export in the response, as today. `SHAREPOINT` uploads it to the project's SharePoint folder. S3 and Google Drive are expected later.
- **Disable download** (`QueryDataPolicy.disable_download`, workspace-level): turns off the Download destination. It defaults to false, so existing workspaces keep downloading and no migration is needed. SharePoint has no policy switch: configuring the workspace credentials and a project folder is the approval to export there. Like `disable_copy_data`, the field is read only from the workspace policy. Changing it needs `FEATURE_QUERY_POLICY`; enforcement does not check the license. Who may export is still `bb.sql.export` (#21690): an export grant satisfies that permission but never adds a destination, so with Download disabled and no project SharePoint folder, Export is refused for everyone.
- **Export** (`ExportRequest.destination`, `ExportResponse.uri`): `SQLService.Export` rejects a disabled Download, or SharePoint without the plan feature, credentials, or a project folder, with an error before running the query, for every caller including MCP. Unspecified means `DOWNLOAD`. A SharePoint export uploads the statement and result files unzipped into a per-export folder `<UTC>-<email>-<database>-<id>` and returns the folder URL. The folder is resolved before the query runs. Files up to 4 MiB upload in one request and larger ones through upload sessions, in parallel, with bounded retries that honor `Retry-After` and reconcile lost responses. A failure before the first upload reports that nothing was uploaded. Zip passwords apply only to downloads. Batch export reports each database separately.
- **Workspace SharePoint credentials** (`settings/EXPORT` → `ExportSetting.sharepoint`): Entra tenant ID, client ID, and a write-only client secret (`client_secret_set` reports whether one is stored). Mask paths `value.export.sharepoint.*`; `bb.settings.set`. Configured from Integrations → Export Destinations, a table with one row per provider; SharePoint opens a sheet with its setup steps and credentials, and can be removed there. Enterprise plan (`FEATURE_SHAREPOINT_EXPORT`); not available in SaaS.
- **Project SharePoint folder** (`Project.export_setting.sharepoint.url`, mask `export_setting`, `bb.projects.update`): the URL of a library root or folder. Browser URLs (library views with `id=`, `/:f:/r/` links) are normalized and resolved on save. Malformed → `InvalidArgument`; unresolvable or missing credentials → `Faile

title: fix(advisor): check only defined names in Oracle identifier rules
body:
## Summary

With `naming.identifier-no-keyword` turned on, Oracle SQL review warned about references to Oracle built-ins, not about names the user chose:

- `SELECT COUNT(1) INTO v ...` → `Identifier "COUNT" is a keyword and should be avoided`
- `x := coll.COUNT;` (collection method) → `COUNT`
- `n := SQL%ROWCOUNT;` → `SQL`
- `RAISE_APPLICATION_ERROR(-20001, SQLCODE || SQLERRM);` → `SQLCODE`

On the customer script from BYT-10301 (MBBank Oracle 19c), main reports 14 warnings, all of this kind. The script only parses on main since the BYT-10301 parser fixes, so these warnings only now show up.

**Cause:** `omniIdentifiers` (`backend/plugin/advisor/oracle/utils.go`) collected every `*ast.ObjectName` and `*ast.ColumnRef`. That covers every function-call name, every column or variable reference, and the implicit `SQL` cursor.

**Fix:** the collector now returns only names a statement defines:

- the name in any CREATE statement: the `Name` field of every omni `Create*Stmt` node (table, view, index, cluster, user, role, tablespace, and so on, plus subprograms inside a package), and generic CREATE statements such as CREATE DIRECTORY
- column definitions (CREATE TABLE, ALTER TABLE ADD/MODIFY, object type attributes), view column lists, constraint names, and partition names
- column aliases, table aliases, and CTE names and columns
- rename targets (ALTER TABLE RENAME / RENAME COLUMN / RENAME CONSTRAINT / RENAME PARTITION, ALTER INDEX and ALTER TRIGGER RENAME, and `RENAME a TO b`)
- PL/SQL declarations: variables, constants, exceptions, record fields, parameters, cursors, types, subtypes, and loop or FORALL indexes

References are left out, and built-ins are always references, so we don't need a hard-coded list of built-ins.

### Why only defined names

- The MySQL, MSSQL, and Snowflake versions of `NAMING_IDENTIFIER_NO_KEYWORD` check only defined names: CREATE TABLE and ALTER TABLE names, columns, constraints, and indexes.
- Every hit asserted in the existing Oracle fixtures is a defined name (`CREATE TABLE "table"`, column `name`). **No existing fixture needed changing.**
- Someone writing a script can't rename a column or object that already exists, and can't rename a built-in. A naming rule can only act where the name is chosen.

### Behavior changes beyond the false positives

- **No longer flagged:** references to existing objects, e.g. `UPDATE t SET name = 1`, `COMMENT ON COLUMN t.name`, or `ALTER TABLE t DROP CONSTRAINT "LEVEL"`. A keyword name is still flagged where it is defined.
- **Newly flagged:** a few kinds of definition the old collector skipped: column aliases (`SELECT ... AS "DATE"`), rename targets, partition names, and PL/SQL declarations at the point where they're declared. Before, a keyword-named PL/SQL variable was flagged at each reference; now it's flagged once, at its declaration.
- **`naming.identifier-case` uses the same collector**, so it changes the same way, matching the Snowflake version of that rule. Its existing fixtures

title: feat(frontend): split Plans and Releases lists by change source
body:
Before: Plans listed ClickOps and GitOps Plans together with no way to tell them apart, Releases listed release artifacts with no deploy progress and no link to the Plan that deployed them, and GitOps setup had its own sidebar entry.

After: Plans lists ClickOps Plans and Releases lists GitOps Plans, each with its deploy progress. Plans gains a status filter and a created range. Releases shows each GitOps Plan's release, source commit, stages, and creation time, offers GitOps setup at the top right, and shows a setup empty state for projects without GitOps changes. The release detail page is retired: its URL opens the Plan that deployed the release. This implements the approved "B with A2" design for BYT-10019 (PRs 2–4 of the plan) and builds on #21635.

## Screenshots

Captured on a disposable server seeded with a failed ClickOps Plan, a draft ClickOps Plan, and a GitOps Plan.

**Plans** (ClickOps only; the GitOps Plan is not listed)

![Plans lists only ClickOps Plans](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e5efe1f2-43b9-4aa3-8969-9dfe42e333d9)

**Plans with `status: Failed`** keeps only the failed Plan.

![Plans filtered to status Failed](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/52d3d78d-3168-4cc2-a2c9-0520d540b231)

Status offers Failed, Running, Waiting (not started or pending), and Done, and accepts several values.

**Releases** (GitOps Plans)

![Releases lists GitOps Plans](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9f5cf3ed-e737-4a06-8e37-f765d6481d44)

A row opens the Plan's rollout, or Plan Detail when it has none. Source links to the commit.

**Releases empty state** (no GitOps Plans in the project; dashed box across the content width)

![Releases setup empty state with a dashed border](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a3f1394a-b0c2-428d-bf24-ddabc3204c82)

When filters hide existing GitOps Plans, the page shows "No data" with a Clear filters action instead.

## How

- `PlanTable` moves out of the Plans page into `routes/project/PlanTable.tsx`. Each page passes its own columns, and both use `createPlanStagesColumn` so stage progress renders identically.
- `buildPlanFilter` sends the `has_release`, `release`, and `task_status` filters from #21635. The `status` scope maps to task statuses in `stores/app/plan.ts`.
- Releases fetches each distinct release once per page with the cached `fetchRelease` to read its VCS source. Rows render without waiting, and Source shows "-" while loading, on failure, for an archived release, or with no VCS source.
- `releaseDetailRedirect.ts` loads on `releases/:releaseId`: one active Plan referencing the release redirects to it; none, several, or a failed lookup redirects to Releases filtered by a `release` scope. This keeps the CI summary links bytebase-action writes working.
- The sidebar drops GitOps. Releases is highlighted on `/gitops` and on a GitOps Plan's detail page, which Plan Detail publishes through `viewedPlan` in the plan store.
- The release card in Plan Detail and Issue Detail

Improve Agent landing guidance with bounded, context-scoped evidence instead of generic recommendations.

- Add read-only overview tools for workspace, project, governance, Issues, and databases.
- Guide the Agent to use the relevant overview before answering readiness, governance, Issue, or database-state questions.
- Attach validated Issue and database references to evidence-backed answers.
- Render expandable evidence links to the corresponding project resources.
- Keep landing starters read-only while allowing them to use the new bounded overview tools.

Part of BYT-10118

## Implementation

### Scoped overview tools

Add:

- `get_workspace_overview`
  - Accessible project, instance, and database setup state.
  - The current member's relevant open Issues.

- `get_project_overview`
  - The current member's relevant Issues, accessible databases, and open database-change Issues.

- `get_project_governance_overview`
  - Approval, Plan-check, SQL-review, rollout-concurrency, and approval-rule summaries.

- `get_issue_overview`
  - Exact project-scoped Issue, Plan, Plan-check, review-run, Rollout, and bounded task-run state.

- `get_database_overview`
  - Exact project-scoped database lifecycle, instance, environment, release, backup, and sync state.

Each overview validates its chat context and represents unavailable, partial, not-configured, and not-started data explicitly.

### Agent behavior

- Project chats use evidence before describing project readiness, governance, a specific Issue, or a specific database.
- Workspace chats use evidence before suggesting setup or a next step.
- Responses answer the member's question directly, disclose material limitations, and recommend at most one next step when supported by evidence.
- Landing starters remain read-only: no mutation, navigation, DOM actions, or generic API discovery.

### Evidence references

- Persist validated evidence in assistant-message metadata.
- Render expandable evidence below the final answer.
- Link valid project-scoped Issue and database references to their detail pages.
- Ignore invalid, cross-project, or unsupported references.

## Tests

Added or expanded coverage for:

- Read-only tool registration and execution.
- Workspace, project, governance, Issue, and database overview behavior.
- Partial, unavailable, mismatch, and scope-validation cases.
- Prompt instructions for evidence-backed answers.
- Evidence extraction, attachment, rendering, and routing.
- Landing-starter scope and translated-text recognition.

title: feat(plan): filter plans by release and task status
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"boojack"} -->
_Requested by **Bob** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01YKpvHqdF2paJ6J4PK8kkTM?thread=cmsg_01YKpvHqdF2paJ6J4PK8kkTM5e51EYvZFPwo83dTjoRLQL)_

Before: ListPlans could not tell GitOps Plans from ClickOps Plans, could not find the Plans for one Release, and could not filter by task status.

After: ListPlans accepts three new filters. `has_release == true|false` splits Plans by whether any spec references a Release. `release == "projects/{project}/releases/{release}"` returns the Plans for one Release (a name from another project matches nothing). `task_status in [...]` matches Plans with any task currently in one of the given Task.Status values.

How: the task status expression used by the Plan stage summaries moved into `taskStatusQuery` in backend/store/task.go, and both the stage summaries and the new `task_status` filter use it, so they cannot disagree (latest run decides; skipped tasks are SKIPPED; AVAILABLE shows as PENDING; no run is NOT_STARTED). Every task join includes project, covered by a two-project collision test.

Query plan (PostgreSQL 16, 10,000 Plans per project, 5 tasks and 2 runs per task): `has_release == true && task_status in ["FAILED"]` with LIMIT 50 ran in 28 ms; the no-match worst case that scans every Plan ran in 144 ms. Both use plan_pkey, idx_task_plan_id_environment, and uk_task_run_task_id_attempt.

Part of BYT-10019 (PR 1 of 5).

title: fix: distrust compromised eMudhra certificates in container images
body:
## Summary

Bytebase server and action images built with Go 1.27.1 and older CA bundles can accept certificates chaining through compromised eMudhra intermediates. Update all three Dockerfiles to Go 1.27.3 and patched distribution trust stores so these chains are rejected.

- Use Alpine 3.24.3 runtime images and Go's Alpine 3.24 builder; explicitly install GCC and binutils for the server's Clang build.
- Upgrade the Debian action builder and runtime from Bookworm (Debian 12) to Trixie (Debian 13).
- Install runtime CA packages directly and remove builder-to-runtime certificate copies. The verified bundles are Alpine `20261020-r0` and Debian `20250419+deb13u1`.

## Validation

- Built all three complete Linux ARM64 images with `docker build --pull` and verified each application binary uses Go 1.27.3.
- In each image, curl and a Go TLS probe rejected both `dv-g3b-emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com` and its `dv-g3b-aaa` cross-signed counterpart with certificate verification errors; valid HTTPS to `example.com` succeeded.
- Verified the Go 1.27.3 probe also rejects both chains with the old CA bundle.
- All three binaries passed `--help` smoke checks; `git diff --check` passed.
- AMD64 was not tested locally. This changes container build configuration only; no Go, frontend, or proto source changes.

Existing published images and deployments require a rebuild and redeployment to receive the fix.

title: test(e2e): nightly cloud regression routine for the e2e suite
body:
## Summary

Adds `.claude/skills/e2e-routine`, the skill a cloud scheduled task runs nightly against `main`, and two harness changes that non-interactive runs needed. The suite runs in no CI workflow today; this routine is where it runs.

**What the routine does** (`SKILL.md`, phases with gate evidence):

1. Preflight the VM (`preflight.sh`), decide whether `main` moved since the last recorded run (`should-run.sh`, ledger on the orphan branch `claude/e2e-ledger`), build the frontend-embedded binary (`build.sh`), run the whole suite detached from the tool shell with three attempts per test and a two-hour cap (`run-suite.sh`).
2. Classify every red test from the Playwright JSON report (`summarize.py`): infra, flipped `test.fail()` lock, flake, test isolation, spec rot (a product PR changed behavior on purpose) or product regression, per the truth table in `references/triage.md`, each verified by an isolated rerun and evidence files.
3. Attribute an owner (`attribute.py`): the commits since the last green run that touched the area's sources or the quoted UI text (resolved through the locale files), mapped to Linear assignees by `owners.json`; widens to the spec's last change when nothing in the window explains the failure.
4. File or propose Linear issues in the team named by `E2E_ROUTINE_LINEAR_TEAM` (proposals only until `E2E_ROUTINE_FILE_ISSUES=1`), open a test-only adaptation PR for spec rot, record the run (`ledger.sh`), and report.

`ROUTINE_PROMPT.md` holds the task's prompt, the cloud environment settings (Custom network for the Playwright CDN, `setup-env.sh` for Node 24, the `bytebase` system user embedded Postgres needs under root, Postgres server binaries on PATH, Chromium) and the first-run checklist.

**Harness changes**

- `global-setup.ts`: `ensureBrowser()` calls the project's Playwright binary directly. Through `pnpm exec`, pnpm's dependency check tried to purge `node_modules` and aborted on the missing TTY, which killed global setup in every non-interactive run.
- `mode-start-new-bytebase.ts`: the license resolves from `BYTEBASE_E2E_LICENSE`, else from the dev-signed `BB_DEV_ENTERPRISE_LICENSE` already committed in `frontend/.env.dev` (valid only on a binary built without the `release` tag). A plain `pnpm exec playwright test` is now the licensed run; README and AGENTS.md updated.

## Verification

First cloud run on 2026-10-22 (environment `bytebase-e2e-run`, main 3bd8108): setup cached, preflight all OK, build 504 s, suite 43 min, 196 passed / 20 failed / 1 flaky; the routine classified 17 reds as spec rot with the right culprit PRs (independently confirmed by #21631), 1 product finding, recorded the ledger and reported. The three lessons from that run are in the last commit. Locally: `pnpm --dir frontend fix` and `pnpm --dir frontend test` green; an unlicensed `workspace-banner.spec.ts` run proves the license fallback.

Overlaps #21631 in `mode-start-new-bytebase.ts` (different hunks); whichever lands second rebases.

🤖 Generate

title: fix(sql-editor): stop schema-tree rows remounting so the hover panel shows
body:
Fixes [BYT-10343](https://linear.app/bytebase/issue/BYT-10343/sql-editor-table-hover-panel-never-appears-because-schema-tree-rows).

## What users saw

In the SQL Editor's Schema pane, resting the pointer on a table, view or column row never showed the metadata hover panel. Meanwhile the browser kept rebuilding the tree's rows for as long as the pointer stayed still.

## Mechanism

1. The shared `Tree` passed an inline arrow function as the `children` of react-arborist's `<Tree>`. react-arborist uses `children` as the **row component type**. A new function on every render is a new type, so React unmounted and remounted every visible row whenever the Tree re-rendered.
2. `SchemaPaneInner` subscribed to the whole hover context, including the pointer position. A row's `mouseenter` called `setPosition`, which re-rendered the pane and the Tree, which remounted the rows.
3. The browser fired `mouseenter` again on the new row under the resting pointer. That restarted the panel's 1-second open delay and set the position again, so the loop never settled and the panel never opened.

## Fix

- **Tree:** react-arborist now gets one module-level row component for the Tree's lifetime. The per-render `renderNode` reaches it through React context, so rows still re-render with fresh output but never remount. This also covers the other `Tree` users: the connection pane, sheet tree, classification tree and schema-diagram navigator.
- **Schema pane hover state:** the provider now exposes two contexts. Stable actions (`update`, `setPosition`, `cancel`, `isActive`) go to the pane and rows. The changing state and position go only to `HoverPanel`, so moving the pointer no longer re-renders the pane.
- `HoverPanel` gets a `data-testid` so the e2e test can find it.

## Measurements

body:
## Summary

Brings the Playwright e2e suite back to green on `main` and closes the gaps the first nightly runs exposed. Test-only: every change is under `frontend/tests/e2e/`.

- **Approval gate.** New projects deny approval by the last plan editor (`allow_last_plan_editor_approval=false`, #21298). The existing plan-detail specs turn the option on through `authorMayApprove` (cherry-picked from #21533, which this PR supersedes), and a new describe in the review spec covers the option off: the editor is a candidate but Approve is disabled with the reason and the API refuses, a second admin approves, and the editor can still reject.
- **Sessions outlive the run.** The setup project captures the admin's storage state once; access tokens defaulted to one hour with single-use refresh, so every spec after the first hour landed on the sign-in page. The disposable workspace now sets a 24-hour access token right after the license is installed. A 15-hour local run lost its whole tail to this before the fix; a 1.1-hour run after it had no sign-in failure.
- **Outdated specs adapted to intentional UI changes**, each citing its product PR: targets sheet rows (#21300), "Open SQL Editor" link (#21438), export format select and settings switches (#21489), MCP policy description (#21517), inline threads opening independently and the "position/count" navigator (#21543), the Saved queries pane no longer being the default aside tab, and the setup wizard's post-setup routes and intros (#21594).
- Harness: `ensureBrowser()` calls the project's Playwright binary directly (`pnpm exec` ran a dependency check that aborted without a TTY), and the port probe refuses a port with a loopback listener.

## Verification

Full suite on this branch (local, main 3bd8108): 221 passed, 12 failed in 1.1 h. All 12 were then rerun in isolation with retries and passed (36/36 and 8/8), except the setup wizard and saved-query specs, which were adapted here and pass (2/2, 8/8). The five SQL editor timeouts reproduced only under a load average of 12 on the host. The schema-diagram `test.fail()` lock (BYT-9481) stays: it passes intermittently.

Not in this PR: the SQL editor schema-tree render loop (`tree.tsx` passes an inline function as the arborist row component) is still on main but was not the cause of any failure here; proposed as its own issue.

title: feat(review): run the standard rule review in place of V1 on dev builds
body:
Part of [BYT-10098](https://linear.app/bytebase/issue/BYT-10098/implementation-sql-review-standard-policy).

## Why

The standard rule review (SQL Review V2's `RULE` reviewer) had no trigger, its findings never placed in the statement, and V1's plan-check SQL review ran beside it. On a dev build, this makes V2 the review a person actually goes through: it runs with the plan checks, replaces V1's SQL review there, holds the automatic rollout until its threads are resolved, and shows the latest run in the statement. Release builds keep V1 unchanged.

## What

### One switch, dev builds only

- `config.Profile.SQLReviewV2`, set only in `profile_dev.go` (the non-`release` build). `sqlReviewV2Enabled()` is its frontend counterpart, as before. The backend integration tests leave it off, so V1 keeps its coverage; the review run lifecycle test turns it on.

### Backend, under the switch

- `RunReview` runs the `rule` reviewer only under the switch; elsewhere it returns `UNIMPLEMENTED`. The AI reviewer is not gated.
- The rule review starts wherever the plan checks run: issue creation, a plan SQL update, and `RunPlanChecks`. An issue the review does not apply to is skipped. On issue creation and a plan SQL update, its run is in place before the approval check or the plan checks are signaled, since either can lead to the rollout.
- The plan checks skip `STATEMENT_ADVISE` on the engines the rule review covers (PostgreSQL, MySQL, OceanBase, MariaDB, TiDB, MSSQL, Oracle, Snowflake), which it supersedes; V1 keeps advising the others, such as DynamoDB and BigQuery, and the rule review skips their targets. `GHOST_SYNC` keeps running: it dry-runs gh-ost against the instance, which the `ONLINE_MIGRATION` rule, reading the SQL alone, cannot. `STATEMENT_SUMMARY_REPORT` stays too.
- The automatic rollout waits until the rule review is `DONE` and no thread on the issue is open, whatever its priority or author. Resolving a thread and completing a review run ask the rollout creator to look again. A manual "Bypass and deploy" still works after acknowledging the open threads.
- Each review run records the plan's `approvalInputVersion`, as a plan check run does. A plan with SQL to review and no run for its current version holds the rollout, and the rollout creator starts that review itself, as the approval evaluator does for plan checks. A failed slot write therefore holds the rollout rather than letting unreviewed SQL through. A run for an earlier version restarts even when the plan has nothing left to review: it completes with no findings, which supersedes the earlier ones.
- `ReviewMetadata.superseded` (store and v1, field 5): a `DONE` run marks every earlier result of its reviewer superseded, whatever its thread state, in the transaction that posts its results, and leaves `updated_at` alone. A `FAILED` run marks nothing.

### Plan page, under the switch

- The Checks row shows the rule review's status beside the plan checks: queued, running, open findings, or the failu

title: feat(mcp): let MCP sessions grant and revoke masking exemptions after the user confirms
body:
# feat(mcp): let MCP sessions grant and revoke masking exemptions after the user confirms

Part of BYT-9292 user journey 1: the last piece of the three PRs in `plans/2026-10-13-mcp-decision-matrix.md` (row 8). #21588, #21593 and #21626 are merged; this PR builds on #21626's shared confirmation helper.

An agent can now request and approve access, turn on just-in-time access and revoke a grant. The remaining dead end in the journey is masking: when a user needs a column unmasked for a while, only the console can grant the exemption. An exemption is a standing policy change, broader than a single-statement access grant, so it goes through the user's confirmation, like an approval.

What changes:

- **A new tool, `grant_masking_exemption`,** adds one exemption to a project's `MASKING_EXEMPTION` policy after the user confirms in an MCP form. It names one member and a scope:
  - one database, optionally narrowed to a schema, a table or a column; the database must belong to the project, or the exemption would cover nothing; a database on a project-owned instance is named under its project (`projects/{p}/instances/…`), as the API names it;
  - or every database in the project, current and future, which takes an explicit `allDatabases: true`, so an agent that forgets the database does not exempt the whole project. The project must exist: an exemption written under an unknown project ID would apply to a project created later with that ID.

  The member must name one principal (`user:`, `group:`, `serviceAccount:` or `workloadIdentity:`), as the console's exemption picker does; `allUsers`, which the policy API also accepts, would unmask the scope for everyone and is refused. It takes an optional expiry and reason. The tool writes the condition itself, in the console's form, the expiry as JavaScript's `toISOString` writes it (`request.time < timestamp("2026-10-27T00:00:00.000Z") && (resource.instance_id == "…" && …)`), so the agent never supplies CEL, the form cannot show a narrower scope than the one written, and a revoke compares a tool-made and a console-made condition character for character.
- **A new tool, `revoke_masking_exemption`,** removes one member's exemption. The agent passes the condition exactly as `GetPolicy` returns it. The console's create page appends without merging, so one member can sit in several entries with the same condition; the tool removes the member from every exact match, and the form states how many. An entry left with no member is dropped. No match is refused, with the member's current conditions named.
- **Every other entry is written back as read.** The tools round-trip whole entries (title, description and location survive), where the console's revoke regroups the list and rewrites other entries' expressions.
- **The confirmation covers the exact write.** The digest covers the list as read and the `UpdatePolicy` request built from it, so changed arguments, or an exemption changed while the form was open (including a dupl

title: feat(mcp): let MCP sessions turn just-in-time access on or off, and revoke access grants
body:
# feat(mcp): let MCP sessions turn just-in-time access on or off, and revoke access grants

Part of BYT-9292 user journey 1, the last of the three PRs in `plans/2026-10-13-mcp-decision-matrix.md` (rows 9 and 10), split in two: this one, then masking exemptions. #21588 and #21593 are merged.

An agent can now file an access request and, after the user confirms, approve it. Two dead ends remain on that path. In a project with just-in-time access off, the request is refused, and only the console can turn the setting on. And once the work is done, the agent cannot revoke the grant it was given. Both close for users who hold the permissions: admins, DBAs and project owners hold `bb.projects.update` and `bb.accessGrants.revoke`; a developer's or member's agent still can do neither.

What changes:

- **A new tool, `set_just_in_time_access(project, enabled)`,** turns one project's just-in-time access on or off after the user confirms in an MCP form, the same elicitation `decide_issue` uses. The form has three lines: the change and who makes it, the project ID on a line of its own (`Project: "hr"`), and what the change does:
  - on: "Active grants that have not expired apply again at once."
  - off: "Active grants here stop applying (not revoked); new requests are refused."

  Both are what the code does: with the setting off, `preCheckAccess` ignores grants for queries and exports, and `CreateAccessGrant` refuses new requests. A project already in the requested state is reported as unchanged, without asking.
- **The confirmation covers the exact write.** The form's request state carries a digest of the `UpdateProject` request the tool will send, signed with the workspace, user, client, procedure and project. A client resends the call with its answer, so an answer that comes back with other arguments is stale, and nothing changes.
- **`UpdateProject` moves from EXCLUDED to WRITE, but only `set_just_in_time_access` can use it.** The tool attaches the confirmation to its internal request, and the gate serves the call only when the procedure and project match. `call_api` cannot set a context value, so it is refused, pointed to the tool for this setting and to the console for every other.
- **Both directions go through the form.** Turning just-in-time access off is a tightening, which the decision matrix would serve without a prompt. Serving it apart would take a second path through `call_api` for one value of one field.
- **`RevokeAccessGrant` moves from EXCLUDED to WRITE.** It removes access, so it needs no confirmation. `bb.accessGrants.revoke` still applies, and the handler refuses anything but an active grant.
- **A confirmation expires after ten minutes.** The signed request state now carries when the user was asked, under the MAC. A just-in-time write's digest repeats for the same project and value, so without a bound an accepted answer could be replayed whenever the setting flipped back. --- backend/api/mcp/tool_confirm.go (+198/-0)
@@ -0,0 +1,198 @@
+package mcp
+
+import (
+	"bytes"
+	"context"
+	"crypto/hmac"
+	"crypto/sha256"
+	"encoding/base64"
+	"fmt"
+	"strconv"
+	"strings"
+	"time"
+
+	"github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk/mcp"
+)
+
+// confirmDecisionRequestID is the ID a confirmation is filed under, and
+// confirmDecisionField the form field it asks for. The client echoes both back,
+// so the two halves of one tool call must agree on them.
+const (
+	confirmDecisionRequestID = "confirm"
+	confirmDecisionField     = "confirm"
+)
+
+// confirmationStatePurpose names this use of the server secret, so the key
+// that signs a confirmation's request state signs nothing else.
+const confirmationStatePurpose = "bb.mcp.confirmation.request_state"
+
+// confirmationLifetime bounds how long after asking an answer is acted on. The
+// signed state carries no nonce, and a write's digest repeats whenever the same
+// write is asked again, so without it an accepted answer could be replayed
+// once the write it confirmed became possible again.
+const confirmationLifetime = 10 * time.Minute
+
+// confirmableWrite is a write a tool asks the user to confirm before making it.
+// The request state is signed for its procedure and resource, so an answer to
+// one confirmation cannot be replayed for another.
+type confirmableWrite interface {
+	confirmedProcedure() string
+	confirmedResource() string
+}
+
+// canShowConfirmation reports whether the client declared the form a
+// confirmation needs. A tool checks it before reading any answer: a client that
+// declared no form cannot have shown one, so an answer it sends is not a
+// confirmation.
+func canShowConfirmation(req *mcp.CallToolRequest) bool {
+	return req != nil && req.Session != nil && clientSupportsElicitation(req.Session)
+}
+
+// askToConfirm returns the result that asks the user to confirm w. The SDK
+// elicits within this tools/call and re-invokes the handler with the answer
+// and the request state, the same multi round-trip shape as
+// elicitDatabaseChoice. A client on the 2026-07-28 protocol answers and echoes
+// the state itself.
+func (s *Server) askToConfirm(ctx context.Context, w confirmableWrite, digest []byte, message, title, description string) *mcp.CallToolResult {
+	return &mcp.CallToolResult{
+		RequestState: s.signConfirmationState(ctx, w, digest, time.Now()),
+		InputRequests: mcp.InputRequestMap{
+			confirmDecisionRequestID: &mcp.ElicitParams{
+				Mode:    "form",
+				Message: message,
+				RequestedSchema: map[string]any{
+					"type": "object",
+					"properties": map[string]any{
+						confirmDecisionField: map[string]any{
+							"type":        "boolean",
+							"title":       title,
+							"description": description,
+						},
+					},
+					"required": []string{confirmDecisionField},
+				},
+			},
+		},
+	}
+}
+
+// confirmationAnswer returns the answer and request state a call carries, if
+// it answers a confirmation.
+func confirmationAnswer(req *mcp.CallToolRequest) (mcp.InputResponse, string, bool) {
+	if req.Params == nil {
+		return nil, "", false
+	}
+	response, answered := req.Params.InputResponses[confirmDecisionRequestID]
+	return response, req.Params.RequestState, answered
+}
+
+// confirmationReply is a call's answer to a confirmation this server sent.
+type confirmationReply struct {
+	response mcp.InputResponse
+	// matches is whether the user was asked about the write the call would make.
+	matches bool
+	// expired is whether the user was asked longer ago than confirmationLifetime.
+	expired bool
+}
+
+// signedReply returns the call's answer to a confirmation this server signed
+// for this caller and write, and whether it carries one. An answer without such
+// a state is no answer: a client can send one on a call that was never asked,
+// so the call is asked like a first one.
+func (s *Server) signedReply(ctx context.Context, req *mcp.CallToolRequest, w confirmableWrite, digest []byte) (*confirmationReply, bool) {
+	response, state, answered := confirmationAnswer(req)
+	if !answered {
+		return nil, false
+	}
+	asked, askedAt, signed := s.verifyConfirmationState(ctx, w, state)
+	if !signed {
+		return nil, false
+	}
+	return &confirmationReply{
+		response: response,
+		matches:  bytes.Equal(asked, digest),
+		expired:  time.Since(askedAt) > confirmationLifetime,
+	}, true
+}
+
+// staleReason says why a confirmed answer cannot be acted on, or "" when it
+// can. mismatch is the tool's words for an answer about a different write. An
+// expired answer is reported, not asked again: an older client gets one second
+// round per call, so a form sent there would go unanswered.
+func (r *confirmationReply) staleReason(mismatch string) string {
+	switch {
+	case r.expired:
+		return fmt.Sprintf("the user was asked more than %d minutes ago", int(confirmationLifetime.Minutes()))
+	case !r.matches:
+		return mismatch
+	default:
+		return ""
+	}
+}
+
+// confirmationOutcome reports whether the answer confirms the write, and if
+// not, why, in words the result can carry.
+func confirmationOutcome(response mcp.InputResponse) (bool, string) {
+	elicited, ok := response.(*mcp.ElicitResult)
+	if !ok || elicited == nil {
+		return false, "the confirmation answer could not be read"
+	}
+	switch elicited.Action {
+	case "accept":
+		if confirmed, ok := elicited.Content[confirmDecisionField].(bool); ok && confirmed {
+			return true, ""
+		}
+		return false, "the form was submitted without the confirmation checked"
+	case "decline":
+		return false, "the user declined"
+	case "cancel":
+		return false, "the user cancelled"
+	default:
+		return false, fmt.Sprintf("the confirmation answer %q is not one Bytebase acts on", elicited.Action)
+	}
+}
+
+// signConfirmationState returns the request state the form is sent with: a
+// digest of what the user is asked about and when they were asked, signed
+// together with who asks, through which client, and which write on which
+// resource.
+func (s *Server) signConfirmationState(ctx context.Context, w confirmableWrite, digest []byte, askedAt time.Time) string {
+	askedAtUnix := strconv.FormatInt(askedAt.Unix(), 10)
+	return base64.RawURLEncoding.EncodeToString(digest) + "." + askedAtUnix + "." +
+		base64.RawURLEncoding.EncodeToString(s.confirmationMAC(ctx, w, digest, askedAtUnix))
+}
+
+// verifyConfirmationState returns the digest a request state carries, when the
+// user was asked, and whether this server signed it for this caller and this
+// write.
+func (s *Server) verifyConfirmationState(ctx context.Context, w confirmableWrite, state string) ([]byte, time.Time, bool) {
+	parts := strings.Split(state, ".")
+	if len(parts) != 3 {
+		return nil, time.Time{}, false
+	}
+	digest, err := base64.RawURLEncoding.DecodeString(parts[0])
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, time.Time{}, false
+	}
+	askedAtUnix, err := strconv.ParseInt(parts[1], 10, 64)
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, time.Time{}, false
+	}
+	mac, err := base64.RawURLEncoding.DecodeString(parts[2])
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, time.Time{}, false
+	}
+	if !hmac.Equal(mac, s.confirmationMAC(ctx, w, digest, parts[1])) {
+		return nil, time.Time{}, false
+	}
+	return digest, time.Unix(askedAtUnix, 0), true
+}
+
+func (s *Server) confirmationMAC(ctx context.Context, w confirmableWrite, digest []byte, askedAtUnix string) []byte {
+	key := hmac.New(sha256.New, []byte(s.secret))
+	_, _ = key.Write([]byte(confirmationStatePurpose))
+	signed := strings.Join([]string{getWorkspaceID(ctx), getUserEmail(ctx), getOAuth2ClientID(ctx), w.confirmedProcedure(), w.confirmedResource(), askedAtUnix, ""}, "\x00")
+	mac := hmac.New(sha256.New, key.Sum(nil))
+	_, _ = mac.Write(append([]byte(signed), digest...))
+	return mac.Sum(nil)
+}

title: chore: bump omni to 8031142a and adapt to its changes
body:
## Summary

Bump `github.com/bytebase/omni` from `431fd0dff942` to `8031142a6c5e` (11 commits) and adapt Bytebase to what changed. Two of the changes needed fixes here: Oracle now parses parenthesized queries, and omni's MySQL parser now rejects MariaDB syntax that Engine_MARIADB still routes through it.

### Oracle: parenthesized queries and EXCEPT (omni #453, #467, #494)

- **Query span / masking.** A parenthesized query that ORDER BY or a row limit follows, or that a WITH clause precedes, parses as a wrapper `SelectStmt` whose `Larg` holds the query and whose own select list is empty. The span read that empty list and returned no results. `query_result_masker.go` masks only columns with a masker, so `(SELECT ssn FROM emp) ORDER BY 1` came back unmasked. Before the bump this statement failed to parse. The span now reads through the wrapper.
- **Result limit.** A statement starting with `(` got no limit. A row limit inside a parenthesized last set operand (`… UNION ALL (SELECT … FETCH FIRST 3 ROWS ONLY)`) was taken for the whole query's limit, so the union ran unlimited. omni chains set operands through `Rarg`, and in the AST only `Loc` tells a parenthesized operand from the rest of the chain. The rewrite therefore lexes the operand to check whether one pair of parentheses encloses it, and appends `FETCH NEXT` after it.

### MariaDB: fallback to omni's MariaDB parser (omni #487, #488)

omni's MySQL parser now accepts only MySQL 8.0's `CREATE OR REPLACE` and `ALTER TABLE … DROP` forms. `ParseStatements` for Engine_MARIADB uses that parser, so `CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE/INDEX/PROCEDURE/FUNCTION/TRIGGER/DATABASE/USER` and `DROP [COLUMN] IF EXISTS` now failed the statement-advise and statement-report plan checks with a syntax error.

`parseMariaDBStatements` tries omni's MySQL parser first. When that fails and omni's MariaDB parser accepts the statement, it wraps the statement in a new `*mariadb.OmniAST`. When both fail, it reports the MariaDB parser's error. The fallback also clears older false syntax errors on MariaDB-only syntax: sequences, `RETURNING`, `UUID`/`INET` types, system versioning, periods.

The MySQL code paths do not read the MariaDB AST. Each one degrades as follows:

| Path | Behavior on a MariaDB-only statement |
|---|---|
| V1 advisors | skip it (they already skip non-MySQL ASTs) |
| Prior backup check | reports it, since the backup transform parses with omni's MySQL parser and would fail the rollout |
| Statement types | `STATEMENT_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED`, the existing convention for unclassified statements |
| Walk-through | skips the whole sheet: the MySQL catalog cannot run the statement, and simulating the rest without it would check them against the wrong schema |
| Changed resources | skips it and counts it in the new `ChangeSummary.SkippedStatements` |
| Statement summary report | no report, with a warning, so approval and the release check never read an undercounted `affected_rows` |
| SQL editor write targets | `writeTargetsFro

title: fix(frontend): coordinate HTTP token refresh with a shared worker
body:
## Summary

On plain HTTP origins, `navigator.locks` is unavailable and session refresh fails. Keep the existing Web Locks/BroadcastChannel flow where supported and use a SharedWorker otherwise. The worker owns the refresh request and shares its result across tabs, avoiding concurrent use of the backend's single-use refresh token.

The fallback uses a separate Connect client with cookies and no UI interceptors. Same-tab callers share one promise. The client waits for the worker readiness handshake before dispatching a refresh. Startup errors and timeouts close the unused port and retry within the same shared refresh promise, up to three attempts with 250 ms and 500 ms delays. If startup retries are exhausted, the auth interceptor returns temporary unavailability without expiring the session; later API requests can retry startup throughout a longer rollout. Failures or timeouts after readiness require reloading the page before trying the worker again. The worker refresh RPC has no client deadline: the page watchdog gives startup and the dispatched refresh separate 35-second intervals, and rejects waiting callers without aborting an in-flight token rotation. Backend token rotation is unchanged, with no grace period.

This is an independent alternative to #21616; that PR is unchanged.

## Validation

- `pnpm --dir frontend fix` and `pnpm --dir frontend test` pass: guards, Biome, TypeScript, production bundle, and 586 test files / 6,614 tests.
- Added tests for Web Locks selection, fallback selection, concurrent worker ports, rotations lasting beyond the page watchdog without starting a second request, shared failures, later refreshes, recoverable worker startup errors and timeouts, a full refresh watchdog interval after slow startup, terminal failures after readiness, stale worker errors, and unavailable SharedWorker.
- Chromium verification using the built fallback on a LAN HTTP origin (`isSecureContext === false`, no `navigator.locks`) against a simulated single-use refresh endpoint: two tabs produce one request, both succeed, the next rotation uses the replacement HTTP-only cookie, and closing the initiating tab does not interrupt the remaining tab's refresh.
- No full Bytebase browser E2E run; the browser endpoint above was simulated.

- Review follow-up: Chromium verification with a production-built worker and a simulated old-replica HTML response confirmed that a single refresh call survives the initial HTML response: two worker loads produce exactly one refresh request. Interceptor regression tests verify that recovery and repeated startup retry exhaustion do not set the session-expired flag or show a reauthentication notification, and that a later request recovers once the worker becomes available.

## Compatibility and limits

HTTP fallback requires SharedWorker with module-worker support. Unsupported or blocked workers fail explicitly rather than issuing competing requests. HTTPS/localhost deployments retain the existing Web Locks path. Lo

title: feat(review): run the AI review from the plan page
body:
## Why

The AI review could only be started through the API, so nobody could try it, or see its findings, from the plan page. This adds a Run button and the run's status beside the plan checks, following the plan check pattern: a button starts a run, the page reads its status with the same polling, and a run is never started twice while one is queued or running.

## What

- An "AI review" block under CHECKS at the bottom of the CHANGES card (`PlanDetailAIReview`), right after the plan checks, in their layout: heading, Run button on the right, status line below. It does not follow the selected spec tab, since a review run belongs to the whole issue.
- Status from `GetReviewRun` on `projects/{p}/issues/{i}/reviewRuns/ai`:
  - A slot that never ran reads "Not run yet".
  - Queued or running reads "Running".
  - DONE reads "Finished" with the finish time, in a neutral style, since DONE does not mean the change passed.
  - FAILED shows the run's error as plain text.
- The run is read with the plan page's snapshot, beside the plan check run, so there is one polling loop. While the run is queued or running the page polls actively (500 ms to 4 s), then drops back to the idle cadence (1 s to 16 s), as for plan checks.
- Run sends `RunReview` and adopts the run it returns. It is disabled while a run is queued or running, so a second click cannot start a second paid run, and while the slot has not been read yet. A refused `RunReview` (for example the switch turned off meanwhile) shows the server message and changes nothing else.
- When a run reaches DONE, the issue's comments are listed again once, so new findings appear without a reload.
- Shown only when all of these hold:
  - dev builds (`sqlReviewV2Enabled()`, the feature is dark-launched);
  - an open issue, a draft included;
  - no rollout;
  - AI and the AI review switch both on;
  - `bb.reviewRuns.get`.

  Without `bb.reviewRuns.run` it shows the status but no button. With AI or the switch off it is hidden, not disabled, since only a workspace admin can change them.

## Checked in a browser

On a throwaway backend and dev frontend with AI turned on against an unreachable endpoint and the switch on: "Not run yet", then Run, then "Running" with Run disabled, then "Failed" with the provider error, then Run enabled again. At 375 px the heading and button stay on one row and the error wraps. A DONE run was not reachable without a real provider; the tests cover it.

## Not in this PR

- A backend no-op for a run of the same version. The disabled button covers double clicks from the page; `RunReview` still replaces a running execution when called directly.
- Automatic runs on save, which wait on the frequency rule.
- The RULE slot. This button starts the AI review only.

## Tests

- `PlanDetailAIReview.test.tsx`: not run yet, Run sends the right name and adopts the run, disabled while queued, running, or unread, finished and failed display, a refused RunReview, status without run permission, a draft issue,

title: fix(sql): require bb.sql.explain even under an access grant
body:
## Summary

- An access grant exempted its target database from the IAM check before the permission was looked at, so a grant holder could send the approved statement with the explain flag (or as a typed `EXPLAIN`) and read its plan with no explain role.
- A grant conveys data access, not the right to read plans. The granted-target shortcut in `accessCheckWithGrantedTargets` now covers data permissions only; `bb.sql.explain` always comes from IAM.
- Adds a store-backed test proving the grant still covers the approved select (with or without a role) and refuses explain until the user holds `bb.sql.explain`. The test fails on the unfixed code.

Closes the second of the two §3.5 leaks in `docs/design/query-plan-visualizer.md` ("A data access grant exempts it").

## Breaking Changes

A user whose only access to a database is an active access grant can no longer explain the approved statement there. They need a role carrying `bb.sql.explain` on the database, as every other user already does.

## Testing

- `go test -count=1 ./backend/api/v1/ -run 'Explain|AccessGrant|PreCheckAccess|SQLIAM'`
- `~/go/bin/golangci-lint-2.13.2 run --fix -j 8 --allow-parallel-runners` (one pre-existing `revive` finding in `backend/plugin/db/util/ssh_test.go`, untouched by this change)
- `go build -ldflags "-w -s" -p=16 -o ./bytebase-build/bytebase ./backend/bin/server/main.go`
- Not run: the E2E harness, which needs `BYTEBASE_E2E_LICENSE`; access grants are a licensed feature, so the unlicensed Docker smoke path cannot create one either.

title: fix: finish adapting Oracle splitting and SQL Server SET checks to omni
body:
## Summary

Two adaptations that the omni bump in bytebase/bytebase#21613 missed. Neither caused a compile error or failed an existing test.

### Oracle: embedded Java/JavaScript source was cut short before execution

omni (bytebase/omni#443) marks `CREATE JAVA … AS`, `CREATE MLE MODULE … AS`, and inline MLE call specs as `SegmentEmbeddedSource`. Text in these segments must not be read with the SQL lexer, because a Java or JavaScript `--` decrement lexes as a SQL comment. `SplitSQL` still trimmed every segment with that lexer, so source whose last line held `n--` lost its tail. The Oracle driver executes exactly that text.

Fix: `SplitSQL` no longer trims embedded-source segments; omni already bounds them.

### SQL Server: `SET` option lists slipped past the NOEXEC/PARSEONLY refusal

omni (bytebase/omni#475) now parses `SET A, B ON`. `Options` lists every name, while `Option` holds only the first. The `QueryConn` statement-type check read `Option`, so `SET ANSI_NULLS, NOEXEC ON` got through. Before the bump, omni rejected the list form, so the query was refused anyway.

Fix: the check reads every entry in `Options`, which omni fills on every `SET` form.

## Evidence

| Scenario | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Oracle 23ai Free, driver `Execute` of an inline MLE function ending in `n--` | Execute **succeeds**; Oracle stores `{{ return n` and reports `PLS-00881: missing closing delimiter '}}'` | Oracle stores the full `{{ return n--; }};` |
| SQL Server 2022, `QueryConn("SET ANSI_NULLS, NOEXEC ON; DELETE FROM dbo.t;")` | Returns success with "Affected Rows: 0"; the DELETE never ran | `SET NOEXEC is not supported` |
| SQL Server 2022, `QueryConn("SET ANSI_NULLS, NOEXEC ON; SELECT 1;")` | Misleading "cannot match the batch's result sets … separate with GO" | `SET NOEXEC is not supported` |

The Oracle image used for this has MLE disabled (`ORA-00439`) and no JVM, so I compared the source Oracle stored rather than running the code. `CREATE MLE MODULE` can't run through the go-ora client at all (`ORA-24970`), independent of this change.

## Test plan

- `TestPLSQLSplitSQLKeepsEmbeddedSourceWhole` (Java source, MLE module, inline MLE call spec) fails on all three cases without the fix and passes with it.
- `TestGetStmtType` gains list cases (NOEXEC, PARSEONLY, and a harmless list). Two fail without the fix.
- `TestQueryConnMatchesResultsToStatements` (real SQL Server container) gains the list-form `DELETE` case.
- Tests pass for `parser/plsql`, `parser/tsql`, `db/oracle`, `db/mssql`, `advisor/oracle`, `advisor/mssql`, `schema/oracle`, and `schema/mssql`. `golangci-lint` reports no new issues; the server builds.
- The Playwright E2E harness wasn't run: it needs `BYTEBASE_E2E_LICENSE`, which isn't configured here, and it only provisions a Postgres sample, which reaches neither path.

title: chore: bump omni to 431fd0df and adapt to its changes
body:
## Summary

Bumps `github.com/bytebase/omni` from `3165d7e5a683` to `431fd0dff942` (51 commits) and adapts Bytebase to every change that affects it. I checked each omni commit for impact on Bytebase. The ones that needed changes:

| omni change | Bytebase adaptation |
| --- | --- |
| bytebase/omni#435: `ParseError` is `{Message, Position}` in every engine; trino/googlesql/doris/starrocks `Parse` returns `error` | doris, starrocks, trino, googlesql, spanner, snowflake, partiql, and cassandra adapters read the new shape (`errors.As`, `FirstError`) |
| bytebase/omni#464: MySQL-family node `Loc` starts at its first token, so `WITH … UPDATE/DELETE` starts at `WITH` | **Regression fix.** MySQL/TiDB prior backup and the MySQL affected-rows EXPLAIN recovered the `WITH` clause from the text *before* the node and silently dropped it (the backup `SELECT` referenced an undefined CTE, and CTE names were no longer excluded from backup targets). They now read the clause from the node's start up to its depth-0 `UPDATE`/`DELETE` keyword |
| bytebase/omni#457–#462, #431, #445: SQL Review V2 packages for pg, mysql (+OceanBase), mariadb, tidb, mssql, oracle, snowflake | Registered in `reviewrun.reviewFuncs`, which was empty, so every rule review run failed with "has no standard rule reviewer" |
| bytebase/omni#442 and the `review` contract: `DISALLOW_DROP_OBJECT` covers every dropped object except constraints; `DISALLOW_RENAME` also covers views | Proto comments (+ generated docs/types) and all 5 locale descriptions updated |
| bytebase/omni#480: TiDB `CREATE/ALTER/DROP SEQUENCE` parse | Dispatcher fallback tests now use `FLASHBACK TABLE`, which omni still rejects. Statement types, resource changes, and the prior-backup DDL guard go through the pingcap bridge, so they are unaffected |
| bytebase/omni#466: `/*! */` offsets are now source offsets | Executable-comment guards are still needed (a slice can end inside one), but their comments claimed the old behavior; corrected. Snowflake diagnose comment likewise |

Checked and needing no change: statement `Line/Column` now count code points (Bytebase only reads `ByteStart/ByteEnd`; elasticsearch already counted code points); googlesql/snowflake diagnostic columns (Bytebase converts from the byte `Offset`); pg catalog fidelity fixes (no Bytebase code matches the old error wording); trino/googlesql strict parse and fail-closed analysis (queries with trailing junk now fail span analysis, which is safer for masking); oracle/mssql/mariadb grammar fixes; the keyword-map concurrency fix.

## Test plan

- `go test ./backend/...`: 117 packages pass, including the server-backed `backend/tests`. `TestCollision_RunReviewLifecycle` previously asserted the Postgres rule run *fails* with "has no standard rule reviewer" and said to flip it once omni registered the engine; it now expects `DONE`.
- New `TestReviewFuncsEvaluateRules` runs every registered reviewer.
- Existing `TestBackup` / `TestAffectedRowsQuery` (mysql) and `TestBackupR

- `golangci-lint` reports only pre-existing revive findings in untouched files.
- Server build passes.
- Verified manually against a real BigQuery dataset: a `DELETE` without `WHERE` now produces the expected ERROR advice, and a scoped `UPDATE` passes and rolls out.

title: feat(review): bound an AI review run by the CI sample and a server-wide limit
body:
## Why

An AI review run reviews every database of the plan, and each database costs up to 20 model calls. A save on a 200-database group would pay for 200 reviews, and runs side by side multiply the requests in flight at the provider: each run allows 8, and the scheduler starts every claimed run in its own goroutine. This PR bounds both before automatic runs can start a review on every save.

## What

- The AI review covers the project's CI sample, the same databases plan checks sample: the first `ci_sampling_size` targets of each spec, or every target when the setting is 0, its default. The executor calls `DeriveCheckTargets` instead of `DeriveReviewTargets`.
- The rule review is unchanged and still evaluates every target.
- `ReviewRun.Status.DONE` now says what each reviewer covers: every unit in the reviewer's scope was evaluated, where RULE's scope is every target and AI's is the CI sample. The comments on `DeriveCheckTargets`, `DeriveReviewTargets`, both call sites, and `ci_sampling_size` (v1 and store) say the same. The v1 comment of `ci_sampling_size` also read "database rows" while the code samples databases, now fixed.
- A server-wide limit: every AI run on the server shares 16 slots (`aiReviewServerConcurrency`), on top of the 8 per run (`aiReviewRunConcurrency`, renamed from `aiReviewConcurrency`). The executor is created once and holds a `*semaphore.Weighted`.
  - A unit takes its slot before the review starts, so waiting does not count against the reviewer's 10-minute timeout, and gives up waiting when the run's context ends.
  - The slot is released by `defer`, a panicking review included.
  - The schema loads after the slot is taken, so all runs together hold at most one schema per slot.

## Not in this PR

- Frequency rules (a save that leaves the SQL unchanged starts nothing, a daily cap): they belong with automatic runs, which do not exist yet.
- The project settings text for `ci_sampling_size` still names only CI data validation. The AI review UI is dev-only, so naming it on a production settings page waits for the docs and locales work.

## Notes for the reviewer

- The limit is per process. With several replicas, the load at the provider is 16 times the replica count.
- A superseded run is not canceled (the review run design fences its completion instead), so it keeps its slots and keeps calling the model until it ends. Stopping a superseded AI run early belongs with automatic runs, where saves make supersedes common.
- A DONE AI run resolves the open AI findings of earlier runs. If `ci_sampling_size` drops, or a new database sorts into the first N, findings on databases that left the sample are resolved though nobody fixed them.
- `reviewSlots` is a two-method interface so the shared-limit test can observe a review waiting; without it the test passed with the limiter removed.
- #21589 also edits `ai_review_executor.go`. Whichever lands second needs a small rebase.

## Tests

- `TestCISampleBoundsOnlyTheAIReview`: a database

title: feat(advisor): require WHERE on BigQuery UPDATE and DELETE
body:
## Summary

BigQuery had no SQL review rule beyond the builtin max-SQL-size check and no advisor package. This adds `STATEMENT_WHERE_REQUIRE_UPDATE_DELETE` for BigQuery.

- New `backend/plugin/advisor/bigquery` package. The rule walks the omni GoogleSQL AST and flags `UPDATE` and `DELETE` with no `WHERE`, including inside `BEGIN ... END` scripts. `MERGE` actions are not flagged.
- Registered in `backend/server/ultimate.go` beside the other advisor packages.
- Rule listed for `BIGQUERY` in `sql-review-schema.yaml` and the prod and dev templates (level ERROR, matching the other engines). No frontend code change: the review UI derives engine tabs from the yaml.

## Test plan

- `go test ./backend/plugin/advisor/bigquery/` with a fixture covering UPDATE and DELETE with and without WHERE, multi-statement line numbers, MERGE, and a BEGIN...END script.
- `go test ./backend/plugin/advisor/` for the yaml template consistency tests.
- Frontend `sqlReview.test.ts` plus the full `pnpm test` gate.
- Built with `embed_frontend` and checked in the app: the Advanced template shows a BigQuery tab with the rule at Error, and the saved policy stores it. Not exercised against a live BigQuery instance.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

+// Package bigquery is the advisor for BigQuery.
+package bigquery
+
+import (
+	"context"
+	"fmt"
+	"strings"
+
+	omniast "github.com/bytebase/omni/googlesql/ast"
+
+	storepb "github.com/bytebase/bytebase/backend/generated-go/store"
+	"github.com/bytebase/bytebase/backend/plugin/advisor"
+	"github.com/bytebase/bytebase/backend/plugin/advisor/code"
+	"github.com/bytebase/bytebase/backend/plugin/parser/base"
+
+	// Registers the BigQuery parser so ParseStatements resolves the engine.
+	_ "github.com/bytebase/bytebase/backend/plugin/parser/bigquery"
+	"github.com/bytebase/bytebase/backend/plugin/parser/googlesql"
+)
+
+var (
+	_ advisor.Advisor = (*WhereRequireForUpdateDeleteAdvisor)(nil)
+)
+
+func init() {
+	advisor.Register(storepb.Engine_BIGQUERY, storepb.SQLReviewRule_STATEMENT_WHERE_REQUIRE_UPDATE_DELETE, &WhereRequireForUpdateDeleteAdvisor{})
+}
+
+// WhereRequireForUpdateDeleteAdvisor is the advisor checking for WHERE clause requirement for UPDATE and DELETE statement.
+type WhereRequireForUpdateDeleteAdvisor struct {
+}
+
+// Check checks for WHERE clause requirement.
+func (*WhereRequireForUpdateDeleteAdvisor) Check(_ context.Context, checkCtx advisor.Context) ([]*storepb.Advice, error) {
+	level, err := advisor.NewStatusBySQLReviewRuleLevel(checkCtx.Rule.Level)
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, err
+	}
+
+	checker := &whereRequireForUpdateDeleteChecker{
+		level: level,
+		title: checkCtx.Rule.Type.String(),
+	}
+
+	for _, stmt := range checkCtx.ParsedStatements {
+		ast, ok := stmt.AST.(*googlesql.AST)
+		if !ok || ast.Node == nil {
+			continue
+		}
+		checker.checkStmt(ast.Node, stmt.Text, stmt.BaseLine())
+	}
+
+	return checker.adviceList, nil
+}
+
+type whereRequireForUpdateDeleteChecker struct {
+	adviceList []*storepb.Advice
+	level      storepb.Advice_Status
+	title      string
+}
+
+// checkStmt flags UPDATE and DELETE statements without a WHERE clause,
+// including those nested in scripts (BEGIN ... END, IF, loops). MERGE
+// WHEN ... THEN UPDATE/DELETE actions are separate merge nodes and are not
+// flagged.
+func (c *whereRequireForUpdateDeleteChecker) checkStmt(node omniast.Node, text string, baseLine int) {
+	omniast.Inspect(node, func(n omniast.Node) bool {
+		switch stmt := n.(type) {
+		case *omniast.UpdateStmt:
+			if stmt.Where == nil {
+				c.addAdvice("UPDATE", text, baseLine, stmt.Loc.Start)
+			}
+		case *omniast.DeleteStmt:
+			if stmt.Where == nil {
+				c.addAdvice("DELETE", text, baseLine, stmt.Loc.Start)
+			}
+		default:
+		}
+		return true
+	})
+}
+
+func (c *whereRequireForUpdateDeleteChecker) addAdvice(statementType, text string, baseLine, offset int) {
+	c.adviceList = append(c.adviceList, &storepb.Advice{
+		Status:        c.level,
+		Code:          code.StatementNoWhere.Int32(),
+		Title:         c.title,
+		Content:       fmt.Sprintf("WHERE clause is required for %s statement.", statementType),
+		StartPosition: base.ConvertANTLRLineToPosition(baseLine + statementLineForOffset(text, offset)),
+	})
+}
+
+// statementLineForOffset returns the 1-based line within text that holds the
+// byte offset. An unknown (-1) or out-of-range offset clamps to the text bounds.
+func statementLineForOffset(text string, offset int) int {
+	if offset < 0 {
+		offset = 0
+	}
+	if offset > len(text) {
+		offset = len(text)
+	}
+	return strings.Count(text[:offset], "\n") + 1
+}

title: feat(review): edit the AI review policy on the SQL review pages
body:
Built on #21589 (the AI review switch), now merged.

## Why

The AI review checks every database change against a plain-language policy, the `REVIEW_AI` policy at the workspace and the project level. Today the policy can be set only through the API. This PR puts its editor on the SQL Review pages, beside the standard rules and the AI review switch.

## What

- Workspace SQL Review page: a "Review policy" field under the "Review changes with AI" switch. It saves from the page's one footer together with the standard rules and the switch. Each part keeps its own draft, Cancel reverts all of them, Update saves only the changed parts, and the page shows one "Updated" only when every changed part saved. A failed save keeps its draft.
- Project SQL Review page: the same field under the read-only switch, saved at the project level through the project page's footer. Its description says the project policy adds to the workspace policy and wins where the two conflict. The project footer now follows the same one-notification rule, so `useProjectStandardRules.save` returns whether it saved and the page notifies.
- A save sends the mask `["review_ai_policy"]` with `allowMissing`, so a new policy is created enforced and a policy paused through the API stays paused. A paused policy shows a note under the field.
- Blank text deletes the policy, since the server rejects blank content. Blank follows Go's `strings.TrimSpace`.
- Text over 64 KiB, counted in UTF-8 bytes, shows the exact byte counts under the field and disables Update.
- On both pages the AI review section reads top to bottom: the heading, the introduction, the switch, the policy title, and the policy box. Both sections on both pages, the standard rules and the AI review, are now `FormSection`s in a new `single-column` layout, with the switch and the policy field in a `FormFieldGroup`. The introduction says what the policy applies to: on the workspace page, every project, which can add its own; on the project page, that the project policy adds to the workspace one and wins where they conflict.
- The empty policy box shows example rules in grey, different per level and none of them a standard rule: the workspace hint shows engineering practice that needs the schema, the project hint rules about the project's own data.
- For an existing policy the field is editable with `bb.policies.update` or `bb.policies.delete`, at the page's level, and for a new one with `bb.policies.create`. A role with update but not delete cannot clear the text, and a role with delete but not update can only clear it, which removes the policy. Everyone else sees the text, or "No review policy.".

- `FormSection` gains `layout="single-column"`, the same 24px section title with the header above the content at every width, and a `description` slot under the title. The UX contract names both. The default layout put the heading in a column beside the content, and the dense `stacked` layout has a 16px title. The standard rules section c
