+		// FT.DICTADD mutates a dictionary even though Redis flags it readonly.
+		{
+			statement: "FT.DICTADD dict term",
+			valid:     false,
+			allQuery:  false,
+		},
+		// Core read commands added in Redis 7.4.
+		{
+			statement: "HTTL h FIELDS 1 f",
+			valid:     true,
+			allQuery:  true,
+		},
+		// Read-only script mode only blocks commands flagged "write", so Lua
+		// still reaches SELECT and the readonly-flagged module commands that
+		// mutate state. See knownExclusions in
+		// TestReadCommandsMatchServerFlags.
+		{
+			statement: "EVAL_RO \"return redis.call('GET','k')\" 0",
+			valid:     false,
+			allQuery:  false,
+		},
+		{
+			statement: "EVALSHA_RO abc 0",
+			valid:     false,
+			allQuery:  false,
+		},
+		{
+			statement: "FCALL_RO fn 0",
+			valid:     false,
+			allQuery:  false,
+		},
+		// SELECT switches the connection to another logical database, so a
+		// later read escapes the database the request was authorized against.
+		{
+			statement: "select 3",
+			valid:     false,
+			allQuery:  false,
+		},
+		{
+			statement: "select 3\nkeys *",
+			valid:     false,
+			allQuery:  false,
+		},
 	}
 
 	for _, test := range tests {
@@ -36,8 +127,98 @@ func TestValidateQuery(t *testing.T) {
 			require.Error(t, err)
 		} else {
 			require.NoError(t, err)
-			require.Equal(t, test.valid, gotValid)
-			require.Equal(t, test.allQuery, gotAllQuery)
+			require.Equal(t, test.valid, gotValid, test.statement)
+			require.Equal(t, test.allQuery, gotAllQuery, test.statement)
+		}
+	}
+}
+
+// TestReadCommandsMatchServerFlags diffs the core allowlist against a snapshot
+// of the flags Redis reports for itself, so a Redis upgrade that ships new read
+// commands fails here instead of reaching a customer. See the snapshot header
+// for how to regenerate it.
+func TestReadCommandsMatchServerFlags(t *testing.T) {
+	// knownExclusions holds commands Redis flags "readonly" that Bytebase
+	// deliberately keeps out of the gate. Every entry needs a reason: the flag
+	// means "does not write the keyspace", not "has no side effects".
+	//
+	// SELECT is not listed. Redis does not flag it readonly, so the reverse
+	// check below is what keeps it out of the allowlist.
+	knownExclusions := map[string]string{
+		// Read-only script mode only rejects commands flagged "write", so a
+		// script still reaches SELECT and every readonly-flagged module command
+		// that mutates state. Verified on redis-stack-server 7.4.7: running
+		// EVAL_RO "redis.call('SELECT',1); return redis.call('GET','marker')"
+		// against database 0 returns database 1's value, and a no-writes
+		// function called through FCALL_RO both crosses databases and adds a
+		// RediSearch dictionary term via FT.DICTADD.
+		"eval_ro":    "Lua reaches SELECT and readonly-flagged mutating module commands",
+		"evalsha_ro": "same as eval_ro",
+		"fcall_ro":   "same as eval_ro, through a no-writes function",
+	}
+
+	content, err := os.ReadFile("testdata/core_readonly_commands.txt")
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+
+	serverReadOnly := map[string]bool{}
+	for line := range strings.SplitSeq(string(content), "\n") {
+		line = strings.TrimSpace(line)
+		if line == "" || strings.HasPrefix(line, "#") {
+			continue
+		}
+		serverReadOnly[line] = true
+	}
+	require.NotEmpty(t, serverReadOnly, "snapshot has no commands")
+
+	allowed := map[string]bool{}
+	for command := range readCommands {
+		allowed[command] = true
+	}
+	for container, subcommands := range doubleNameReadCommands {
+		for subcommand := range subcommands {
+			allowed[container+" "+subcommand] = true
 		}
 	}
+
+	var rejected []string
+	for command := range serverReadOnly {
+		if allowed[command] {
+			continue
+		}
+		if _, ok := knownExclusions[command]; ok {
+			continue
+		}
+		rejected = append(rejected, command)
+	}
+	slices.Sort(rejected)
+	// assert, not require: a run that breaks both directions must report both.
+	assert.Emptyf(t, rejected,
+		"Redis flags these commands readonly but the gate rejects them: %v. "+
+			"Add each to readCommands or doubleNameReadCommands, or to knownExclusions with a reason.",
+		rejected)
+
+	var unflagged []string
+	for command := range allowed {
+		if !serverReadOnly[command] {
+			unflagged = append(unflagged, command)
+		}
+	}
+	slices.Sort(unflagged)
+	assert.Emptyf(t, unflagged,
+		"the gate accepts these but Redis does not flag them readonly: %v. "+
+			"Either the name is wrong, or the command has side effects and must be removed.",
+		unflagged)
+}
+
+// TestModuleReadCommandsWellFormed guards the module allowlist, which has no
+// snapshot because module presence varies per instance. A key that is not a
+// lowercase dotted name can never match, since isReadCommand lowercases the
+// first token and module commands carry the dot inside it.
+func TestModuleReadCommandsWellFormed(t *testing.T) {
+	require.NotEmpty(t, moduleReadCommands)
+	for command := range moduleReadCommands {
+		require.Equal(t, strings.ToLower(command), command, "module command must be lowercase")
+		require.Contains(t, command, ".", "module command must be dot-namespaced")
+		require.False(t, readCommands[command], "module command duplicated in readCommands: %s", command)
+	}
 }

title: docs: refresh the v1 API audit against HEAD and rewrite it in plain terms
body:
## What

Re-verified every finding in the v1 API audit against `fd4ef828e6`, removed the ones that are fixed, and rewrote the rest in plain language.

## Why

The doc had drifted twice over. It still listed problems that shipped fixes weeks ago, and it read like a trace log — each finding opened with a file path and a call chain rather than with what actually breaks, so it was hard to skim and hard to prioritize from.

## Removed as fixed

Each verdict was confirmed by reading the code at HEAD, not by trusting commit messages.

| Finding | Fixed by |
|---|---|
| T8 `CreateWorksheet` enforced nothing | #21169 — `CreateSavedQuery` is now IAM + `bb.savedQueries.create` |
| T12 `GetActuatorInfo` anonymous workspace leak | #21184 — anonymous access and the `name` field removed |
| T13 `SearchWorksheets` filter-after-pagination | #21160 + #21178 — predicate pushed into SQL before `LIMIT` |
| T18 worksheet write/delete gated on `.get` | #21169 + #21181 — per-verb permissions |
| T9 login lockout (self-hosted only) | #21189 — failed logins audited, tested end-to-end |

## Worth a second look

**T9 is only half fixed.** The lockout now works self-hosted and has a passing end-to-end test, but on SaaS a login that omits `workspace` still writes no audit row, so the counter reads zero and the limit never fires — and that is exactly what the hosted sign-in page sends by default, since `resolveWorkspaceName()` falls back to `""` with no `?workspace=` param. There is no IP rate limiter behind it. I promoted this to the top of "What I'd do" rather than letting it read as closed.

**The actuator fix moved a smaller surface rather than removing it.** `GetAuthenticationRestriction`, which replaced it, is anonymous by design and does not require membership, so a real workspace ID returns 200 and a fake one returns `InvalidArgument` — a workspace-existence oracle. Kept as a narrowed T12 item.

## Corrections

Two counts were simply wrong and are now re-measured at HEAD:

- Dead `permission` annotations on CUSTOM RPCs: **15 of 45**, not 20 of 44.
- Unescaped CEL call sites in the frontend: **11**, not 12 (one was fixed incidentally by #21136).

The api-linter section is now marked as a stale 2026-08-04 baseline instead of reading as current — the worksheet→saved-query rename moved part of that surface and I did not re-run the linter.

## Everything else still reproduces

T10, T11, T14, T15, T16, and all six T18 items reproduce verbatim at HEAD with refreshed citations. The three patches parked from the earlier session (`SearchProjects` ×2, `DiffSchema`) never landed independently, so `DiffSchema` is now written up as Tier 2's one live instance rather than a passing mention.

## Testing

Docs-only change to a single tracked file. Pre-PR checklist sections 2–8 all hit their skip conditions: no code, no `backend/store/` or `backend/migrator/`, no proto, no new files or directories. Claims were verified by reading the cited code at HEAD; a few (repo/RPC counts, the actuat

title: feat(frontend): separate self-service account settings from admin recovery
body:
Implements [docs/design/split-profile-self-service-vs-admin.md](https://github.com/bytebase/bytebase/blob/main/docs/design/split-profile-self-service-vs-admin.md) (merged in #21191). Frontend only — no proto or backend change.

## Problem

`ProfilePage` was mounted both at `/setting/profile` (editing yourself) and at `/users/:email` (looking at someone else), and the create-user sheet doubled as an edit form for the same fields. The symptoms:

- Clicking a directory row opened an edit sheet while clicking the name **in that row** opened a page.
- One `Edit` toggle flipped name, email, phone and password together, so a password change — which revokes every refresh token — happened silently inside a generic "Save".
- One permission flag stood in for both "can I edit myself" and "can I edit this other person", so a normal user saw their own email as inert text and an admin saw a 2FA card addressed to the account owner.

## What changed

**Admin actions live in the Users row menu.** Reset password and Reset MFA lead, since they are why an admin opens it. The row itself is no longer clickable — the menu is its only affordance.

This is shaped around self-hosted deployments, where SMTP is optional and unconfigured by default, so an admin setting the password directly is the only recovery path inside the product. The reset dialog therefore generates a policy-compliant password and shows it **once**, for the admin to relay out of band. "Reset MFA" leads with the fact that a user who still has recovery codes does not need an admin at all, and states the real consequence, which differs by whether the workspace requires MFA.

**`/users/:email` is replaced by a hover card** carrying avatar, name, email and a deactivated badge. Workspace role is deliberately absent: not actionable there, duplicated on the members page, and rendering it made a personal settings page read the entire workspace IAM policy to draw one badge.

**Your own account is one page at `/account`**, with password and 2FA behind their own dialogs.

## Breaking Changes

| Removed | Replacement |
|---|---|
| `/setting/profile` | `/account` |
| `/setting/profile/two-factor` | `/account/two-factor` |
| `/users/:principalEmail` | hover card on the name; administration via the Users row menu |

No redirects are kept, so existing bookmarks and runbook links to these URLs will 404.

Also changed: **self-service email change is removed.** Changing an email moves the identity someone signs in with, so it is now an admin action from the Users row menu only. A consequence worth flagging: an admin can no longer change their *own* email and must ask another admin. That exclusion is what fixes the self-eject bug below; say the word if you would rather have it back with the storage-migration side effects restored.

## Review notes

A `/code-review` pass over this diff found and fixed 15 issues. The ones worth knowing about:

- The reset-password dialog stayed dismissible **after** issuing the password. An o

title: fix: name the right RPC in DeleteUser/UndeleteUser SaaS guards
body:
## What

`DeleteUser` and `UndeleteUser` both open with a SaaS-mode guard whose error message was copy-pasted from `CreateUser`:

```
CreateUser is not available in SaaS mode, add users via workspace IAM policy instead
```

So an admin deactivating or restoring a user on SaaS got an error about a different RPC, pointing at guidance that didn't match what they were trying to do. Each message now names its own operation and the corresponding IAM policy action:

| RPC | Message |
|---|---|
| `DeleteUser` | `DeleteUser is not available in SaaS mode, remove users from the workspace IAM policy instead` |
| `UndeleteUser` | `UndeleteUser is not available in SaaS mode, add users back to the workspace IAM policy instead` |

Text only — same code path, same `CodeUnimplemented`, same guard conditions.

## Testing

- No test asserted on the old string. `CodeUnimplemented` appears in zero test files, and the two Go tests touching these RPCs (`backend/tests/user_test.go`, `backend/tests/login_audit_test.go`) never exercise the SaaS branch.
- `golangci-lint run --allow-parallel-runners` → 0 issues; `gofmt -l` clean.
- `go test -count=1 ./backend/api/v1/` passes.
- Full server build passes.

## Follow-up

`UpdateEmail` ([user_service.go:642](https://github.com/bytebase/bytebase/blob/claude/awesome-euclid-e0872c/backend/api/v1/user_service.go#L642)) has the same copy-pasted `CreateUser` message. Left out of this PR because the right SaaS guidance for an email change isn't obvious — identity provider, workspace IAM policy, or not supported at all. Happy to fix in a follow-up once that's settled.

title: docs: separate self-service account settings from admin recovery
body:
## What

Design proposal for splitting the user profile surface. Doc only — no code.

Today `ProfilePage` is mounted both at `/setting/profile` (editing yourself) and `/users/:email` (looking at someone else), and the create-user sheet on the Users page doubles as an edit form for the same fields. The visible symptoms: clicking a directory row opens an edit sheet while clicking the name *in that row* opens a page; one `Edit` toggle flips name, email, phone and password together, so a password change — which signs the user out of every session — happens silently inside a generic "Save"; and one permission flag stands in for both "can I edit myself" and "can I edit this other person".

## Why this shape

The proposal is built around what admins actually do here: a user forgot their password, or lost their authenticator. That framing matters most self-hosted, where SMTP is optional and unconfigured by default, so an admin setting the password directly is the only recovery path inside the product.

- **Admin actions move to a row menu** on the Users page — recovery in two clicks, no navigation. Follows Metabase, the closest analog (self-hosted, local passwords, optional SMTP), which also shows the admin a temporary password to hand over when no mail is configured.
- **`/users/:email` is deleted**, replaced by a hover card showing avatar, name, email and a deactivated badge. A read-only account page is about seven fields — a popover's worth, not a destination. Linear works the same way: no admin user page, a hover popover for identity, and a profile page that shows the person's *work* rather than their account.
- **Your own account stays one page**, moving to `/account`, with password and 2FA behind their own dialogs rather than a shared Save.

## Two findings worth separate attention

Both surfaced while writing this and are described in the doc's phase 2:

1. **Forced password change is already built end to end** — login response, reset page and route guard all exist. It just never fires for an admin reset, so an admin-set password is currently a permanent credential the admin knows. Only the trigger is missing.
2. **"Forgot password" is shown even when no mail is configured**, and the request is deliberately silent so it can't reveal whether an account exists. Self-hosted users click it, are told to check their email, and nothing ever arrives.

## Notes

- Pre-PR checklist: sections 2–7 skip (docs-only); section 8 skipped as no new directory is added.
- `origin/claude/user-profile-ux-separation-2sadm0` holds an implementation of an **earlier revision** of this design — it builds the dedicated `UserDetailPage` that this proposal replaces with a hover card. It should be reworked or dropped rather than merged as-is.

diff:
--- docs/design/split-profile-self-service-vs-admin.md (+134/-0)
@@ -0,0 +1,134 @@
+# Separate self-service account settings from admin account recovery
+
+Status: proposal · 2026-08-18
+
+## Problem
+
+One component serves two audiences. `ProfilePage` is mounted both at `/setting/profile` (editing
+yourself) and at `/users/:email` (looking at someone else), and the create-user sheet on the Users
+page doubles as an edit form for the same fields. That produces:
+
+- In one directory row, **clicking the row opens an edit sheet and clicking the name in that row
+  opens a page**. Both mean "open this user."
+- A single `Edit` toggle flips name, email, phone and **password** into edit mode together. Changing
+  a password signs the user out of every session — silently, inside a generic "Save".
+- One permission flag decides both "can I edit myself" and "can I edit this other person", so a
+  normal user sees their own email as dead text with no explanation, and an admin viewing someone
+  else gets a 2FA card whose copy is addressed to the account owner.
+- In cloud, admins can't edit other users at all, so the page quietly degrades into a read-only
+  screen that still looks editable.
+
+## What admins actually do here
+
+Almost always one of two things: **a user forgot their password**, or **a user lost their
+authenticator**. Correcting a name or an email is rare.
+
+Recovery matters most self-hosted, where there is no guaranteed mail server — SMTP is optional and
+unconfigured by default, so an admin setting the password directly is the only recovery path inside
+the product. (The `bytebase recovery` CLI covers the case where no admin can sign in either.) Two
+related facts:
+
+- The **"Forgot password" link shows even with no mail configured**, and the request is deliberately
+  silent so it can't reveal whether an account exists. Users click it, are told to check their email,
+  and nothing arrives.
+- **Recovery codes already work at sign-in**, single-use, so a user who lost their authenticator but
+  kept their codes never needs an admin. True today, invisible today.
+
+## What admins can change
+
+Email address, password, turning MFA off, deactivate/reactivate, roles, and display name and phone.
+
+Turning MFA *on* for someone else is impossible — enrollment needs a secret from that person's own
+setup — so the only coherent admin action is a reset.
+
+In cloud, every one of these is blocked against other users **except roles**: name, phone, password,
+MFA, email and deactivation are all self-only there, while role assignment through the workspace IAM
+policy still works — it is how members are added in the first place.
+
+These aren't one uniform "edit user" capability. Name and phone are ordinary profile fields the user
+also edits themselves. Email, password, deactivation and roles each go through their own API and
+permission — email in particular changes the identity the person signs in with. Different
+consequences deserve different confirmations, so each gets its own dialog rather than sharing one
+form.
+
+## Prior art
+
+**Metabase** is the closest analog — self-hosted, local passwords, optional SMTP. Admin actions live
+in a **row menu**: edit, reset password, deactivate. With no SMTP configured it **shows the admin a
+temporary password to hand over**. Okta offers the same choice explicitly; Keycloak marks admin-set
+passwords temporary so they must be changed at next login.
+
+**Linear** answers the other half. It has **no admin user page** — role and suspend live in the
+members table — and a **hover popover** on avatars for identity at a glance. It does have a profile
+page, but that page shows the person's assigned issues: a work view, not an account view.
+
+Grafana and GitLab do have per-user admin pages, but they carry sessions, identities and org
+membership. Page-versus-menu tracks how much state there is to inspect, not who is acting.
+
+## Design
+
+**Admin actions move to the Users row menu.** Reset password and Reset MFA sit at the top, above
+edit, change email and deactivate. Recovery becomes two clicks with no navigation.
+
+The overflow menu becomes the row's only affordance — the row itself stops being clickable, which is
+what removes the two-destinations-per-row problem. The create-user sheet goes back to creating: its
+edit mode disappears, and with it the password field it currently reuses for edits. Role assignment
+is not in the menu and does not move; roles are workspace IAM rather than user data, and they stay on
+the members page where they are managed alongside groups.
+
+*Reset password*: generate or type a password, then show it once with a copy button, stating that it
+must be delivered out of band and that the user's sessions have all been signed out.
+
+*Reset MFA*: leads with the self-service path — if they still have recovery codes, no admin action is
+needed. The confirmation states the real consequence, which differs by policy: when the workspace
+requires MFA the user is forced into setup at next sign-in; when it doesn't, they simply have no MFA
+until they re-enroll. Named **Reset MFA**, not "Disable 2FA" — the intent is recovery, and "disable"
+is also what you'd call deliberately weakening an account.
+
+**`/users/:email` is deleted, replaced by a hover card** showing **avatar, name, email, and a
+"deactivated" badge**. Nothing else. The card answers one question — "who is this?" — asked in
+passing about a name in an issue line. Email disambiguates people with the same display name;
+deactivated tells you they've left. Roles and groups don't answer that question and overflow a
+popover; last login would leak everyone's activity pattern, since every member can read user records.
+Keeping it to identity means the card needs no IAM lookup and looks the same to every viewer.
+
+Names become hover triggers rather than links. No redirect is kept — nothing links to the old route
+after this change.
+
+**Your own account stays one page**, at `/account`. There are only two editable fields — name and
+phone — plus email, password and two-factor. That is a page with sections, not a set of tabs.
+
+What has to change isn't the page count but where the password lives: it moves out of the shared form
+into its own dialog, so changing it is a deliberate act with its own confirmation rather than a side
+effect of "Save". Two-factor gets the same treatment. The existing 2FA setup wizard keeps its own
+route, since it is a genuine multi-step flow.
+
+The route moves because today `/setting/profile` sits as a sibling of `/setting/general` and
+`/setting/subscription`, making "my account" a peer of "this workspace's billing" — the same
+conflation as everything above, in the URL tree. Nobody does that: Sentry namespaces personal
+settings under `/settings/account/*`, GitHub splits `/settings/*` (you) from `/orgs/:org/settings/*`
+(the org), Grafana keeps personal at `/profile/*` outside the admin tree. Workspace settings stay
+where they are.
+
+(Bytebase's singular `/setting` is also off-convention — everyone uses plural. Renaming it touches
+every workspace settings URL and is unrelated to this change, so it belongs in a separate cleanup.)
+
+## Phasing
+
+**Phase 1 — frontend only.** Everything above.
+
+**Phase 2 — two small backend changes.**
+
+1. **Make an admin-set password temporary.** Forced password change is already built end to end — the
+   login response, reset page and route guard all exist. It just never fires for an admin reset, so
+   today an admin-set password is a permanent credential the admin knows. Only the trigger is
+   missing. (Related: an admin reset currently postpones password-rotation expiry.)
+2. **Hide "Forgot password" when no mail is configured**, pointing at the workspace admin instead.
+   Independent of everything above and shippable on its own.
+
+## Alternatives
+
+Keeping `/users/:email` as a read-only account card — the content is popover-sized and every inbound
+link is incidental. Giving admins a dedicated page — recovery is a two-click errand, not a
+destination. Branching harder on "is this me" inside one component — the bugs above come precisely
+from one flag standing in for two different authorization questions.

title: feat(instance): add Sample Project Instance lifecycle
body:
## Summary

- add the SaaS-only `PrepareSampleProjectInstance` API and localized one-click Sample Project Instance entry point
- provision an isolated PostgreSQL role/database under an unpredictable persisted Instance ID, seed it as the sample role, synchronously discover it, and preserve one lifetime entitlement per Workspace
- add startup/hourly expiration and stale-reservation cleanup with bounded cleanup-only preflight, one-record transactions, active-session fencing, and retained Bytebase metadata
- require authenticated `verify-full` target TLS with optional mounted CA trust, and document the lifecycle architecture, credential hygiene, and operations
- keep the Manager-to-API failure seam transport-neutral, with private target/transaction details and atomic target provisioning cleanup
- create databases with connections disabled until dedicated-role ACLs are established, and durably retain exact owned-resource state when provisioning cleanup cannot finish

## Testing

- `golangci-lint run --allow-parallel-runners`
- `go build -ldflags "-w -s" -p=16 -o ./bytebase-build/bytebase ./backend/bin/server/main.go`
- `buf format -d --exit-code proto && buf lint proto`
- focused real-PostgreSQL API, lifecycle-manager, target, runner, and store suites
- provisioning interruption matrix across every role/database/ACL/schema/seed boundary
- latest-head full lifecycle package, full store package (469s), API lifecycle, migration, lint, and server-build gates
- `pnpm --dir frontend check`
- `pnpm --dir frontend type-check`
- `pnpm --dir frontend test` (442 files, 3,583 tests)
- Cloud SQL smoke test compiles and is opt-in

`go test ./...` completed all ordinary packages and the changed packages. The container-heavy `backend/store` and `backend/tests` packages exceeded the default 10-minute package timeout; `backend/store` passed when rerun with a 20-minute timeout (509s), while `backend/tests` again exceeded 20 minutes with no assertion failure reported.

title: fix(mysql): stop downloading the RDS CA bundle on every connection
body:
## What

`getRDSConnection` calls `getRDSCertPool` on **every** connection, which is an uncached HTTPS `GET` to `s3.amazonaws.com/rds-downloads/rds-combined-ca-bundle.pem`. This PR makes that download happen once per process, skips it entirely when it cannot be used, and lets a configured `ssl_ca` replace it.

Present on `main` and in every released version I checked (3.19.0, 3.20.1, 3.21.1).

The bundle URL is also stale: every CA in `rds-combined-ca-bundle.pem` expired by 2025-06-01, so `verify_tls_certificate=true` without `ssl_ca` cached a pool that could never verify a modern RDS instance. This PR swaps to AWS's current `https://truststore.pki.rds.amazonaws.com/global/global-bundle.pem`.

## Why

Applying a migration to 32 sharded databases opens 32 connections at once, so the rollout issued 32 concurrent downloads of the same file. Any one of them failing failed that task.

We hit this in production against Aurora MySQL with `AWS_RDS_IAM`. Roughly 40% of task runs failed with:

```
failed to get RDS cert pool: Get "https://s3.amazonaws.com/rds-downloads/rds-combined-ca-bundle.pem": net/http: TLS handshake timeout
```

The same schema migration landed on 29, then 29, then 29, then 31 of 32 shard databases across four attempts before converging. Measured from inside the pod, the stall was ~10.5s in the TLS handshake against `http.DefaultTransport`'s 10s `TLSHandshakeTimeout` — so about half of a concurrent burst crossed the limit. Serial requests from the same pod completed in ~85ms.

There is a second, configuration-independent problem. When `verify_tls_certificate` is false, the downloaded pool is placed in:

```go
tls.Config{RootCAs: rootCertPool, InsecureSkipVerify: true}
```

with no `VerifyPeerCertificate`. The pool is never consulted, so in that configuration the download is pure overhead that can only add failures.

That is the configuration we run: with `verify_tls_certificate: true` our IAM schema sync against Aurora MySQL failed with `x509: certificate signed by unknown authority`, so we disabled verification — and then still paid a download per connection for a pool that is discarded. Change 2 below is what would let us turn verification back on without depending on the network.

## Changes

1. **Skip the download when `verify_tls_certificate` is false.** Behaviour-preserving: with `InsecureSkipVerify: true` and no verifier, `RootCAs` had no effect. Now the config is built without touching the network.

2. **Honour `ssl_ca` when `verify_tls_certificate` is true.** `util.GetTLSConfig` already does this for the password path (`backend/plugin/db/util/ssl.go`); the IAM path ignored `ssl_ca` completely. With this, an operator can serve RDS IAM connections with no outbound network access at all. `ssl_ca_path` needs no handling here — `util.HasTLSPath` shows paths are resolved to inline PEM earlier in the pipeline.

   The system pool is deliberately *not* used as a fallback, since RDS certificates chain to Amazon RDS CAs that are not in

title: chore: bump omni for Oracle constraint_state support (BYT-10010)
body:
Picks up [bytebase/omni#399](https://github.com/bytebase/omni/pull/399): full Oracle `constraint_state` support, engine-verified against Oracle 23ai (39/40 statement-level agreement). Fixes [BYT-10010](https://linear.app/bytebase/issue/BYT-10010/sql-review-rejects-valid-oracle-using-index-local-table-constraint) — MBBank's `PRIMARY KEY (...) USING INDEX LOCAL` partitioned DDL rejected by SQL Review since 3.19.0.

## Adaptation audit (beyond the bump)

- **Compilation**: no changes needed — new AST fields (`TableConstraint.UsingIndexLocal`/`Tablespace`, `ColumnConstraint` equivalents, `CreateViewStmt.Constraints`) are additive.
- **Schema extraction**: `extractTableConstraint` consumes `AlterTableCmd.Constraint` only on `AT_ADD_CONSTRAINT`; the newly populated nodes on `AT_MODIFY_CONSTRAINT` are ignored there, so no phantom constraints.
- **Advisors**: statements that previously failed at parse (`NOT NULL ENABLE`, `USING INDEX ...`) now reach the rules, so `table.require-pk` / `column.no-null` etc. produce correct results on DBMS_METADATA-style DDL automatically. No rule reads the new fields yet; wiring local-index semantics into `IndexMetadata` is deferred to a separate issue per the BYT-10010 discussion.
- **Tests**: `parser/plsql`, `advisor/oracle`, `schema/oracle` all pass unmodified; added an end-to-end `Diagnose` regression test for the customer statement and the DBMS_METADATA shape.

After merge: cherry-pick to 3.21.x for MBBank (regression window 3.19.0–3.21.x).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

+	require.NoError(t, migrator.MigrateSchema(ctx, db))
+
+	pgURL := fmt.Sprintf(
+		"host=%s port=%s user=postgres password=root-password database=postgres",
+		container.GetHost(), container.GetPort(),
+	)
+	stores, err := store.New(ctx, pgURL, false)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	t.Cleanup(func() { require.NoError(t, stores.Close()) })
+
+	const email = "member@example.com"
+	activeCondition := `request.time < timestamp("2099-01-01T00:00:00Z")`
+	expiredCondition := `request.time < timestamp("2000-01-01T00:00:00Z")`
+	tests := []struct {
+		workspace  string
+		memberType string
+		condition  string
+		want       bool
+	}{
+		{workspace: "active-direct", memberType: "direct", condition: activeCondition, want: true},
+		{workspace: "expired-direct", memberType: "direct", condition: expiredCondition},
+		{workspace: "active-group", memberType: "group", condition: activeCondition, want: true},
+		{workspace: "expired-group", memberType: "group", condition: expiredCondition},
+		{workspace: "active-all-users", memberType: "allUsers", condition: activeCondition, want: true},
+		{workspace: "expired-all-users", memberType: "allUsers", condition: expiredCondition},
+	}
+
+	var want []string
+	for _, test := range tests {
+		_, err := db.ExecContext(ctx, `INSERT INTO workspace (resource_id) VALUES ($1)`, test.workspace)
+		require.NoError(t, err)
+
+		member := common.FormatUserEmail(email)
+		switch test.memberType {
+		case "group":
+			group, err := stores.CreateGroup(ctx, &store.GroupMessage{
+				Workspace: test.workspace,
+				Email:     test.workspace + "@example.com",
+				Title:     test.workspace,
+				Payload: &storepb.GroupPayload{Members: []*storepb.GroupMember{{
+					Member: common.FormatUserEmail(email),
+					Role:   storepb.GroupMember_MEMBER,
+				}}},
+			})
+			require.NoError(t, err)
+			member = common.FormatGroupEmail(group.Email)
+		case "allUsers":
+			member = common.AllUsers
+		default:
+			require.Equal(t, "direct", test.memberType)
+		}
+
+		payload, err := protojson.Marshal(&storepb.IamPolicy{Bindings: []*storepb.Binding{{
+			Role:      "roles/workspaceMember",
+			Members:   []string{member},
+			Condition: &expr.Expr{Expression: test.condition},
+		}}})
+		require.NoError(t, err)
+		_, err = stores.CreatePolicy(ctx, &store.PolicyMessage{
+			Workspace:         test.workspace,
+			Resource:          common.FormatWorkspace(test.workspace),
+			ResourceType:      storepb.Policy_WORKSPACE,
+			Payload:           string(payload),
+			Type:              storepb.Policy_IAM,
+			InheritFromParent: false,
+			Enforce:           true,
+		})
+		require.NoError(t, err)
+		if test.want {
+			want = append(want, test.workspace)
+		}
+	}
+
+	workspaces, err := stores.ListWorkspacesByEmail(ctx, &store.FindWorkspaceMessage{
+		Email:          email,
+		IncludeAllUser: true,
+	})
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	got := make([]string, 0, len(workspaces))
+	for _, workspace := range workspaces {
+		got = append(got, workspace.ResourceID)
+	}
+	slices.Sort(got)
+	slices.Sort(want)
+	require.Equal(t, want, got)
+
+	for _, test := range tests {

+			Email:          email,
+			IncludeAllUser: true,
+		})
+		require.NoError(t, err)
+		if test.want {
+			require.NotNil(t, workspace)
+		} else {
+			require.Nil(t, workspace)
+		}

title: feat!: split bb.savedQueries.manage into per-verb permissions
body:
## What

Replaces the saved-query admin backstop `bb.savedQueries.manage` with standard per-verb IAM evaluation, per the amended design in `docs/design/saved-queries-model.md`:

- **Permission family** is now `create`, `search`, `get`, `getIamPolicy`, `setIamPolicy`, `update`, `delete`, `list` — one per RPC. The creator owns every per-object permission; a VIEWER binding carries `{get, getIamPolicy}`, EDITOR adds `update`; a project- or workspace-level role grant reaches every saved query in scope.
- **`setIamPolicy` sits in no bundle and no predefined role** — sharing stays the creator's unless a custom role grants it deliberately, which also gives admins an opt-in path to revoke a departed user's grants.
- **One evaluation function** (`hasSavedQueryPermission`: creator → bindings → role walk, bindings first) and **one masking rule** (a caller lacking a method's permission gets NotFound, never PermissionDenied, so private names stay unprobeable).
- **Search/SearchFolders return what the caller holds `get` on** — the same rule as GetSavedQuery; role-`get` holders (admins) see everything, gated by `search`.
- **Hardening from review**: the search family and all per-object fetches fence to the caller's workspace and active projects; service accounts and workload identities never match group grants (proto invariant enforced); the principal-type→member-name switch is unified in `common.FormatPrincipalMember` (iam, utils, and the service delegate); star toggles no longer read the unbounded statement.
- **Frontend**: per-verb helpers (`isSavedQueryDeletableV1`/`isSavedQueryShareableV1`) wired into the tree context menu and share popover; rename failures are surfaced (the global middleware ignores NotFound).
- **Migration `3.22/0009`** expands custom-role `manage` → `get` + `getIamPolicy` + `update` + `delete` (no `setIamPolicy`), covering both pre-release roles and the shipped `bb.worksheets.manage` population that 0007 renames in the same upgrade.

## Why

`manage` was a non-standard lump the rest of the permission vocabulary doesn't have: it hid the sub-project IAM shape (owner → bindings → project roles), blocked custom-role granularity (read-only support, cleanup-only roles), and made the policy RPCs' access rules read wrong. Per-verb permissions make saved-query access ordinary IAM evaluation with the saved query as a sub-project policy attachment point.

## Breaking Changes

Relative to current `main` (the `manage` model never shipped in a release; `bb.worksheets.*` upgrades land directly on the new vocabulary):

- `bb.savedQueries.manage` is removed; `get`, `getIamPolicy`, `setIamPolicy`, `update`, `delete` are added.
- Per-object denials answer **NotFound instead of PermissionDenied** (Update/Delete/SetSavedQueryPolicy included).
- **Search is widened** for role-`get` holders (was strictly caller-scoped); archived-project rows are no longer searchable.
- **EDITOR bindings can re-file** (`folder` is an ordinary update field); **star follows read*

title: feat(mcp): classify every v1 RPC and lint the classification complete (1b-1)
body:
Every v1 RPC now carries `mcp_method_class`, and CI fails on one that does not. Main proved it mid-review: #21184 added `AuthService/GetAuthenticationRestriction`, and the merge failed the lint by name until it was classified. That last clause is the point of the PR: five rounds of this series have found MCP-reachable methods one batch at a time, and a new RPC could always arrive unclassified. It cannot now.

**Only FORBIDDEN is enforced.** READ, WRITE and EXCLUDED are recorded classifications with no request-time reader — the gate that selects between them is 1b-2. The enum comment says so, the interceptor comment says so, and the interceptor's dispatch test pins that all three still dispatch. The exception is FORBIDDEN, which the existing interceptor enforces the moment it is annotated; see the behavior change below.

## The classification

| Class | Methods | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| READ | 48 | served to a read-only session and above |
| WRITE | 40 | served to a read-write session only |
| EXCLUDED | 93 | served by no mode this phase ships |
| FORBIDDEN | 28 | never served, enforced today |
| **total** | **209** | |

`backend/api/v1/testdata/mcp_method_classification.md` renders it row by row. It is a rendering, not the source of truth — the annotations are — and a stale file fails CI. Regenerate with:

```
MCP_INVENTORY=write go test ./backend/api/v1/ -run TestMCPClassificationInventory
```

Seeded from the closed #21141's inventory, re-verified against current main handler by handler. Its `ai.op.*` identifiers and capability universe are not revived.

## Admin-class exclusion is a fourth class, not FORBIDDEN

`EXCLUDED` is new. It means no phase-1 mode serves the method, and it is deliberately not FORBIDDEN, because the two differ in whether they can ever be undone. An admin-capable ceiling — if one is ever built — could legitimately serve an EXCLUDED method; that is a product decision nobody has made. It could never serve a FORBIDDEN one, because FORBIDDEN names a mechanism that breaks the MCP boundary itself. Folding them together would put the ordinary admin API into the same durable-never set as credential minting, and any future widening would have to re-litigate both at once.

`mcp_exclusion_reason` is required on every EXCLUDED row, so an exclusion nobody wrote down cannot happen:

| Reason | Rows |
|---|---|
| `ADMINISTERS_THE_WORKSPACE` | 78 |
| `RETURNS_A_STORED_SECRET` | 8 |
| `READS_OTHER_USERS_SQL` | 3 |
| `SENDS_DATA_TO_A_THIRD_PARTY` | 2 |
| `OPENS_AN_ADMIN_CONNECTION` | 2 |

**Counterargument, pre-written:** a fourth value is one more thing the gate has to switch on, and today EXCLUDED and FORBIDDEN behave identically — nothing serves either. YAGNI says use FORBIDDEN and split later. Against that: they do not behave identically now — FORBIDDEN denies at the interceptor and EXCLUDED dispatches, which the dispatch test pins — and every FORBIDDEN row carries a reason describing a credential or boundary mechanism. Ninety-three

title: refactor(saved-query): replace the batch update with MoveMySavedQueries
body:
Follow-up to #21178, from review discussion on that PR.

`BatchUpdateSavedQueries` promised a general batch update and delivered one narrow operation. Its update mask admitted exactly one field, `folder`, while its row selection inherited the whole Search filter grammar — including `starred` and `shared`, terms no caller used and that a write could not act on. A read filter doubling as a write selector is the kind of thing that goes wrong later, when somebody adds a field that's harmless to read by and dangerous to write by.

## What it is now

```proto
// Move the caller's own saved queries into a folder, named individually or a
// whole folder at a time.
rpc MoveMySavedQueries(MoveMySavedQueriesRequest) returns (MoveMySavedQueriesResponse)
    POST /v1/{parent=projects/*}/savedQueries:moveMy

message MoveMySavedQueriesRequest {
  string parent = 1;
  repeated string names = 2;    // set this...
  string source_folder = 3;     // ...or this, not both
  string target_folder = 4;
}
```

The filter grammar is gone from the write path entirely. **"My"** follows the convention this API already uses for caller-scoped methods (`SearchMyAccessGrants` / `accessGrants:searchMy`), and here it carries the authorization rule: the store scopes every move to `creator = caller`, so nobody else's rows are candidates.

## Behavior changes

- **Moving a folder carries its descendants.** Renaming `a/b` to `a/c` also moves `a/b/deep` → `a/c/deep`, in one statement over rows locked in primary-key order. The client previously enumerated paths and issued one call each, deepest-first, which left a half-moved tree if it failed midway. The frontend now sends only top-level moves and patches the cache per destination folder.
- **Filing is creator-only**, and the **admin backstop no longer writes or stars** either. It reads, re-shares, and deletes — what incident response and orphan cleanup need. Rewriting somebody's draft or reorganising their tree isn't an administrative act, so those stay with the creator, and content editing with EDITOR grantees.

That last one is narrower than `dataform.admin` and Databricks workspace admins, which the design doc previously cited for parity. Decision 5 in `docs/design/saved-queries-model.md` now records the divergence, and the access rules gained explicit `star` and `file` lines rather than folding them into `write`.

## Testing

`TestMoveSavedQueries` covers subtree moves, exactly-one-of validation, folder-into-itself rejection, boundary-slash normalization, and unfiling (an empty target drops the prefix rather than leaving `/tail`). The lock-order test and the audit-attribution case in `acl_test.go` follow the rename — note `MoveMySavedQueries` is no longer a `Batch*` method, so its parent resolves through the single-request path, which still needs its `resource_reference` or the audit row files under the workspace.

Green: full `backend/store` (394s), `backend/api/v1` (248s), saved-query integration suites, 3542/3542 frontend tests,

title: feat!: share saved queries with per-object VIEWER/EDITOR grants
body:
Implements the sharing half of [docs/design/saved-queries-model.md](docs/design/saved-queries-model.md). Saved queries go from "private to the creator, admins aside" to per-object grants: a saved query is reachable by its **creator**, by anyone a **VIEWER or EDITOR binding** names, and by the **`bb.savedQueries.manage` backstop**. Sharing targets `user:` and `group:` principals; groups are stored as references and never expanded, so a 1,000-member group costs what a 3-member one does and membership stays live.

## Breaking Changes

- **Existing saved queries migrate owner-private.** `saved_query.bindings` starts empty for every row, so anything that was shared via the old `visibility` flag is now creator-only until re-shared. This is the one-time reset the design specifies, and BigQuery's own classic→modern path. The `Share with project` shortcut that reproduces the old audience in one click is **not** in this PR (see Follow-ups), so re-sharing is per-principal for now.
- **`SearchSavedQueries` is caller-scoped and no longer widened by the admin backstop.** An admin previously saw every saved query in the project here; they now see their own plus what's shared with them, and read everyone's through `ListSavedQueries`. Same for `SearchSavedQueryFolders`.
- **The discovery gate is `bb.savedQueries.search` alone**, no longer "search or manage". Every predefined role holding `manage` also holds `search`, so only a hand-rolled custom role with `manage` but not `search` loses Search access — and it gained nothing from it once Search became caller-scoped.
- **`UpdateSavedQuery` returns `PermissionDenied`** where it used to return `NotFound`, for a caller who can read but not write (a VIEWER). `NotFound` is still the answer for callers who cannot read at all.

## What changed

**Storage** — migration `3.22/0008` adds `saved_query.bindings jsonb` holding a protojson array **at the root**. That shape is load-bearing: the access queries probe it with `@>` against a `gin (jsonb_path_ops)` index, and a wrapper object would need an expression index instead.

**API** — `GetSavedQueryPolicy` / `SetSavedQueryPolicy`. The read is gated on `read(s,u)` and returns the whole policy — that's how a grantee learns whether they may edit, since nothing caller-relative rides on the `SavedQuery` resource. The write needs `share(s,u)` and is compare-and-swap on an etag derived from the bindings themselves, so a full-replacement write can't silently reinstate a grant somebody just revoked. An EDITOR binding carries content writes only: sharing, re-filing, and deleting stay with the creator and admins.

A `shared == true` filter replaces `creator != me` for the Shared view. The two differ for an admin, for whom `creator != me` also matches saved queries nobody shared with them.

**Search pagination** — the read predicate moved into SQL instead of filtering the page afterwards, fixing a pre-existing bug where a page of ten could return two rows *and* a next-page token.

title: feat(audit): audit saved query writes, not reads
body:
## What

Annotates `UpdateSavedQuery` and `BatchUpdateSavedQueries` with `bytebase.v1.audit`, and revises `docs/design/saved-queries-model.md` to match on two points.

Saved queries had **no** audit annotations before the rename, and only `Create`/`Delete` after it. This settles the policy: **every RPC that mutates a saved query or its policy is audited; no read RPC is.** `SetIamPolicy` joins the set when sharing lands.

## Why the design doc changed

The doc previously audited *content reads* — an annotation on `GetSavedQuery` and `ListSavedQueries` — which required two compensating mechanisms to work: a metadata-only carve-out in `SearchSavedQueries` for rows an admin reached solely via the override, and an audit event emitted from `UpdateSavedQuery` only when the write exercised that override. Both are dropped. The rule is now derivable from the method rather than from who the caller happened to be, and the same line the rest of the v1 API already draws.

Two costs are recorded in the doc rather than glossed:

- **Autosave writes are audit events.** The editor saves on a 2-second debounce, so saved-query writes will dominate the audit log by volume. This is the price of a rule that doesn't special-case the hot path.
- **Admin reads leave no trail.** The control on `bb.savedQueries.manage` / `bb.savedQueries.list` is that neither is in a default member role, not an after-the-fact read log.

Request statements are redacted the way `CreateSavedQuery` already does it — without that, every autosaved SQL statement would land in the audit log. The response side was already covered by the existing `*v1pb.SavedQuery` case.

## Pagination section rewrite

Unrelated to audit, but it was a documented requirement the codebase never had. The doc specified keyset cursors, "never OFFSET", and an `O(page)` guarantee resting on a `(creator, project, updated_at DESC, resource_id DESC)` index that was never created. In fact `storepb.PageToken` carries only `{limit, offset}` and has no cursor field, and ~22 call sites across the v1 API paginate with `LIMIT/OFFSET`. Saved queries follow the convention; keyset would be a platform-wide change, out of scope here. Worth noting the as-built title ordering is *less* exposed to offset paging's skip/repeat window than the doc's `updated_at` ordering would have been, since titles only change on explicit create/rename/delete while autosave bumps `updated_at` constantly.

## Not a breaking change

No removed or renamed RPCs, fields, or endpoints; the proto diff adds a method option only. The regenerated descriptors contain exactly that option on the two methods and nothing else. Deployments should expect audit log growth from the autosave path.

## Testing

- `go build -ldflags "-w -s" ./backend/bin/server/main.go`
- `golangci-lint run --allow-parallel-runners` — no new issues
- `go test ./backend/api/v1/...` — passing
- `pnpm --dir frontend check`, `pnpm --dir frontend type-check`
- `buf lint proto`

title: fix(instance): ask for the keytab in the form, not through a failed connection
body:
## Problem

#21165 made the server refuse to carry a stored Kerberos keytab to a destination
the caller moved. The instance form had no idea.

The keytab is `INPUT_ONLY`, so it reads blank on edit and the form sends it blank
unless the operator uploads a new file. Any host or port edit on a Hive Kerberos
instance therefore went out without one, and the server refused it.

That refusal arrived from inside the pre-save connection test. The operator saw a
connection-failure dialog and went looking at the network for a problem that was
really "re-upload your .keytab".

## Fix

The form now makes the same comparison the server does, over the same projection:
`host`, `port`, `additional_addresses`, `ssh_host`, `ssh_port`,
`extra_connection_parameters`, and the KDC host and port.
`movesKeytabToNewDestination` in `frontend/src/components/instance/common.ts`
mirrors `dataSourceDestination` in
`backend/api/v1/instance_service_converter.go` field for field.

It runs on the extracted data source, the value the form would send, so the
default port the form fills in and the SSH fields it drops count as a move here
exactly as they do there. The stored side comes from `instance.dataSources`,
matched by data source ID.

`checkDataSource` is where the check lands. That predicate gates the Update
button, the Test Connection button, and Create, and it runs over the admin data
source and every read-only one. The operator gets a field-level error under the
keytab upload and never reaches the connection dialog for this.

Reading the diff: `extractDataSourceFromEdit` moved up in `InstanceFormContext`,
unchanged, so that `checkDataSource` can reach it. `git diff -M --patience`
shows it as a pure relocation.

## Two things the server knows and the form cannot

**Whether a keytab is stored.** The server refuses only when one actually is
(`len(storedKrb.GetKeytab()) > 0`). No `keytab_set` companion exists — the
`DataSource` message ships `ssl_ca_set` and friends for exactly this write-only
problem, but `KerberosConfig` has none — so the form infers it from the data
source still authenticating with Kerberos. **A Kerberos data source stored
without a keytab is therefore blocked here on an edit the server would accept.**
That state is not reachable through this form, which requires a keytab on
create; it is reachable through the API. The doc comment records the guess and
names the flag that would remove it. Adding that flag is a proto and backend
change, so it is not in this PR.

**Which fields are addresses.** The Go projection has a test that fails until a
newly added `DataSource` field is classified in or out. A hand-copied projection
with no such test is how this bug comes back: the frontend stops seeing a move
while the server keeps refusing it. The TypeScript side now has the same walk,
over the v1 `DataSource`, over `KerberosConfig`, and over the SASL mechanism
oneof.

title: fix(audit): redact batch instance updates and the IAM credential oneof
body:
Three holes in what an audit row records, all on the instance write path.

## BatchUpdateInstances was never redacted

`getRequestString` switches on the concrete request type and had no case for
`BatchUpdateInstancesRequest`, so the request fell through to the default branch
and `protojson.Marshal` wrote every data-source secret in the batch verbatim.
The handler fans the batch out to `UpdateInstance` in process, so the inner
`UpdateInstanceRequest` never re-enters the audit interceptor — no redacted row
existed anywhere. This is not MCP-specific and not gated on anything: it leaked
for every caller on every call. The response side gets the same case, as its
`BatchCreateSheetsResponse` twin already has.

## redactDataSource skipped two secrets

The whole `iam_extension` oneof — `azure_credential`, `aws_credential` and
`gcp_credential`, whose `GCPCredential.content` is a full service-account key —
and `authentication_private_key_passphrase`. Every leaf secret here is
`INPUT_ONLY`, so a write request is the only place it appears, which is exactly
what an audit row records. This one bit on all six instance write paths, not
just the batch.

The oneof keeps its variant instead of being cleared, so the row still records
which credential type was supplied. What survives mirrors the read path
(`instance_service_converter.go`): the Azure tenant and client IDs name the
principal and are not `INPUT_ONLY`, so they stay. A variant added later is
dropped whole rather than logged.

Keeping the AWS `role_arn` was considered — it names a principal rather than
authenticating as one. It is dropped anyway, because "no `INPUT_ONLY` field
survives redaction" is an invariant a descriptor walk can check forever, and a
hand-kept exception list is the drift this change exists to stop.

## redactDataSource also panicked on a nil data source

It was the one redactor without a nil guard, behind a `proto.Clone(d).(*T)`
assertion that cannot fail for a typed nil and so never caught what it looked
like it was guarding. A rejected `AddDataSource` with no `data_source` is
audited like any other failure, so any caller could crash the interceptor:

```go
getRequestString(&v1pb.AddDataSourceRequest{Name: "instances/foo"})
// panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
```

## The FORBIDDEN reason now names the AI-endpoint retarget

`update_mask=["value.ai.endpoint"]` keeps the stored `api_key` and repoints it,
so the next `AIService/Chat` puts that key in an auth header to a host the caller
just wrote. SaaS refuses AI setting writes outright (`setting_service.go:370`),
so it is a self-hosted vector, and the comment says so. BOT-53 will read this
text to decide what must stay forbidden when `UpdateSetting` is split; an
unnamed vector is one that gets reopened. Comment only — no classification,
interceptor or method-list change.

## Sweep

Walked every message in the compiled `bytebase.v1` descriptor set for a
transitive `Instance` or `DataSource`, then jo

title: fix: estimate MySQL affected rows from the JSON plan's DML target node
body:
Fixes [BYT-9858](https://linear.app/bytebase/issue/BYT-9858/mysql-affected-row-review-treats-explainrows-as-rows-affected).

## What

The `STATEMENT_AFFECTED_ROW_LIMIT` rule and the SQL summary (`CountAffectedRows`) both took the **first non-null `rows` value of tabular `EXPLAIN`** as the affected-row count. That value is a plan node's rows-examined estimate. When the optimizer drives the plan from another table — e.g. `UPDATE ... WHERE EXISTS (...)` rewritten to a semijoin — the first row is the driving table's scan estimate and wildly overstates the affected rows. A customer statement targeting ~12k rows was rejected as affecting ~3.9M.

Both paths now run `EXPLAIN FORMAT=JSON` first. MySQL and MariaDB flag the DML target table's plan node with `"update"`/`"delete"`, and that node carries the optimizer's cumulative cardinality estimate for rows actually reaching the modify step (`rows_produced_per_join`, falling back to the per-scan estimate scaled by `filtered`). Multi-target `DELETE a, b FROM ...` nodes are summed. When no flagged node is found (INSERT plans, servers that don't mark the target), the code falls back to the existing tabular heuristic, so behavior is unchanged there. The statement `LIMIT` cap and the OceanBase JSON-plan path are untouched.

New shared extractor: `backend/plugin/parser/mysql/explain_plan.go`, used by `backend/plugin/advisor/mysql/rule_statement_affected_row_limit.go` and `backend/plugin/db/mysql/stats.go`.

## Testing

- Extractor unit tests run against 9 real `EXPLAIN FORMAT=JSON` fixtures captured from MySQL 8.0 and MariaDB 11 (semijoin, antijoin, IN-materialization, ORDER BY/LIMIT wrapper, multi-target delete, single-table, SELECT-only fallback).
- The advisor/driver mock explain drivers now dispatch on query shape; added tests proving the JSON target-node estimate is preferred over the tabular first-row value, and that `LIMIT` still caps the JSON estimate. Existing tests (now exercising the fallback path) pass unchanged.
- End-to-end against live containers with a 400k-row target table (customer statement shape, real affected rows = 4000):

| Statement | Real rows | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| MySQL 8.0 `UPDATE ... EXISTS` | 4,000 | 100,232 | **3,816** |
| MySQL 8.0 single-table `DELETE` range | 200 | 200 | 200 |
| MySQL 8.0 `UPDATE ... LIMIT 10` | — | 10 | 10 |
| MariaDB 11 `UPDATE ... EXISTS` | ~100 | 10,000 | 10,000 (no regression; MariaDB's plan carries no join-filtered estimate on the target node) |

- `golangci-lint run` clean; full `go build` of the server passes.

title: feat!: add saved query permissions, folders, and stars
body:
Implements [docs/design/saved-queries-model.md](docs/design/saved-queries-model.md) up to — but deliberately excluding — per-object sharing enforcement. Third phase after #21159 (rename) and #21160 (visibility removal).

## What changed

**Permissions.** The `bb.worksheets.*` family becomes `bb.savedQueries.{create,search,list,manage}`:

| Permission | Gates |
|---|---|
| `create` | creating a saved query in a project (IAM-enforced at the interceptor) |
| `search` | per-project discovery — `SearchSavedQueries` and `SearchSavedQueryFolders`, both returning only rows the caller can read |
| `list` | the grant-independent governance surface: `ListSavedQueries` across creators, e.g. an offboarding review |
| `manage` | admin backstop that can reach any saved query in scope |

`bb.worksheets.get` is dropped rather than renamed. Reading one saved query is decided per-object by `canAccessSavedQuery` (creator, or `manage` in scope), so a workspace-level read permission would be a second, redundant answer to a question the object already answers. Discovery stays a permission because "this role doesn't browse saved queries here" is a meaningful project-level statement.

**Folders.** A `folder` path column on `saved_query` (`''` = unfiled) replaces the `saved_query_organizer` table. A folder is a path on rows, so empty folders cannot exist and there is no addressable folder resource. `BatchUpdateSavedQueries` re-files matching rows with a `folder`-only update mask.

**Stars.** Row existence in `saved_query_star (saved_query, principal)`. A star is the caller's own marker — invisible to others, carrying no access — so `UpdateSavedQueryStar`'s only requirement is read access to the query being starred, which also keeps private saved query names unprobeable.

**`SearchSavedQueryFolders` replaces `ListSavedQueryFolders`.** Folders are a derived view over the `folder` column, not a resource collection, so `List` was wrong twice over: it advertised a `savedQueryFolders` collection with nothing addressable in it, and it put a `List`-named method under the `search` gate while `ListSavedQueries` means the cross-creator governance surface. It is now a custom method on the `savedQueries` collection (`savedQueries:searchFolders`) that reads as the sibling of `SearchSavedQueries`, which is exactly what it is.

## Breaking Changes

| Area | Change | Migration |
|---|---|---|
| Permissions | `bb.worksheets.{get,list,manage}` → `bb.savedQueries.{search,list,manage}` | `0007` rewrites custom-role permission arrays in place |
| Proto | `UpdateSavedQueryOrganizer`, `BatchUpdateSavedQueryOrganizer` removed; `ListSavedQueryFolders` → `SearchSavedQueryFolders` | callers move to `UpdateSavedQueryStar` / `BatchUpdateSavedQueries` |
| Proto | `SavedQuery.folders` (repeated) → `SavedQuery.folder` (path string); field 12 reserved | `0007` backfills paths by joining the creator's organizer segments with `/` |
| Proto | `SavedQueryOrganizer`, `SavedQueryFolder` messages removed | — |
|

title: fix(audit,instance): record denied validate-only calls, keep a keytab off a new destination
body:
Two live gaps found while shipping #21156. Neither touches classification.

## 1. `validate_only` suppressed the audit row for denials

`createAuditLog` returned before writing anything whenever
`isValidateOnlyRequest(e.request)` was true. `isValidateOnlyRequest` reads only
the top-level field and does not recurse, so it applies to the six audited
request messages that carry it: `UpdateDataSource`, `AddDataSource`,
`CreateInstance`, `CreateIdentityProvider`, `UpdateSetting` and
`CreateDatabaseGroup`. Three of those are on methods MCP forbids.

An agent that set the flag therefore got an unlogged attempt at a FORBIDDEN
method. #21156 pinned this as an A/B: two identical MCP denials of
`UpdateDataSource`, same session, same method, one flag apart, produced one
audit row between them.

The skip now applies only when the call also SUCCEEDED. A dry run Bytebase
accepted changed nothing worth recording, which is the case the skip was
written for; a refused attempt is worth exactly as much as any other refused
attempt.

**Every failure records, not only a policy denial, and that is deliberate.**
The instance form runs a validate-only connection test before each save and on
each Test Connection click, so most of the rows this adds are failed connection
tests rather than refusals — a real volume change on a common flow. Keying on a
denial code instead would be the same shape of hole this closes: it would record
the refusals that happen to carry that code and silently drop every other
rejected attempt.

One residual, deliberately not changed: for the three instance methods,
`validate_only` means "dial the request's endpoint now", so a dry run that
SUCCEEDS is the case where the connection actually reached the caller's host —
and that one still writes no row. It is not invisible (`checkAndLogInstanceConnection`
emits `slog.Info("instance connection check completed")`), but it is not on the
audit page.

**Redaction of the newly-logged rows.** Verified: all five secret-bearing
messages above already have a case in `getRequestString`'s switch, so the new
rows go through the same redaction as every other row on those methods, and the
check stays where it was relative to that call. `CreateDatabaseGroup` has no
case but carries no secret field. The response side is moot — every newly
logged row has `e.rerr != nil`, and all six handlers return `nil, err` on every
error path.

Two pre-existing gaps in `redactDataSource` are NOT fixed here and are not new
to this change — a plain, non-validate-only `UpdateDataSource` already writes
them today: the whole `iam_extension` oneof (`azure_credential.client_secret`,
`aws_credential.{access_key_id,secret_access_key,session_token}`,
`gcp_credential.content` — a full GCP service-account key) and
`authentication_private_key_passphrase` are unmasked. They belong with the
BOT-55 redaction work.

## 2. A keytab survived a destination change

`retainStoredKeytabs` matched stored data sources by ID and nothing compared

title: fix(frontend): land EDITOR-mode workspaces on the SQL Editor after re-auth
body:
Fixes BYT-10056. Customer-reported (Lucid), on 3.20.0.

> We have Bytebase configured to land on the SQL Editor page, but when I re-auth it always redirects me to the workspace instead.

## The bug

`appFeatures` is only populated by `loadWorkspaceProfile()`, and `main.ts` calls that at bootstrap **only when a session already exists**. A sign-in boots signed out, so the profile is never fetched (the setting is authenticated-only and 401s). `login()` refreshed the user, server info and workspace list but not the profile, so both the EDITOR check in `login()` and the one in `rootGuard`'s `resolveRootRedirect()` read the hard-coded `PIPELINE` default. `resolveRootRedirect` then fell through to the landing page, because the last-visit fallback deliberately ignores `/sql-editor` paths.

Regression from **3.19.0** (`f75589919e`), which replaced the reactive Vue `DummyRootView` watcher with a one-shot router-loader read. The branch logic was ported faithfully; the timing was not. Still present through 3.21.0, so upgrading does not help.

## The fix

Load the workspace profile in `login()` and `signup()` before anything reads the change mode. Authentication is the first moment the setting is readable.

Then delete both store-level EDITOR branches and navigate to `"/"`, letting `resolveRootRedirect()` resolve it. It already owns "where does `/` go"; the branches were copies of that policy that disagreed with each other and with the guard. They only fired when the destination was already `"/"`, so this is behavior-preserving. `auth.ts` is 17 lines shorter.

That divergence was not cosmetic: `signup()`'s copy had no redirect check, and it had been dead only because signup boots signed out. Loading the profile would have woken it up and started dropping deep links.

## Verification

Live, against a running instance with `databaseChangeMode = EDITOR`, via an isolated-Chrome Playwright repro. Before, signing in from the bare root landed on `/landing`, with the profile arriving 21ms **after** the redirect was decided. After, both the bare root and a `/sql-editor` deep link land on the SQL Editor.

Tests, all mutation-verified (each fails when the code it covers is removed):
- `login()` hands `rootGuard` a loaded profile and navigates to `"/"`
- `signup()` does the same, and keeps an explicit `?redirect`
- `rootGuard` sends EDITOR to the SQL Editor, and falls back to landing while the profile is unloaded (the bug, documented)
- matching `"/"` yields a route with a loader (the seam the fix depends on)

The root-redirect path had no coverage at all before this.

Full suite: 440 files / 3532 tests.

## Known follow-ups (not in this PR)

- `SetupPage.homePath` keeps a third copy of the EDITOR rule and omits the last-visit branch. Folding it in changes onboarding behavior for a PIPELINE user with a meaningful last visit, so it wants its own tests.
- `loadWorkspaceProfile`'s bare `.catch()` swallows a failed `GetSetting`, leaving `PIPELINE`. A custom role lacking `bb.

## Summary

   Adds secret-free audit records for release, saved query, and password reset security events, implementing the content-bearing and
 authentication batches of the [audit coverage plan](docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-12-v1-api-audit-coverage.md).

   ### Newly audited RPCs

   - `ReleaseService.CreateRelease`, `UpdateRelease`
   - `SavedQueryService.CreateSavedQuery`, `DeleteSavedQuery`
   - `AuthService.RequestPasswordReset`, `ResetPassword`

   Also fixes `SendEmailLoginCode` audit attribution, which previously wrote rows without a validated workspace parent.

   ## Key changes

   - **Unauthenticated attribution**: the handler validates workspace membership (`parseAndSetAuditWorkspace`) and the interceptor accepts only
 that workspace — never ACL resources, the caller token, or the response. Unknown, deleted, service-account, and workload-identity targets
 produce no audit row.
   - **Redaction**: password reset `code`/`new_password`, release SQL, saved query content, and webhook URLs are masked or dropped; email is
 preserved for attribution. All redactors clone before modifying.
   - **Resource extraction**: `getRequestResource` is method-aware and reuses the shared reflection helper for standard AIP resources;
 `SavedQuery` gains resource references so its lifecycle rows resolve to the owning project.
   - **Behavior**: password reset now skips deleted accounts, and `ResetPassword` re-verifies workspace membership captured at send time to
 prevent policy bypass.

 no-workspace fallback.

   ## Generated code

body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #21159, finishing the storage side of the rename and front-loading a cutover the saved-queries redesign already commits to. [docs/design/saved-queries-model.md](https://github.com/bytebase/bytebase/blob/main/docs/design/saved-queries-model.md) replaces the three-state visibility flag with per-object grants and **migrates every existing row owner-private with no mapping** for `PROJECT_READ`/`PROJECT_WRITE` (owners re-share by hand from the new dialog). Since the flag's data cannot carry forward, this PR removes the visibility model entirely rather than carrying it dead into the access-model phase — and renames the tables to `saved_query` / `saved_query_organizer` in the same migration.

**Resulting access rule** (the design's cutover semantics): a saved query is private to its creator; workspace `bb.worksheets.manage` is the admin backstop. Per-object sharing arrives with the bindings redesign.

## What changed

- **DB**: migration `3.22/0006` drops `worksheet.visibility`, renames `worksheet` → `saved_query` and `worksheet_organizer` → `saved_query_organizer` (organizer link column `worksheet` → `saved_query`), renames the four named indexes (`IF EXISTS`-guarded), and **moves the connected-database reference from the `(instance, db_name)` columns into the payload** as the database's canonical resource name (`SavedQueryPayload.database`), backfilled only when the database still belongs to the query's own project (the design's carry rule). `LATEST.sql` and `TestLatestVersion` updated. Auto-named constraints keep their old names on upgraded installs — cosmetic drift only.
- **Proto**: `SavedQuery.Visibility` enum and field removed (field number 10 and the name reserved), visibility filter and update-mask docs trimmed, per-RPC access comments rewritten. The store payload proto renames to `SavedQueryOrganizerPayload` — field names are unchanged, so stored protojson payloads need no rewrite.
- **Store**: `worksheet.go` → `saved_query.go` with the renamed tables and a `SavedQuery*` message/method surface; the project purge, principal email-rename, and instance-nullify writers move to the new table names; both CEL visibility filter branches removed — including the `in`-operator branch that would otherwise have queried the dropped column at runtime.
- **Backend service**: `canRead`/`canWrite` collapse to a shared creator-or-admin check; the project-scoped permission branches (which cited a permission no predefined role grants — audit finding T7/T8) and the visibility conversions are gone. `validateSavedQueryDatabase` still enforces existence, same-project ownership, and scope canonicality at write time (project form for project instances — BOT-36 coverage retained), and stores the validated canonical name.
- **Bug fix (project/workspace instance references)**: reads now return the stored canonical name **without per-row instance resolution**. Previously `convertToAPISavedQuery` re-fetched the instance for every row and returned `No

title: refactor: rename worksheet to saved query across API, backend, and frontend
body:
## Summary

Phase 1 of [docs/design/saved-queries-model.md](https://github.com/bytebase/bytebase/blob/main/docs/design/saved-queries-model.md) (decision 1 / G8): rename **worksheet → saved query**, the industry-standard term, while the API is already slated to break for the access-model redesign. This PR is the rename only — no access-model, store, or schema changes.

## What changed

**Proto / API**
- `WorksheetService` → `SavedQueryService` (`saved_query_service.proto`): all nine RPCs, messages, HTTP paths (`/v1/{parent=projects/*}/savedQueries`, `/savedQueryFolders`), and resource names (`projects/{project}/savedQueries/{savedQuery}`). Generated Go/TS/openapi/grpc-doc regenerated; unrelated remote-plugin drift reverted.

**Backend**
- `backend/api/v1/saved_query_service.go` is a 1:1 mechanical rename of the v1 layer; gate logic, conversions, and behavior are unchanged. The store layer and the `worksheet` table keep their names — the service converts at the boundary. Resource-name helpers, route registration, and tests renamed alongside.

**Frontend**
- Identifiers, files, and the deep-link route (`/sql-editor/projects/:project/savedQueries/:savedQuery`) renamed; UI copy reworded in all five locales, following BigQuery's localized term per language (已保存的查询 / 保存済みクエリ / consulta guardada / truy vấn đã lưu).
- UX wording pass beyond the mechanical rename: plural pane label ("Saved queries"), "New query" action, direct confirm questions ("Delete this saved query?"), access labels "Project can view / Project can edit" instead of enum-speak, "Access" instead of the misleading "Link access", tab-based close copy, and share-dialog descriptions in plain language without raw permission IDs. Pre-existing es machine-translation errors in the same section fixed.

**Upgrade continuity (three layers)**
- `storage-migrate` v2 stage (`bb.storage-migration-v2`) backfills the renamed localStorage pref keys and rewrites persisted tab/sidebar values.
- `normalizePersistedTab` keeps a lazy read-path backstop for legacy-shaped tabs.
- `rewriteLegacyPath` rewrites legacy `/sheets/{id}` deep links before the router mounts (bookmarks and shared links arrive as full page loads), and `?panel=worksheet` maps to the renamed panel.

## Breaking Changes

- The v1 worksheet API is renamed wholesale: service, RPCs, messages, JSON field names, HTTP paths, and resource names. External scripts calling `/v1/**/worksheets` or `bytebase.v1.WorksheetService` break at upgrade (hard cutover per design decision 8) — needs a release-notes callout.
- Frontend deep links move to `/savedQueries/`; legacy links are rewritten client-side at load, so existing bookmarks keep working.
- **Not** breaking: DB schema and store layer are untouched; existing data needs no migration. Permission IDs stay `bb.worksheets.*` (renaming them requires a role-row data migration and moves with the access-model phase — noted in a `SavedQueryService` comment).

## Testing

- Backend: build, `go vet`, `golangci-li

title: fix(mcp): forbid the methods that give away a credential for another principal
body:
Closes BOT-52. Follows #21152 in the same lane.

## Why this batch is different from #21152

#21152 forbade the methods that re-issue or rewrite the **caller's own** credential. Every one of those is eventually contained by acting on that one principal: revoke the OAuth grant, flip the workspace MCP switch, deactivate the human.

These give away a credential for a principal that is **not** the caller. None of those three levers reaches what they leave behind.

All are admin-permission gated. That is not a mitigation here — a workspace admin running an agent is the target scenario, and prompt injection does not require the agent to be hostile.

## Annotated `mcp_method_class = FORBIDDEN` (11)

| Method | What it gives away |
|---|---|
| `ServiceAccountService/CreateServiceAccount` | plaintext `bbs_` key for a **new** principal |
| `ServiceAccountService/UpdateServiceAccount` | re-keys an **existing** privileged account, plaintext returned, no proof of the old key |
| `WorkspaceService/RotateDirectorySyncToken` | plaintext SCIM token |
| `UserService/CreateUser` | fresh principal with a caller-chosen password |
| `UserService/UpdateEmail` | rebinds **any** account to a caller-chosen address; the reset flow then mails the code there |
| `IdentityProviderService/CreateIdentityProvider` | SSO trust anchor |
| `IdentityProviderService/UpdateIdentityProvider` | SSO trust anchor |
| `IdentityProviderService/TestIdentityProvider` | stored client secret / LDAP bind password, carried to a caller-supplied host |
| `SettingService/TestEmailSetting` | stored SMTP password, carried to a caller-supplied host |
| `WorkloadIdentityService/CreateWorkloadIdentity` | issuer + subject `ExchangeToken` later validates against |
| `WorkloadIdentityService/UpdateWorkloadIdentity` | same |

The workload-identity pair is the sharpest: `ExchangeToken` validates an external OIDC token against `wi.Config` (`auth_service.go:1501`) and is `allow_without_credential`, so once the anchor is written the Bytebase token is minted **from outside** — no MCP session involved, nothing left to revoke.

One new reason constant covers all eleven, because they are one mechanism:

> it hands someone control of a principal other than the caller, which revoking this session would not take back

## The wholesale-vs-writes ruling: **writes + Test, not wholesale**

`#21141`'s inventory flagged IdP reads, so this was a live question. The reads do not leak a secret:

- `convertIdentityProviderConfigFromStore` blanks `ClientSecret` on both OAuth2 and OIDC and `BindPassword` on LDAP — `idp_service.go:476`, `:494`, `:531`, each with a `// SECURITY: We do not expose` comment. It is the **only** read conversion, used by `GetIdentityProvider` (`:50`) and `ListIdentityProviders` (`:81`).
- `ListIdentityProviders` is `allow_without_credential` — the login page calls it unauthenticated. Forbidding an endpoint any anonymous HTTP client can already read would be theater, and would cost an agent legitimate work.
