title: fix(pg): disable TLS verification for multi-host fallbacks
body:
## Summary
- Use PostgreSQL-compatible `sslmode=require` when TLS is enabled but server certificate verification is disabled.
- Apply Bytebase TLS settings to pgx primary and fallback TLS configs for multi-host PostgreSQL and CockroachDB data sources.
- Add regression tests covering libpq-style multi-host configs so pgx fallbacks skip server certificate verification, carry mTLS client certificates, and use Bytebase's custom CA verification policy per host.

## Why
For multi-host PostgreSQL-compatible data sources, pgx builds separate TLS configs for the primary host and each fallback host. Bytebase previously patched only the primary host config after `pgx.ParseConfig`, so fallback hosts still used verifying TLS configs and could fail with `x509: certificate signed by unknown authority` even when `VerifyTlsCertificate=false`.

The same primary-only patching also meant inline client certificates and inline CA verification policy were not consistently present on fallback TLS configs. This PR keeps pgx's per-host fallback TLS settings and applies Bytebase's TLS material and verifier per parsed host.

## Pre-PR Checklist
- Breaking change check: no breaking change; this restores the configured TLS behavior for PostgreSQL-compatible multi-host configs.
- Composite-PK query safety: skipped; no `backend/store/` or migrator changes.
- SonarCloud properties: skipped; no new files or directories.

- [x] `golangci-lint run --allow-parallel-runners`

title: refactor(advisor/tidb): migrate column_disallow_changing trio to omni AST (Phase 1.5 §1.5.3 batch 11)
body:
## Summary

Three theme-coupled advisors migrated as one unit. No helper coupling between them (verified via pre-batch grep) — ship-as-unit is theme- and cadence-driven, not load-bearing. All Recipe A. ALTER TABLE only (no CreateTable arm in any of the pingcap-tidb predecessors; preserved).

**35 of 51 advisors merged once this lands (32 → 35).** 16 remaining + 1 Class III blocked.

## Cumulative #21 — latent pingcap false-positive fixed (cumulative table entry, no fixture pin)

Pre-batch step 2a flagged `spec.NewColumns[0].Tp.String()` usage in `disallow_changing_type`. Empirical verification surfaced:

**Pingcap's `FieldType.String()` appends a `BINARY` charset annotation on types stored with binary charset:**
| Type | Pingcap render | Omni built string |
|---|---|---|
| BLOB | `"blob BINARY"` | `"blob"` |
| TINYBLOB | `"tinyblob BINARY"` | `"tinyblob"` |
| VARBINARY(N) | `"varbinary(N) BINARY"` | `"varbinary(N)"` |

The pingcap-typed `disallow_changing_type` rule compared this against `column.GetProto().Type` from the catalog (which stores `"blob"` from INFORMATION_SCHEMA — no charset suffix). `normalizeColumnType` has no `"blob"` case, so default-branch identity-lowercase yielded `"blob"` vs `"blob binary"` → `ALTER TABLE t MODIFY a BLOB` on a BLOB column (no-op type change) was incorrectly flagged.

**Latent pingcap false-positive silently fixed by this migration.** Omni's `DataType.Name` is the bare type name; omni-built rendering matches catalog rendering → no false-positive.

**Why no fixture pin:** mock test catalog (`MockMySQLDatabase.tech_book`) has no BLOB column; adding one would have cross-engine impact (mysql + tidb + mariadb + oceanbase share it). Pinned conceptually via plan-doc cumulative #21 with empirical receipts.

**Mysql parallel:** mysql analog (rewritten during mysql omni migration) builds type string from `DataType.Name + Length + Scale + Unsigned` — same shape, also free of this false-positive.

## Cardinality contract: 1 advice per ALTER TABLE statement (preserved pingcap)

All three pingcap-typed predecessors used a Visitor with `break` after first match — exactly ONE advice per top-level ALTER TABLE statement. The omni port replicates this with explicit `break`.

**Mysql analog diverges** — emits per-cmd without breaking, producing N advices for N matching specs. Cardinality divergence preserved on the tidb side per invariant #7's "preserve pingcap behavior" rule.

Pinned each advisor with multi-spec fixtures:
- `disallow_change`: `ALTER TABLE t CHANGE COLUMN a c int, CHANGE COLUMN b d int;` → 1 advice
- `disallow_changing_order`: `MODIFY a int FIRST, MODIFY b int AFTER c` → 1 advice
- `disallow_change_type`: `MODIFY id bigint, MODIFY name varchar(20)` → 1 advice

## FIRST/AFTER omni shape (verified empirically)

Pingcap: `spec.Position.Tp != ast.ColumnPositionNone`.
Omni: `cmd.First bool || cmd.After string != ""` (separate fields; both empty when no position specified).

## Pre-batch protocol receipts

title: refactor(advisor/tidb): migrate auto-increment trio to omni AST (Phase 1.5 §1.5.3 batch 10)
body:
## Summary

Three theme-coupled advisors migrated as one unit. No helper coupling between them — ship-as-unit is theme- and sibling-parity-driven, not load-bearing. All Recipe A.

**32 of 51 advisors merged once this lands (29 → 32). 19 remaining + 1 Class III blocked.**

## Step 2a's first real use — caught a BLOB/TEXT-class bug pre-merge

`must_integer`'s pingcap source dispatches on `case mysql.TypeTiny, mysql.TypeShort, mysql.TypeInt24, mysql.TypeLong, mysql.TypeLonglong:` — step 2a's grep flagged this immediately in pre-batch protocol. Cross-reference + empirical parse-test surfaced a new type-byte unification:

**`mysql.TypeTiny` covers TINYINT + BOOL + BOOLEAN** (BOOL/BOOLEAN are TINYINT aliases in MySQL). Omni splits the alias differently than #18's BLOB/TEXT split:
- `TINYINT` stays as `DataType.Name = "TINYINT"`
- `BOOL` AND `BOOLEAN` both pre-normalize to `DataType.Name = "BOOLEAN"` (not "TINYINT")

Without empirical verification, a mechanical port of `omniIsIntegerType` matching only canonical int-family names would have flagged `CREATE TABLE t(b BOOL AUTO_INCREMENT, KEY(b))` as non-integer — regression vs pingcap-tidb.

Fixed in-batch: `omniIsIntegerType` in `utils.go` includes `"BOOLEAN"` (diverges from mysql analog's list, which omits it — long-standing mysql gap, not introduced by this PR). Pinned with three regression-direction fixtures: `BOOL AUTO_INCREMENT`, `BOOLEAN AUTO_INCREMENT`, `TINYINT AUTO_INCREMENT` — all expected as no-advice.

**This is the first instance of step 2a (added after cumulative #18's miss) working as designed** — caught the same class of bug (charset-style type-byte unification) pre-merge that batch 8 needed Codex P1 to flag post-merge.

Plan-doc cumulative #20 added documenting the TINYINT/BOOLEAN unification.

## must_unsigned: Zerofill preservation

Pingcap's `mysql.HasUnsignedFlag(column.Tp.GetFlag())` returned true when EITHER the unsigned flag OR the zerofill flag was set (ZEROFILL implies UNSIGNED in MySQL). Omni splits the bits — `Unsigned` and `Zerofill` are separate booleans on `DataType`.

Port checks both via `Unsigned || Zerofill` (matches mysql analog). Pinned with `INT ZEROFILL AUTO_INCREMENT` + `INT UNSIGNED ZEROFILL AUTO_INCREMENT` fixtures (both no-advice expected).

## initial_value: preserved pingcap scope (CREATE TABLE only)

Pingcap-typed advisor only matched `*ast.CreateTableStmt` for the `TableOptionAutoIncrement` check. Mysql analog also handles `ALTER TABLE ... AUTO_INCREMENT = N` via the `ATTableOption` arm — that broader scope is a mysql-side behavior, NOT something the tidb migration should adopt. Preserved per invariant #7's caveat on mysql-analog non-authority.

omni's `TableOption.Value` is string-typed (pingcap's `option.UintValue` was uint64) — parse via `strconv.ParseUint` and skip parse failures (matches pingcap's implicit-skip on type-assert miss).

## Helpers + shared types

Added to `utils.go`:
- `omniIsIntegerType(dt *DataType) bool` — covers TINYINT/SMALLINT/MEDIUM

title: refactor(advisor/tidb): migrate column_require_default to omni AST (Phase 1.5 §1.5.3 batch 9)
body:
## Summary

**Closes BYT-9414.** Migrates the last consumer of pingcap-typed `needDefault` to omni AST, then deletes the helper. Small, clean cleanup batch.

29 of 51 advisors merged once this lands (28 → 29). 22 remaining + 1 Class III blocked.

## What's migrated

- `advisor_column_require_default.go` → omni AST (Recipe A).
- Reuses `omniNeedDefault` from `utils.go` (batch-7 pre-migration) — already handles AutoIncrement / Generated / column-level PK / BLOB+TEXT / JSON / geometry exemptions per cumulative #14 + #18.
- Local helpers added:
  - `omniHasDefaultValue` — one-line nil check on omni's `ColumnDef.DefaultValue` (omni surfaces DEFAULT directly; pingcap stored it in `Options[]`).
  - `tablePKColumnsFromConstraints` — table-level PRIMARY KEY column-name scan. Mirrors pingcap-typed `getPkColumnsFromConstraints`. Column-level PK is handled by `omniNeedDefault` via the column's own constraints.
- `columnData` reused (already declared in `advisor_column_auto_increment_must_integer.go`, same package).

## What's cleaned up

- `needDefault` (pingcap-typed) deleted from `utils.go`.
- Two pingcap imports (`mysql`, `types`) dropped — no longer used in utils.go.
- `omniNeedDefault` doc comment updated to remove the BYT-9414 tracking reference.

`grep -rn 'needDefault\b' backend/plugin/advisor/tidb/ --include='*.go' | grep -v omniNeedDefault | grep -v _test.go` returns zero hits.

## Codex round-2: PK name normalization (fixed in commit `117812d8`)

Codex P2 correctly flagged: omni preserves the user's literal case on both `column.Name` and `constraint.Columns` — no normalization — so a case-sensitive lookup misses the PK exemption when the user writes the column and the PK reference at different casings.

Empirical reproduction (pre-fix):
```sql
CREATE TABLE t(A INT, PRIMARY KEY(a))
→ "Column `t`.`A` doesn't have DEFAULT."  (incorrectly flagged; `A` is exempt as PK column)
```

Pre-omni pingcap-tidb used `.L` (lowercase identifier form) on both store and lookup. The omni mechanical port lost that normalization. Fix: lowercase on both sides via `strings.ToLower` before the map check. Pinned with two fixture cases (`A INT, PRIMARY KEY(a)` and `mycol INT, PRIMARY KEY(MyCol)`).

Pattern documented in plan-doc cumulative #19.

## Step 2a: type-enum cross-reference

Zero `mysql.Type*` / `column.Tp.GetType()` hits in the pingcap source for this advisor — confirms the cleanup-batch character. Step 2a doesn't apply.

## TEXT-family transitive coverage pin

Added a fixture case: `ALTER TABLE tech_book ADD COLUMN a TEXT; ... TINYTEXT; ... MEDIUMTEXT; ... LONGTEXT;` — all expected as no-advice (default-exempt). Locks the cumulative #18 contract: a future refactor of `omniNeedDefault` cannot silently drop TEXT names without this fixture failing.

## Cross-engine analog findings (empirically verified)

Two mysql gaps were noted during shape audit. Both verified against pre-omni mysql via `git show 699ff60c20^:...`:

1. **mysql `omniPKColumnNames` case-sensitivity

title: fix(react): full-cell click target for selection columns

## Summary
- Makes the entire checkbox column the click target across the React selection tables (databases, instances, database revisions, projects, issues). Clicking near (but not exactly on) the 16px checkbox now toggles selection instead of navigating to the resource page.
- Three local shape-specific fixes — one mechanism per table shape:
  - **Column-driven tables** (`DatabaseTableView`, `InstancesPage`): new `onCellClick`/`onHeaderClick` fields on the column type, wired on `<TableCell>` / `<TableHead>`.
  - **Inline JSX tables** (`DatabaseRevisionTable`, `ProjectTable`): `onClick` + `cursor-pointer` directly on the select `<TableHead>` / `<TableCell>`. ProjectTable's existing `stopPropagation` is upgraded to also toggle (still respects the default-project disabled state).
  - **Flex-div rows** (`IssueTable`): wraps the `Checkbox` in a `self-stretch` div so the click target fills the row height without changing horizontal layout.
- No change to `ui/checkbox.tsx` — the existing `onClick={(e) => e.stopPropagation()}` on the inner `Checkbox` is preserved everywhere; it's load-bearing for preventing double-toggle when the checkbox itself is clicked.

Closes BYT-9447.

title: feat(mongodb): bump gomongo + omni and remove mongosh fallback
body:
## Summary

Concludes the mongosh deprecation. The MongoDB driver now runs every statement through `gomongo`; the mongosh process-spawn path, its telemetry sender, and the mongosh dependency in the published image are all removed.

Builds on three dependency-side PRs that landed first:
- [bytebase/gomongo#29](https://github.com/bytebase/gomongo/pull/29) — `toArray()` no-op, `db.runCommand({...})`, `explain()` on read ops, comment-only statement no-op
- [bytebase/omni#127](https://github.com/bytebase/omni/pull/127) — trailing-comma tolerance in argument lists
- [bytebase/gomongo#30](https://github.com/bytebase/gomongo/pull/30) — bump omni in gomongo

## Changes

### Driver simplification — `backend/plugin/db/mongodb/mongodb.go`
- Drop `executeWithMongosh`, `executeWithMongoshSingle`, `queryConnWithMongosh`, `buildMongoshBaseArgs`, `isFallbackError`
- `Execute()` runs gomongo directly; any gomongo error surfaces to the caller instead of being retried via mongosh
- `QueryConn()` runs gomongo directly; the `--eval` string-quoting, `sh -c` invocation, temp-file plumbing, and result-file parsing are all gone — result conversion always goes through `convertGomongoResult`
- `isMongoStatement`, `getSimpleStatementResult`, `convertRows` become dead code and are removed along with their unit tests

### Telemetry sender — `backend/component/telemetry/` (deleted)
- `ReportGomongoFallback` was the package's only event. With the fallback path gone, the entire package becomes dead code. Deleted, including the `InitGlobalReporter` call in `backend/server/server.go`

### Build and CI
- `scripts/Dockerfile`: drop `apk add npm` and `npm install -g mongosh@2.5.0` (~100 MB image-size reduction)
- `.github/workflows/backend-tests.yml`: drop the mongosh download step (~50 lines)

### Dependency bumps
- `github.com/bytebase/gomongo` → `v0.0.0-20260510192859-8526a440b352`
- `github.com/bytebase/omni` → `v0.0.0-20260509101155-5091fce0322a`

**Net diff: −819 / +25 across 10 files.**

## Breaking Changes

Statements that previously fell back to mongosh now error directly. Each was an intentional deprecation candidate (verified against production `gomongoFallback` telemetry):

| Pattern | Migration |
|---------|-----------|
| Legacy `db.coll.insert(…)` / `db.coll.remove(…)` / `db.coll.update(…)` | Use `insertOne` / `insertMany` / `deleteOne` / `deleteMany` / `updateOne` / `updateMany` |
| Top-level bareword expressions: `ObjectId('…')`, `Long(\"…\")`, standalone `find()` / `findOne(…)` / `getCollection()` | Wrap in `db.coll.<op>` |
| `.forEach(function(d){...})` JS callbacks | Use `aggregate([...])` pipelines |
| Sort with quoted direction: `.sort({field: \"-1\"})` | Pass a numeric `-1` / `1` |

Other historical fallback patterns are now handled natively by the new gomongo (`count()`, `pretty()`, `toArray()`, `db.runCommand({...})`, `.explain()` on read ops, comment-only statements, trailing commas in args). No regression for those.

## Test plan

title: fix(frontend): stop wiping user-scoped localStorage on logout
body:
## Summary

- Removes the `*.<email>`-suffix `localStorage` cleanup from both the Vue (`frontend/src/store/modules/v1/auth.ts`) and React (`frontend/src/react/stores/app/auth.ts`) logout flows.
- Keys are already user-scoped, so cross-user contamination was not a concern. The wipe was a regression introduced alongside the storage-key registry refactor (#19218) and clobbered SQL Editor tabs, recent visits, and other productivity state on every logout.
- Same-email re-login now restores SQL Editor tabs and other user-scoped UI state, matching the close-tab persistence users already expect.

Fixes [BYT-9432](https://linear.app/bytebase/issue/BYT-9432/logout-wipes-user-scoped-localstorage-including-sql-editor).

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm --dir frontend fix` (no diff)
- [x] `pnpm --dir frontend check` passes
- [x] `pnpm --dir frontend type-check` passes
- [x] `pnpm --dir frontend test` (1850/1850 passing)
- [x] Manual: open SQL Editor, create unsaved tabs, sign out → user-scoped keys persist in DevTools Local Storage; sign back in same email → tabs and unsaved SQL restore.

+## Task 1: Remove cleanup from the Vue auth store

+**Files:**

+```ts

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>i18next/react-i18next (react-i18next)</summary>

### [`v17.0.7`](https://redirect.github.com/i18next/react-i18next/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#1707)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/i18next/react-i18next/compare/v17.0.6...v17.0.7)

- feat: `useTranslation([nsA, nsB, ...])` now passes its full namespace list to `getFixedT` via the new `scopeNs` opt (requires `i18next` ≥ v26.0.10). This makes selector calls with a secondary-namespace prefix resolve correctly under default `nsMode`: `t($ => $.nsB.foo)` previously missed silently because the bound `ns` was the primary string only and i18next's selector rewrite needed an array. Resolution semantics are unchanged — plain `t('key')` lookups still stay isolated to the primary namespace by default; use `nsMode: 'fallback'` to opt into multi-ns fallback resolution as before. Fixes [i18next#2429](https://redirect.github.com/i18next/i18next/issues/2429) for `useTranslation`-based callers.

### [`v17.0.6`](https://redirect.github.com/i18next/react-i18next/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#1706)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/i18next/react-i18next/compare/v17.0.5...v17.0.6)

- fix: restore the v17 `nodesToString` output format consumed by `i18next-cli`'s extractor while still rendering [1919](https://redirect.github.com/i18next/react-i18next/issues/1919) correctly
  - 17.0.5 fixed [1919](https://redirect.github.com/i18next/react-i18next/issues/1919) by changing what `nodesToString` produced, which inadvertently changed the extracted translation strings for keep-tags wrapping non-keep React elements
  - The fix now lives in the renderer: indexed `<N>` placeholders nested inside a keep-tag are scoped to that tag's own original React children (matching kept tags by name and positional occurrence at each level), so the translation string format produced by `nodesToString` is unchanged

### [`v17.0.5`](https://redirect.github.com/i18next/react-i18next/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#1705)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/i18next/react-i18next/compare/v17.0.4...v17.0.5)

- fix: `<Trans />` no longer breaks child rendering when a kept HTML node (`transKeepBasicHtmlNodesFor`) wraps a non-keep React element [191

title: feat(plan): audit plan spec add/remove/update mutations
body: ## Summary Records add/remove/update of plan specs as a structured `issue_comment` event so the diff surfaces in the issue activity feed. - New `IssueComment.event = planUpdate { from_specs, to_specs }` carrying a before/after snapshot of `Plan.Spec[]`. - Server emits the audit comment on every `UpdatePlan` that touches `specs` (best-effort: failure is logged, not fatal to the update). - React renderer (`IssueDetailCommentList`) shows per-spec rows: added / removed / modified-sheet (with "View Details" diff dialog) / changed-targets (with +added / -removed) / prior-backup toggle / generic-fallback. - Activity-feed icon differentiates: green Plus when all-added, red Trash when all-removed, Pencil otherwise. - `diffPlanSpecs` util compares two `Plan_Spec[]` using `@bufbuild/protobuf` `equals` on stripped clones; results are cached per event payload via `WeakMap` so the icon + body components don't redo the diff per render. - Shared spec accessors (`sheetNameOfSpec`, `targetsOfSpec`, `enablePriorBackupOfSpec`) centralized in `frontend/src/utils/v1/issue/plan.ts`. ## Test plan - [ ] `go test -v -count=1 ./backend/tests/ -run "^TestPlanUpdate"` - [ ] `go test -v -count=1 ./backend/tests/ -run "^TestPlanAuditCollision"` - [ ] `pnpm --dir frontend test -- --run diffPlanSpecs` - [ ] Manually: edit a plan's spec SQL → confirm activity row appears with chip + View Details diff - [ ] Manually: add / remove a spec → confirm Plus / Trash icon variants - [ ] Manually: toggle prior-backup → confirm "enabled / disabled prior backup" row

title: chore(deps): drop lestrrat-go/jwx, use go-jose in oidc test
body:
## Summary
- The oidc test (`backend/plugin/idp/oidc/oidc_test.go`) was the only consumer of `lestrrat-go/jwx/v3`. It used `jwk.Import` + `jwk.Set` to JWK-encode an RSA public key for the fake `/jwks` endpoint.
- Replaced with `go-jose/go-jose/v4`, which is already a direct dependency in this repo (`backend/plugin/idp/wif/`). `jose.JSONWebKey{Key, Use, Algorithm}` marshals to the same JWKS-compatible JSON.
- Removed `lestrrat-go/jwx/v3` from `go.mod`/`go.sum` along with its transitive deps.

## Why not bump to jwx/v4
Renovate proposed bumping jwx to v4 (#PR-jwx-v4 — separate branch). `jwx/v4@v4.0.2` directly imports `encoding/json/v2` and `encoding/json/jsontext`, both gated behind `//go:build goexperiment.jsonv2`. Adopting v4 would require setting `GOEXPERIMENT=jsonv2` in `backend-tests.yml`, `golangci-lint.yml`, and every dev shell — for a single test file. This change avoids that entirely.

## Test plan
- [x] `go test -count=1 ./backend/plugin/idp/oidc/` passes without `GOEXPERIMENT`
- [x] `golangci-lint run --allow-parallel-runners ./backend/plugin/idp/oidc/...` clean
- [x] `go build ./backend/bin/server/main.go` succeeds
- [x] `go mod tidy` produces no diff

- Replace `window.confirm` in delete-spec with `AlertDialog`; uses existing `bbkit.confirm-button.*` keys (added missing `cannot-undo` to all 5 React locales)
- Fix leave-confirm dialog: Cancel/Discard buttons no longer no-op. Refactored from deferred-`next()` (which fragile against async-save races) to an intent pattern — capture target, abort synchronously, re-issue on confirm. When `isEditing` flips false while a prompt is open (e.g. title save completed), auto-navigate to the captured target.
- Prevent in-page spec switch from bypassing the leave guard: dropped the optimistic local `selectedSpecId` update in `selectSpec`; URL is now the only driver. Parent's URL-sync effect split so a child-set `selectedSpecId` isn't snapped back to the URL value.
- "Add Change" on an already-created plan no longer creates an empty-statement spec on the backend. The new spec is held as a local draft (with a local sheet) and rendered as a tab; the first statement save commits the sheet and the spec together via `patchPlanStatement` (now appends when the spec isn't yet in `page.plan.specs`).
- Draft selection is tracked separately from `selectedSpecId` so the leave-confirm dialog overlays the draft instead of snapping the UI to the URL-bound spec while the user decides.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm --dir frontend type-check`
- [x] `pnpm --dir frontend test` (1845 tests, 195 files)
- [x] `pnpm --dir frontend check` (i18n + layering + locale sort)
- [x] Delete spec → AlertDialog confirms; Cancel/Delete both work
- [x] Edit statement → click nav link → leave dialog Cancel keeps you on page; Discard navigates
- [x] Edit statement → click another spec tab → same dialog flow; Discard navigates to target spec
- [x] Add Change → pick targets → confirm → no backend call yet; draft tab `*` auto-selects with editor in edit mode
- [x] Save SQL on draft → one `updatePlan` commits sheet + spec; URL updates to new spec
- [x] On draft → click another existing spec → leave dialog appears with draft still visible; Cancel keeps draft; Discard navigates to clicked spec; draft tab remains in strip until committed

### [`v11.0.9`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/blob/HEAD/pnpm/CHANGELOG.md#1109)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v11.0.8...v11.0.9)

##### Patch Changes

- Fixed installation of GitLab-hosted dependencies. pnpm now downloads the tarball from `https://gitlab.com/<user>/<project>/-/archive/<sha>/<project>-<sha>.tar.gz` instead of the GitLab API endpoint that contained an encoded slash (`%2F`) between user and project. The encoded slash both triggered `406 Not Acceptable` responses from GitLab and produced virtual store directory names that Node refused to import (`ERR_INVALID_MODULE_SPECIFIER`) [#​11533](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/11533).
- Honor `NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG` (and its lowercase `npm_config_userconfig` form) as a low-priority fallback when locating the user-level `.npmrc`. This restores compatibility with environments that point npm at a custom auth file via that env var — most notably `actions/setup-node`, which writes registry credentials to `${runner.temp}/.npmrc` and exports `NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG` to reference it. Without this, GitHub Actions workflows using `actions/setup-node` to authenticate to private registries broke after upgrading to pnpm v11. PNPM-prefixed env vars and `npmrcAuthFile` from the global `config.yaml` continue to take precedence [#​11539](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/11539).
- Fix `pnpm pack` not bundling dependencies listed in `bundleDependencies` (or `bundledDependencies`). The npm-packlist upgrade in pnpm 11 changed its API to require the caller to pre-populate the dependency tree, which the wrapper was not doing — `bundleDependencies` were silently dropped from the tarball [#​11519](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/11519).

body:
## Summary
- Add Oracle `OmniAST` wrapper plus `ParsePLSQLOmni`, `GetOmniNode`, and byte-offset position helper.
- Add focused tests for Oracle omni parsing, wrapper extraction, parse errors, and Unicode offset conversion.
- Upgrade `github.com/bytebase/omni` to `v0.0.0-20260509021101-01140a7b9722`.

## Test Plan
- [x] `go test ./backend/plugin/parser/plsql -count=1`
- [x] `golangci-lint run --fix --allow-parallel-runners`
- [x] `golangci-lint run --allow-parallel-runners`
- [x] `go build -ldflags "-w -s" -p=16 -o ./bytebase-build/bytebase ./backend/bin/server/main.go`

## Pre-PR Checklist
- Breaking change check: no API/schema/proto/config/UI workflow changes.
- Composite-PK query safety: skipped, no `backend/store` or migrator changes.
- SonarCloud properties: no update needed; new Go source and test files are under existing included patterns.

diff:
--- backend/plugin/parser/plsql/omni.go (+72/-0)
@@ -0,0 +1,72 @@
+package plsql
+
+import (
+	"unicode/utf8"
+
+	"github.com/bytebase/omni/oracle/ast"
+	oracleparser "github.com/bytebase/omni/oracle/parser"
+
+	storepb "github.com/bytebase/bytebase/backend/generated-go/store"
+	"github.com/bytebase/bytebase/backend/plugin/parser/base"
+)
+
+// OmniAST wraps an omni AST node and implements the base.AST interface.
+type OmniAST struct {
+	// Node is the omni AST node (e.g. *ast.SelectStmt, *ast.CreateTableStmt).
+	Node ast.Node
+	// Text is the original SQL text of this statement.
+	Text string
+	// StartPosition is the 1-based position where this statement starts.
+	StartPosition *storepb.Position
+}
+
+// ASTStartPosition implements base.AST.
+func (a *OmniAST) ASTStartPosition() *storepb.Position {
+	return a.StartPosition
+}
+
+// ParsePLSQLOmni parses SQL using omni's parser and returns an ast.List.
+// This is the recommended entry point for new Oracle code that needs omni AST nodes.
+func ParsePLSQLOmni(sql string) (*ast.List, error) {
+	return oracleparser.Parse(sql)
+}
+
+// GetOmniNode extracts the omni AST node from a base.AST interface.
+// Returns the node and true if it is an OmniAST, nil and false otherwise.
+func GetOmniNode(a base.AST) (ast.Node, bool) {
+	if a == nil {
+		return nil, false
+	}
+	omniAST, ok := a.(*OmniAST)
+	if !ok {
+		return nil, false
+	}
+	return omniAST.Node, true
+}
+
+// ByteOffsetToRunePosition converts a byte offset in sql to a 1-based line:column
+// where column is measured in Unicode code points (runes), matching storepb.Position semantics.
+func ByteOffsetToRunePosition(sql string, byteOffset int) *storepb.Position {
+	if byteOffset > len(sql) {
+		byteOffset = len(sql)
+	}
+
+	line := int32(1)
+	runeCol := int32(0) // 0-based rune count on current line
+	i := 0
+	for i < byteOffset {
+		r, size := utf8.DecodeRuneInString(sql[i:])
+		if r == '\n' {
+			line++
+			runeCol = 0
+		} else {
+			runeCol++
+		}
+		i += size
+	}
+
+	return &storepb.Position{
+		Line:   line,
+		Column: runeCol + 1, // convert to 1-based
+	}
+}
--- backend/plugin/parser/plsql/omni_test.go (+59/-0)
@@ -0,0 +1,59 @@
+package plsql
+
+import (
+	"testing"
+
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
+
+	"github.com/bytebase/omni/oracle/ast"
+
+	storepb "github.com/bytebase/bytebase/backend/generated-go/store"
+	"github.com/bytebase/bytebase/backend/plugin/parser/base"
+)
+
+func TestParsePLSQLOmni(t *testing.T) {
+	list, err := ParsePLSQLOmni("SELECT * FROM T; INSERT INTO T VALUES (1);")
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	require.NotNil(t, list)
+	require.Len(t, list.Items, 2)
+
+	first, ok := list.Items[0].(*ast.RawStmt)
+	require.True(t, ok)
+	require.IsType(t, &ast.SelectStmt{}, first.Stmt)
+
+	second, ok := list.Items[1].(*ast.RawStmt)
+	require.True(t, ok)
+	require.IsType(t, &ast.InsertStmt{}, second.Stmt)
+}
+
+func TestParsePLSQLOmniReturnsParseError(t *testing.T) {
+	_, err := ParsePLSQLOmni("SELECT * FROM")
+	require.Error(t, err)
+}
+
+func TestOracleOmniASTWrapper(t *testing.T) {
+	node := &ast.SelectStmt{}
+	start := &storepb.Position{Line: 2, Column: 3}
+	omniAST := &OmniAST{
+		Node:          node,
+		Text:          "SELECT 1 FROM DUAL",
+		StartPosition: start,
+	}
+
+	var parsed base.AST = omniAST
+	require.Equal(t, start, parsed.ASTStartPosition())
+
+	got, ok := GetOmniNode(parsed)
+	require.True(t, ok)
+	require.Same(t, node, got)
+
+	got, ok = GetOmniNode(nil)
+	require.False(t, ok)
+	require.Nil(t, got)
+}
+
+func TestOracleByteOffsetToRunePosition(t *testing.T) {
+	position := ByteOffsetToRunePosition("SELECT\n日本 FROM DUAL", len("SELECT\n日"))
+	require.Equal(t, int32(2), position.Line)
+	require.Equal(t, int32(2), position.Column)
+}

title: refactor(react): unify selection bar across my-issues, projects, instances, databases
body:
## Summary

Four pages currently have their own bespoke "N items selected → batch actions" bar — `ProjectsPage`, `DatabaseBatchOperationsBar` (used on Databases / Instance Detail / Project Databases), `InstancesPage`, and `IssueTable.BatchActionBar` (used on My Issues / Project Issue Dashboard). They were near-identical in shape but each had its own styling, layout quirks, and minor bugs.

This PR consolidates them onto a single shared `SelectionActionBar` component:

- New component: `frontend/src/react/components/SelectionActionBar.tsx`
- Floating pill at the viewport bottom-center (`fixed bottom-6 left-1/2 -translate-x-1/2`), layered via the shared `LAYER_SURFACE_CLASS` so it passes the layering scanner
- Tri-state checkbox for select-all-on-page / clear, count label, and a row of action buttons
- Declarative `actions: SelectionAction[]` API + a `children` slot for richer custom actions (e.g. `InstancesPage`'s split-dropdown Sync)
- Leading count cluster uses `shrink-0`; only the actions group scrolls horizontally on narrow viewports, so the count never disappears
- `tone: "destructive"` adds a red text/border override for delete-like actions

Migrated four batch bars onto it:

| Page | Behavior |
|---|---|
| ProjectsPage | Archive / Restore / Delete (Delete tone=destructive) |
| DatabaseBatchOperationsBar (3 callers) | up to 7 actions: Change DB / Export / Sync / Edit Labels / Edit Env / Transfer / Unassign |
| InstancesPage | Sync (split dropdown via `children` slot) / Edit Env / Assign License |
| IssueTable.BatchActionBar (2 callers) | Close / Reopen with disabled-reason tooltips |

## Notable changes outside the new component

- `DatabaseTable` gains an optional `onDatabasesChange(databases)` callback so its 3 page callers can compute "all selected on visible page" for the bar's checkbox. JSDoc notes the callback identity must be stable.
- `InstancesPage`'s `SyncDropdown` migrated from a hand-rolled `position: absolute` dropdown (which got clipped by the bar's overflow context) to the shared `DropdownMenu` primitive (BaseMenu, portals via `getLayerRoot("overlay")`).
- `instance.selected-n-instances` i18n call corrected from `{ n }` to `{ count }` to match the React locale's `_one`/`_other` plural shape (the old call rendered the literal key).
- Sheet/dialog modals in the migrated pages moved to the end of their JSX for clarity (they portal, so this is layout-neutral).
- Stale `bg-blue-100` strip pattern removed from all four batch-bar implementations.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm --dir frontend test` — 1847 passing, including 8 new tests for `SelectionActionBar` (count=0 short-circuit, hidden/disabled actions, click handlers, checkbox toggle, destructive tone class, custom children, disabledReason wrapping)
- [x] `pnpm --dir frontend type-check` — clean
- [x] `pnpm --dir frontend check` — ESLint, Biome, React i18n consistency, layering scanner, locale sorter all pass
- [ ] Manual smoke on each consumer pag

### [`v9.0.0`](https://redirect.github.com/actions/github-script/releases/tag/v9.0.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/actions/github-script/compare/v8.0.0...v9.0.0)

**New features:**

- **`getOctokit` factory function** — Available directly in the script context. Create additional authenticated Octokit clients with different tokens for multi-token workflows, GitHub App tokens, and cross-org access. See [Creating additional clients with `getOctokit`](https://redirect.github.com/actions/github-script#creating-additional-clients-with-getoctokit) for details and examples.
- **Orchestration ID in user-agent** — The `ACTIONS_ORCHESTRATION_ID` environment variable is automatically appended to the user-agent string for request tracing.

**Breaking changes:**

- **`require('@​actions/github')` no longer works in scripts.** The upgrade to `@actions/github` v9 (ESM-only) means `require('@​actions/github')` will fail at runtime. If you previously used patterns like `const { getOctokit } = require('@​actions/github')` to create secondary clients, use the new injected `getOctokit` function instead — it's available directly in the script context with no imports needed.
- `getOctokit` is now an injected function parameter. Scripts that declare `const getOctokit = ...` or `let getOctokit = ...` will get a `SyntaxError` because JavaScript does not allow `const`/`let` redeclaration of function parameters. Use the injected `getOctokit` directly, or use `var getOctokit = ...` if you need to redeclare it.
- If your script accesses other `@actions/github` internals beyond the standard `github`/`octokit` client, you may need to update those references for v9 compatibility.

##### What's Changed

- Add ACTIONS\_ORCHESTRATION\_ID to user-agent string by [@​Copilot](https://redirect.github.com/Copilot) in [#​695](https://redirect.github.com/actions/github-script/pull/695)
- ci: use deployment: false for integration test environments by [@​salmanmkc](https://redirect.github.com/salmanmkc) in [#​712](https://redirect.github.com/actions/github-script/pull/712)
- feat!: add getOctokit to script context, upgrade [@​actions/github](https://redirect.github.com/actions/github) v9, [@​octokit/core](https://redirect.github.com/octokit/core) v7, and related packages by [@​salmanmkc](https://redirect.github.co

title: fix(role-grant): permission-aware DDL/DML environment warnings (BYT-9390)
body: ## Summary Replaces the muted/blue messaging on four role-grant surfaces with a permission-aware yellow warning that frames the risk as *"selecting an environment lets the grantee run DDL/DML directly in SQL Editor without approval."* **Surfaces touched** - Admin grant drawer (`MembersPage`) - Developer request drawer (`RequestRoleSheet`) - Approver issue page (`IssueDetailRoleGrantDetails`) — adds new Environments row - Member-list current-binding banner — extracted to `MemberBindingEnvironmentBanner` for testability **Architecture** - Boolean `roleHasEnvironmentLimitation` → permission-aware `getRoleEnvironmentLimitationKind` returning `"DDL" | "DML" | "DDL/DML" | undefined`. Bit-identical gate, more informative. - New shared `DDLWarningCallout` component with discriminated-union props for 4 variants: `drawer`, `binding-some`, `binding-all`, `binding-none`. The first three render yellow `Alert variant="warning"`; `binding-none` (DDL/DML gated, benign state) renders blue `Alert variant="info"`. - Layout pattern across surfaces: section label → warning callout → input/content (matches the JIT-issue page). **i18n** - 4 new keys under `project.members.*` × 5 React locales (en/zh/ja/es/vi). - 3 old keys removed (`allow-ddl`, `allow-ddl-all-environments`, `disallow-ddl-all-environments`); `allow-ddl` also removed from 5 Vue locales. - Locale-format guard test pins `{{kind}}` placeholder presence across all 5 locales. **Tests** - 1800 tests pass (187 files). New tests: helper unit (5), `DDLWarningCallout` (5 + type-check assertions), `MemberBindingEnvironmentBanner` (3), `IssueDetailRoleGrantDetails` (5 incl. stale-state regression), locale guard (20). - `pnpm fix && pnpm check && pnpm type-check && pnpm test` all clean. ## Test plan - [ ] Manual smoke test (per plan §10.4): 13 scenarios across 4 surfaces × 5 locales × role variations (DDL/DML, DDL-only, DML-only, query-only). Requires running dev server. - [ ] Verify the issue page warning sits inside the Environments section and reads "DDL/DML statements can be directly run in SQL Editor in the listed environments without approval." - [ ] Verify the member-list `binding-none` card uses the blue info box with "DDL/DML statements require approval before running in SQL Editor." - [ ] Verify the admin grant drawer warning appears between the Environments label and the multiselect. - [ ] Verify locale switching renders translated copy for all 5 locales with correct `{{kind}}` interpolation. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ## Screenshots - Issue page - Request role drawer - Grant role drawer

Check the [Dependency Dashboard](../issues/2527) for more information. --- ### Release Notes
pnpm/pnpm (pnpm) ### [`v10.33.4`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v10.33.4): pnpm 10.33.4 [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v10.33.3...v10.33.4) #### Patch Changes - Pin the integrity of git-hosted tarballs (codeload.github.com, gitlab.com, bitbucket.org) in the lockfile so that subsequent installs detect a tampered or substituted tarball and refuse to install it. Previously the lockfile only stored the tarball URL for git dependencies, so a compromised git host or a man-in-the-middle could serve arbitrary code on later installs without lockfile changes. A new `gitHosted: true` field is recorded on git-hosted tarball resolutions in the lockfile, letting every reader/writer route them by a single typed check instead of pattern-matching the tarball URL in each call site. Lockfiles written by older pnpm versions are enriched on load (URL fallback) so the field can be relied on uniformly across the codebase. - Fix a regression where `pnpm --recursive --filter '!' run/exec/test/add` would include the workspace root in the matched projects. The workspace root is now correctly excluded by default when only negative `--filter` arguments are provided, matching the [documented behavior](https://pnpm.io/cli/recursive). To include the root, pass `--include-workspace-root` [#​11341](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/11341). #### Platinum Sponsors
#### Gold Sponsors

title: refactor(advisor/tidb): extract index-family spine + fix TEXT regression on INDEX_TYPE_NO_BLOB (batch 8 follow-up)
body:
## Summary

Two follow-up fixes to PR #20229 (batch 8 omni migration), merged before review feedback could land. Both commits standalone.

### Commit 1 — Sonar duplication fix (extraction)

PR #20229 was flagged at **36.6% duplicated lines on new code** (51% on `advisor_index_primary_key_type_allowlist.go`, 31.1% on `advisor_index_type_no_blob.go`). The flagged duplication was the CREATE TABLE column/constraint loop + ALTER TABLE command-arm dispatch, repeated 3 times across the index family (batch-2's `advisor_index_pk_type` + batch-8's blob/allowlist).

Extracts two helpers in `utils.go`:
- `collectIndexFamilyCreateTable` — walks `CreateTableStmt.Columns`/`Constraints`.
- `collectIndexFamilyAlterTable` — walks `AlterTableStmt.Commands`, dispatching `ATAddColumn` / `ATAddConstraint+ATAddIndex` / `ATChangeColumn+ATModifyColumn` and resolving `CHANGE COLUMN`'s old name.

Each advisor passes an `indexFamilyCallbacks` struct (`onColumn`, `onConstraint`, `onChangeColumn`); per-rule logic stays in callback bodies. Top-level type switch stays per-advisor (BLOB has `CreateIndexStmt`; the other two don't — asymmetric, kept in-file). Advice content + code stay per-advisor.

Side effect on batch-2 `advisor_index_pk_type.go`: case-arm coverage broadens from `case ATAddConstraint:` to `case ATAddConstraint, ATAddIndex:` (helper unifies). Empirically equivalent today per cumulative #17 — tidb omni does not emit `ATAddIndex`. Defensive against future grammar evolution.

Net: **-244 lines** of duplicated scaffolding across 3 advisors, **+115 lines** of helper. Spine exists once instead of three times.

### Commit 2 — TEXT-family regression fix (Codex P1)

Codex flagged a real false-negative on the omni migration: pingcap's `mysql.TypeBlob` enum value unified BLOB and TEXT (TEXT is BLOB with non-binary charset), so the pingcap-typed advisor flagged `CREATE TABLE t(c TEXT, INDEX(c(10)))` — rendering the type as `is blob` (accidentally accurate via type-enum unification). Omni gives TEXT its own `DataType.Name` ("TEXT", "TINYTEXT", etc.); the batch-8 mechanical port matched only the four BLOB names via `isBlobType`, **silently dropping TEXT-in-INDEX coverage**.

Cumulative #14 in the completion-plan table already documents the BLOB/TEXT split pattern — exactly the failure mode the table is meant to prevent. The plan doc now also has a dedicated cumulative #18 entry for this case and a step 2a (type-enum cross-reference) pre-batch invariant to catch the class going forward. Honest miss during the original shape audit.

**Empirical reproduction** on the merged batch-8 code:
```
CREATE TABLE t(c TEXT, INDEX(c(10)))   →   no advice (regression)
```

Fix: extend `isBlobType` to match BLOB AND TEXT families (8 names total). Pinned with three new fixture cases in `index_type_no_blob.yaml`:
- `CREATE TABLE t(c TEXT, INDEX(c(10)))` (single TEXT)
- TINYTEXT/MEDIUMTEXT/LONGTEXT in INDEX (cardinality + breadth across the TEXT family)

title: fix(plsql): trailing ';' leak with hidden tokens (BYT-9367)
body:
## Summary

- **Bug:** Oracle SQL splitter leaked a trailing `;` into the next statement's text/range when hidden-channel tokens (whitespace, comments) separated the statement's parse-tree stop from the `;`. Issue execution emitted `ORA-00900: invalid SQL statement at position: 1` for inputs like `INSERT(...) ;\n\nINSERT(...) ;`.
- **Fix:** Replaced the single-token `;` lookahead in `plsql.SplitSQL` with a channel-aware loop that walks past hidden tokens to find a trailing `;`, and bails on the first default-channel non-`;` token. Also corrected a latent 1-byte off-by-one in `byteOffsetStart` bookkeeping (visible as 1-byte/1-column shifts in 4 existing fixtures, text unchanged).
- **Parallel-path fix:** `plsql.ParsePLSQL` (used by `base.ParseStatements` for AST classification) had the same single-token bug, surfacing as `STATEMENT_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED` even when `Statement.Text` was clean. Mirrored the fix and extracted a shared `consumeTrailingSemicolon` helper used by both call sites.
- **Trino audit:** ruled out — `TrinoParser.g4`'s `singleStatement` rule requires `;` in the parse tree, so the leak shape can't occur. See spec §7.

## Files

- `backend/plugin/parser/plsql/split.go` — channel-aware loop + UTF-8-safe byte-offset bookkeeping; helper extraction.
- `backend/plugin/parser/plsql/plsql.go` — mirror the loop in `ParsePLSQL`.
- `backend/plugin/parser/plsql/test-data/test_split.yaml` — 5 new fixtures (cells b/c/d/f/h of the design table) + 4 mechanical 1-byte/1-column shifts in existing fixtures (text unchanged).
- `backend/plugin/parser/plsql/test-data/test_statement_type.yaml` — 3 new BYT-9367 entries (cells b/c/d) for AST-classification regression.
- `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-07-oracle-splitter-trailing-semicolon-leak-design.md` — design (v4, reviewed through 4 iterations).
- `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-05-07-oracle-splitter-trailing-semicolon-leak.md` — implementation plan.

## Test plan

- [x] `go test -count=1 ./backend/plugin/parser/plsql/` — all subtests pass (15 existing + 5 new splitter, 11 existing + 3 new statement-type).
- [x] `go test -count=1 ./backend/plugin/parser/...` — all 22 parser packages pass.
- [x] `go test -count=1 ./backend/...` — full backend suite green except for 5 pre-existing environmental flakes (mongosh missing, mssql/tidb testcontainer connection refused, accounts.google.com network timeout, postgres LEFT() UTF-8 upstream bug already patched locally) — none related to this change.
- [x] Empirically verified regression coverage: reverting the helper call in `plsql.go` makes `TestGetStatementType` fail with `[INSERT, UNSPECIFIED]` vs expected `[INSERT]` — the YAML test catches the AST-classification bug.
- [x] `golangci-lint run --allow-parallel-runners ./backend/plugin/parser/plsql/...` — 0 issues.
- [x] `go build -ldflags "-w -s" -p=16 -o ./bytebase-build/bytebase ./backend/bin/server/main.go` — clean.

## Review trail

Spec reviewed through 4 iterations (4 reviewers per pass) before implementation. Im

+func consumeTrailingSemicolon(allTokens []antlr.Token, stopIdx int) int {

+			return nextIdx
+		}
+		if next.GetChannel() == antlr.TokenDefaultChannel {

+		}
+	}

title: refactor(advisor/tidb): migrate index_type_no_blob + index_primary_key_type_allowlist to omni AST (Phase 1.5 §1.5.3 batch 8)
body:
## Summary

Migrates the last two pingcap-AST consumers of `tableNewColumn` / `columnNameToColumnDef` from `utils.go`, then deletes those helpers. **Closes BYT-9395**, completing the index-family advisor migration on tidb omni (alongside `index_pk_type` from batch 2).

- `advisor_index_type_no_blob.go` → omni AST (Recipe A)
- `advisor_index_primary_key_type_allowlist.go` → omni AST (Recipe A)
- `utils.go`: drop `tableNewColumn` / `columnNameToColumnDef` types and methods; add `omniDataTypeNameCompact` helper.

Coupled-by-shared-helper rationale: shipping the two together removes the partial-migration state that BYT-9395 was tracking. Doing one without the other leaves the same dead-code condition in `utils.go`.

## Empirical finding (drives a new fixture pin)

Before locking case-arms, parsed every `ALTER TABLE ADD …` syntactic form through `ParseTiDBOmni` and inspected the resulting `cmd.Type`. Findings:

| Form | `cmd.Type` |
|---|---|
| `ADD PRIMARY KEY (col)` (bare) | `ATAddConstraint` |
| `ADD CONSTRAINT pk PRIMARY KEY (col)` | `ATAddConstraint` |
| `ADD INDEX (col)` / `ADD KEY (col)` | `ATAddConstraint` |
| `ADD CONSTRAINT idx INDEX (col)` | `ATAddConstraint` |
| `ADD UNIQUE / UNIQUE KEY / UNIQUE INDEX (col)` | `ATAddConstraint` |
| `ADD CONSTRAINT uq UNIQUE (col)` | `ATAddConstraint` |
| `ADD FULLTEXT INDEX (col)` | `ATAddConstraint` |
| `ADD SPATIAL INDEX (col)` | `ATAddConstraint` |
| `ADD FOREIGN KEY (a) REFERENCES p(b)` | `ATAddConstraint` |
| `ADD CONSTRAINT fk FOREIGN KEY ...` | `ATAddConstraint` |

**`ATAddIndex` is never emitted by current tidb omni for any of these forms.** Cumulative #8's mysql claim that bare-keyword forms split to `ATAddIndex` does not apply to tidb omni today. Sibling parity is preserved with `case ATAddConstraint, ATAddIndex:` (cost-free, future-proof, matches what other tidb advisors do).

Important consequence: **batch-2's `advisor_index_pk_type.go:139` (`case ATAddConstraint:`-only) is empirically correct — no latent miss.** This PR pins that contract retroactively in `index_pk_type_limit.yaml` with a named-CONSTRAINT fixture.

## Recipe + reuse

- Both advisors use Recipe A — top-level type-switch on `*ast.CreateTableStmt` / `*ast.AlterTableStmt` (and `*ast.CreateIndexStmt` for BLOB). Pingcap visitors returned `(in, false)` from Enter (no descent), so this is a structural mirror.
- Reuses `tableNewOmniColumn` + `pkData` from `advisor_index_pk_type.go` (batch 2).
- New `omniDataTypeNameCompact` (= `strings.ToLower(dt.Name)`) lives in `utils.go`. Mirrors mysql analog of the same name. Distinct from `formatColumnType` in `advisor_index_pk_type.go` — that one uppercases `INT`/`BIGINT` for the allowlist comparison; this one is strictly lowercase to match pingcap's `tidbparser.TypeString` rendering and mysql's lowercase-rendered fixtures.

## Behavior preserved (NOT changed during migration)

These are intentional migration-scope boundaries — any alignment with the mysql analog is a separate behavior change to

+// RetryIssueApproval re-runs approval-template finding for an issue stuck
+// in CHECKING. The synchronous post-create path in `postCreateIssue`
+// swallows errors (e.g. CEL evaluation failure against a malformed
+// workspace approval rule), and there is no event-driven retry for
+// non-DATABASE_CHANGE issue types — once stuck, only this RPC (or a
+// direct DB edit) gets the issue back into a resolved state.
+//
+// Authorization mirrors `RequestIssue`: only the issue creator may
+// retry. The action is a self-service for "my issue is stuck"; an
+// operator who needs to unstick someone else's issue should fix the
+// underlying workspace approval rule and (if necessary) ask the issue
+// creator to click Retry.
+//
+// Idempotent: returns the existing issue unchanged when approval-finding
+// has already completed.
+func (s *IssueService) RetryIssueApproval(ctx context.Context, req *connect.Request[v1pb.RetryIssueApprovalRequest]) (*connect.Response[v1pb.Issue], error) {
+	issue, err := s.getIssueMessage(ctx, req.Msg.Name)
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, err
+	}
+
+	user, ok := GetUserFromContext(ctx)
+	if !ok {
+		return nil, connect.NewError(connect.CodeInternal, errors.New("user not found"))
+	}
+	if !canRequestIssue(issue.CreatorEmail, user) {
+		return nil, connect.NewError(connect.CodePermissionDenied, errors.New("only the issue creator can retry approval finding"))
+	}
+
+	// No-op fast path: nothing to retry if the previous attempt completed.
+	if issue.Payload.GetApproval().GetApprovalFindingDone() {
+		issueV1, err := s.convertToIssue(issue)
+		if err != nil {
+			return nil, connect.NewError(connect.CodeInternal, errors.Wrapf(err, "failed to convert to issue"))
+		}
+		return connect.NewResponse(issueV1), nil
+	}
+
+	if err := approval.FindAndApplyApprovalTemplate(ctx, s.store, s.webhookManager, s.licenseService, issue); err != nil {
+		// Surface the underlying cause (e.g. CEL error in the workspace
+		// approval rule) so the operator can fix it.
+		return nil, connect.NewError(connect.CodeFailedPrecondition, errors.Wrap(err, "approval finding still failing"))
+	}
+
+	uid := issue.UID
+	refreshed, err := s.store.GetIssue(ctx, &store.FindIssueMessage{
+		Workspace:  common.GetWorkspaceIDFromContext(ctx),
+		ProjectIDs: []string{issue.ProjectID},
+		UID:        &uid,
+	})
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, connect.NewError(connect.CodeInternal, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to refresh issue"))
+	}
+	if refreshed == nil {
+		return nil, connect.NewError(connect.CodeNotFound, errors.New("issue not found after retry"))
+	}
+
+	// Mirror the post-approval side effects that `postCreateIssue` and the
+	// approval runner perform when finding completes — without these, an
+	// auto-approved (template-less / SKIPPED) retry result would leave the
+	// issue out of CHECKING but skip the actual work:
+	//   * ACCESS_GRANT / ROLE_GRANT → activate the grant via
+	//     `completeAccessRequestIssue`.
+	//   * DATABASE_CHANGE with a plan → enqueue rollout creation.
+	approved, err := utils.CheckIssueApproved(refreshed)
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, connect.NewError(connect.CodeInternal, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to check approval state"))
+	}
+	if approved {
+		switch refreshed.Type {
+		case storepb.Issue_ACCESS_GRANT, storepb.Issue_ROLE_GRANT:
+			if completed, completeErr := completeAccessRequestIssue(ctx, s.store, user.Email, refreshed); completeErr != nil {
+				slog.Warn("failed to complete access request issue after retry", log.BBError(completeErr))
+			} else {
+				refreshed = completed
+			}
+		case storepb.Issue_DATABASE_CHANGE:
+			if refreshed.PlanUID != nil {
+				s.bus.RolloutCreationChan <- bus.PlanRef{ProjectID: refreshed.ProjectID, PlanID: *refreshed.PlanUID}
+			}
+		default:
+			// DATABASE_EXPORT auto-approve has no follow-up step.
+		}
+	}
+
+	issueV1, err := s.convertToIssue(refreshed)
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, connect.NewError(connect.CodeInternal, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to convert to issue"))
+	}
+	return connect.NewResponse(issueV1), nil
+}

body:
## Summary

Phase 1.5 §1.5.3 batch 7 of the TiDB advisor migration to omni AST. Two-advisor cleanup-pair batch closing two long-standing Linear tickets.

**Migration progress: 26 of 51 advisors on omni AST.**

## Migrated advisors (Recipe A, both)

| File | Cardinality | Closes |
|---|---|---|
| `advisor_column_set_default_for_not_null.go` | per-column (build list, append after switch) | **BYT-9362** (delete `canNull`) |
| `advisor_column_disallow_set_charset.go` | per-statement (single advice, first-violation-wins via break) | **BYT-9412** (delete `getColumnCharset`) |

## Pre-batch protocol applied

Per recent session lessons (batches 5 + 6 round-1/2/3):

1. **Read both pingcap visitor bodies BEFORE locking Recipe choice** — both confirmed Recipe A. EXPLAIN-DDL doesn't parse in either grammar (verified empirically in batch 6); the matched stmt types can't nest themselves; no wrapper risk.

2. **Counted appends for cardinality contract** —
   - `set_default_for_not_null`: builds `notNullColumnWithNoDefault` list during visitor, appends one advice per list entry after the switch → **per-column cardinality**, preserved.
   - `column_disallow_set_charset`: sets `code` flag, breaks inner column loop on first violation, breaks outer specs loop on first violating spec, single append after switch → **per-statement cardinality with first-wins semantics**, preserved.

3. **Audited omni's case-arm splits for ALTER TABLE** — `ATAddColumn` / `ATChangeColumn` / `ATModifyColumn`. Mirrored pingcap's coverage exactly. No `ATConvertCharset` concern here (column-level only, not table-level).

## NEW helper: `omniNeedDefault`

Added to `utils.go` as the omni-typed sibling of pingcap's `needDefault`. Required because `needDefault` has TWO consumers and only one (`set_default_for_not_null`) migrates in this batch — the other (`column_require_default`) stays pingcap-typed until a future batch.

**Empirically verified** for omni's column type representation:
- BLOB family: `BLOB`, `TINYBLOB`, `MEDIUMBLOB`, `LONGBLOB` → no default needed
- TEXT family: `TEXT`, `TINYTEXT`, `MEDIUMTEXT`, `LONGTEXT` → no default needed (separate from BLOB in omni; pingcap unified under TypeBlob)
- JSON, geometry types → no default needed
- `AutoIncrement` direct bool field, `Generated *GeneratedColumn` direct field, `Constraints[].Type == ColConstrPrimaryKey` for inline PK

## Cumulative table touchpoint (no new entry)

This batch hits the column-AST shape territory mapped in batch 6 (cumulative #14). The `omniColumnCharset` accessor added in batch 6 is reused by `column_disallow_set_charset` exactly as predicted — the reuse hypothesis held empirically (verified by reading the pingcap visitor body first; it reads `column.Tp.GetCharset()` which omni exposes via `TypeName.Charset`, exactly what the accessor abstracts).

The TEXT-vs-BLOB split in omni's TypeName.Name (vs pingcap's unified TypeBlob enum) is an interesting sub-divergence that didn't show up in batch 6's audit because batch 6's

body:
## Summary

Phase 1.5 §1.5.3 batch 6 of the TiDB advisor migration to omni AST.
Migrates the 4-advisor charset/collation/comment family — recovery-rhythm batch after batch 5's churn (CollateExpr + EXPLAIN-wrapped-DML rounds).

**Migration progress: 24 of 51 advisors on omni AST.**

## Migrated advisors

| File | Recipe | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `advisor_charset_allowlist.go` | A | CREATE/ALTER on Database + Table; column-level via `TypeName.Charset` |
| `advisor_collation_allowlist.go` | A | Same shape; column-level via `TypeName.Collate` (NOT in Constraints[]) |
| `advisor_table_comment_convention.go` | A | Single `*ast.CreateTableStmt` match |
| `advisor_column_comment_convention.go` | A | CREATE/ALTER TABLE; comment value in `ColumnDef.Comment` direct field |

## Recipe choice — empirically verified, not name-pattern-matched

Per Vincent's hard pre-flight gate after batch 5's Recipe-A miss on EXPLAIN-wrapped DML, every advisor's pingcap Visitor body was read first. All 4 return `(in, false)` (continue recursion), which by the heuristic would suggest Recipe B. **But empirically:**

- `EXPLAIN CREATE TABLE …`, `TRACE CREATE TABLE …` etc. fail to parse in BOTH pingcap and omni grammars (TiDB's `EXPLAIN` is for SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/REPLACE — not DDL).
- The matched stmt types (CreateDatabase, CreateTable, AlterDatabase, AlterTable) cannot nest themselves.
- No wrapper exists that embeds them.

So Recipe A is safe for all 4. The `(in, false)` recursion in pingcap was load-bearing only when something nested matched — for these advisors there was nothing to find.

## Shape audit findings — NEW cumulative shape divergence #14

TiDB option representation simplification: omni replaces pingcap's enum-tagged option model with a string-named simpler form. Multiple sub-divergences caught empirically:

| Aspect | Pingcap | Omni |
|---|---|---|
| TableOption | `{Tp: TableOptionCharset, StrValue: "..."}` | `{Name: "CHARACTER SET" \| "CHARSET", Value: "..."}` |
| DatabaseOption | `{Tp: DatabaseOptionCharset, Value: "..."}` | `{Name: "CHARACTER SET" \| "CHARSET", Value: "..."}` |
| Keyword shorthand | Canonicalized at enum level (`CHARSET` and `CHARACTER SET` both → TableOptionCharset) | **NOT canonicalized** — Name preserves user's keyword form. **Critical wrinkle:** mechanical migration matching only `"CHARACTER SET"` silently misses the shorthand. Existing test fixtures that use `CHARSET` form would have failed had I not caught this. |
| Column-level CHARSET | `column.Tp.GetCharset()` (method on FieldType) | `column.TypeName.Charset` (direct string) |
| Column-level COLLATE | `column.Options[ColumnOptionCollate].StrValue` | `column.TypeName.Collate` (direct string, NOT in Constraints[]) |
| Column-level COMMENT | `column.Options[ColumnOptionComment].Expr` (needs restoreNode) | `column.Comment` (direct string) + `Constraints[]` has `ColConstrComment` marker for "clause was written" signal |

title: refactor(advisor/tidb): migrate WHERE-required pair + leading-wildcard LIKE to omni AST (Phase 1.5 §1.5.3 batch 5)
body:
## Summary

Phase 1.5 §1.5.3 batch 5 of the TiDB advisor migration to omni AST. Migrates the WHERE-required pair plus the first Recipe B (sub-walk) advisor in a single PR for family coherence — all 3 are WHERE-clause-related rules.

**Migration progress: 20 of 51 advisors on omni AST.**

This is the **first batch with Recipe B** in the migration. Per Phase 1.5 calibration framing, reviewer attention to the Visitor implementation is warranted.

## Migrated advisors

| File | Recipe | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `advisor_stmt_where_required_for_select.go` | **B** | Walks into sub-selects; existing fixture proves this is required (see Recipe choice below) |
| `advisor_stmt_where_required_for_update_delete.go` | A | No nested UPDATE/DELETE possible in standard SQL |
| `advisor_stmt_no_leading_wildcard_like.go` | **B** | Walks WHERE expressions for `*ast.LikeExpr` at any depth |

## Recipe-A vs B determined empirically (NOT by name pattern)

Per pre-batch protocol, read each pingcap-typed Visitor body before locking the recipe choice.

**`where_required_for_select` is Recipe B, not A.** The pingcap Visitor returns `(in, false)` (continue recursion). Existing fixture proves this is required:

```yaml
- statement: SELECT id FROM tech_book WHERE id > (SELECT max(id) FROM tech_book)
  changeType: 1
  want:
    - status: 2
      content: '"SELECT id FROM tech_book WHERE id > (SELECT max(id) FROM tech_book)" requires WHERE clause'
```

The OUTER has a WHERE; the trigger comes from the INNER subquery. A naive Recipe A migration (top-level type-switch) would silently regress on this fixture — same shape of bug as batch 3's `no_select_all` round-1 fix (cumulative table item #5).

**`where_required_for_update_delete` is Recipe A.** Standard SQL doesn't allow nested UPDATE/DELETE. Subqueries inside are SELECTs (handled by the SELECT advisor).

**`no_leading_wildcard_like` is Recipe B.** Walks WHERE expressions to find `*ast.LikeExpr` nodes at any nesting depth.

## Recipe B failure-mode checklist (per plan §1.5.0)

| # | Item | `where_required_for_select` | `no_leading_wildcard_like` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `Visit(node) Visitor` signature (NOT pingcap's `Enter` returning `(Node, bool)`) | ✓ | ✓ |
| 2 | `Visit(nil)` post-order signal handled | ✓ `if node == nil { return nil }` | ✓ same |
| 3 | No built-in pre/post framing — depth tracking manual | N/A — no per-subtree state | N/A |
| 4 | Returning `nil` to skip subtree | Returns `v` always (full walk; no benefit to skipping) | Optimization: `if v.found { return nil }` after first hit |
| 5 | Mutable state across recursion | None | `found` flag — instantiated **fresh per top-level statement** in outer loop, not reused across statements (matches pingcap's `checker.leadingWildcardLike = false` reset) |

## Shape audit findings — NEW cumulative shape divergence #10

| Advisor / batch | Pingcap shape | Omni shape | Class |
|---|---|---|---|
| `where_required_for_select` (batch 5) | `node.From != nil` (`*TableRefsClause`

## Summary

Phase 1.5 §1.5.3 batch 4 of the TiDB advisor migration to omni AST.
Migrates 3 naming-convention advisors via Recipe A (top-level type-switch).

**Migration progress: 17 of 51 advisors on omni AST.**

## Migrated advisors

| File | Recipe | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `advisor_naming_index_convention.go` | A | Mirrors mysql `case ATAddConstraint, ATAddIndex` to cover both ALTER syntactic forms |
| `advisor_naming_unique_key_convention.go` | A | Single `ConstrUnique` arm covers pingcap's 3-way Uniq/UniqKey/UniqIndex split |
| `advisor_naming_foreign_key_convention.go` | A | Uses `constraint.RefTable` / `constraint.RefColumns` (omni flat fields) |

## Pre-batch checklist

### Coupling scan

Cross-file helpers in the trio:

| Helper | Definition site (before) | Consumers | Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `getTemplateRegexp` | `advisor_naming_index_convention.go:244` | all 3 trio files | Moved to `utils.go` |
| `indexMetaData` (struct) | `advisor_naming_index_convention.go:132` | all 3 trio files | Moved to `utils.go` |

Both helpers are AST-agnostic Go (no pingcap types). Clean move — no Linear cleanup ticket needed (unlike `canNull`/BYT-9362 or `tableNewColumn`/BYT-9395, which stay pingcap-typed for un-migrated consumers).

### Shape audit findings (NEW divergence — proposed cumulative table item #8)

| Advisor / batch | Pingcap shape | Omni shape | Class |
|---|---|---|---|
| `naming_*_convention` (batch 4) | `ALTER TABLE ADD INDEX` and `ALTER TABLE ADD CONSTRAINT name INDEX` both produce `AlterTableAddConstraint` (single enum) | omni splits: `ATAddIndex` (no CONSTRAINT keyword) vs `ATAddConstraint` (with CONSTRAINT keyword) | Latent coverage gap if mechanically ported — `case ATAddConstraint` only would miss bare `ADD INDEX`. Mirrored mysql omni `case ATAddConstraint, ATAddIndex` to cover both. Same applies to UNIQUE forms. |

Existing cumulative table items consulted (from plan §1.5.0 invariant #7):
- **Item #2** (`ConstrUnique` unification): omni unifies pingcap's `ConstraintUniq`/`ConstraintUniqKey`/`ConstraintUniqIndex` under single `ConstrUnique`. UK advisor's switch becomes single arm; covers all 3 syntactic forms.

Spot-check on constraint-name handling per session-baseline review note: `constraint.Name` is the same field name in both pingcap and omni (verified at `omni/tidb/ast/parsenodes.go:459`). No divergence.

### Fixture pins

New fixtures pin the discovered divergences:

- `naming_index_idx.yaml`: `ALTER TABLE ... ADD CONSTRAINT name INDEX` (pass + violation pair) — pins `ATAddConstraint+ConstrIndex` path.
- `naming_index_uk.yaml`: `ALTER TABLE ... ADD UNIQUE INDEX` and `ADD UNIQUE KEY` (4 cases: 2 forms × pass+violation each) — pins `ATAddIndex+ConstrUnique` path AND the `ConstrUnique` unification on the ALTER side.

If omni regresses on either split, these fixtures fail loudly.

### Behavior preserved (NOT aligned with mysql)

`CREATE FULLTEXT INDEX` / `CREATE SPATIAL INDEX` continue to be checked by the index naming conventi

title: refactor(advisor/tidb): migrate 4 STATEMENT_DISALLOW_* rules to omni AST (Phase 1.5 §1.5.3 batch 3)
body:
## Summary

First Class IIa batch — advisors that consume both AST nodes AND the statement's source text for advice content. Four rules migrated:

| Rule | File | Recipe |
|---|---|---|
| `STATEMENT_DISALLOW_COMMIT` | `advisor_stmt_disallow_commit.go` | A — top-level type switch on `*ast.CommitStmt` |
| `STATEMENT_SELECT_NO_SELECT_ALL` | `advisor_stmt_no_select_all.go` | **B — `omniast.Walk`** (wildcard can appear in nested subqueries) |
| `STATEMENT_DISALLOW_ORDER_BY` | `advisor_stmt_disallow_order_by.go` | A — top-level switch on Update/Delete |
| `STATEMENT_DISALLOW_LIMIT` | `advisor_stmt_disallow_limit.go` | A — top-level switch on Update/Delete/Insert |

**Migration progress: 14 of 51 advisors on omni AST.**

Independent of PRs #20195 (batch 1) and #20198 (batch 2) — different files, parallel-mergeable.

## First Recipe B in the migration

`no_select_all` is the first advisor in this migration that genuinely required Recipe B. The existing yaml fixture exercises this with:

```sql
SELECT a, b FROM (SELECT * FROM t1 JOIN t2) t
```

The outer SELECT has no wildcard; the inner subquery does. A top-level type switch silently misses it (caught immediately by `TestTiDBRules`). Switched to `omniast.Walk` with a `Visit(node) Visitor` implementation — returning `v` to recurse, `nil` to skip subtrees, and ignoring the `Visit(nil)` post-order signal since this advisor has no post-order work.

## New shared helper: `OmniStmt.TrimmedText()`

Added to `utils.go`:

```go
func (s OmniStmt) TrimmedText() string {
    return strings.TrimSpace(s.Text)
}
```

Mirrors mysql omni's `TrimmedStmtText` pattern. Needed because multi-statement input passes leading newlines through `Statement.Text`; pingcap's `node.Text()` returned the trimmed form. Without this helper, advice content embeds raw newlines:

- Pre-fix: `Commit is not allowed, related statement: "\nCOMMIT;"`
- Post-fix: `Commit is not allowed, related statement: "COMMIT;"`

All 4 advisors in this batch use it.

## Notable API mappings

| Pingcap | Omni |
|---|---|
| `node.Order != nil` (UpdateStmt/DeleteStmt) | `len(node.OrderBy) > 0` |
| `node.Limit != nil` | `node.Limit != nil` (same shape) |
| `node.Select` (interface, can be `*SelectStmt` or `*SetOprStmt`) | `node.Select` (concrete `*SelectStmt`; UNION/INTERSECT/EXCEPT collapse to a single SelectStmt with a `SetOp` field) |
| `node.Fields.Fields[].WildCard != nil` | `*ast.StarExpr` in `TargetList[]` |
| `*ast.CommitStmt` | `*ast.CommitStmt` (same) |
| `node.Text()` (statement source text, trimmed by parser) | `ostmt.TrimmedText()` |

## Pre-batch checklist

1. **Coupling scan.** `useLimit` was local to `disallow_limit.go`; inlined as `insertUsesLimit` during migration. No cross-file coupling found.
2. **Shape audit.** Pingcap's `*ast.SetOprStmt` (a separate type for `SELECT ... UNION SELECT ...`) collapses to omni's `*SelectStmt` with a `SetOp` field — same kind of unification we saw in batch 2's ConstrUnique. The branch logic for `useLimit` simplifie

title: refactor(advisor/tidb): migrate 5 more rules to omni AST (Phase 1.5 §1.5.3 batch 2)
body:
## Summary

Class I batch following the recipe from PR #20140 (pilot) and PR #20195 (batch 1). Five TiDB SQL review rules migrated to omni AST.

| Rule | File | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `DATABASE_DROP_EMPTY_DATABASE` | `advisor_database_drop_empty_db.go` | Recipe A — DropDatabaseStmt |
| `TABLE_NO_FOREIGN_KEY` | `advisor_table_no_fk.go` | Recipe A — CreateTableStmt + AlterTableStmt with ATAddConstraint |
| `SCHEMA_BACKWARD_COMPATIBILITY` | `advisor_migration_compatibility.go` | Recipe A — `ostmt.Text` for advice content. Includes silent bug fix — see "Acknowledged behavior changes" below. |
| `TABLE_REQUIRE_PK` | `advisor_table_require_pk.go` | Recipe A — most complex of the batch; tracks PK state across multiple statement types. Includes silent panic-fix — see "Acknowledged behavior changes". |
| `INDEX_PK_TYPE_LIMIT` | `advisor_index_pk_type.go` | Recipe A — adds `formatColumnType` helper for fixture stability |

**Migration progress: 10 of 51 advisors on omni AST.**

Independent of PR #20195 (batch 1) — different files, separate parallel-mergeable.

## Acknowledged behavior changes

The migration is mostly mechanical, but the omni AST shape revealed two pre-existing bugs in the original pingcap-typed code. Both got fixed silently as a side-effect of structural translation. **Naming both explicitly** so future readers can find them via blame:

### `migration_compatibility.go` — `ConstraintUniqIndex` was missed

The original pingcap-typed code at lines 104-106 of `advisor_migration_compatibility.go` (pre-migration) was:

```go
if spec.Constraint.Tp == ast.ConstraintPrimaryKey ||
    spec.Constraint.Tp == ast.ConstraintUniq ||
    spec.Constraint.Tp == ast.ConstraintUniqKey {
    code = advisorcode.CompatibilityAddUniqueKey
    break
}
```

Pingcap had three unique constraint types: `ConstraintUniq`, `ConstraintUniqKey`, **and `ConstraintUniqIndex`**. The original code only checked the first two. So `ALTER TABLE t ADD UNIQUE INDEX idx (col)` previously emitted **no** compatibility advice — a missed case.

omni unifies all three under `ConstrUnique`. Post-migration `ADD UNIQUE INDEX` correctly routes through the unique-key advice path and gets flagged. This is a **silent bug fix** visible to customers: migrations that previously slipped past the compatibility check will now be flagged.

Code comment at the `ConstrUnique` branch acknowledges this explicitly.

### `advisor_table_require_pk.go` — `PRIMARY KEY ((expr))` no longer panics

The original `convertConstraintToKeySlice` did `key.Column.Name.String()` without nil-checking `key.Column`. For TiDB's `PRIMARY KEY ((expr))` functional-PK syntax, pingcap leaves `key.Column` nil and populates `key.Expr` instead, so the original would **panic with a nil-pointer dereference** on functional PKs.

The migrated `constraintPKColumns` returns an empty slice for expression PKs (graceful skip). The advisor reports no PK columns for the table — the conservative behavior given the advisor cannot inspect express

title: fix(sql-editor): export the original SQL, not the row-limit-rewritten one
body:
## Summary

The SQL Editor's single-result export drawer was sending the *already-rewritten* statement to the export endpoint, capping every export at the editor's Result Limit dropdown (default 1000) regardless of the value chosen in the export form.

When a query is run, the backend rewrites `SELECT * FROM t` into `SELECT * FROM t LIMIT 1000` and returns that string in `result.statement`. The export drawer then sent that rewritten string as the export payload along with the form's row count (e.g. 10000). The backend's LIMIT rewriter applies `min(existing, requested)`, so the existing `LIMIT 1000` stuck and the ZIP came back with at most 1000 rows.

The fix sends `params.statement` (the original user SQL) — matching what the multi-result "export all" path in `ResultViewV1.vue:114` and the React `BatchQuerySelect.tsx:222` already do. Backend semantics are unchanged: any `LIMIT` the user actually typed is still honored via `min(user, requested)`.

This is a long-standing defect — same symptom as the closed [issue #13534](https://github.com/bytebase/bytebase/issues/13534) (reported on 2.22.2, closed 2024-08).

## Reproduction (verified locally on `main`)

Seeded a 5000-row Postgres table, then exercised `SQLService.Export` directly:

| Statement sent | Form `limit` | Result before fix |
|---|---|---|
| `SELECT * FROM export_repro LIMIT 1000` *(what the editor was sending)* | 10000 | ZIP `.sql` shows `LIMIT 1000`, CSV has 1000 rows |
| `SELECT * FROM export_repro` *(what the editor sends after this fix)* | 10000 | ZIP `.sql` shows `LIMIT 10000`, CSV has 5000 rows |
| `SELECT * FROM export_repro LIMIT 5` *(user-written LIMIT)* | 10000 | ZIP `.sql` shows `LIMIT 5`, CSV has 5 rows |

Third row confirms the backend's `min(user-written, requested)` semantics still apply correctly when the original statement is forwarded.

## Test plan
- [ ] In the SQL Editor, run a query that returns more than 1000 rows against a Postgres database.
- [ ] Open the export drawer, set Export rows to 10000, format CSV, click Confirm.
- [ ] Open the downloaded ZIP — `.sql` file shows `LIMIT 10000` (or no LIMIT if the engine doesn't auto-rewrite), CSV contains all expected rows.
- [ ] Repeat with the SQL itself containing `LIMIT 5` — exported file should still cap at 5 rows.

-                  statement: result.statement,

body:
## Summary

First Class I advisor batch in Phase 1.5. Migrates three TiDB SQL review rules from the legacy pingcap parser to omni AST, following the pilot recipe established in PR #20140.

| Rule | Class | Approach |
|---|---|---|
| `NAMING_TABLE` (`advisor_naming_table.go`) | I | Recipe A — top-level type switch on CreateTableStmt / AlterTableStmt / RenameTableStmt |
| `NAMING_COLUMN` (`advisor_naming_column.go`) | I | Recipe A — same set of types, plus per-column iteration |
| `TABLE_DROP_NAMING_CONVENTION` (`advisor_table_drop_naming_convention.go`) | I | Recipe A — top-level switch on DropTableStmt |

**Migration progress:** 5 of 51 advisors on omni AST (2 from §1.5.1 pilot + 3 from this batch).

## Pre-batch checklist

Per plan §1.5.0, mandatory steps:

1. **Coupling scan.** No unexported helpers shared cross-file in this batch beyond `getTiDBOmniNodes` (already in utils.go). One unrelated coupling — `getTemplateRegexp` shared between index/unique/foreign-key naming rules — was identified but those rules are NOT in this batch (they're Class IIa due to `in.Text()` usage in their internal-error path; queued for batch 2).
2. **Shape audit.** Compared each migration against the analogous `mysql/rule_*.go` omni rule. Branch structure matches one-to-one — no pingcap-vs-omni desugaring divergence found in this batch.
3. **Yaml fixture coverage.** `TestTiDBRules` green for all three rules.
4. **Pingcap-import quarantine.** No remaining `github.com/pingcap/tidb/pkg` references in the migrated files.

## API mappings used

Verified against plan §1.5.0 "Verified API mapping" table:

| Pingcap | Omni |
|---|---|
| `node.Table.Name.O` | `node.Table.Name` |
| `column.Name.Name.O` | `col.Name` |
| `column.OriginTextPosition()` | `ostmt.AbsoluteLine(col.Loc.Start)` |
| `node.Cols` | `n.Columns` |
| `node.Specs[].Tp` | `n.Commands[].Type` |
| `ast.AlterTableRenameTable` | `ast.ATRenameTable` |
| `ast.AlterTableRenameColumn` | `ast.ATRenameColumn` |
| `ast.AlterTableAddColumns` | `ast.ATAddColumn` |
| `ast.AlterTableChangeColumn` | `ast.ATChangeColumn` |
| `spec.NewTable.Name.O` | `cmd.NewName` (string) |
| `spec.NewColumnName.Name.O` | `cmd.NewName` (string) |
| `spec.NewColumns` / `NewColumns[0]` | `cmd.Columns` (multi-form) **or** `cmd.Column` (single-form) — defensive read |
| `node.TableToTables` | `n.Pairs` (`[]*RenameTablePair`) |
| `table2Table.NewTable.Name.O` | `pair.New.Name` |

## Defensive reads applied

`naming_column`'s ATAddColumn handler reads both `cmd.Columns` and `cmd.Column` (mutually exclusive in practice but not enforced by the type) — same pattern as the pilot's `column_no_null`. Without the defensive split, omni populating both fields simultaneously would double-count column names.

- `advisor_naming_index_convention.go`, `advisor_naming_unique_key_convention.go`, `advisor_naming_foreign_key_convention.go` — these are Class IIa (use `in.Text()` for internal-error advice content) and share the

title: fix(databricks): apply user-selected row limit to SQL Editor queries
body:
## Summary

- The Databricks driver discarded `db.QueryContext`, so the row-limit toggle in the SQL Editor (default 1000) was silently ignored. Queries that returned more than ~25 MiB of inline response payload aborted with `Statements executed with disposition=INLINE can have a result size of at most 20214400 bytes` and the result grid stayed empty.
- Forward `queryContext.Limit` into `execStatementSync` and set `RowLimit` on `dbsql.ExecuteStatementRequest` when non-zero. Sync and dump paths pass `0` so admin queries (`SHOW CREATE TABLE`, `DESC FORMATTED`, `SELECT VERSION`) remain unbounded.
- Side benefit: Databricks now reports `truncated=true` on the response when the limit clips the result set.

Out of scope: switching the disposition to `EXTERNAL_LINKS` for results that exceed the inline cap even after the user limit is applied. The 1000-row default keeps almost every SQL Editor query well under 25 MiB; the `EXTERNAL_LINKS` path requires fetching pre-signed chunk URLs and re-stitching the result set, which is a separate, larger change.

Refs [BYT-9379](https://linear.app/bytebase/issue/BYT-9379/databricks-sql-editor-support).

## Test plan

- [x] `golangci-lint run --allow-parallel-runners ./backend/plugin/db/databricks/...` — 0 issues
- [x] `go build -ldflags "-w -s" -p=16 -o ./bytebase-build/bytebase ./backend/bin/server/main.go`
- [ ] Manual: against a Databricks instance, run `SELECT * FROM samples.tpch.customer` (or any moderately wide table) in the SQL Editor with the default 1000-row toggle. Expect the result grid to render rows, not the INLINE-size error.
