title: feat(mongodb): migrate parser from ANTLR to omni
body:
## Summary

- Migrate `backend/plugin/parser/mongodb/` from ANTLR-based parsing (`github.com/bytebase/parser/mongodb`) to Bytebase's omni parser framework (`github.com/bytebase/omni/mongo`)
- Upgrade `github.com/bytebase/omni` to `v0.0.0-20260402100940-de2123e1bfb3` (adds mongo subpackage)
- Upgrade `github.com/bytebase/gomongo` to `v0.0.0-20260403033636-f6c50d4ab888` (omni-based internally)
- Net ~1,800 line reduction across the package

## Changes

All 7 registered parser functions now use omni APIs:

| Function | Old (ANTLR) | New (Omni) |
|---|---|---|
| `ParseMongoShell` | ANTLR lexer/parser pipeline | `mongo.Parse()` + `OmniAST` wrapper |
| `SplitSQL` | Delegates to ParseMongoShell | Unchanged |
| `Diagnose` | ANTLR error listener | `parser.ParseError` type assertion |
| `GetStatementRanges` | ANTLR rune offsets → LSP | Omni byte offsets → LSP |
| `GetQueryType` | 400-line ANTLR listener (50+ methods) | `analysis.Analyze()` (50 lines) |
| `AnalyzeMaskingStatement` | 500-line ANTLR listener | `analysis.Analyze()` (60 lines) |
| `Completion` | ANTLR C3 algorithm | `completion.Complete()` |

### Behavioral differences

A few edge cases are classified differently by omni's analysis compared to the old ANTLR listener:

| Statement | Old | New | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| `db.users.isCapped()` | SelectInfoSchema | DML | Omni doesn't classify `isCapped` as info |
| `db.users.find({}).explain()` | Explain | Select | Omni recognizes `explain()` as prefix only |
| `rs.help()` / `sh.help()` | SelectInfoSchema | DML | Omni treats help as generic operation |
| `db.runCommand({find:...})` | Select | SelectInfoSchema | Omni classifies runCommand as meta-operation |

None of these affect security (access restrictions are same or stricter).

## Test plan

- [x] All existing MongoDB parser tests pass (with updated expectations for behavioral differences)
- [x] Completion test data re-recorded for new omni engine output
- [x] Zero ANTLR imports remain in `backend/plugin/parser/mongodb/`

- [x] Full project builds successfully

- Replace ANTLR-based `SplitSQL` (~500 lines across `splitMySQLStatement`, `splitDelimiterModeSQL`, `splitByParser`, etc.) with omni's `parser.Split()` — a pure lexical splitter that handles compound blocks, DELIMITER, quotes, and comments
- Update test data: omni filters empty segments (comment-only, trailing whitespace) which all callers already skip via `if stmt.Empty { continue }`
- Upgrade `github.com/bytebase/omni` to v0.0.0-20260403085552-f9d38cd66ef2 (fixes `IF NOT EXISTS` split bug)
- Net: **-553 lines**

## Test plan
- [x] `go test -count=1 ./backend/plugin/parser/mysql/...` — all pass
- [x] `go test -count=1 ./backend/plugin/advisor/mysql/...` — all pass
- [x] Verified: DELIMITER, compound blocks (BEGIN/END, IF, LOOP, WHILE, REPEAT, CASE), CRLF, unicode, escaped strings all split correctly

--- AGENTS.md (+214/-0)
@@ -0,0 +1,214 @@
+This file provides guidance to AI coding assistants when working with code in this repository.
+
+## Project Architecture
+
+- Database schema is defined in `./backend/migrator/migration/LATEST.sql`
+- Database migration files are in `./backend/migrator/<<version>>/`
+  - `TestLatestVersion` in `./backend/migrator/migrator_test.go` needs update after new migration files are added
+  - `./backend/migrator/migration/LATEST.sql` should be updated for DDL migrations
+- Files in `./backend/store` are mappings to the database tables
+
+## Development Workflow
+
+**ALWAYS follow these steps after making code changes:**
+
+### Go Code Changes
+
+1. **Format** — Run `gofmt -w` on modified files
+2. **Lint** — Run `golangci-lint run --allow-parallel-runners` to catch issues
+   - **Important**: Run golangci-lint repeatedly until there are no issues (the linter has a max-issues limit and may not show all issues in a single run)
+3. **Auto-fix** — Use `golangci-lint run --fix --allow-parallel-runners` to fix issues automatically
+4. **Test** — Run relevant tests before committing
+5. **Build** — `go build -ldflags "-w -s" -p=16 -o ./bytebase-build/bytebase ./backend/bin/server/main.go`
+6. **Tidy** — After upgrading Go dependencies, run `go mod tidy` to clean up `go.mod` and `go.sum`
+
+### Frontend Code Changes
+
+1. **Fix** — Run `pnpm --dir frontend fix` to auto-fix ESLint + Biome issues (format, lint, organize imports)
+2. **Check** — Run `pnpm --dir frontend check` to validate without modifying files (for CI)
+3. **Type check** — Run `pnpm --dir frontend type-check`
+4. **Test** — Run `pnpm --dir frontend test`
+
+### Proto Changes
+
+1. **Format** — Run `buf format -w proto`
+2. **Lint** — Run `buf lint proto`
+3. **Generate** — Run `cd proto && buf generate`
+
+## Build/Test Commands
+
+### Backend
+
+```bash
+# Build
+go build -ldflags "-w -s" -p=16 -o ./bytebase-build/bytebase ./backend/bin/server/main.go
+
+# Start backend
+PG_URL=postgresql://bbdev@localhost/bbdev go run ./backend/bin/server/main.go --port 8080 --data . --debug
+
+# Run single test
+go test -v -count=1 github.com/bytebase/bytebase/backend/path/to/tests -run ^TestFunctionName$
+
+# Run multiple tests
+go test -v -count=1 github.com/bytebase/bytebase/backend/path/to/tests -run ^(TestFunctionName|TestFunctionNameTwo)$
+
+# Lint
+golangci-lint run --allow-parallel-runners
+```
+
+### Frontend
+
+```bash
+# Install dependencies
+pnpm --dir frontend i
+
+# Dev server
+pnpm --dir frontend dev
+
+# Fix (ESLint + Biome: format, lint, organize imports)
+pnpm --dir frontend fix
+
+# Check (validate without modifying, for CI)
+pnpm --dir frontend check
+
+# Type check
+pnpm --dir frontend type-check
+
+# Test
+pnpm --dir frontend test
+```
+
+### Proto
+
+```bash
+# Format
+buf format -w proto
+
+# Lint
+buf lint proto
+
+# Generate
+cd proto && buf generate
+```
+
+### Database
+
+```bash
+# Connect to Postgres
+psql -U bbdev bbdev
+```
+
+## Code Style
+
+### General
+
+- Follow Google style guides for all languages
+  - [Go](https://google.github.io/styleguide/go/)
+  - [TypeScript](https://google.github.io/styleguide/tsguide.html) and [JavaScript](https://google.github.io/styleguide/jsguide.html)
+- Write clean, minimal code; fewer lines is better
+- Prioritize simplicity for effective and maintainable software
+- Only include comments that are essential to understanding functionality or convey non-obvious information
+
+### Go
+
+- Use standard Go error handling with detailed error messages
+- Always use `defer` for resource cleanup like `rows.Close()` (sqlclosecheck)
+- Avoid using `defer` inside loops (revive) — use IIFE or scope properly
+
+### API and Proto
+
+- Follow [AIPs](https://google.aip.dev/general)
+- When AIP and the proto guide conflict, AIP takes precedence
+- Use `HELLO` for enum names, not `TYPE_HELLO`
+
+### Frontend
+
+- Follow TypeScript style with strict type checking
+- **i18n**: All user-facing display text in the UI must be defined and maintained in locale files under `./frontend/src/locales/` using the i18n internationalization system. Do not hardcode any display strings directly in the source code
+  - **No Empty Objects**: Do not add empty JSON objects (e.g., `"key": {}`) to locale files. Remove any empty objects you encounter
+- **Button Spacing**: Use `gap-x-2` for ALL button groups (modals, drawers, toolbars, inline actions). Never use `space-x` for buttons. See `./frontend/.claude/BUTTON_SPACING_STANDARDIZATION.md` for full guidelines
+
+### React (New Code)
+
+The frontend is migrating from Vue to React. **All new UI code should be written in React.**
+
+**Stack**: React + [Base UI](https://base-ui.com/) (`@base-ui/react`) + Tailwind CSS v4 + shadcn-style component patterns
+
+**Component patterns**:
+- Build UI components in the shadcn style — `class-variance-authority` (cva) for variant props, `clsx`/`tailwind-merge` for class merging
+- Wrap Base UI primitives (Button, Tabs, Input, etc.) with styled variants in `./frontend/src/react/components/ui/`
+- Use `useTranslation()` from `react-i18next` for i18n
+- Use CSS custom properties (`--color-accent`, `--color-error`, `--color-control-border`, etc.) for theme tokens shared with the Vue layer
+
+**Tailwind CSS v4**:
+- CSS-first config in `./frontend/src/assets/css/tailwind.css` — no JS config file
+- Custom utilities use `@utility`, design tokens use `@theme`
+- Default border color is `currentcolor` (compat shim in `tailwind.css` preserves v3 behavior)
+
+**Accessing Vue state from React**:
+- `useVueState(getter)` — React hook that subscribes to Vue reactive state (Pinia stores, refs, computed) via `useSyncExternalStore`. React components access stores directly — no bridge layer needed
+- React pages are self-contained: import Pinia stores, `router`, utility functions directly
+- React `.tsx` is compiled by esbuild (`react-tsx-transform` Vite plugin) and type-checked separately via `tsconfig.react.json` (excluded from vue-tsc)
+
+## Naming
+
+- Use American English
+- Avoid plurals like "xxxList" for simplicity and to prevent singular/plural ambiguity stemming from poor design
+
+### Imports
+
+- Use organized imports (sorted by the import path)
+
+### Formatting
+
+- Use linting/formatting tools before committing
+
+### Error Handling
+
+- Be explicit but concise about error cases
+
+## Pull Request Guidelines
+
+- **Code Review** — Follow [Google's Code Review Guideline](https://google.github.io/eng-practices/)
+- **Author Responsibility** — Authors are responsible for driving discussions, resolving comments, and promptly merging pull requests
+- **Description** — Clearly describe what the PR changes and why
+- **Testing** — Include information about how the changes were tested
+- **SonarCloud** — When creating or updating a PR, update `.sonarcloud.properties` to reflect the latest file structure. Use `sonar.exclusions` for generated code, build artifacts, and dependencies (directory paths only). Use `sonar.test.inclusions` for test file patterns (wildcards like `**/*_test.go`). Use `sonar.cpd.exclusions` to skip copy-paste detection on test files
+
+### Breaking Change Check (MANDATORY before `gh pr create`)
+
+**This is a required step in the PR creation workflow. Run `git diff main...HEAD` and check every item below BEFORE writing the `gh pr create` command. This step comes after pushing the branch and before creating the PR.**
+
+1. **API breaking changes** — removed/renamed endpoints, changed request/response formats, removed/renamed query parameters
+2. **Database schema breaking changes** — dropped columns/tables, non-backward-compatible migrations
+3. **Proto breaking changes** — removed/renamed fields, changed field numbers/types, removed RPCs
+4. **Configuration breaking changes** — removed flags, changed default behavior, renamed environment variables
+5. **Behavior changes** — changed default values, altered existing workflows, modified permission/access control logic
+6. **Webhook/event changes** — renamed/removed events, changed payload formats
+7. **UI workflow changes** — redesigned user-facing flows that change how users perform existing tasks (e.g., merging steps, splitting pages, changing navigation)
+
+**If ANY of the above apply:**
+1. Add `--label breaking` to the `gh pr create` command
+2. Include a `## Breaking Changes` section in the PR description summarizing what changed and what users need to be aware of
+
+Do NOT skip this check. Do NOT assume changes are non-breaking without reviewing the diff.
+
+## Common Go Lint Rules
+
+Always follow these guidelines to avoid common linting errors:
+
+- **Unused Parameters** — Prefix unused parameters with underscore (e.g., `func foo(_ *Bar)`)
+- **Modern Go Conventions** — Use `any` instead of `interface{}` (since Go 1.18)
+- **Confusing Naming** — Avoid similar names that differ only by capitalization
+- **Identical Branches** — Don't use if-else branches that contain identical code
+- **Unused Functions** — Mark unused functions with `// nolint:unused` comment if needed for future use
+- **Function Receivers** — Don't create unnecessary function receivers; use regular functions if receiver is unused
+- **Proper Import Ordering** — Maintain correct grouping and ordering of imports
+- **Consistency** — Keep function signatures, naming, and patterns consistent with existing code
+- **Export Rules** — Only export (capitalize) functions and types that need to be used outside the package
+- **Linting Command** — Always run `golangci-lint run --allow-parallel-runners` without appending filenames to avoid "function not defined" errors (functions are defined in other files within the package)
+
+## Miscellaneous
+
+- The database JSONB columns store JSON marshalled by `protojson.Marshal` in Go code. `protojson.Marshal` produces camelCased keys rather than the snake_case keys defined in the proto files. e.g. `task_run` becomes `taskRun`
+- When modifying multiple files, run file modification tasks in parallel whenever possible, instead of processing them sequentially

title: fix(plan): use contains for title filters and dedupe locale keys
body:
## Summary
Switch plan title filtering to use `contains()` instead of `matches()`.

## What changed
- updated the frontend plan filter builder to emit `title.contains(...)`
- made the plan filter backend accept `contains()` and reject `matches()` for plan titles
- updated plan filter tests to enforce the hard switch
- regenerated protobuf/OpenAPI/grpc-doc artifacts after updating the proto docs
- removed duplicate keys from `frontend/src/locales/en-US.json` so frontend lint/check passes

## Why
The previous client code emitted `matches()` for a substring search, which does not match CEL's meaning. This change aligns the plan filter API and client usage around `contains()` for substring semantics.

## Impact
Plan title searches now use CEL-consistent `contains()` syntax.

## Breaking Changes
- `ListPlans` plan-title filters no longer accept `title.matches("...")`
- callers must switch to `title.contains("...")`
- this affects older UIs and external API clients that still send the previous filter form

## Validation
- `go test ./backend/store -run TestGetListPlanFilter -count=1`
- `buf generate` (from `proto/`)
- `pnpm --dir frontend check`

title: refactor(parser/mysql): migrate statement type detection to omni AST [BYT-9115]
body:
## Summary
- Replace ANTLR `GetANTLRAST()` + 4-level nested context traversal with `GetOmniNode()` + flat omni AST type switch in `GetStatementTypes()`
- Delete unused `StatementTypeChecker` listener (`statement_type_check.go`) — no external callers
- Reduces `GetANTLRAST()` call sites in mysql advisor/parser from 4 to 3

## Test plan
- [x] `go test -count=1 ./backend/plugin/parser/mysql/ -run ^TestGetStatementType$` passes
- [x] `go test -count=1 ./backend/plugin/parser/mysql/...` passes
- [x] `go test -count=1 ./backend/plugin/advisor/mysql/...` passes

BYT-9115

title: feat(frontend): migrate /users page from Vue to React
body:
## Summary

- Full React rewrite of the `/users` settings page (`SettingWorkspaceUsers.vue` → `UsersPage.tsx`)
- Implements all 3 tabs: **Users** (self-hosted), **Members** (SaaS), **Groups**
- Implements all 4 drawers: CreateUserDrawer, CreateGroupDrawer, AADSyncDrawer, EditMemberRoleDrawer
- Adds grouped multi-select role picker (RoleMultiSelect) matching Vue RoleSelect behavior
- Adds 63 i18n keys to React locale files (all 5 languages)

## What changed

| Component | Before (Vue) | After (React) |
|-----------|-------------|---------------|
| Page shell + tabs | `SettingWorkspaceUsers.vue` | `UsersPage.tsx` |
| User table + pagination | `UserDataTable` + `PagedTable.vue` | `UserTable` + `usePagedData` hook |
| Group table (expandable) | `UserDataTableByGroup` | `GroupTable` + `GroupRow` |
| Create/edit user | `CreateUserDrawer.vue` | `CreateUserDrawer` (inline) |
| Create/edit group | `CreateGroupDrawer.vue` | `CreateGroupDrawer` (inline) |
| SCIM/Entra sync | `AADSyncDrawer.vue` | `AADSyncDrawer` (inline) |
| Member management (SaaS) | `WorkspaceMembers.vue` + `MemberDataTable` + `MemberDataTableByRole` + `EditMemberRoleDrawer.vue` | `MemberTable` + `MemberTableByRole` + `EditMemberRoleDrawer` (inline) |
| Route | `SettingWorkspaceUsers.vue` | `ReactPageMount.vue` → `UsersPage` |

## Test plan

- [ ] `/users` loads correctly (self-hosted mode: Users + Groups tabs)
- [ ] Users tab: search, pagination (rows per page + load more), add user, edit user, deactivate, restore
- [ ] Groups tab: search, expand groups to see members, add group, edit group, delete group
- [ ] Query param `?name=groups/...` opens group drawer
- [ ] Entra Sync drawer: shows SCIM endpoint/token, copy buttons, reset token
- [ ] Members tab (SaaS mode): view by members, view by roles, grant access, revoke access, batch revoke
- [ ] Feature badges for plan-gated features (directory sync, user groups, custom roles)
- [ ] Permission guards disable buttons for users without permissions
- [ ] Tab switching syncs with URL hash
- [ ] Inactive users toggle and table work correctly
- [ ] Deactivating a user moves them to inactive list; restoring moves them back

> [!WARNING]
> Some dependencies could not be looked up. Check the [Dependency Dashboard](../issues/2527) for more information.

### GitHub Vulnerability Alerts

#### [CVE-2026-34986](https://redirect.github.com/go-jose/go-jose/security/advisories/GHSA-78h2-9frx-2jm8)

### Impact

Decrypting a JSON Web Encryption (JWE) object will panic if the `alg` field indicates a key wrapping algorithm ([one ending in `KW`](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/go-jose/go-jose/v4#pkg-constants), with the exception of `A128GCMKW`, `A192GCMKW`, and `A256GCMKW`) and the `encrypted_key` field is empty. The panic happens when `cipher.KeyUnwrap()` in `key_wrap.go` attempts to allocate a slice with a zero or negative length based on the length of the `encrypted_key`.

This code path is reachable from `ParseEncrypted()` / `ParseEncryptedJSON()` / `ParseEncryptedCompact()` followed by `Decrypt()` on the resulting object. Note that the parse functions take a list of accepted key algorithms. If the accepted key algorithms do not include any key wrapping algorithms, parsing will fail and the application will be unaffected.

This panic is also reachable by calling `cipher.KeyUnwrap()` directly with any `ciphertext` parameter less than 16 bytes long, but calling this function directly is less common.

Panics can lead to denial of service.

### Fixed In

4.1.4 and v3.0.5

### Workarounds

If the list of `keyAlgorithms` passed to `ParseEncrypted()` / `ParseEncryptedJSON()` / `ParseEncryptedCompact()` does not include key wrapping algorithms (those ending in `KW`), your application is unaffected.

If your application uses key wrapping, you can prevalidate to the JWE objects to ensure the `encrypted_key` field is nonempty. If your application accepts JWE Compact Serialization, apply that validation to the corresponding field of that serialization (the data between the first and second `.`).

### Thanks

Go JOSE thanks Datadog's Security team for finding this issue.

title: refactor(advisor/mysql): migrate all 87 advisor rules to omni AST [BYT-9123]
body:
## Summary
- Migrate all 87 MySQL SQL review advisor rules from ANTLR tree walking to omni AST type switches
- New `generic_checker_omni.go`: `OmniRule` interface + `OmniBaseRule` + `RunOmniRules()` dispatcher (following PG pattern)
- New `utils_omni.go`: ~25 MySQL AST extraction utilities
- 9 rules further simplified using `ast.Inspect` for recursive traversal
- Upgrade omni to `870fdbd` (adds `Walk`/`Inspect` for MySQL AST)
- Net reduction: **-4659 lines** (5184 added, 9843 removed)

## What changed
Every `rule_*.go` in `backend/plugin/advisor/mysql/` changed from:
```go
antlrAST, ok := base.GetANTLRAST(stmt.AST)
antlr.ParseTreeWalkerDefault.Walk(checker, antlrAST.Tree)
```
to:
```go
node, ok := mysqlparser.GetOmniNode(stmt.AST)
switch n := node.(type) {
case *ast.CreateTableStmt: ...
case *ast.AlterTableStmt: ...
}
```

## Known limitation
`rule_builtin_prior_backup_check` retains 1 `GetANTLRAST` call — depends on `ExtractTables()` which needs ANTLR AST. Tracked in BYT-9125.

title: feat(mcp): simplify resolveDatabase with workspace-scoped ListDatabases
body:
## Summary

- Replace N+1 API call pattern (`SearchProjects` + N × `ListDatabases`) with a single workspace-scoped `ListDatabases` call
- Extract `workspace_id` from the JWT token already validated in MCP auth middleware — zero extra API calls
- Add project filter to CEL expression (was previously handled by parent parameter in per-project calls)
- Return actionable error message when user lacks `bb.databases.list` permission

## Details

The `resolveDatabase` function previously listed all accessible projects via `SearchProjects`, then called `ListDatabases` per project. This was O(N+1) where N = number of projects. Now it makes a single `ListDatabases(parent: "workspaces/{id}")` call with CEL filters for name, instance, and project.

| Before | After |
|--------|-------|
| `SearchProjects` + N × `ListDatabases` | 1 × `ListDatabases` with workspace parent |
| Workspace ID ignored in JWT | Extracted from `workspace_id` claim |
| Project filter via parent parameter | Project filter via CEL expression |
| 403 per-project silently skipped | 403 returns actionable error with permission name |

title: fix(parser): fix CRLF line endings causing query truncation

## Summary
- Fix multi-line SQL queries with `\r\n` line endings being truncated when sent to the database (e.g., `GROUP BY store_id` → `GROUP BY stor`)
- Rewrite `applyMultiStatements` to track byte offsets directly instead of reverse-engineering positions via `strings.Index`
- Fix `CalculateLineAndColumn` to skip `\r` so line/column positions are correct for `\r\n` input across all parsers

## Root Cause
The standard SQL splitter (ClickHouse, SQLite, Hive, Databricks) used `applyMultiStatements` which stripped `\r` via `TrimRightFunc`, then `SplitSQL` used `strings.Index` to find the stripped text in the original `\r\n` string. The search failed silently (`sqlPos` defaulted to 0), and `endPos` was computed from `len(sqlTrimmed)` which was shorter than the actual span — truncating the query.

Introduced in `eec45b0ce5` (add Statement.Range field for byte offset tracking) which changed `SplitSQL` from using `applyMultiStatements` output text directly to re-extracting text from the original statement via offset computation.

## Test plan
- [x] 3 new CRLF regression tests in `test_split.yaml` (multi-line without semicolon, multiple statements, single statement with semicolon)
- [x] All 10 existing standard split tests pass
- [x] All 8 parser split test suites pass (mysql, pg, tsql, plsql, redshift, spanner, trino, standard) — no regressions from `CalculateLineAndColumn` change

title: refactor(frontend): migrate custom approval page from Vue to React
body:
## Summary

- Migrate the `/custom-approval` settings page from Vue to React with full feature parity
- Add two reusable Base UI wrapper components: `Dialog` and `Switch`
- Add `@dnd-kit/core` + `@dnd-kit/sortable` for drag-and-drop rule reordering
- Add i18n keys to all 5 React locale files

## Components

| Component | Responsibility |
|-----------|---------------|
| `CustomApprovalPage.tsx` | Page wrapper — loading, feature gate, source sections |
| `RulesSection.tsx` | Per-source rules table with drag-and-drop reordering |
| `RuleEditDialog.tsx` | Create/edit rule modal with ExprEditor, templates |
| `ApprovalStepsTable.tsx` | Approval flow steps with role select, reorder |
| `RoleSelect.tsx` | Role dropdown for approval steps |
| `utils.ts` | Factor lists, option configs, templates (ported from Vue) |
| `dialog.tsx` | Reusable Base UI Dialog wrapper |
| `switch.tsx` | Reusable Base UI Switch wrapper |

## Test plan

- [ ] Navigate to `/custom-approval` — page loads with all 6 source sections
- [ ] Add a rule — template presets work, CEL editor renders correct factors per source
- [ ] Edit a rule — fields pre-populate, condition loads correctly
- [ ] Delete a rule — confirmation shown, rule removed
- [ ] Drag-and-drop reorder — ghost element visible, order persists
- [ ] Skip approval toggle — hides/shows approval steps table
- [ ] Permission gating — non-admin sees read-only interface
- [ ] Feature gating — scrolls to FeatureAttention banner when gated

## Summary

- [ ] Click Edit, change format to XLSX, click Save -- verify XLSX is persisted and displayed

--- backend/plugin/parser/tsql/omni.go (+119/-0)
@@ -0,0 +1,119 @@
+package tsql
+
+import (
+	"unicode/utf8"
+
+	"github.com/antlr4-go/antlr/v4"
+	omnimssql "github.com/bytebase/omni/mssql"
+	"github.com/bytebase/omni/mssql/ast"
+	antlrparser "github.com/bytebase/parser/tsql"
+
+	storepb "github.com/bytebase/bytebase/backend/generated-go/store"
+	"github.com/bytebase/bytebase/backend/plugin/parser/base"
+)
+
+// OmniAST wraps an omni AST node and implements the base.AST interface.
+// During migration, it also implements AntlrASTProvider so that callers
+// still using GetANTLRAST() can fall back to the ANTLR tree.
+type OmniAST struct {
+	// Node is the omni AST node (e.g. *ast.SelectStmt, *ast.CreateTableStmt).
+	Node ast.Node
+	// Text is the original SQL text of this statement.
+	Text string
+	// StartPosition is the 1-based position where this statement starts.
+	StartPosition *storepb.Position
+
+	// antlrAST is lazily populated when AsANTLRAST() is called.
+	// This field will be removed once all callers are migrated to omni.
+	antlrAST *base.ANTLRAST
+	// antlrParsed tracks whether we've attempted the ANTLR parse.
+	antlrParsed bool
+}
+
+// ASTStartPosition implements base.AST.
+func (a *OmniAST) ASTStartPosition() *storepb.Position {
+	return a.StartPosition
+}
+
+// AsANTLRAST implements base.AntlrASTProvider for backward compatibility.
+// It lazily parses the SQL text with the ANTLR parser and caches the result.
+// This will be removed once all TSQL modules are migrated to omni.
+func (a *OmniAST) AsANTLRAST() (*base.ANTLRAST, bool) {
+	if a.antlrParsed {
+		return a.antlrAST, a.antlrAST != nil
+	}
+	a.antlrParsed = true
+
+	// Use lenient ANTLR parsing (no error listeners) since omni already
+	// validated the SQL. The ANTLR tree is only needed for backward-compatible
+	// tree walking by callers that haven't migrated to omni yet.
+	tree, tokens := parseSingleTSQLLenient(a.Text)
+	a.antlrAST = &base.ANTLRAST{
+		StartPosition: a.StartPosition,
+		Tree:          tree,
+		Tokens:        tokens,
+	}
+	return a.antlrAST, true
+}
+
+// parseSingleTSQLLenient parses a single T-SQL statement without error listeners.
+// Returns the parse tree and token stream; errors are silently ignored.
+func parseSingleTSQLLenient(statement string) (antlr.Tree, *antlr.CommonTokenStream) {
+	inputStream := antlr.NewInputStream(statement)
+	lexer := antlrparser.NewTSqlLexer(inputStream)
+	stream := antlr.NewCommonTokenStream(lexer, antlr.TokenDefaultChannel)
+	p := antlrparser.NewTSqlParser(stream)
+
+	lexer.RemoveErrorListeners()
+	p.RemoveErrorListeners()
+	p.BuildParseTrees = true
+
+	tree := p.Tsql_file()
+	return tree, stream
+}
+
+// ParseTSQLOmni parses SQL using omni's parser and returns omni Statement objects directly.
+// This is the recommended entry point for new code that needs omni AST nodes.
+func ParseTSQLOmni(sql string) ([]omnimssql.Statement, error) {
+	return omnimssql.Parse(sql)
+}
+
+// GetOmniNode extracts the omni AST node from a base.AST interface.
+// Returns the node and true if it is an OmniAST, nil and false otherwise.
+func GetOmniNode(a base.AST) (ast.Node, bool) {
+	if a == nil {
+		return nil, false
+	}
+	omniAST, ok := a.(*OmniAST)
+	if !ok {
+		return nil, false
+	}
+	return omniAST.Node, true
+}
+
+// ByteOffsetToRunePosition converts a byte offset in sql to a 1-based line:column
+// where column is measured in Unicode code points (runes), matching storepb.Position semantics.
+func ByteOffsetToRunePosition(sql string, byteOffset int) *storepb.Position {
+	if byteOffset > len(sql) {
+		byteOffset = len(sql)
+	}
+
+	line := int32(1)
+	runeCol := int32(0) // 0-based rune count on current line
+	i := 0
+	for i < byteOffset {
+		r, size := utf8.DecodeRuneInString(sql[i:])
+		if r == '\n' {
+			line++
+			runeCol = 0
+		} else {
+			runeCol++
+		}
+		i += size
+	}
+
+	return &storepb.Position{
+		Line:   line,
+		Column: runeCol + 1, // convert to 1-based
+	}
+}

title: feat(parser): migrate MySQL core parsing to omni parser
body:
## Summary
- Replace ANTLR-based MySQL parsing with omni parser in `parseMySQLStatements()`
- Add `OmniAST` wrapper with lazy ANTLR fallback (`AsANTLRAST()`) so existing advisors, schema walk-through, and other callers keep working during migration
- Upgrade omni to latest version which fixes `ALTER TABLE PARTITION BY`, `INT SIGNED`, and `LONG VARCHAR/VARBINARY` parser gaps
- Re-record advisor test expectations to match omni parser behavior

## Key changes
- **New file**: `backend/plugin/parser/mysql/omni.go` — `OmniAST`, `ParseMySQLOmni()`, `GetOmniNode()`, `ByteOffsetToRunePosition()`
- **Modified**: `backend/plugin/parser/mysql/mysql.go` — `parseMySQLStatements()` now uses omni, with `parseSingleStatementLenient()` for ANTLR fallback
- **Test data**: 70+ advisor YAML files re-recorded, walk-through test updated

## Known issue
- `ALTER TABLE t ADD PRIMARY KEY pk_a (col)` — omni rejects this syntax. MySQL 8.0 actually accepts it (undocumented), though the name is silently ignored. Tracked separately.

## Test plan
- [x] `go test ./backend/plugin/parser/mysql/...` — pass
- [x] `go test ./backend/plugin/advisor/mysql/...` — pass
- [x] `go test ./backend/plugin/schema/mysql/...` — pass (including testcontainer tests)
- [x] `go build` — pass
- [x] `golangci-lint run` — 0 issues

title: fix(frontend): disable audit log "Load more" during refresh
body:
## Summary
- Disable the "Load more" button in the Audit Log page while a refresh fetch is in progress
- Prevents race condition where `loadMore` could be triggered with a stale `nextPageToken` when filters/sort/page size change

Fixes https://github.com/bytebase/bytebase/pull/19810#discussion_r3026617911

## Test plan
- [ ] Change filters/sort/page size and verify "Load more" button is disabled during refresh
- [ ] Verify "Load more" still works correctly after refresh completes

title: refactor(frontend): migrate Audit Log page from Vue to React
body:
## Summary
- Migrate the workspace Audit Log page (`/audit-log`) from Vue to a self-contained React component
- Delete `SettingWorkspaceAuditLog.vue`, add `AuditLogPage.tsx` with full feature parity
- Add i18n keys for audit-log across all 5 React locale files and `common.from`/`common.to` to Vue locales

## What's included
- **AdvancedSearch** with actor (free-text), method, and level scope filters
- **TimeRangePicker** with second-precision datetime-local inputs (default: last 30 days)
- **Resizable columns** via drag handles on column headers with `<colgroup>` width control
- **Sortable Time column** with clear sort indicator
- **Export dropdown** (CSV/JSON/XLSX) with permission gating (`bb.auditLogs.export`)
- **JSONStringView** with expand-to-modal and Escape key dismiss
- **Pagination** with page size selector and "Load more" (cursor-based)
- **Error notifications** via `pushNotification` for fetch and export failures
- **Feature gating** via `FeatureAttention` for `FEATURE_AUDIT_LOG`

## Test plan
- [ ] Navigate to `/audit-log` and verify data loads
- [ ] Filter by method, level, and actor using the search bar
- [ ] Change time range via the datetime picker and verify results update
- [ ] Sort by Time column (asc/desc/none)
- [ ] Resize columns by dragging the handle on column header edges
- [ ] Export in CSV/JSON/XLSX formats
- [ ] Expand JSON cells via hover button and dismiss with Escape/backdrop click
- [ ] Verify pagination with "Load more" and page size changes
- [ ] Verify i18n renders correctly (switch to zh-CN)

---

> [!WARNING]
> Some dependencies could not be looked up. Check the [Dependency Dashboard](../issues/2527) for more information.

### GitHub Vulnerability Alerts

#### [CVE-2026-4800](https://redirect.github.com/lodash/lodash/security/advisories/GHSA-r5fr-rjxr-66jc)

### Impact

The fix for [CVE-2021-23337](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-35jh-r3h4-6jhm) added validation for the `variable` option in `_.template` but did not apply the same validation to `options.imports` key names. Both paths flow into the same `Function()` constructor sink.

When an application passes untrusted input as `options.imports` key names, an attacker can inject default-parameter expressions that execute arbitrary code at template compilation time.

Additionally, `_.template` uses `assignInWith` to merge imports, which enumerates inherited properties via `for..in`. If `Object.prototype` has been polluted by any other vector, the polluted keys are copied into the imports object and passed to `Function()`.

### Patches

Users should upgrade to version 4.18.0.

The fix applies two changes:
1. Validate `importsKeys` against the existing `reForbiddenIdentifierChars` regex (same check already used for the `variable` option)
2. Replace `assignInWith` with `assignWith` when merging imports, so only own properties are enumerated

### Workarounds

Do not pass untrusted input as key names in `options.imports`. Only use developer-controlled, static key names.

#### [CVE-2026-2950](https://redirect.github.com/lodash/lodash/security/advisories/GHSA-f23m-r3pf-42rh)

### Impact

Lodash versions 4.17.23 and earlier are vulnerable to prototype pollution in the `_.unset` and `_.omit` functions. The fix for [CVE-2025-13465](https://redirect.github.com/lodash/lodash/security/advisories/GHSA-xxjr-mmjv-4gpg) only guards against string key members, so an attacker can bypass the check by passing array-wrapped path segments. This allows deletion of properties from built-in prototypes such as `Object.prototype`, `Number.prototype`, and `String.prototype`.

The issue permits deletion of prototype properties but does not allow overwriting their original behavior.

### Patches

This issue is patched in 4.18.0.

### Workarounds

None. Upgrade to the patched version.

title: fix(oauth2): return usable URLs in OAuth discovery for self-hosted mode
body:
## Summary
- The OAuth authorization server metadata endpoint (`/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`) was returning URL templates with literal `:workspaceID` placeholders (e.g., `/api/workspaces/:workspaceID/oauth2/register`)
- RFC 8414 requires these to be directly usable URLs, so any compliant client (e.g., MCP SDK) failed with `"failed to create client"` when attempting dynamic client registration
- For self-hosted mode, return legacy `/api/oauth2/*` paths that don't require a workspace ID. For SaaS mode, resolve the actual workspace ID from the store

- [ ] Verify SaaS mode returns workspace-scoped URLs with resolved workspace ID

title: refactor(i18n): separate React i18n locale files from Vue
body:
## Summary

- **Separate React locale files** — React gets its own JSON files at `frontend/src/react/locales/` (main + dynamic/), decoupled from Vue's `frontend/src/locales/`

### Motivation
- Make the HTTP client timeout configurable to avoid the hardcoded `120s` causing `context deadline exceeded` for large SQL files when running `bytebase-action check`.

title: feat(plan): enrich plan responses with approval and rollout status
body:
## Summary
- Add plan-level approval status and rollout stage task status summaries to the Plan API
- Batch-load related issue, plan check, and rollout task data when converting plans
- Expose the new fields through generated API schemas and client types

## Breaking Changes
- **Proto**: New fields added to `Plan` message — `approval_status` (field 13) and `rollout_stage_summaries` (field 14). New sub-messages `Plan.RolloutStageSummary` and `Plan.TaskStatusCount`. These are additive and backward-compatible for protobuf wire format, but API consumers may see new fields in JSON responses
- **Store API**: `FindPlanCheckRunMessage` now uses `ProjectIDs` (slice) instead of single `ProjectID`. Internal callers must update accordingly
- **API behavior**: `ListPlans` and `GetPlan` responses now include `approvalStatus` and `rolloutStageSummaries` fields that were not previously present

## Key Changes
- Extend Plan with linked issue approval status and per-stage task status counts
- Aggregate rollout task execution state with a single SQL query and normalize internal task-run states to API-visible task statuses
- Reuse the same conversion path for both GetPlan and ListPlans, while supporting multi-project plan check lookups

## Motivation
- Let plan consumers read approval progress and rollout execution status without separate issue or rollout fetches
- Keep the added status enrichment efficient for plan lists by avoiding per-plan task queries

## Testing
- `cd proto && buf generate && buf lint`
- `go test ./backend/api/v1 ./backend/store`

title: fix: resolve SQL error when filtering instances by host/port with matches()
body:
## Summary
- Fix SQL error `column "ds" does not exist (SQLSTATE 42703)` when using `.matches()` CEL filter for "host" and "port" fields in `GetListInstanceFilter`
- The `ds` alias was referenced without a defining FROM clause; wrapped the condition in an `EXISTS` subquery using `jsonb_array_elements(instance.metadata -> 'dataSources')` to properly extract and search data source entries
- This aligns with the equality operator for the same fields which already correctly queries the JSONB `dataSources` array

## Test plan

- [ ] Manually test instance list filtering with `.matches()` on host and port fields
- [ ] Verify existing equality filters for host/port still work correctly

--- backend/store/instance.go (+3/-1)
@@ -893,7 +893,9 @@ func GetListInstanceFilter(filter string) (*qb.Query, error) {
 				case "resource_id":
 					return qb.Q().Space("LOWER(instance.resource_id) LIKE ?", "%"+strings.ToLower(strValue)+"%"), nil
 				case "host", "port":
-					return qb.Q().Space(fmt.Sprintf("ds ->> '%s' LIKE ?", variable), "%"+strValue+"%"), nil
+					return qb.Q().Space(
+						fmt.Sprintf(`EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM jsonb_array_elements(instance.metadata -> 'dataSources') AS ds WHERE ds ->> '%s' LIKE ?)`, variable),
+						"%"+strValue+"%"), nil
 				default:
 					return nil, errors.Errorf("unsupport variable %q", variable)
 				}

title: refactor(plan): unify rollout flows under the plan detail page
body: ## Summary - Consolidate plan, issue, and rollout navigation around the new plan detail page - Simplify header actions and sidebar behavior for database change plans - Remove obsolete rollout-only views and stale route fallbacks ## Breaking Changes - **UI workflow**: The plan detail page is now a standalone layout, no longer nested under the issue layout. Users navigating to plan detail will see a new unified view combining changes, review, and deploy - **Removed action**: `ROLLOUT_CREATE` action button has been removed. Rollout creation for non-deferred plans is now managed within the Plan Detail Page's Deploy section - **Route changes**: Legacy `/plans/:planId/rollout/...` routes now redirect to the canonical plan detail deploy view. Old rollout-specific URLs will still work via redirects but the rollout-only views are removed - **Behavior change**: Creating a rollout no longer automatically marks the linked issue as "DONE" — the issue lifecycle is now decoupled from rollout creation - **Navigation change**: After issue approval, navigation now goes to the plan detail page (deploy section) instead of a separate rollout page ## Key Changes - Route legacy rollout URLs to the canonical plan detail deploy view and remove the project rollout dashboard entry - Rework the plan detail layout with shared sticky side-panel primitives, container-driven responsive behavior, and cleaner phase state handling - Move issue discussion access into the review section, refine metadata/status handling, and simplify the plan header link for database change issues - Drop unused rollout header actions and rollout-only views, and update navigation helpers and polling/initialization logic to match the new flow - Clean up related locale keys and link active-state behavior to avoid incorrect content-area styling ## Motivation - Make the plan detail page the single source of truth for changes, review, and deploy workflows - Reduce duplicated rollout-specific UI and route logic that was drifting out of sync - Improve layout maintainability and predictable behavior across desktop, mobile, and long-content scenarios ## Testing - `pnpm -C frontend run check` - `pnpm -C frontend run test` - `rm -rf frontend/node_modules/.tmp && pnpm -C frontend run type-check` ## Screenshots

body:
## Summary
- make `QueryRequest.data_source_id` and `ExportRequest.data_source_id` optional in the API contract and resolve datasources server-side
- enforce at most one `READ_ONLY` datasource per instance and add a migration to dedupe legacy duplicate read-only datasources
- update first-party SQL editor flows to support automatic datasource selection while keeping manual override support

## Testing
- `buf lint proto`
- `go test -v -count=1 ./backend/migrator -run '^(TestLatestVersion|TestMigration3_17_15_DedupeReadOnlyDataSources)$'`
- `go test -count=1 ./backend/tests -run '^(TestDataSource|TestSQLExport|TestSQLExportDataSourceResolution|TestSQLQueryDataSourceResolution|TestSQLQueryStopOnError|TestSensitiveData|TestSQLReviewForMySQL)$'`
- `golangci-lint run --allow-parallel-runners`

- `pnpm --dir frontend install --frozen-lockfile`

- `pnpm --dir frontend type-check`
- `pnpm --dir frontend test`

## Breaking Changes
- `QueryRequest.data_source_id` and `ExportRequest.data_source_id` no longer need to be sent by clients; when omitted, the server now uses the single `READ_ONLY` datasource if present, otherwise the `ADMIN` datasource.
- Instances are now limited to at most one `READ_ONLY` datasource. A migration rewrites legacy metadata to keep the first `READ_ONLY` datasource and remove additional ones.
- First-party SQL editor flows now default to automatic datasource selection unless the user explicitly chooses a datasource override.

title: fix(mysql): resolve unqualified SET columns in prior backup for UPDATE JOIN
body:
## Summary

- Fix `UPDATE ... JOIN` with unqualified SET columns (e.g., `SET col = 1` instead of `SET t1.col = 1`) failing prior backup's plan check with "no matched updated table" error
- Use database metadata to resolve unqualified column names to their owning table, instead of only supporting single-table UPDATE statements
- Apply the same fix to both MySQL (`backend/plugin/parser/mysql/backup.go`) and TiDB (`backend/plugin/parser/tidb/backup.go`), which shared the same bug

## Test plan

- [x] Create a MySQL instance with Prior Backup enabled, create a plan with `UPDATE t1 INNER JOIN t2 ON ... SET unqualified_col = 1 WHERE ...` — plan check succeeds
- [x] Same test with a TiDB instance — plan check succeeds
- [x] Verified qualified SET columns (`SET t1.col = 1`) still work (regression)
- [x] Verified single-table UPDATE with unqualified columns still works (regression)

closes #19776

title: fix(pg): add whitespace between LIMIT and FOR UPDATE clause
body:
## Summary

Fix missing whitespace when inserting LIMIT before FOR UPDATE/SHARE clause.

Before: `SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = 1 LIMIT 10FOR UPDATE` (invalid SQL)
After: `SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = 1 LIMIT 10 FOR UPDATE`

## Root cause

`findLimitInsertPosition` returns the byte offset of `FOR` keyword via `ast.ListSpan(sel.LockingClause).Start`. The inserted text `" LIMIT 10"` has a leading space but no trailing space, so it directly abuts `FOR`.

## Fix

`findLimitInsertPosition` now returns a second value indicating whether the insertion is before a locking clause. When true, `rewriteSelectLimit` uses `" LIMIT %d "` (with trailing space) instead of `" LIMIT %d"`.

## Test plan

- [x] Existing `TestGetStatementWithResultLimit/SELECT_with_FOR_UPDATE` passes (expects `LIMIT 10 FOR UPDATE`)
- [x] All 24 LIMIT rewriter tests pass
- [x] Build + lint clean

title: feat(frontend): add shadcn-style UI components with Base UI
body:
## Summary

- Introduce a React component library following [shadcn/ui](https://ui.shadcn.com/) conventions, using **@base-ui/react** primitives instead of Radix UI
- Add `class-variance-authority` (cva) for typed variant props and `clsx` for conditional class composition
- Refactor `SubscriptionPage.tsx` to use the new components, replacing raw HTML elements and hardcoded Tailwind colors

## Motivation

As we gradually migrate from Vue/Naive UI to React, we need a consistent, well-structured component library. shadcn/ui is the de facto standard for React + Tailwind projects, but it traditionally depends on Radix UI. Since we already have `@base-ui/react` installed (MUI's headless primitive library), we use that as the underlying primitive layer instead.

This gives us:
- **Accessible primitives** — keyboard navigation, focus management, ARIA attributes from Base UI
- **Typed variant API** — `<Button variant="outline" size="sm">` via cva
- **Design token consistency** — all colors reference existing CSS custom properties (`--color-accent`, `--color-control-border`, etc.) so React components match the Vue app during migration
- **Standard file structure** — `components/ui/`, `lib/utils.ts`, named exports — familiar to any React developer

## New Components

| Component | Primitive | Variants |
|-----------|-----------|----------|
| `Button` | `@base-ui/react/button` | default, outline, ghost, destructive, link × default, sm, lg, icon |
| `Input` | `@base-ui/react/input` | — (consistent styling with readonly/disabled states) |
| `Textarea` | native `<textarea>` | — (Base UI has no textarea primitive) |
| `Badge` | native `<span>` | default, secondary, destructive, success |

## File Structure

```
src/react/
├── lib/
│   └── utils.ts              # cn() = twMerge + clsx
├── components/
│   └── ui/
│       ├── button.tsx
│       ├── input.tsx
│       ├── textarea.tsx
│       └── badge.tsx
```

## SubscriptionPage Changes

- Raw `<button>` → `<Button>` / `<Button variant="ghost" size="icon">`
- Raw `<input>` → `<Input>`
- Raw `<textarea>` → `<Textarea>`
- Inline badge `<span>` → `<Badge variant="destructive">` / `<Badge variant="secondary">`
- Hardcoded Tailwind colors (`text-gray-400`, `border-gray-200`, `text-indigo-600`) → design tokens (`text-control-placeholder`, `border-block-border`, `text-accent`)
- Oversized pencil icon (`h-8 w-8`) → properly sized (`h-5 w-5`)

## Test plan

- [ ] `pnpm --dir frontend type-check` passes
- [ ] `pnpm --dir frontend check` passes
- [ ] Subscription page renders correctly at `/setting/subscription`
- [ ] Button variants render with correct colors and hover states
- [ ] Input/Textarea show proper focus rings, disabled states
- [ ] Badge variants display with correct background/text colors
- [ ] Copy workspace ID button works
- [ ] Upload license flow works

title: refactor(pg): remove legacy differ and migration generation code
body:
## Summary

- Remove ~10,700 lines of dead PG code: the legacy `GetDatabaseSchemaDiff` + `GenerateMigration` path has been fully replaced by the omni SDL path (`catalog.LoadSDL` → `catalog.Diff` → `catalog.GenerateMigration`)
- Delete `generate_migration.go` (5192 lines), 3 PG ANTLR comparers (`index_comparer.go`, `function_comparer.go`, `view_comparer.go`), and 5 legacy test files
- Clean up `differ.go`: remove all `OldASTNode`/`NewASTNode` fields (zero references after deletion) and drop `antlr/v4` + `bytebase/parser/postgresql` imports from the shared schema differ package

## Why this is safe

- Production PG migration has two API entry points (`DiffSchema`, `DiffMetadata`), both route through the omni SDL path — the legacy differ is never called for PG in production
- The `OldASTNode`/`NewASTNode` fields had zero references across the entire codebase
- PG comparers fall back safely to `DefaultXxxComparer` when not registered
- Other engines (MySQL, MSSQL, Oracle, TiDB) are unaffected — they don't use PG ANTLR types

title: refactor(pg): delete GetDatabaseMetadata and unify migration to DiffSDLMigration [BYT-9010]
body:
## Summary
- Delete ANTLR-based `GetDatabaseMetadata` (~2,900 lines) — DDL text parsing now handled by omni `LoadSDL`
- Unify all PG migration paths to single `DiffSDLMigration(sourceSDL, targetSDL)` core
- `SDLMigration` and `DiffMigration` become generic functions that call `MetadataToSDL` + `DiffSDLMigration`
- Refactor `DiffSchema` API: extract `resolveMetadata`, remove dead code
- Add `DiffSchemaTextMigration` → replaced by `DiffSDLMigration` → cleaned up
- Add filter tests for bbdataarchive and SkipDump behavior
- Migrate 10 deleted ANTLR tests to omni equivalents

## Architecture after this PR
```
DiffSDLMigration(engine, sourceSDL, targetSDL)  ← only registered interface
  PG: LoadSDL → Catalog → Diff → GenerateMigration

MetadataToSDL(engine, metadata) → SDL text       ← generic, uses GetDatabaseDefinition
SDLMigration = MetadataToSDL + DiffSDLMigration   ← generic wrapper
DiffMigration = 2x MetadataToSDL + DiffSDLMigration  ← generic wrapper with fallback
```

body:
## Summary

Redesign the masking exemption list page to support classification level conditions and fix UX issues with the flat table view. Part of BYT-9097 / BYT-9098.

- **Responsive layout**: Split-panel (member list + detail) on wide screens, expandable list on narrow
- **Member-grouped view**: Exemptions grouped by member, then by grant (same description+expiration+level merged)
- **Classification level display**: Per-resource level badges in the resource table, level-only grants shown as key-value cards
- **Auto-generated grant titles**: `hr_prod (schema public)`, `bbdev, hr_prod +1 more`, `All databases, level ≤ 3`
- **AdvancedSearch filter bar**: Same pattern as issue list page, with database/member/status scopes and Active/Expired/All preset tabs
- **Grant-level status filtering**: Active tab shows only active grants per member, Expired tab shows only expired
- **Fix resource.database CEL bug**: Rewrite `resource.database` to `resource.instance_id + resource.database_name` in expression mode (bug from #19728)

### New files (14)
- `exemptionDataUtils.ts` + `.test.ts` — Pure data logic with 57 tests (parsing, grouping, merging, title generation)
- `useExemptionData.ts` — Vue composable wrapping utils with policy fetch/revoke
- `useExemptionSearchScopeOptions.ts` — AdvancedSearch scope factory
- `ExemptionSearchBar.vue` / `ExemptionPresetTabs.vue` — Search + tabs
- `ExemptionMemberList.vue` / `ExemptionMemberItem.vue` — Member list
- `ExemptionDetailPanel.vue` / `ExemptionGrantSection.vue` — Grant detail
- `ExemptionResourceTable.vue` / `ExemptionLevelCard.vue` / `LevelBadge.vue` — Leaf components

### Modified files
- `ProjectMaskingExemption.vue` — Rewired with responsive layout
- `GrantAccessForm.vue` — Fix `resource.database` → `resource.instance_id + resource.database_name`
- `types.ts` — Added `ExemptionGrant`, `ExemptionMember`, `ClassificationLevel`
- 5 locale files — New i18n keys

### Key design decisions
- **Grant merging**: Exemptions with same (description, expiration, classificationLevel) are merged into one grant with combined + deduplicated resources
- **Auto-titles over "Unnamed grant"**: Titles derived from resource hierarchy (database → schema → table, ignore columns)
- **Expiry display**: Relative time (blue) + absolute date inline for active; strikethrough for expired; amber for never-expires
- **No classification level filter**: The comparison operators (>=, <=, ==) don't map cleanly to a dropdown filter
- **Preserved `MaskingExceptionUserTable.vue`**: Still used by `GrantAccessDrawer.vue`

+package pricing
+
+import (
+	"github.com/pkg/errors"
+
+	storepb "github.com/bytebase/bytebase/backend/generated-go/store"
+)
+
+// PriceModel holds the inputs for price calculation.
+type PriceModel struct {
+	Plan     *PlanLimitConfig
+	Interval storepb.SubscriptionPayload_BillingInterval
+	Seats    int32
+}
+
+// NewPriceModel validates inputs and returns a PriceModel.
+func NewPriceModel(plan storepb.SubscriptionPayload_Plan, interval storepb.SubscriptionPayload_BillingInterval, seats int32) (*PriceModel, error) {
+	limit := GetPlanLimit(plan)
+	if limit == nil {
+		return nil, errors.Errorf("unknown plan %v", plan)
+	}
+	if !limit.SelfServicePurchase {
+		return nil, errors.Errorf("plan %v does not support self-service purchase", plan)
+	}
+	if interval == storepb.SubscriptionPayload_BILLING_INTERVAL_UNSPECIFIED {
+		return nil, errors.New("billing interval is required")
+	}
+	if seats < 1 {
+		return nil, errors.Errorf("seats must be at least 1, got %d", seats)
+	}
+	if limit.MaximumSeatCount >= 0 && seats > limit.MaximumSeatCount {
+		return nil, errors.Errorf("seats %d exceeds maximum %d for plan %v", seats, limit.MaximumSeatCount, plan)
+	}
+	return &PriceModel{
+		Plan:     limit,
+		Interval: interval,
+		Seats:    seats,
+	}, nil
+}
+
+// GetPrice returns the total price in USD cents.
+func (m *PriceModel) GetPrice() int64 {
+	billableSeats := m.Seats - m.Plan.FreeSeatCount
+	if billableSeats < 0 {
+		billableSeats = 0
+	}
+	monthlyPrice := int64(billableSeats) * m.Plan.PricePerSeatPerMonth
+
+	switch m.Interval {
+	case storepb.SubscriptionPayload_YEAR:
+		return monthlyPrice * 12
+	default:
+		return monthlyPrice
+	}
+}
+
+// GetStripeInterval returns the Stripe recurring interval string.
+func (m *PriceModel) GetStripeInterval() string {
+	if m.Interval == storepb.SubscriptionPayload_YEAR {
+		return "year"
+	}
+	return "month"
+}
+
+// GetPlanText returns a display name for the plan.
+func (m *PriceModel) GetPlanText() string {
+	switch m.Plan.Plan {
+	case storepb.SubscriptionPayload_TEAM:
+		return "Pro Plan"
+	case storepb.SubscriptionPayload_ENTERPRISE:
+		return "Enterprise Plan"
+	default:
+		return "Free Plan"
+	}
+}

+name: Build and Push Cloud Image to GAR
+
+on:
+  workflow_dispatch:
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+
+env:
+  GAR_LOCATION: us-central1
+  GAR_REPOSITORY: bytebase
+  IMAGE_NAME: bytebase-cloud
+
+jobs:
+  build-and-push:
+    runs-on: depot-ubuntu-24.04-arm-4
+    steps:
+      - name: Checkout code
+        uses: actions/checkout@v6
+
+      - name: Extract build args
+        run: |
+          echo "GIT_COMMIT=$(git rev-parse HEAD)" >> $GITHUB_ENV
+
+      - name: Set up Cloud SDK
+        uses: google-github-actions/setup-gcloud@v3
+        with:
+          project_id: ${{ secrets.GCP_PROJECT_ID }}
+
+      - name: Authenticate to Google Cloud
+        uses: google-github-actions/auth@v3
+        with:
+          credentials_json: ${{ secrets.GCP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_KEY }}
+
+      - name: Configure Docker for Artifact Registry
+        run: |
+          gcloud auth configure-docker ${{ env.GAR_LOCATION }}-docker.pkg.dev
+
+      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
+        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3
+
+      - name: Build and push Docker image
+        uses: docker/build-push-action@v6
+        with:
+          context: .
+          file: scripts/Dockerfile
+          push: true
+          tags: |
+            ${{ env.GAR_LOCATION }}-docker.pkg.dev/${{ secrets.GCP_PROJECT_ID }}/${{ env.GAR_REPOSITORY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}:latest
+          build-args: |
+            VERSION=cloud
+            GIT_COMMIT=${{ env.GIT_COMMIT }}
+            RELEASE=release

title: fix: remove TiDB non-transaction statement handling for TiDB
body: ## Summary - remove TiDB-specific non-transaction statement bucketing during migration execution - execute TiDB statements in source order for both transaction and auto-commit modes - add TiDB container regression tests for CREATE INDEX inside a transaction and prepared-statement flows containing CREATE INDEX text ## Root cause Bytebase treated statements containing `CREATE INDEX` text as non-transactional and moved them to the end of execution. That reordered scripts like `SET @sql := ...; PREPARE stmt FROM @sql;`, causing `PREPARE` to run before `@sql` was assigned. ## Testing - go test -v -count=1 ./backend/plugin/db/tidb - golangci-lint run --allow-parallel-runners - go build -ldflags "-w -s" -p=16 -o ./bytebase-build/bytebase ./backend/bin/server/main.go Close BYT-9091

title: refactor: move workspace branding to workspace table payload
body:
## Summary

Move workspace metadata (title, branding logo) from the `setting` table into a JSONB `payload` column on the `workspace` table. Add `GetWorkspace` API for the login page.

### Schema
- **`workspace` table**: Replaced `name text` column with `payload jsonb` (`WorkspacePayload` proto: `title`, `branding_logo`)
- **Migration `0013`**: Adds `payload` column, migrates `name` into `payload.title`, drops `name` column. Idempotent.

### Proto
- **`WorkspacePayload`** (store proto): New message with `title` and `branding_logo` fields
- **`Workspace`** (API proto): Added `string logo` field
- **`GetWorkspace` RPC**: `GET /v1/{name=workspaces/*}` with `allow_without_credential`
  - `workspaces/-`: resolves current/default workspace (login page logo)
  - `workspaces/{id}`: requires auth + membership verification
- **`WorkspaceProfileSetting`**: Removed `branding_logo` field (reserved 16)
- **`ResourcePackage`**: Deprecated — replaced by `GetWorkspace`

### Store
- `WorkspaceMessage.Name` → `WorkspaceMessage.Payload` (`*storepb.WorkspacePayload`)
- All workspace CRUD methods updated to read/write JSONB payload
- `UpdateWorkspace` supports `title` and `logo` fields

### API
- `GetWorkspace`: Returns workspace name, title, logo. Unauthenticated for `workspaces/-`, auth+membership check for specific workspaces
- `UpdateWorkspace`: Now supports `logo` in update_mask
- `GetResourcePackage` in actuator: Logo check moved to workspace payload
- `BrandingLogo` feature detection reads from workspace payload instead of setting

### Frontend
- `ProfileBrandingLogo`: Unified component with `size` prop, uses imported default logo asset
- `BrandingSetting`: Updated to use workspace API for logo management

## Test plan
- [x] `go build` passes
- [x] `golangci-lint` clean
- [ ] Integration tests

title: feat: support classification level in masking exemption policy
body:
## Summary

- Allow exemption policy CEL expressions to use `resource.classification_level` so users can grant exemptions like `classification_level <= 3`
- Redesign the masking exemption list table to show raw CEL conditions instead of fragile parsed Resource column
- Fix multiple bugs: classification config not loading, CEL expression data loss on submit, multiple exemptions created for multi-table selection

## Backend

- Add `resource.classification_level` (int) to `MaskingExemptionPolicyCELAttributes` for validation
- Pass classification level through `evaluateExemptionOfColumn` for runtime evaluation
- Add test cases for classification-level-based exemption matching

## Frontend

- Add `resource.classification_level` factor to CEL expression builder in the Grant Exemption form with comparison operators (`<=`, `>=`, `==`, etc.)
- Fetch `DATA_CLASSIFICATION` setting in `TableDataTable` and `GrantAccessForm` so classification config is available
- Build CEL string directly in expression mode to preserve non-resource conditions (fixes silent data loss)
- Combine multiple resource selections into a single exemption with `||` instead of creating separate exemptions per table
- Redesign exemption list: replace structured Resource column with Condition column showing raw CEL expression

title: refactor: change classification level from string to int
body:
## Summary

- Replace opaque string `level_id` on `DataClassification` with explicit numeric `level` (int32) to enable ordered comparisons like `resource.classification_level <= 3` in CEL masking rules
- Remove `Level.id` (string) — `Level.level` (int32) is now the sole identifier
- Add equality (`==`, `!=`), comparison (`<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`), and collection (`in`, `not_in`) operators for classification level in the frontend CEL builder
- SQL migration converts stored JSONB classification configs and masking rule CEL expressions from string to int format

## Breaking Changes

- **Proto**: `DataClassification.level_id` (string, field 4) → `DataClassification.level` (int32, field 4). `Level.id` (string, field 1) removed, `Level.level` (int32, field 4) added. `MaskingReason.classification_level` changed from string to int32.
- **CEL expressions**: `resource.classification_level` changes from string to int type. Existing expressions like `resource.classification_level in ["2", "3"]` must become `resource.classification_level in [2, 3]`. Migration handles this automatically.
- **Stored data**: JSONB in `setting` (DATA_CLASSIFICATION) and `policy` (MASKING_RULE) tables is migrated automatically.

## Test plan

- [x] Migration tested against local database (`psql -U bbdev bbdev`) — verified classification configs and masking rule CEL expressions convert correctly
- [x] `TestEvalMaskingLevelOfColumn` passes
- [x] `TestLatestVersion` passes
